A property developer in Cornwall was attacked with corrosive liquid outside his home, leaving him with life-changing injuries and a loss of vision. Nicole Phillips, 45, from Hastings, has been charged with perverting the course of justice and is due to appear at Bodmin Magistrates Court. Mr. Christopheros, a businessman in the event and property management industries, is also facing charges of grievous bodily harm with intent.

A Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route has erected signs warning pilgrims not to defecate along the famous path, as angry residents complain about the practice. The signs, which show a squatting figure defecating within a red circle with a diagonal line across it, have become an attraction for pilgrims. The pilgrimage attracts thousands of pilgrims every year, but there are few places to go when nature calls.

A massive fire consumed a building that was once home to a Michigan strip club on Wednesday afternoon. The blaze took place at a Flint intersection and started at about 1pm. Only the building itself and a few nearby power lines were affected. The site was not a vacant facility, and an investigation into what was behind the blaze continues.

A woman of Arab and Jewish descent who was strip-searched at a Detroit-area airport has reached a settlement in a lawsuit filed on her behalf. The federal government will give Shoshana Hebshi $40,000 as compensation for being humiliated on the 10th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks after armed agents forced her from a plane at Detroit Metropolitan Airport, made her undress during a search, and held her for hours. The settlement sends a message that discrimination is not tolerated and will help protect future passengers from similar experiences.

A plane crash landed at Hiroshima Airport in Japan, injuring 20 people and causing the airport to be closed. The Airbus A320, bound from Incheon International Airport in South Korea, reportedly missed the runway and skidded off, spinning 180 degrees and facing the wrong way. Local media reported a hard landing and no sign of the landing gear, with evacuation slides deployed. The crash occurred on August 12, 2021, at 8pm local time.

Mark-Francis Vandelli, a well-to-do reality star on Made In Chelsea, has opened up his watch collection to the Evening Standard, showcasing 16 expensive timepieces that he has been collecting since his teens. The 26-year-old, who currently owns a number of pieces worth several thousand pounds, revealed his favorite items and the history behind them in an interview with the newspaper. His most expensive watch is a Cartier white gold Moonphase, which he bought from a shop on Sloane Street in Chelsea earlier this year, and a Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42, which he purchased on holiday in Italy and can be bought secondhand on the internet for £6,500.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy is selling his extensive collection of antiques, including a 3D diorama of the Battle of Agincourt, a longbow made from yew, and a portrait of himself holding the bow, in a £100,000 auction. The collection, which he has built up over his career, includes paintings, furniture, swords, flintlock rifles, silverware, and crystal chandeliers. Hardy, 89, is downsizing his home and is auctioning off more than 200 items. The sale is being conducted by Dominic Winter auctioneers at its saleroom in South Cerney, Gloucestershire.

A Brazilian commuter, Nelson Felippe, took a photo of a woman hugging another woman on a train platform and shared it on Facebook, expressing his disapproval of the scene. The image quickly went viral, with Felippe warning against homophobia and public displays of affection. Felippe, who works at the Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro, was actually observing a public transport safety regulation, and his post has received thousands of comments, with users praising his witty way of exposing homophobia.

A young English cricket fan, Jonathan Stevenson, wrote a letter to Richie Benaud, the legendary Australian cricket player, asking for tips on left-handed leg spin almost 20 years ago. Benaud's detailed response, dated September 27, 1996, included notes on spin bowling for left-hand bowlers and was accompanied by a full sheet of notes. The letter, signed by Benaud, was shared on Twitter as a tribute to the "great man" and included advice on different deliveries and how to deliver them.

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg predicts that the future of travel will be virtual, with the company purchasing virtual reality headset maker Oculus last year. Zuckerberg believes that users will be able to capture and share 3D scenes and environments, allowing them to explore locations from multiple viewpoints. Facebook announced plans to support virtual reality on its newsfeed, enabling users to put on a VR headset and explore a location of their choosing. Zuckerberg also mentioned that VR is more than just another platform and can create a range of human experiences. Marriott hotels have already trialled Oculus Rift on a tour of hotels across America, allowing guests to sample different holiday destinations.

A loving boyfriend has granted his girlfriend her birthday wish of having their wedding photographs taken, even though they can't officially get married yet because she is bedridden in hospital due to bone cancer. Guo Kai, a firefighter, has been at his girlfriend's bedside every day, and family and friends helped her put on a beautiful wedding dress for the photos. Dong Hui, 22, chose a wedding dress with embroidered flowers and had her make-up done before posing with her husband-to-be. The couple met a year ago after a mutual friend introduced them and quickly fell in love. Guo arranged for professional photographers to come to the hospital to take the pictures, and the wedding and photo shoot is a dream for them all.

Blaine Boudreaux, a 34-year-old man with a history of DUIs, was charged with intoxication manslaughter, intoxicated assault, and failure to stop and render aid involving death in connection to three separate DUI collisions that took place within three hours in Houston. Boudreaux, who allegedly ran a red light and slammed his Dodge pickup truck into a Honda Civic, killed a 6-year-old boy and injured his mother. The suspect was arrested at the scene after failing a field sobriety test.

Microsoft has launched a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions within the company, with the aim of expanding opportunity and representing its customers. The positions will be based at Microsoft's Redmond campus in Washington and will be run in partnership with Specialisterne, a Danish nonprofit that helps train people with autism for careers in IT. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella was forced to apologize for saying that women don't need to ask for a raise and should just trust the system to pay them well, but the company is now focusing on diversity.

Two deputies involved in the fatal shooting of Eric Harris in Tulsa, Oklahoma, have been reassigned due to threats against them and their families. The shooting occurred when Reserve Deputy Robert Bates shot Harris, who was trying to arrest him. The deputies are not charged with a crime but have come under criticism for their actions. The sheriff's office has suspended operations of the drug unit pending a review of the April 2 shooting of Harris. The shooting has led to allegations of forgery and unqualified training, with the sheriff denying those allegations. The family of Eric Harris has demanded justice and changes in policy.

Katie Prager, a 24-year-old woman with cystic fibrosis, is in desperate need of a life-saving lung transplant due to an infection called Burkholderia Cepacia. Her husband, Dalton, has already received new lungs, but Katie is waiting for a transplant at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. Her insurance company, Kentucky Medicaid, will not cover the out-of-state treatment, leaving the couple in a race against time to save Katie's life.

The Sleep Cycle app data reveals that the world sleeps the least on Tuesdays, with Americans waking up at 7am and being in the worst mood all week. The best sleep quality worldwide occurs on Wednesdays, with China recording the highest sleep quality that night. The app tracks sleep phases using the phone's accelerometer and has more than two million active users.

Mexican artist Frida Kahlo's unpublished love letters to her lover Jose Bartoli, written during her secret three-year romance with him while she was married to muralist Diego Rivera, are expected to fetch upwards of $120,000 when they go up for auction at Doyle New York on April 15. The letters, written in Spanish between August 1946 and November 1949 and saved by Jose until his death in 1995, were passed down through different generations of his family until they reached the current owner. The collection of 25 letters, which comprise more than 100 pages, includes passionate messages, original drawings, and other personal items. The letters shed light on Frida's important paintings, an unknown pregnancy, and her relationship with Diego, as well as her adoration for her lover.

In this article, McCluskey, the leader of Unite, a powerful trade union in the UK, is portrayed as a charismatic and popular figure who is highly popular with activists. However, the article also highlights the sinister and potentially dangerous nature of McCluskey and his union's influence in British politics, as they seek to use their financial and organizational muscle within the Labour movement to drag Britain back to the dark days of the 1970s. The article also mentions that McCluskey's union, Unite, is intertwined with the Labour Party's structure, MPs, and finances, and remains addicted to failed socialist policies of the past.

A zookeeper captured footage of various animals drinking water in their enclosures using a GoPro camera. The footage shows a range of drinking methods, from a rhino almost kissing the surface of the water to a lemur delicately licking it. The zookeeper, Elad Hershkowitz, filmed the animals for 30 hours and then edited the footage down to four minutes. Some animals were initially skeptical about the foreign object in their troughs, but eventually got used to the camera's presence and drank freely. The zookeeper anticipated a range of reactions from the animals and ensured the camera was secure before the experiment.

A recent poll suggests that only 25% of voters believe David Cameron is hungriest to win the election, while 43% think Ed Miliband is most up for the fight. The poll also shows that voters generally believe Cameron wants to win less than Miliband. Cameron is seen as the strongest leader compared to Miliband, but voters appear to think he wants to win less. The article also mentions that Cameron is using a "sleeves rolled up" strategy to show he is fighting hard for a Tory victory.

A man accused of assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov has told a court he was beaten and pressured into confessing to the murder. Zaur Dadaev, one of five Chechen men accused of killing Nemstov, told the court he had been abducted, beaten, and pressured into confessing. Dadaev had previously confessed to the murder but now says he was beaten and pressured into making that statement. The case has sparked protests in Russia, with more than 20,000 people marching in Moscow to demand justice for Nemstov's death.

A 4-month-old baby boy named Sonit Awal was pulled from the rubble of a Nepal earthquake that killed over 5,000 people and injured many more. The baby was buried for 22 hours after his home collapsed during the 7.8-magnitude earthquake. His father, Shyam Awal, frantically searched for him amid the debris, but gave up hope until he heard faint cries from below. The soldiers returned and lifted Sonit clear of the rubble at 10 a.m. on Sunday, and he was taken to Bhaktapur Hospital, where he was found to be uninjured. The baby's unlikely rescue provides some hope to a country that has experienced so much loss.

A Church of Scientology-backed organization is facing a land use battle over plans to turn a patch of secluded land near the presidential retreat Camp David into a drug rehab center. Narcocon, a drug rehab network affiliated with the Church of Scientology, argues that the property has historic significance due to President Herbert Hoover's catch of a fish there, while opponents view it as a trick to circumvent zoning laws. The proposed designation could allow Narcocon to build a center for twelve patients, using sauna sessions and the teachings of Scientology founder L. Ron Hubbard. The program, which can cost more than $30,000 per month, aims to eliminate addiction cravings by flushing them out through a regimen of exercise, sauna sessions, and mega-doses of the vitamin Niacin.

The article describes the transformation of Kabul, Afghanistan, following the end of the U.S. military presence. Despite the city's population increasing due to the influx of refugees, many workers have lost their jobs and are now isolated and fearful of reprisals. The article highlights the challenges faced by the city's residents, including the loss of their English-speaking skills, the isolation of the community, and the fear of violence.

Two Navy SEALs died and another was critically injured while training in a pool at a Virginia military base, according to a Navy spokesman. The incident occurred on Friday at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story. Both SEALs were assigned to Naval Special Warfare Group Two and were not wearing gear at the time of the incident. The investigation into the incident is ongoing.

NBC, the broadcasting giant holding live rights to the Premier League in the United States, expects to see more people watching Premier League matches in the country than in Britain in the near future. The company has doubled US interest in the English top division in the past two years, with some 32 million Americans watching at least one top-flight English game live in 2019-20. NBC has transported their entire Premier League production from their HQ in Connecticut to England for this weekend's matches, with star anchor Rebecca Lowe presenting Burnley's match against Arsenal. The company is enhancing coverage and influencing young American football fans' choices, with replica Premier League shirts becoming more common in the country.

In a heated exchange on the Andrew Marr Show, Boris Johnson accused Ed Miliband of doing "more damage to the country than he did to his brother" and claimed that Labour could not take power without the support of the SNP. The two politicians engaged in a verbal battle, with Johnson accusing Miliband of being a "monkey" and Johnson saying that Miliband would do "more damage to this country than he did to his brother." The exchange ended with both men trying to laugh off the attack.

A 26-year-old Oregon prisoner Dustin Irons was slapped with an extra 30 days behind bars for dropping his trousers and flashing a judge during a court hearing. Despite being in handcuffs, Irons became disgruntled and exposed himself to the judge, leading to his punishment. Sheriff's office quickly covered him up and bundled him back to his cell. Captain Stewart Harp admitted that Irons' behavior was "pretty creative." Irons, who was already in prison for trashing a hotel room and assaulting people inside, faces another disciplinary investigation and could be put into a segregation unit.

Jenson Button believes McLaren has made significant progress in Formula One since their poor start to the season in Australia, with improvements in Malaysia. Although Button and Fernando Alonso retired during the race, the team discovered the car was competitive alongside other midfield runners. Button hopes further steps have been taken going into this weekend's race in Shanghai, where McLaren is now comparing themselves with the Force Indias, Saubers, and Lotuses. Despite the positives, Button acknowledges the entire team still has a long way to go.

A hospital in Western Australia, the $2 billion Fiona Stanley Hospital, was found to have blood and bone fragments on supposedly sanitised medical instruments, leading to the hospital being stripped of its medical service provider Serco and fined $60,000. The hospital has been found to continue operating with poorly sanitised instruments, raising concerns about the safety of its patients. The incident has damaged the hospital's public image and generated morale issues among its workforce.

A couple who chose to forgo their dream wedding to pay for IVF treatment and eventually conceive twins celebrated their happy ending by getting married and having a white wedding. Becca and Dale Litchfield, who had given up on their dream wedding, were overjoyed when they discovered their fertility treatment had worked and welcomed twins, Darci-Mai and Stanley. The couple, who had spent £5,500 on two rounds of IVF, were now able to celebrate their perfect family and the chance to say their "I do's" after years of trying.

A family-friendly coffee shop in Omaha, Nebraska, had its Facebook page hacked and flooded with pornography after an employee clicked on a malicious link in an email. The hack lasted for 24 hours, during which time the page was replaced with adult cartoons similar to those posted on other brands. The company issued an apology and removed the inappropriate content, but it was not until a day later that Facebook was contacted to regain control of the account.

A young Shibu Inu puppy at an American Kennel Club center attempted to bark at a husky dog, causing laughter and confusion among onlookers. The video shows the Shibu Inu squeaking and squawking, attempting to bark at the husky, which then whined back. The dogs continued to vocalize at one another, with people in the video laughing and mimicking their actions. The video concludes with the husky losing interest and the Shibu Inu settling down.

Liam Plunkett, an experienced English fast bowler, is eager to make a comeback in the West Indies Test series. He aims to use his pace to lead England to victory and has trained hard to become the fastest bowler on the pitch. Plunkett is competing for a place in the England Test side with Chris Jordan and Mark Wood, and he relishes the opportunity to prove himself against the West Indies batsmen.

Paul Smith, a boxer from Liverpool, is set to face Andre Ward in a unification fight for the WBA super-middleweight title. The bout is seen as a warm-up for Ward's rematch with Carl Froch, who is ranked among the top five pound-for-pound boxers in the world. The WBA has ordered Ward and Froch to meet in a unification fight, and Froch is turning his attention to his other ambition before retirement - a first appearance on the Las Vegas Strip, against the namesake son of Mexican legend Julio Cesar Chavez.

In Parma, Missouri, a small town with a predominantly black population, five of its six police officers and several other top officials resigned after the election of the first African American mayor, Tyrus Byrd. The resignations were attributed to "safety concerns," and the town's residents, including Byrd's father, Simon Wofford, who was defeated in the election, believe the departures were unwelcome. The town has struggled with crime, and residents have expressed concern about the lack of police presence on the streets.

Manchester City midfielder Yaya Toure will not be forced out of the club, but the team is set to make him available this summer. Toure, who has played a major role in City's recent trophy-laden period, is content with his life at the Etihad Stadium and is not in a rush to leave. However, the Ivorian's wages are a stumbling block towards a potential move, with Inter Milan showing interest but being wary of the huge salary. City is resisting attempts by Valencia to pull out of a £24 million deal for Alvaro Negredo to fund a move for Radamel Falcao.

A new study suggests that more than two-thirds of people taking antidepressants may not actually have depression, as the majority of those taking SSRIs, the most commonly prescribed type of antidepressant, did not meet the criteria for clinical depression. The study, published in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, found that 38% of those taking antidepressants did not meet the criteria for obsessive compulsive disorder, panic disorder, social phobia, or generalised anxiety disorder. The researchers concluded that antidepressants are commonly used in the absence of clear evidence-based indications.

Doris Fuller, the mother of a mentally ill daughter who killed herself, revealed her daughter's struggles with bipolar disorder and psychosis, which led to her death. Fuller wrote about how her daughter's illness, which went undiagnosed until her early 20s, eventually drove her to suicide. Despite receiving proper treatment, Natalie eventually decided to stop taking her medications, which brought her troubles back, even more acute than before. Fuller described her daughter as the bravest person she had ever known, and her suicide did not change that.

A 10-year-old boy named Koby Hodder nearly died after suffering a cardiac arrest in the school playground while playing British Bulldog, a game involving running from one side of a field to another without being caught. His heart stopped for 12 minutes, and he was later diagnosed with the same heart condition as footballer Fabrice Muamba, who had a similar cardiac arrest in 2012. Teachers at Koby's school were able to give him CPR until paramedics arrived and saved his life by giving him two shocks with a defibrillator.

Baroness Hale of Richmond, Britain's most senior female judge, has called for changes to England and Wales' divorce laws to remove the need for allegations of adultery and blame, aiming to reduce bitterness in matrimonial disputes. She proposed a one-year cooling-off period after declaring that a marriage has permanently broken down, allowing couples to sort out arrangements for children and money before obtaining a divorce. Lady Hale, who was behind the move for 'no fault' divorce 20 years ago, believes this overhaul would encourage couples to take responsibility for their actions and make arrangements for their children and finances before obtaining a divorce.

Tottenham Hotspur is considering a state-of-the-art stadium with a retractable pitch that could accommodate an NFL franchise, potentially sharing the stadium with the Buffalo Bills and Jacksonville Jaguars. The stadium, set to be completed for the 2018-19 season, would feature NFL-style synthetic surfaces and extra-large changing rooms. The NFL is expected to have a permanent franchise in London within five years, and the proposed stadium design could offer logistical advantages for NFL teams. However, Tottenham's decision to share the stadium with the NFL could impact the Football Association's plans for Wembley Stadium.

U.S. lawmakers have written to FIFA President Sepp Blatter, urging the global football governing body to remove Russia from hosting the 2018 World Cup due to its role in the Ukraine crisis and occupation of Crimea. The senators, including Republican John McCain, believe that allowing Russia to host the World Cup at a time when it should be condemned would bolster the prestige of the Russian regime. The letter comes as England is planning a bid to host the 2028 tournament and is also interested in bidding for the 2026 World Cup.

Universal announced that the sequel to the box office blockbuster "Fifty Shades of Grey" will hit theaters on February 10, 2017, and the third film in the series will debut on February 9, 2018. Niall Leonard, who is married and has two sons with the author, will write the script for the second film. The author, Erika Leonard, has been credited with keeping a strong amount of creative control when it comes to Universal's adaptations of her books. The second film is titled "Fifty Shades Darker."

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis will receive a hero's welcome when he returns to Crystal Palace, but his overall record as a Premier League manager is one of the worst of any long-serving manager. Pulis has never finished in the top half of the Premier League, and he is currently struggling to avoid relegation after West Brom's recent poor form. Pulis has a strong track record with Stoke City and Palace, but his recent season has not been successful, and he is still facing the challenge of avoiding relegation.

Fenerbahce, the Turkish football club, has called for the suspension of the Turkish championship following a gun attack on their team bus during a match against Caykur Rizespor. The attack resulted in the driver being wounded and taken to the hospital, with no mention of any injuries to other individuals. The club's statement emphasizes the importance of solving the attack and finding and punishing the culprits. The incident occurred after Fener's 5-1 win away to Rizespor, with the bus going over a viaduct on its way from Rize to Trabzon.

A massive snow avalanche struck Everest Base Camp on Saturday, trapping hundreds of climbers and rescuers in the freezing cold. The avalanche, which was triggered by the Nepal earthquake, killed at least 17 people and injured dozens more. The rescue efforts are ongoing, with helicopters bringing stranded climbers down from higher camps. The avalanche has also caused significant damage to the Khumbu Icefall, making it impassable for climbers.

Gregory Margolin, a 16-year-old Jewish recruit in the Soviet Red Army during World War II, found himself again in the middle of war in Ukraine. Margolin, who survived one war, was able to survive another, even as a stray missile hit his house, killing his daughter. The family decided to move to Israel, where they felt safer. Margolin, who had survived one war, was brought to Israel as part of a wave of Ukrainian Jewish immigration to support Israel.

John Carver, who was assistant to Ruud Gullit during Newcastle's 1999 derby loss, is now fighting to win the head coach position at his hometown club. He recalls Gullit's controversial decision to leave out star players in the 1999 match, which led to the manager's downfall. Carver believes a positive result against Sunderland on Sunday could help him secure the job, as it would be seen as a motivation for Sunderland to play better.

The Reverend Al Sharpton delivered a sermon and addressed the Walter Scott situation on Sunday morning in North Charleston, South Carolina. He praised Mayor Keith Summey for firing the officer who killed Scott and called for reform in national policing legislation. Sharpton also attended a vigil near the scene of the Scott shooting on Sunday afternoon. Scott, a black driver, was fatally shot by a white police officer after he fled a traffic stop. Sharpton denied that Scott's family barred him from attending his funeral on Saturday, claiming that the National Action Network's convention with thousands of delegates was happening in New York.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers will remind Raheem Sterling of his responsibilities after the forward was caught passing out and puffing on a shisha pipe, which led to a club investigation and potential disciplinary action. Sterling, who is unwilling to sign a new contract at Anfield, scored the opener in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United, but Rodgers said he will speak to the rising star about being a professional. Rodgers praised Sterling's skill and ability, but acknowledged that he may have missed an opportunity to score a second goal.

Union donations to Labour's election campaign have surged, with the party receiving more than £1 million in donations between April 6 and April 12, compared to just £492,512 for the Conservative party. Labour's union donations, which equate to £105,420.80 a day, have boosted the party's war chest and are seen as a potential source of funding for Ed Miliband's leadership. The union donations have been criticized by opponents as a form of political funding, with some suggesting that Labour will be forced to compromise on issues such as spending, borrowing, and taxes in exchange for the union's financial support.

Passengers on a Qatar Airways flight diverted to Birmingham Airport in the UK after severe winds caused two landing attempts at Manchester Airport were initially called to the tarmac by police for kicking off. The flight was eventually allowed to land and refuel, but some passengers were left waiting for hours in the airport. Qatar Airways apologized for the delay, which occurred after strong winds meant the aircraft couldn't land at Manchester. The airline arranged for the transportation of passengers to Manchester.

Canadian pop sensation Justin Bieber will carry Floyd Mayweather's championship belts into the ring ahead of his $300 million Las Vegas mega-fight with Manny Pacquiao on Saturday. The 21-year-old performer has been close friends with Mayweather for years and has accompanied him into the ring on numerous occasions. Bieber is set to lead out Mayweather's entourage at the MGM Grand, according to an insider. Mayweather, who has a 47-0 record on the line, knows this fight is without doubt the biggest of his career and the most lucrative. Bieber confirmed in a video posted online that he will be part of Mayweather's entourage for the mega-fight, shouting 'hell yeah' when asked by reporters.

The article discusses the closure of Corinthian Colleges Inc., a for-profit college that has been struggling to hold accountable. Corinthian, which once enrolled over 70,000 students, is one of the worst "predator colleges" due to its dubious degrees, high student debt, and reliance on federal student aid. The closure is seen as a positive development in the fight against for-profit colleges. Corinthian's closure will help transition students into legitimate postsecondary schools and reduce the default rate of for-profit college students, who account for nearly half of all student loan defaults. The article also highlights the aggressive tactics used by for-profit colleges to enroll students, such as recruiters making 100 phone calls and leaving 100 messages a day.

Pep Guardiola has denied claims of a dispute with former Bayern Munich club doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit the club after being blamed for the defeat by Porto. Muller-Wohlfahrt claimed the bond of trust was damaged, but Guardiola played down the feud. The doctor's decision came after Bayern Munich lost 3-1 to Porto in the Champions League quarter-final. Guardiola also appeared to publicly humiliate Muller-Wohlfahrt eight days before his exit from the club. Muller-Wohlfahrt is a renowned world leader in his field and has been at Bayern for almost 40 years.

Wladimir Klitschko, the reigning heavyweight champion, has recalled his dramatic rise to the top on the eve of his world title defence against Bryant Jennings. The 39-year-old Ukrainian superstar will make his return to US soil for the first time in seven years when he takes on the slick Philadelphian at the iconic Madison Square Garden in New York. Klitschko, who won Olympic gold in Atlanta in 1996, has been reminiscing about how it all started for him when he won gold at the Olympics, instantly catapulting him into a hero in his home country. Despite being just a year short of his 40th birthday, Klitschko believes age has no bearing on how long he can go on for. He will make his return to US soil for the first time in seven years at Madison Square Garden.

Jeremy Clarkson, who was fired from Top Gear in March after attacking a producer during filming, has finally spoken out about his dismissal. He expressed his "heartfelt thanks" to those who supported him and said he would "miss being there." Former presenter Angela Rippon, who first presented the show 38 years ago, expressed interest in returning to the show if invited back. The future of the show is still up in the air, with former newsreader Jodie Kidd and DIY SOS star Nick Knowles being linked to the position. BBC bosses are reportedly trying to hold onto James May and Richard Hammond, who are Clarkson's co-presenters.

In a bizarre incident during Barcelona's 1-0 victory over Celta Vigo, Fabian Orellana, Celta Vigo's striker, threw a lump of grass at Sergio Busquets, leading to Orellana being shown a red card. The incident escalated tensions between the two players, with Busquets grabbing his eye despite the grass striking him. Referee Inaki Vicandi Garrido awarded a straight red card to Orellana, and the match ended with Barcelona earning crucial three points.

In 2013, three people died and over 200 were injured when a pair of bombs went off within 12 seconds of each other at the finish line of the Boston Marathon. This year, the jury convicted Dzhokhar Tsarnaev in the bombings, and federal Judge George A. O'Toole warned jurors not to attend the Boston Marathon or any events or gatherings related to the anniversary or the current running of the Boston Marathon. The sentencing phase of Tsarnaev's trial began on April 21, and the maximum penalty for several of the charges is death.

Tens of millions of Chinese people marked the annual Qingming Festival this weekend by travelling home to their ancestral villages, cleaning tombs, burning fake paper money, and leaving food and drink to ensure their loved ones are not poor or hungry in the afterlife. The festival, also known as Tomb Sweeping Day, is a three-day holiday in China that celebrates the coming spring and the beauty of nature. The festival is one of the 24 Chinese solar terms and is considered the start of spring, with temperatures rising, rainfall increasing, and marking an important time for the land to be prepared for the sowing of seeds.

Paul Simon, 73, has returned to the top of the UK album chart with his latest release, The Ultimate Collection, which has outsold more youthful musicians like Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. The album includes 19 tracks from Simon's 50-year career, including hits from his days with Simon & Garfunkel. Simon's recent tour with Sting is believed to have been the catalyst in helping him reach the top of the charts. This marks his first number one album since The Rhythm of the Saints in 1990.

Iker Casillas, the 33-year-old goalkeeper for Real Madrid, insists he will stay at the club even if David de Gea arrives to displace him as first choice keeper. The Spanish international has spent his entire career at the Bernabeu but has faced criticism in recent seasons. Despite the possibility of a move to Manchester United, Casillas claims he is willing to fight for the jersey he made his own. The Spanish giants have linked to a move for Manchester United's David de Gea, but Casillas is determined to stay and earn his place at the club. Real Madrid is hoping to become the first team to retain the Champions League title, and the team is determined to defend their title, with Casillas focusing on helping the team reach the semi-finals.

Britain was hailed as a "job-creating machine" last night as employment rose to its highest level in history, with the International Monetary Fund praising Chancellor George Osborne's economic strategy. The Conservatives' plan has led to a 557,000 increase in employment since 2010, with Rolls-Royce announcing its biggest-ever order for passenger jets. The IMF and German finance minister praised the Government's "right balance" of spending cuts and tax rises, reducing the deficit from £153 billion under Labour in 2009-10 to £90 billion last year. The Chancellor, speaking at the IMF and World Bank meetings, said the UK economy is "firmly on course" with a halved deficit and strong growth. However, Greece poses a threat to the global economy, and fears are mounting that the recession-battered country will default on its debts, potentially hitting Britain.

SsangYong, a Korean automaker, is launching a new sports utility vehicle (SUV) called Tivoli in the UK, priced under £13,000. The SUV is designed to appeal to thrifty motorists who want value for money. It comes in three trim levels, with a choice of front-wheel drive or 4x4, and a five-year unlimited mileage warranty. The Tivoli is named after the Italian town of Tivoli, known for its Renaissance architecture and garden, and is equipped with features such as seven airbags, cruise control, and a TomTom navigation system. SsangYong expects the Tivoli to double the company's annual UK sales from 2,000 to 4,000 a year.

A chef, Sam Longhurst, created a 10-inch, half-kilogram burger at the Whole Damn Farm restaurant in Manchester, England, containing six forms of three different meats and 2,000 calories. The burger, priced at £13. 50, was inspired by a customer's request for a burger with three kinds of meat. The meal features two beef patties, homemade bacon jam, ham chunks, a whole fried chicken thigh, barbequed pulled pork, and bacon rashers, all sandwiched between two brioche buns. The creation was met with enthusiasm, with customers praising its size and variety of meats.

The Yeo Valley staff canteen, located in Blagdon, North Somerset, offers a high-quality, organic, and locally sourced menu to its 120 dairy workers for as little as £2, prepared by Michelin-starred executive chef Paul Collins. The menu changes daily, featuring dishes like soft-poached quail egg, confit of tomato, and deep fried polenta. The canteen, praised as the world's best staff canteen, has opened to the public at higher prices, with meals priced at £4 for a beef burger and £2 for desserts.

Blues legend B.B. King was hospitalized for dehydration, but he is now feeling much better and has left the hospital. King, who is 89 years old, has used various models of Gibson guitars over the years, including a custom-made signature model named Lucille. He has won multiple Grammy nominations and has released hits such as "The Thrill Is Gone" and "When Love Comes to Town." King has been inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and has performed in Chicago, where he suffered from dehydration and exhaustion after a show.

On Easter Sunday, Manhattan's Fifth Avenue was transformed into a sea of bizarre hats as people celebrated the holiday. The parade featured a mix of conservative and outlandish headwear, including floral bonnets, feathered hats, and elaborate dioramas. Some participants wore traditional church attire, while others opted for more modern and unconventional styles. The event, which has been held annually since the 1880s, attracted a diverse crowd, including Christians, Jews, Hindus, agnostics, and atheists. The parade, which started as a strolling display of what prosperous New Yorkers wore, has evolved into a colorful and eclectic celebration of Easter traditions.

Emergency crews in East of England were called to respond to a series of bizarre and inappropriate calls, including one where a squirrel was reported to have been run over by a car in Epping Forest, and another where a man claimed to have dropped his burger and it was bleeding. The service revealed that they had received 1,248 inappropriate calls in the last two years, with front-line crews attending almost half of them. The service urged people to use common sense when calling 999 and to stop and think about the potential consequences of making a prank call.

In a unique football challenge organized by Audi, Chelsea players Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake, along with their teammates Loic Remy and Willian, competed against each other. The challenge involved shooting balls into the boot of a car from close range, sinking balls from long range, and shooting from the top of a convertible Audi. Hazard and Ake won the first two rounds, while Remy and Willian won the final round. The final challenge involved shooting at cars from long range, with Willian's long-range effort causing damage to one of the Audi's.

Brendan Rodgers has criticized Raheem Sterling's advisor, Aidy Ward, for allegedly being manipulated by outside forces and suggesting that the player would be inclined to stay at Liverpool if left to make a decision alone. Sterling has rejected a contract extension worth £100,000 a week and has just two years left on his deal at the end of this season, but Rodgers said he has sat down with Sterling since the TV interview and told him that his best interest would be served by staying at the club for now, even though there may come a time when he does leave.

Rachel Riley, Countdown's co-presenter, was embarrassed on a recent episode when contestants offered up a rude eight-letter word as their answer to the word game. Host Nick Hewer struggled to stifle his laughter, while celebrity guest Dr Phil Hammond saved the day with a nine-letter word. This is not the first time the show's host has struggled to contain himself when a rude word has popped up. Words such as fart, porn, and poo were among the collection of letters which had the Loose Women star and her co-hosts laughing.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, who was arrested after attempting to buy deadly poison on the internet, was spared jail after pleading guilty to trying to commit suicide. The teenager, who cannot be named for legal reasons, was unaware that his online requests were being tracked by covert counter-terrorism officers. The case highlights the dangers of the dark web, a subsection of the deep web, which is used for illegal activities and can be difficult to monitor.

Lianne Hindle, a 37-year-old mother-of-four who died three hours after giving birth to her daughter Poppy, was found dead in the same hospital bed where she had given birth. The deaths of Lianne Hindle and three other babies and one mother at North Manchester General Hospital prompted an investigation. The hospital called in independent experts to review its maternity units after the spate of 10 deaths in the eight-month period from December 2013 to July last year. The family of Lianne Hindle, whose partner Chris Barnes and his sister Karen have called for action to prevent further tragedies, has concerns about the care she received, including being left alone with a student midwife after the birth.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman, who gave birth to her second child just days after a video surfaced of her training while eight months pregnant, has been congratulated by the official Australian Olympic team's Twitter and her former agency PACE Sports Management. Pittman, who plans to compete in both the Beijing World Championships and the 2016 Rio Olympics, continued to train while pregnant with her son Cornelis, who was born at a healthy 3.1 kilograms on Monday. The athlete's coach, Mike Hurst, said that Pittman trained every second day and was careful to monitor her core temperature throughout her training program. Pittman's new daughter was conceived with an anonymous sperm donor and opened up about her second child to Woman's Day, telling the publication this week that she feels "extraordinarily lucky."

A powerful storm capsized several sailboats participating in a regatta in Alabama, resulting in at least one death and missing persons. The storm rolled through the area around 4 p.m. and a man was plucked from the waters by the Coast Guard around 9 p.m. The storm caused significant damage to the boats and participants, with at least one person confirmed dead. The regatta, which was part of the 57th iteration, involved more than 100 sailboats and as many as 200 people.

Roseanne Barr, 62, has revealed that she is going blind due to macular degeneration and glaucoma, two eye diseases that get progressively worse over time and can steal vision. The comic has helped relieve the pressure in her eyes by using marijuana. The diseases are more common in people over 60, with some people, especially African Americans, at higher risk in their 40s. There is no cure for either disease, but treatments can delay the progression of early-stage glaucoma and halt further vision loss in advanced cases of macular degeneration.

A 17-year-old Oklahoma teenager, Chancey Luna, was convicted of first-degree murder in the 2013 shooting death of Australian college baseball player Christopher Lane, who was killed while jogging in Duncan. The jury recommended that Luna be sentenced to life in prison without parole. Luna's defense attorney argued that he meant only to scare Lane, but the judge denied a second-degree murder conviction, which would have carried a sentence of 10 years to life in prison. Luna did not testify and the defense called just one witness, his mother. Luna was described as remorseful during his sentencing, but his mother insisted that he would never intentionally hurt anyone.

Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger insists his team's poor record against Jose Mourinho will not affect their upcoming match against Chelsea, as the two clubs face off in the Premier League. Wenger, who has lost 12 of their 12 meetings, says the result will depend on the performance on the day. Chelsea, who are currently 10 points behind Arsenal, are expected to be favored in the match, with their strengths in counter-attacks and set-pieces making them a challenge for Arsenal. Wenger also mentions the frosty relationship between the two managers and the importance of respect for Chelsea's best player, Cesc Fabregas, who is expected to return to the Emirates Stadium.

Manny Pacquiao, a Filipino boxer, has become one of the most recognizable figures in the world of sports after a series of major fights, including a bout against Floyd Mayweather, which is scheduled for Saturday night at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. Pacquiao, who was born into poverty in the Philippines, spent his early career boxing in the Far East before gaining recognition on the world stage in 2001. He has faced numerous opponents, including Oscar De La Hoya, Ricky Hatton, Miguel Cotto, and four fights against Juan Manuel Marquez. Pacquiao's rise to fame has been marked by his ability to compete at the highest levels of boxing, despite starting his career as a light-flyweight.

A young footballer, Jack Grealish, has been photographed inhaling nitrous oxide, a drug that is considered illegal. Despite being a top-flight starlet, Grealish's behavior has raised concerns among fans and experts. The article suggests that Grealish's actions may help keep him grounded and focused on his career goals. Wenger, the manager of Arsenal, has emphasized the importance of professional athletes taking care of their bodies and avoiding substances that can slow down their performance.

Sam Barton, a 22-year-old man who underwent £55,000 in cosmetic surgery to resemble reality star Joey Essex, was attacked by a group of men who pelted him with eggs on Easter Monday. The attack followed online abuse and forced Barton to move house. Barton, who has spent £20,000 on teeth treatment, £5,000 on Botox, £2,000 on waxing, and £2,500 on tanning, has also spent £10,400 on two nose jobs, with one free on the NHS. He has been bankrupting himself to finance his plastic surgery and champagne lifestyle, which he hopes to match with TOWIE heroes Joey Essex and Harry Derbidge.

A lockdown was ordered at Manchester University in Indiana after a 'likely prank call' about an armed person near the main administration building. Police received a phone call from someone claiming to have stabbed their roommate and threatening to blow up the administration building. The university advised students to shelter in place and issued a campus alert. No injuries were confirmed, and the lockdown was lifted after the incident was determined to be a prank call.

Edinson Cavani, a key player for Paris Saint-Germain, prepares to face Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals. Despite PSG's recent struggles, Cavani's reputation as a prolific striker makes him a crucial target for Barcelona. The match is expected to be a high-stakes encounter, with both teams facing significant challenges.

Derry Mathews has won the interim WBA lightweight title after defeating Tony Luis in a close fight at Liverpool. Mathews, who was drafted in at the last minute, outperformed Luis in the closing rounds and was given a 114-112, 114-112, 115-112 decision. Mathews' relentless style and aggressive approach, despite Luis' efforts to stay competitive, ultimately proved too much for the Canadian fighter.

Hull FC secured a 28-20 victory over St Helens at Langtree Park, overcoming a 12-10 deficit after the break. The win was a surprise, as Hull had lost to Wigan the previous week. Hull's Jamie Shaul scored the winning try, and Jordan Rankin added the extras. St Helens, despite a strong start, struggled to maintain their lead and were eventually outscored by Hull. The match highlighted the resilience of Hull FC, who bounced back from a derby defeat.

The U.S. Census figures predict that the undocumented and documented immigrant population in the United States could reach a record high of 51 million by 2023, with immigrants accounting for 14.8% of the population by 2060. The report from the Center for Immigration Studies (CIS) states that immigrants will make up one in seven U.S. residents by 2023 and one in five by 2060. The report also predicts that immigration population will grow almost four times faster than the native-born population, reaching 15.8% of the nation's population by 2030, 17.1% by 2040, and 18.8% by 2060. The growth in immigrant population has important implications for workers, schools, infrastructure, congestion, and the environment.

Arsenal's Jack Wilshere made his long-awaited return from injury in a 1-0 defeat by Reading's Under 21s at the Emirates Stadium. Wilshere was joined by other injured first-team players, including Serge Gnabry and Abou Diaby, who managed to last 56 minutes. However, it was Martin Keown's son Niall who scored the eventual winner with a header in the opening minutes. The match was supposed to showcase Arsenal's next generation of talent, but it was Keown who stole the spotlight.

Justin Rose, the English golfer, has been struggling with his form, falling outside the world's top 10 after a bruising Florida swing. However, he has shown signs of improvement with a 69 at the Shell Houston Open, hitting 17 out of 18 greens in regulation. Rose attributes his recent improvement to working on his game over the past two weeks, focusing on his irons, putter, and overall swing. He also mentions that he's focused on his game and not worrying about the rankings, as they change quickly when he's playing well.

A Mayfair mansion, once a milking parlour, has gone on the market for £25 million. The property, which now features modern amenities like an indoor swimming pool and a cinema room, was originally used as a milking parlour and a depot before being demolished in the 19th century. The mansion, which is 8, 139 square feet, has been decorated with modern furnishings and plush carpets, and is being sold by estate agents Wetherell and Knight Frank for £25 million.

Bayern Munich's squad may be weakened by injuries, but Thomas Muller believes their sense of unity is stronger. The team, chasing three titles this season, is without key players like Arjen Robben, Franck Ribery, Bastian Schweinsteiger, and David Alaba for the Champions League game against Porto. Muller says the recent games with a decimated squad helped build a strong unit on the pitch. Bayern Munich will rely heavily on Muller and Robert Lewandowski, who are expected to score goals, as they look to become the first team to beat Porto in the Champions League this season.

Mercedes team-mates Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton visited their team's base in Brackley to discuss strategies for the upcoming Chinese Grand Prix. Despite Hamilton's victory in Malaysia, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff admitted to being worried about Ferrari's victory, which he attributed to their superior tactics and tire performance. The race in China is expected to be challenging, with Mercedes needing to analyze why they were unable to match Ferrari's performance.

Oklahoma Governor Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to perform executions with nitrogen gas if lethal injection is ruled unconstitutional or becomes unavailable. The bill, which was signed on Friday, states that nitrogen causes a quick loss of consciousness and death from lack of oxygen. The governor's office claims that the same "painless" argument used to advance the use of lethal injections has been used to advance the use of nitrogen gas. The bill, which was signed on Friday, allows the state to perform executions with nitrogen gas if lethal injection is ruled unconstitutional or becomes unavailable.

Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice in Swansea's 3-1 win over Hull on Saturday and topped this week's EA Sports' Performance Index after another thrilling installment of Premier League action. The Frenchman, who made a slow start to his career in south Wales after playing second fiddle to Wilfried Bony, has scored four goals in his last six Premier League games and earned a Game Index score of 52.9 this weekend. The EA Sports PPI measures a player's contribution to the success of his team and removes any opinion bias. Gomis is in first place, with Charlie Austin in second place and Eden Hazard in third place.

A massive freezer trawler sank in the Sea of Okhotsk off the coast of Russia, killing at least 56 crew members and leaving 13 missing. The ship, carrying 132 crew members, sank in just 15 minutes after an empty fuel tank and lack of ballast caused it to tip over. More than 1,300 people are involved in the rescue operation, with 63 survivors rescued so far. The sinking is believed to have been caused by a fishing net weighing 80 tons being pulled in, and the bodies of 56 crew members have been recovered.

A new study suggests that a drug originally developed for women with breast cancer could also help men with advanced prostate cancer. Clinical trials show that olaparib, a PARP inhibitor, can delay the moment when prostate cancer gets dangerously out of control. Up to 30% of men with advanced prostate cancer have tumours that have DNA defects and respond particularly well to olaparib. The drug, already used to treat women with breast cancer, can extend the length of time that a prostate cancer patient lives with the disease without it getting worse. Olaparib is the first cancer drug to target inherited genetic mutations and is one of the first of a new class of drugs called PARP inhibitors.

Travel photographer Rhiannon Taylor, 29, from Australia, has turned her passion for photography and globetrotting into a successful business by reviewing and photographing the best hotels, beds, pools, and room service around the world. With more than 12,000 followers on Instagram, she has built relationships with hotels and PR companies, allowing her to stay at exclusive properties and generate further income from featuring them on her site. Her unique concept of "In Bed With" has made her a go-to source for luxury hotel reviews, and she has traveled to over 20 countries to document the best pies, beds, and pools.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was mauled to death after getting caught up in a fight between two adult hippos in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park in eastern South Africa. The calf's mother watched in horror as the hippo was flung into the air before being dragged along the surface of the water. The two male hippos had been fighting for some time and the mother of the calf stayed with her herd, possibly believing it safer to stay out of harm's way herself. The baby stood no chance against the two adults as they brawled in the muddy waters of the nature reserve.

The Football Association is investigating an incident where Branislav Ivanovic was struck on the head by a cigarette lighter thrown from a section of home supporters at Loftus Road. QPR are unlikely to face disciplinary action, but the FA will seek observations from each club and ensure that QPR and the police are taking the necessary steps to identify the culprit via CCTV and for them to face a banning order. Chelsea's celebrations were marred by objects being thrown onto the pitch by the crowd, and the club is reviewing CCTV footage and appealing to witnesses to come forward.

A young mother and her three children were found murdered in their home in Tisdale, Saskatchewan. The suspect in the case was found dead hours later, and while police did not say how he died, they did not rule out homicide. The victim's sister, Laura Gross, described the discovery as "very, very devastating." The family is now trying to raise money for their funeral services and has started a GoFundMe page.

Emily Thornberry, a senior Labour politician, has three homes, including a £1 million property she bought from a housing association eight years ago. She has been criticized for opposing the right to buy policy while renting out a property she bought from a housing association. The housing association chiefs have also been accused of hypocrisy for drawing huge salaries and living in mansions while wishing to deny tenants a foot on the property ladder.

Wiltshire Police dropped an investigation into a vicious assault on a huntsman, despite a wealth of evidence pointing to the identity of a suspected attacker. The attack on Mike Lane, a 40-year-old joint master of the Tedworth Hunt, involved protesters armed with iron bars and a balaclava. The incident, which took place at Everleigh, near Amesbury, involved chase hounds chasing an artificial scent rather than a fox. Lane suffered concussion, broken teeth, and memory loss. Despite giving the police evidence, including names of suspects and their car registration numbers, the investigation was shelved. The case has angered hunt supporters, who believe the police could have done more to identify and prosecute the attackers.

Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes, 21, has stated his intention to remain at the club this summer, despite interest from Premier League teams Manchester United and Chelsea. Gomes has been netting four times in 25 La Liga appearances since leaving Benfica last summer, helping Valencia to fourth place in the table. He has denied being contacted by Chelsea and insists he is happy to stay with Valencia and play in La Liga.

An Australian teenager, Audrey Pekin, was raped twice on Christmas Eve in Bali while holidaying with her family. The alleged attacker, Henry Alafu, lured her to his remote home and then assaulted her in a taxi as she tried to flee. The Indonesian police failed to arrest Alafu, who is believed to be from Nigeria. Ms Pekin described the attack as "a monster" and said she felt "shocked and scared" during the ordeal.

PETA has teamed up with Ashley James, a former Made in Chelsea star, to launch an anti-fur campaign against Harvey Nichols, a department store that previously had a ten-year anti-fur policy. The campaign features a fake skinned fox, and PETA is in talks with billboard companies to mount the poster outside Harvey Nichols. Ashley James, who is vegan, says she wants people to make informed decisions about their purchases and is disgusted by the cruelty involved in the fur industry. Harvey Nichols, which has a range of fur products, including coyote fur from Canada Goose, raccoon fur from Charlotte Simone, and rabbit pelts from Vince, has re-introduced its fur-free policy.

Chile has joined several South American neighbors in recognizing civil unions between people of the same sex, with President Michelle Bachelet enacting a new law on Monday. The new law will take effect in six months and will give legal weight to cohabiting relationships between two people of the same sex and between a man and a woman. The law is intended to end discrimination faced by common-law couples and gives them greater rights in the realms of property, health care, pensions, and inheritance.

Chelsea are on course to become the most dominant title-winners in Premier League history, having led the table for 230 days as of April 10, 2023. The Blues are currently leading by seven points with a game in hand on their title rivals. They face local rivals QPR at Loftus Road, Manchester United at home, and second-placed Arsenal away in their next three games. Chelsea's 2005/06 title-winning side under Mourinho led the table for 257 days.

Cape Verde, a small country off the coast of Africa, is known for having a high concentration of musicians per square kilometer, making it a hub for music. Despite its small size, the country is seeking to leverage its rich cultural heritage, including the batuque, morna, and funana musical styles, to boost its economy. The country's prime minister and culture minister have recognized the potential of music, and the Kriol Jazz Festival, which has been celebrating its seventh edition, has become a significant event in the country. The festival has brought people from all over the world to share in the music, highlighting the country's cultural richness.

A hoax video showing a wave rider surfing in front of the Sydney Opera House has gone viral for the second time, with some users referencing the heavy storms that hit Sydney overnight as the trigger for the strange phenomenon. The video, originally posted by Sydney resident Darren Johnson in June 2012, was quickly debunked by wave experts and YouTube commenters, who pointed out inaccuracies in the video, such as the appearance of rocks around the Opera House and the cardboard-esque appearance of the man in the final shot.

Reading, beaten FA Cup semi-finalists, lost to Birmingham in a Sky Bet Championship game at the Madejski Stadium. Although Reading dominated most of the match, they wasted several chances in the closing stages. Birmingham held firm and grabbed the winner seven minutes from the end, when Clayton Donaldson nodded in his 16th goal of the season. Reading were involved in a dramatic 2-1 defeat against Arsenal in the last four of the Cup at Wembley on Saturday.

Paris Saint-Germain's David Luiz has been ruled out of the Champions League match against Barcelona due to a hamstring injury sustained during a run against Marseille. The Brazilian defender will miss at least four weeks, potentially impacting PSG's title defense and their upcoming quarter-final against Barcelona.

The return of Game of Thrones has led to a significant increase in internet piracy, with more than 100,000 illegal downloads per day reported by anti-piracy firm Irdeto. The show's popularity has prompted a 45% increase in illegal downloads year-on-year, with Brazil and France accounting for almost one million downloads each. The top five illegally downloaded TV shows during the same period were The Walking Dead, Breaking Bad, Vikings, and House of Cards. HBO's announcement of simultaneous global airings and launch of HBO Now in the US aim to curb piracy and recapture revenue.

Leicester City will host West Ham United in a Premier League match on Saturday. Leicester's Matt Upson is out with an Achilles injury, while West Ham's Winston Reid is back after a hamstring problem. Leicester has won just one of their last 10 home matches, while West Ham has won their last seven away games against the Foxes.

A statue of Lucille Ball, the beloved comedian from "I Love Lucy," has sparked controversy in Celoron, New York, due to its unflattering depiction. The statue, based on a moment from the show where Ball is drunk and pitches a health tonic, has attracted over 600 likes on a Facebook page called "We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue." The anonymous creator of the page, who describes himself as a "big fan of Lucy's," argues that the statue should be replaced with more "beautiful" statues of Ball. The statue, which costs an estimated $8,000 to $10,000 to recast, has been criticized for not accurately representing the iconic comedian.

A woman who tipped the scales at almost 20st lost nearly half her body weight after being forced to stand during an 11-hour flight due to her fear of crushing the woman in the seat next to her. Sharon Smith, 43, from Halesowen, West Midlands, joined Weight Watchers Online and ran a 10k race, shedding 4st through joining a slimming club and another 4.5 stone after taking up running. She had always been larger but never happy being overweight, and her weight loss began just under two years ago when she joined Weight Watchers Online.

Nicola Bonn, a 34-year-old mother of a 14-month-old daughter named Poppy, started a blog called Upfront Mama to share her experiences and advice on raising a baby for the first time. She aims to help other new mothers feel less "clueless" by sharing her candid account of bringing up a baby. One of her most popular posts, "Why We Need to Stop Justifying Ourselves," went viral, highlighting the challenges new mothers face when trying to explain their decisions to others.

Two teenage boys, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, from Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, are feared to have traveled to Syria to join ISIS. Hassan is believed to be related to Hammaad Munshi, who was arrested at 15 for his role in a terrorist plot. The families are in shock and worried about their safety, urging anyone with information to contact the police. The boys, who were 17 at the time, reportedly told their relatives they were going on a school trip but used the Easter holidays to flee Britain, boarding a Thomas Cook flight from Manchester Airport to Dalaman in Turkey on March 31.

Stephanie Scott, a beloved school teacher from Leeton, was brutally murdered just days before her much-anticipated wedding. Her father, Robert, described the pain of losing his daughter, who had planned a perfect wedding for her childhood sweetheart, Aaron Leeson-Woolley. The wedding was to be held at the picturesque Eat Your Greens venue, decorated with yellow balloons and flowers, but now the family must prepare for Stephanie's funeral instead. Scott's father has been contemplating the afterlife since her shocking death, but remains confident that his beautiful, sweet daughter is in a better place.

Southampton is reportedly interested in signing Tonny Vilhena, a 20-year-old winger from Feyenoord, who has one year left on his contract. The Saints are also monitoring Jordy Clasie, a £10m-rated midfielder, and are considering making Eljero Elia's loan move from Werder Bremen permanent. Koeman, the Southampton manager, is keen to bolster his squad ahead of possible European qualification. The club is currently seventh in the Premier League table and is exceeding expectations given the mass exodus of key players last summer.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture with beanbags in the library of Ickworth House, Suffolk, in an experiment designed to encourage visitors to 'dwell and take in the atmosphere'. However, this move has angered heritage experts who branded it 'misguided'. The National Trust has since announced that similar experiments will take place at nine other of its venues around the country. Art historian Bendor Grosvenor, who sparked the controversy, believes that the beanbag experiment is patronising and that better ways of attracting new audiences should be considered. The National Trust's director of strategy, curatorship and external affairs, Simon Murray, argues that each house is different and should be treated appropriately, and that the beanbag experiment is a short-term arrangement that may not continue for the whole year.

Former Australian Prime Minister John Howard was photographed standing on the footpath outside the Sydney Conservatorium of Music with a flat tyre, while his driver changed it. Felicity Waterford, who was waiting for her daughter at the Conservatorium, approached the pair and offered assistance. The former PM, who was a complete gentleman, agreed to a selfie with Waterford, who asked if she could take one. The incident came just weeks after Liberal MP Christopher Pyne was challenged to change a tyre on national television after boasting he was a 'fixer'.

West Bromwich Albion's manager Tony Pulis has admitted that Joey Barton "probably had a point" about the team's performance during their defeat to Queens Park Rangers earlier this season. Pulis, who was previously a manager of Gillingham, recalled his own experience of leading a team to a two-goal lead but ultimately losing the match. Pulis praised the team's performances and hopes to continue that success in their upcoming match against QPR.

A rare monkey species, the Bouvier's red colobus monkey, has been rediscovered in the Democratic Republic of Congo after being thought extinct for over 50 years. Researchers captured the first-ever photograph of the monkey, which was previously only known from three specimens. The discovery proves that the species is not extinct and is now being studied to learn more about it. The monkey, which was first discovered in 1887, is known for its distinctive penis shape and is now being studied to understand more about its behavior and habitat.

Kim Kardashian and her family are visiting Armenia for an eight-day trip, where they are exploring the country's rich history and culture. The family is staying at the Armenia Marriott Hotel Yerevan, which is located in the heart of the city. The hotel is surrounded by the Zvartnots International Airport and the Opera House, which is a must-visit place in the Armenian capital. The Kardashian-West crew is staying in the capital's finest digs, the Armenia Marriott Hotel Yerevan, which frames Republic Square at the heart of the city.

A British couple, Patrick and Valerie Jubb, are facing legal battles and potential demolition of their luxury bed and breakfast in southern Spain over illegal additions made by a previous owner. The couple, who purchased the property in 2008, are attempting to sell it but are now trapped in the property due to the ongoing legal dispute. The town hall claims the alterations, including a swimming pool, were illegal and unauthorized. The Jubbs, who are retired and plan to move back to the UK, are facing financial difficulties as their money is tied up in the property.

Apple's iPhone sales surpassed analysts' expectations in the first quarter of 2015, with the company reporting a 40% increase from the previous year. The iPhone accounted for more than two-thirds of Apple's revenue and profit, with sales in China outstripping those in the US. The company's cash reserves have grown to over $200 billion, and iPhone sales have grown by 72% in China. Despite a slight decline in iPad and Mac computer sales, Apple's overall revenue and profit have remained strong.

A 3-year-old girl named Elisa, whose mother Natali Castellanos-Tyler died in a car crash, has been plagued by disturbing nightmares and daytime visions about a mysterious white van. Her father, Craig Tyler, believes that the van may have something to do with the crash, as similar incidents involving a white box truck have been reported in nearby communities. The incident has raised questions about the cause of the crash and the safety of the roads in the area.

Researchers have discovered that the brain can remember 'neutral' or boring events more easily when they are tied to an emotion. This finding suggests that the brain has the remarkable ability to store information that seems inconsequential at the time in case it becomes useful later on. Emotion increases our ability to remember by affecting activity in brain regions involved in emotional processing and also the regions involved in encoding new experiences.

Jahnae Jackson, the girlfriend of a teenager with a life-threatening brain tumour, has put her psychology studies on hold to care for her long-term boyfriend, Jackson Byrnes, who is paralysed and unable to dress himself. The 18-year-olds from northern NSW have raised over $80,000 for his life-saving surgery to be performed by renowned neurosurgeon Dr. Charlie Teo. Jackson's surgery is likely to save his life, but he will still have a long road of rehabilitation ahead as he will be left paralysed for some time.

Nedum Onuoha, a QPR centre-back with 15 months left on his contract, is being targeted by Hull City, Everton, and West Ham United, among other clubs. Onuoha played in QPR's crucial 4-1 win over West Bromwich Albion at the Hawthorns. Stoke manager Mark Hughes is also interested in Onuoha, and QPR have held talks over a move for Catania defender Nicolas Spolli. Additionally, Hull City are showing interest in West Bromwich Albion striker Victor Anichebe, who is likely to be sold this summer.

The article discusses the unique phrases used in different states of the United States, which can seem strange to speakers from other parts of the country. For example, in New York, people use the word "so" for drama, while in San Jose, they say "didn't nobody help him." The researchers at Yale University have created an interactive map that allows users to hear common phrases for each state and their sources. The study reveals that there is variation in sentence structure across the US, with some regions using presentative sentences that are not common elsewhere.

A Canadian man, Kalman Kallai, took a rocking chair on a 9-day journey across Canada from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia, for work purposes. He used the chair to enjoy the scenery and interact with the local environment, including watching planes, posing precariously on a river bed, and dancing with his dad. The video, which features Kallai rocking and making gestures with his hands, highlights the comfort and adventure of traveling in a rocking chair.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood showed his softer side during a press conference by revealing a Twix multi-pack as a win bonus to young fan Charlie Pye, who applied for the club's hotseat after Paul Lambert was sacked. Sherwood joked that Pye's win bonus would be sweets and chocolate, and thanked him for sending him the Twix.

Kell Brook, a world boxing champion, enjoyed a night out at the Premier League Darts in his home town of Sheffield. Dave Chisnall, who won both of his games in week 10, moved onto 17 points in second place. Chisnall said he felt comfortable throughout the night and that he got a great start by defeating Gary Anderson. Raymond van Barneveld, who beat Phil Taylor 7-2, saw his fourth defeat in five.

Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Marco Verratti has praised Zlatan Ibrahimovic for his essential role in the club's Ligue 1 goals, stating that his off-pitch contributions are just as important. Ibrahimovic, who has scored 17 goals for the club this season, will be available for selection for the Champions League quarter-final second leg against Barcelona.

The Ministry of Defence accidentally published a secret RAF aerodrome manual containing vital details of the Falklands Islands' main base, including GPS coordinates and runway depth, on their website, which could be used by Argentina to prepare an invasion. The manual was accidentally uploaded to a public section of the MoD's website and could have been downloaded by Argentine intelligence agents. The RAF is defending the islands with modern Eurofighter Typhoon aircraft, and the MoD has recently announced the purchase of new anti-aircraft missiles to boost island defences.

Paul Anderson, Huddersfield Giants' coach, aims to boost his team's offensive performance to match their defensive efficiency as they seek to climb back up the Super League ladder. The Giants have fallen from third to ninth after losing all three games over the Easter period, but Anderson believes his team can improve with better offensive execution. If they win their next three games, Huddersfield could leapfrog their French opponents, Catalans Dragons, who have the league's best defensive record. The Yorkshire team can also climb to a season-high fourth position if they win their next three games.

Planners in Windsor have allowed two Costa cafes to open less than 500 yards apart, with one replacing a cycle shop and the other a HSBC branch. This has led to concerns from some residents who believe it's overcrowding the area with fast food and coffee shops. However, Costa's planning application argues that the new shop would be a "significant driver to local trade."

The British Veterinary Association (BVA) has withdrawn its support for the controversial shooting of free-running badgers in two four-year pilot culls in Somerset and Gloucestershire, stating that controlled trapping and shooting is more humane. The BVA still supports badger culling to tackle tuberculosis in cattle. The Environment Secretary has promised to roll out more culls across the country if the Tories win the election, with critics arguing that the culls are a 'party political issue'. The culls have been criticized by wildlife groups and animal welfare campaigners, who argue that the low numbers of badgers killed in the pilot culls do not demonstrate the effectiveness of the method.

Portishead founder Geoff Barrow has accused streaming services of giving his music away for free, saying he received just £1,700 in royalties despite 34 million plays. Barrow, who also runs the Invada record label, wants musicians to be paid more and says streaming is hurting young talent, stopping them from establishing themselves. Artists have long railed against low royalties paid from streaming companies, leading to Jay-Z launching his own Tidal service, promising bigger returns for musicians.

Game of Thrones fans who did not want to wait and legally watch HBO's hit series premiere its fifth season tonight have leaked the first four episodes online. The episodes began appearing on torrent download sites on Saturday night, and are thought to have leaked from review copies given to the press. Fans of the show, which follows the ambitions and betrayals of competing noble factions and families in the fantasy world of Westeros, now face the daunting task of avoiding spoilers online as the first four episodes are released over the course of the month.

A 25-year-old singer named Daniel Buccheri composed an emotional song to use as his best man's speech at his brother's wedding. The unique speech, performed by Daniel, was composed to the tune of Stay With Me and included tributes to his brother and his bride. The speech was viewed over 100,000 times online and documented Daniel's brother's love for his new wife, Sarah.

Zara Phillips, the Queen's granddaughter, has revealed that she has committed to a strict exercise and diet regime to get back in shape after the birth of her daughter Mia. The 33-year-old, who is vying for a place on Team GB at the Rio Olympics, started her morning workout at 7am, hitting the exercise bike at her home before her daughter wakes up at 8am. She also spends her day with the horses kept at her mother, Princess Anne's stables, and squeezes in another workout in the afternoon. Zara hopes to be part of the eventing team that goes to the Olympics in Rio, but first she needs to qualify.

Raheem Sterling's interview on social media, where he said he was not ready to sign a new contract at Liverpool, has caused a stir among fans and the club. Some fans believe he should be allowed to leave, while others are concerned about the club's financial situation. Sterling returned to training ahead of the weekend's game against Arsenal, and he has been linked with a move to Arsenal. The situation has been frustrating for many fans, who believe that Sterling should not be allowed to hold the club to ransom.

The article discusses a series of images from Barcelona's training sessions featuring former and current coaches, including Jose Mourinho, Pep Guardiola, Luis Enrique, Laurent Blanc, and Julen Lopetegui.
