The frenzy has drawn comparisons to other food manias around the world, such as cronuts and ramen burgers.

A mother-of-one, Kira Hollis, who was diagnosed with borderline personality disorder and anorexia, has overcome her struggles by becoming a bodybuilder. She was ordered by doctors to go to the gym to gain weight, which led her to turn her life around and become a personal trainer. Now, she is a healthy 9. 5st and says bodybuilding has completely changed her life, giving her focus and purpose. Her story has gone viral, and she has been helped by the Cherry Orchard Clinic and medication from her doctor.

Lewis Ferguson, 18, survived a spectacular fall from Merrion Square during a race at Wincanton on Wednesday, which made him an internet sensation. Despite the fall, Ferguson was back riding out and said he was undeterred from getting back in the saddle. The fall was described as the worst he had ever seen, and Ferguson escaped with only a cut on his nose and a bit of banter from his friends. The incident has been watched by hundreds of thousands of people online.

Hillary Clinton launched her campaign in a unique and unconventional way, using a video, new logo, and a road trip to "rebrand" herself and reframe her message. While some critics dismissed her efforts as "insultingly vapid" or "boring," her campaign team believes that her launch video and road trip have successfully flipped Clinton's message from self-absorbed to empathetic and forward-looking. The campaign's strategy of rebranding and reframing is a key factor in whether Clinton can successfully reframe herself in voters' eyes.

More than 1,700 Chinese students from Yichuan, Shaanxi province, took an exam in their high school's playground on Saturday, as the school allowed freshmen to sit exams outdoors for the first time. The unusual move was made possible due to a lack of indoor space, and the students organized the exam themselves. The school added that it could be a test of the students' organizing capacity. Many students believe sitting the exam outside is a novel way to broaden their horizons and encourage them to feel more relaxed.

Sportsmail has partnered with Gillette to offer a unique chance for one lucky reader to win a pair of Nike Magista Obra boots signed by Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart. The prize includes a new Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor with Flexball technology and a shave gel. Joe Hart, the No. 1 for Manchester City and England, is a Gillette ambassador, making the prize even more special. The competition closes on April 19, and readers can enter by clicking the link provided.

Kecil, a baby orangutan, was rejected by his natural mother and a surrogate mother, but found love with Maggie, an experienced surrogate mother at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo. Maggie has raised four of her own children and another surrogate, and has proven her parenting prowess by helping to raise Kecil for the past 10 months. Kecil, who had to be moved from his birthplace at Toledo zoo 14 months ago after his natural mother failed to bond with him properly, is now settling into his new enclosure and will go on display for the first time this weekend in two hours slots between 10am and midday, allowing him to nap in the afternoons.

A 61-year-old woman died suddenly and was eaten by her pet dogs after being locked in the house for days. The dogs, initially thought to have tried to wake her before becoming desperate for food, ate parts of her vital organs. The most likely cause of death was an accidental overdose of medication, but the exact cause could not be determined due to the dogs' consumption of her organs.

French handball star Nikola Karabatic, a multiple world and Olympic gold medalist, is facing a trial for suspected involvement in an illegal betting case related to his team's loss in a match. Karabatic, along with his younger brother Luka, was previously banned by the French league for betting on the result of a match in which their Montpellier club lost to a struggling team. The trial is expected to take place within months, and Karabatic faces up to five years in prison and a fine.

A gang of six men, including Ahmed Hassan-Sule, 21, and Mohamed Saleh, 22, were convicted of a string of sexual offenses against teenage girls in Banbury, Oxfordshire. The offenses occurred in cars, woods, or at the defendants' homes from 2009 to 2014. The victims, aged between 13 and 16, were targeted at under-18s parties organized by Hassan-Sule. The judge, Zoe Smith, rejected the defense's argument that the girls came forward because they were victims, stating that it was better to be a victim than a "slag." The gang was sentenced to a total of 31 years in jail.

Former New England Patriots star Aaron Hernandez faces multiple trials for murder and other charges in the death of Odin Lloyd, including a potential third trial for a 2012 shooting near a Boston nightclub. Hernandez is also being sued by the families of Odin Lloyd and Daniel de Abreu and Alexander Bradley, who claims Hernandez shot him in a Miami limousine. Hernandez's lawyers argue he couldn't defend himself properly while on trial in Massachusetts.

The Emirates Airline has signed a historic deal with the FA Cup, rebranding it as the Emirates FA Cup. The deal, worth £30 million over three years, will add to Emirates' existing portfolio of sporting sponsorships. The airline has also signed deals with Arsenal, AC Milan, and Hamburg, providing naming rights, branding, and marketing rights to their stadiums and teams.

Michael Phelps, the 18-time Olympic champion, is aiming to compete in the Rio Olympics next year but won't be swimming at the world championships in Russia this summer. He has been banned from the last major international meet before the Rio Olympics due to a second drunken driving arrest. Phelps, who is 29 years old, has been through a difficult time, including a DUI arrest and rehab, and has been able to come out on a better end.

Gareth Bale, a key player for Real Madrid, is doubtful for the Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid due to a calf injury. The Welsh forward limped off during Real's 3-1 home victory over Malaga on Saturday. Real Madrid also lacks Croatian midfielder Luka Modric, who is expected to be unavailable for six weeks due to a knee ligament strain. Real Madrid's striker Karim Benzema is expected to be fit for the match after missing Saturday's encounter with a knee injury.

Older people are more susceptible to emotions when making decisions over their retirement, according to a study by scientists at Texas Tech University. The research found that more than 50% of pensioners with investments during the 2007-2008 global financial crisis panicked and sold their investments after the stock market fell by 30%. Those who followed this path and sold at the lowest point eight years ago with a pension of £100,000 would only have £63,000 today, while if they had resisted the temptation to sell, the same pot would be worth £141,000 today. The study also found that retirees with better-than-average ability to solve 'logic problems' were more unlikely to make misjudgments in the investment market based on their emotions.

Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini is believed to deserve more time to turn around the club's fortunes, according to Stuart Pearce. The team's recent struggles, including a defeat to Manchester United, have led Pearce to suggest that the manager should stay in place. Pearce believes that City needs to make significant changes to their squad in the summer to compete for the title.

Manchester United's stars, including Wayne Rooney, Ander Herrera, and Robin van Persie, are training in the sunshine ahead of their Premier League showdown against Manchester City on Sunday. The match is significant as it marks Manchester United's first game against their rivals since the Sir Alex Ferguson era, and victory could give them a four-point lead in the league. The team is hoping to end their recent run of three consecutive wins against City, which Rooney believes is a "massive game of pride" for the fans.

Fiorentina's hopes of qualifying for the Champions League were dashed as they lost 1-0 to Verona, leaving them nine points behind third-placed AS Roma. Fiorentina's coach, Vincenzo Montella, expressed no complaints about the team's performance, while Verona's Mounir Obbadi scored the winning goal in the 90th minute. Fiorentina's defeat dropped them to sixth place on 49 points, one place and a point behind Sampdoria who occupy the final Europa League qualifying spot.

Miley Cyrus, 22, attended the 30th Annual Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony in Cleveland, Ohio, where she posed for a social media snap with somewhat bushy underarm hair. This sparked controversy on social media, with some users advising Cyrus to shave her armpits and others defending her choice. Cyrus is not the first, and probably won't be the last, to shun her razor in favor of the fuzz.

Barcelona's Lionel Messi, Neymar, and Luis Suarez have scored 102 goals in all competitions this season, taking them five points clear in La Liga. Messi has 49 goals, Neymar has 32, and Suarez has 21. The trio's dominance is due to their ability to score inside the box, with Messi having 30 left-footed and 15 right-footed goals, plus four headers. Barcelona's emphatic win boosted their Liga goal difference to +78, putting pressure on Real Madrid ahead of their match with Almeria.

A 44-year-old woman named Andrea McVeigh was hit by a cyclist who was riding on the pavement, causing her to be sent crashing face-first into the concrete. The cyclist fled the scene, chased by McVeigh's husband, who was left with two three-inch gashes to the middle of her forehead, as well as other facial and hand injuries. The cyclist initially stopped after the impact and appeared to be locking his bike up, but then sped off. McVeigh's husband and a member of the public stopped to help her, and the police have issued an appeal for the cyclist to be caught.

Paul Gregory, a 51-year-old man from Bedford, was fined £795 for having a blue badge, claiming he could only walk 200 meters, when in fact he was a keen walker. He was exposed when Bedford Borough Council staff noticed a newspaper report describing his exploits on a 191-mile hike. Gregory was found guilty of two counts of dishonestly obtaining a blue badge by misrepresenting his physical abilities and was ordered to carry out 150 hours of unpaid work, pay a £60 victim surcharge, and undergo 19 sessions of 'thinking skills'.

Apple has filed a patent for a new method of unlocking a mobile device using facial recognition. The system would automatically unlock the device if the user's face matches a previously taken photo, without the need for the screen to be enabled. The patent was filed in March 2011 and was awarded earlier this week.

Elizabeth Sedway, a 51-year-old mother of two battling cancer, was ejected from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California due to her lack of a doctor's note clearing her to fly. The incident occurred when an airline representative noticed her wearing a surgical mask and asked if she needed anything. After being asked a second time, she indicated she might require extra time to board the plane due to her condition. The family was eventually removed from the flight, and Sedway's husband and sons had to help her and their luggage out of their seats. The airline was concerned she might collapse during the flight, and after being asked to leave, she emailed her oncologist for a note.

A vintage 1973 E-Type Jaguar was involved in a head-on collision with a 1973 Toyota Kluger on Easter Sunday night in Frenchs Forest, Sydney. The Jaguar, worth over $120,000, was completely written off, while all three adults involved were taken to hospital for precautionary measures. The incident occurred on Warringah Road at a traffic light intersection. The crash was captured on camera and shared on the NSW Traffic and Highway Patrol Command's Facebook page, with car enthusiasts expressing sympathy for the owner of the rare Jaguar. The incident comes after police warned motorists to obey road rules during the Easter long weekend to avoid similar accidents.

Google has set up a team to boost the lifespan of phones, tablets, and electric cars, with sources claiming the team focuses on developing flexible and wearable technologies. The team, led by Dr. Ramesh Bhardwaj, has been working on solid-state, thin-film batteries and subfreezing temperature batteries for Google's Project Loon balloons. Apple has also been working on battery technology, with nine job listings for battery-related positions on its recruitment site.

The 223ft Explorer is a luxury superyacht designed by British yacht designer Tony Castro, featuring a helipad, infinity pool, and ample space for storage of supercars, jetskis, and submarines. It can accommodate 12 guests and has a carrying capacity for various toys and tenders. The yacht is expected to cost approximately 40 million euros to build, making it a costly investment for its owners.

Ed Miliband, the leader of the Labour Party, has announced his intention to implement rent controls despite warnings from experts that the plans will backfire. Labour's plans to cap rents are criticized as economically illiterate and could lead to more tenants being evicted by their landlords. The proposals, which include long tenancies and inflation-based rent increases, are seen as loopholes that could benefit landlords and suppress house building.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town fan was removed from his role as a mascot for Reading in the FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal after a video emerged of him backing Arsenal. The young supporter, Ryan Dearnley, said he hoped Arsenal would win, sparking outrage from Reading fans. The Football Association moved him to a mascot position for England instead.

A giant supervoid, 1.8 billion light-years across, may be responsible for a mysterious "Cold Spot" in the universe, as proposed by astronomers seeking to understand the cause of this larger-than-expected cold area. If confirmed, the supervoid would be the largest single structure ever found by humanity. The supervoid appears to be "roughly spherical" and may even contain a "significant substructure" at its center. The supervoid is thought to be causing a "less-dense" region of the universe, which can be explained by the expansion of the universe and the energy lost by light as it travels through the void.

The Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, will display Abraham Lincoln's chair where he was shot in 1865 as part of its observance of the 150th anniversary of the assassination. The chair, which has a dark stain on the back, is believed to be oil from other people's heads who sat in the chair before Lincoln. The museum has housed the chair since its founding 85 years ago and will display it for the 150th anniversary of the assassination on April 15.

A 19-year-old vlogger named Jake Boys surprised his girlfriend Emily Canham with tickets to see One Direction perform in Cardiff, but he made a mistake when booking the flights. He thought the Welsh capital was in the Republic of Ireland, so he booked plane tickets to Dublin instead. The couple is now planning to buy new train tickets to Cardiff for the band's show in June.

A new device called the Roboscan 2M Aeria has been created to scan entire planes for contraband, bombs, and weapons. The device, developed by Romanian company MB Telecom, uses a cone of radiation to sweep across planes and can detect various objects inside. While the radiation emitted by the scanner is not safe yet for humans to be in the plane when it is operated, the company behind it thinks it could become a vital tool in aircraft safety. The Roboscan 2M Aeria is being developed to check trucks at borders in Eastern Europe, where it has helped seize 76,000 packs of illegal cigarettes. The device can scan planes from small private jets to medium-sized commercial airplanes and can be used to detect weapons and other contraband in small or medium-sized jets that land at low-security airports.

A 54-year-old convicted paedophile, Stephen Munden, has gone on the run after vanishing from a psychiatric unit. Munden, who suffers from learning difficulties, was detained under the Mental Health Act after sexually touching a three-year-old girl. He is described as about 5ft 8ins tall, of a heavy build, and has dark hair. Officers believe he may have shaved off his beard before leaving the hospital in Winchfield and have released images of him with both facial hair and a clean shave. Munden was previously convicted of sexually touching a child under the age of 13 and is now subject to a hospital order.

The Championship is in a state of flux, with Middlesbrough holding the top spot despite the leadership changing hands 15 times this season. Seven points separate the top eight teams with six matches to play, and Boro know if they keep winning, they cannot be caught. The upcoming match against Watford at Vicarage Road is a lunchtime kick-off, which could have a psychological effect on other teams. Watford's Odion Ighalo is eager to play in the English top flight, while Bournemouth's Bournemouth have been the surprise package, leading the Championship for 101 days. The promotion race is so precarious that the division could have a completely different top two on Monday evening if Watford and Norwich win and Bournemouth fail to secure three points against Birmingham.

The latest hair trend is grey hair, with women embracing the look on social media under the hashtag #grannyhair. The trend has been popularized by beauty models and influencers, with some even going grey for a more natural look. The trend has been praised for its feel-good factor and has been traced back to fashion designer Jean Paul Gaultier's catwalk show earlier this month.

A couple from Ohio, Randy and Jodi Speidel, died from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning after struggling to raise money for help. The couple, who were unable to make a living due to chronic conditions, had created online fundraisers but failed to draw any donations. They were found dead in their bedroom with two charcoal grills filled with smoldering coals, and a note warning passersby of carbon monoxide inside. The couple had removed their cats from the house to spare their lives.

Liberal Democrat leader Nick Clegg vowed to continue as leader even if the party is reduced to fewer than 30 MPs, despite previous indications that he would quit if the party is left out of power. Clegg emphasized his commitment to serving the country and his party, despite the potential risks of losing the center ground and undoing the sacrifices made over the past five years. He also expressed interest in forming a coalition with the Conservatives, saying he deserved "credit" for the Coalition while enduring "five years of constant bile" from the Labour Party.

A pensioner was saved from a badger by his Jack Russell terrier, which dragged him back indoors. The badger, which was the size of a large pig with six-inch teeth, was spotted by the pensioner while sitting in his garden with his dog. The pensioner was left badly shaken and fears he could have been attacked if his dog had not been there. The National Farmers' Union has issued advice for residents on protecting their property from invading badgers.

Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose to Porto in the Premier League International Cup semi-final on Wednesday, while the Blues were knocked out of the Champions League by Real Madrid. Mourinho, who is closing in on the Premier League title, chose to watch Fulham's match instead of the Champions League fixture.

A property developer in Cornwall was attacked with corrosive liquid outside his home, leaving him with life-changing injuries and a loss of vision. Nicole Phillips, 45, from Hastings, was charged with perverting the course of justice and is due to appear at Bodmin Magistrates Court. Mr. Christopheros, a businessman in the event and property management industries, pleaded not guilty to the charge and was remanded in custody before his trial on June 8.

A Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route has erected signs warning pilgrims not to defecate along the famous path, as angry residents complain about the frequent nature calls. The signs, which show a squatting figure defecating within a red circle with a diagonal line across it, have become an attraction for pilgrims and other visitors. The pilgrimage attracts thousands of pilgrims every year, but there are few places to go when nature calls.

A massive fire consumed a building that was once home to a Michigan strip club on Wednesday afternoon. The blaze took place at a building located on a Flint intersection, and started at about 1pm. Flames: The fire took place where a strip club used to be located in Flint, Michigan, on Wednesday. Destroyed: The blaze struck a building located on a Flint intersection, and started at about 1pm. Former home: A strip club named The Body Shop used to be at the site. Burning: Only the building itself and a few nearby power lines were affected, according to local media. The site was not a vacant facility, the officials also said. Photos taken at the scene showed thick clouds of smoke and large, brightly burning flames. According to MLive, the strip club was known as The Body Shop. The website reported that only the building itself and a few nearby power lines were affected. Local resident Terry Rauh told MLive a fire took place at the building once

Shoshana Hebshi, a woman of Arab and Jewish descent who was strip-searched at a Detroit-area airport on the 10th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks, has reached a settlement in a lawsuit filed on her behalf. The federal government will give her $40,000 as compensation for being humiliated. The settlement sends a message that discrimination is not tolerated and will help protect future passengers from similar experiences.

An Asiana Airlines flight OZ162 crashed and skidded off the runway at Hiroshima Airport in Japan, resulting in 20 injuries. The plane, which had set off from Incheon International Airport in Seoul, South Korea, crashed at 8pm local time and overran the runway. Local media reported that the plane spun 180 degrees after impact and was left facing the wrong way on the runway. The crash injured 20 people, and the airport was closed as a result.

Mark-Francis Vandelli, a well-to-do reality star from Made in Chelsea, has opened up his watch collection to the Evening Standard. He revealed his most expensive watch, a Cartier white gold Moonphase, which he bought for £32,000. The watch has a moon phase feature that rotates depending on the hour of the day. Vandelli also owns a Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42, a Cartier Tortue Collection Privée, and a Rolex yellow gold Oyster Perpetual. He has been collecting watches since his teens and aims to have an impressive collection by the time he reaches middle age.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy is selling his extensive collection of antiques, including a 3D diorama of the Battle of Agincourt, a longbow made from yew, and a portrait of him holding the bow, in a £100,000 auction. The collection, which he has built up over his career, includes paintings, furniture, swords, flintlock rifles, silverware, and crystal chandeliers. The auction, held by Dominic Winter auctioneers, is taking place in South Cerney, Gloucestershire, on Saturday.

A Brazilian commuter, Nelson Felippe, took a photo of a man standing on a yellow safety line on a train platform and posted it on Facebook, expressing his disapproval of the scene. The image quickly went viral, with over 100, 000 views in 24 hours. Felippe's post, which initially appeared to be homophobic, actually revealed that he was observing a public transport safety regulation. The post has been praised for its witty way of exposing homophobia and has received thousands of comments.

A young English cricket fan, Jonathan Stevenson, wrote a letter to Richie Benaud, the legendary Australian cricket player, asking for tips on left-handed leg spin. Benaud, who was a wily leg-spin bowler and middle-order batsman, responded with a detailed letter that included tips on different deliveries and how to deliver them. The letter was signed by Benaud and was shared on Twitter as a tribute to the "great man."

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg predicts that virtual reality will play a key role in the future of travel, allowing users to experience destinations from multiple viewpoints and even change their viewpoints to explore locations in more depth. The company has already purchased virtual reality headset maker Oculus and promised that virtual reality gaming will be coming "this year." Marriott hotels have also trialled Oculus Rift on a tour of hotels across America, allowing guests to sample different holiday destinations.

A 22-year-old woman in China was diagnosed with bone cancer and admitted to the hospital, preventing her from getting married on her birthday. Her boyfriend, Guo Kai, arranged for professional photographers to take wedding photos for her, despite her condition requiring frequent medical attention. The couple met a year ago and have been committed to each other since.

Blaine Boudreaux, a 34-year-old man with a history of DUIs, was charged with intoxication manslaughter, intoxicated assault, and failure to stop and render aid involving death in connection to three separate DUI collisions that took place within three hours in Houston. Boudreaux, who allegedly ran a red light and slammed his Dodge pickup truck into a Honda Civic, killed a 6-year-old boy and injured his mother. The suspect was arrested at the scene after failing a field sobriety test.

Microsoft has launched a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions within the company, with positions based at its Redmond campus in Washington and run in partnership with Specialisterne, a Danish nonprofit that helps train people with autism for careers in IT. The program aims to expand opportunity and represent customers, with Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella apologizing for comments about women needing to trust the system to pay them well.

Two deputies involved in the fatal shooting of Eric Harris in Tulsa, Oklahoma, have been reassigned due to threats against them and their families. The shooting occurred when Reserve Deputy Robert Bates shot Harris, who was trying to arrest him. The deputies are not charged with a crime but have come under criticism for pinning Harris' head to the ground. The sheriff has suspended the drug unit pending a review of the April 2 shooting. The FBI has cleared the agency of any civil rights violations. The shooting has revealed a "deep-seated problem" within the department and the family has demanded justice.

Katie Prager, a 24-year-old woman with cystic fibrosis, is in desperate need of a life-saving lung transplant due to an infection called Burkholderia Cepacia. Her husband, Dalton, has already received new lungs but Katie is waiting for a transplant at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. Katie's insurance company, Kentucky Medicaid, will not cover the out-of-state treatment, leaving the couple in a race against time to save Katie's life.

The Sleep Cycle app analyzed data from over two million users to discover that the world's earliest wake-up time is on a Monday in South Africa, while Americans wake up at 7am and are in the worst mood all week. Slovakia topped the list for national average sleep quality, while the UK was in 45th place and the US was in 49th. The best sleep quality worldwide occurs on a Wednesday night, with China recording the highest sleep quality in the world that night. Users in Finland get the most hours of sleep on a Saturday, while people in Japan get an average of just six hours and nine minutes sleep. The data also revealed that Americans typically don't rise until 8:24am on Fridays and report the best wake-up mood.

Mexican artist Frida Kahlo wrote passionate love letters to her lover Jose Bartoli from 1946 to 1949 while she was married to muralist Diego Rivera. The letters, which were saved by Jose until his death in 1995, are expected to fetch upwards of $120,000 when they go up for auction at Doyle New York on April 15. The letters, which comprise more than 100 pages, were written in Spanish between August 1946 and November 1949 and were passed down through different generations of Jose's family until they reached the current owner. Frida signed her letters to Jose 'Mara', which biographer Hayden Herrera explained is probably short for 'Maravillosa', a name Jose would call her. The collection also includes an original drawing of a sleeping cat, pressed flowers, ribbon, beads, and drafts of a few of Jose's responses.

Trade union leader Len McCluskey, known for his militant stance and socialist ideology, is highly popular with Labour Party activists. However, his union, Unite, is a potent, sinister force in British politics, seeking to use its financial and organizational muscle to drag Britain back to the dark days of the 1970s. McCluskey, who keeps a drawing of Lenin in his office and once boasted of presiding over more strikes than any other union boss, is open about his yearning for that period when the unions held the government to ransom. The union's influence on Labour candidates is chilling, and its socialist policies, including a major expansion in the public sector, higher taxation, and ever more state spending, are intertwined with the Labour Party's structure and finances.

Zoologist Elad Hershkowitz captured footage of various animals drinking water in their enclosures using a GoPro camera. The footage shows a range of drinking behaviors, from a rhino almost kissing the surface of the water to a lemur delicately licking it. The zookeeper placed the camera in the animals' water troughs and filmed them for 30 hours, cutting the final footage down to four minutes. The animals were initially skeptical about the foreign object in their troughs, but eventually got used to the camera's presence and drank freely. The zookeeper anticipated a range of reactions from the animals and ensured the camera was secure before the experiment.

A recent opinion poll revealed that only 25% of voters believe David Cameron is hungriest to win the election, while 43% think Ed Miliband is most up for the fight. The poll suggests that voters perceive Cameron as less eager to win compared to Miliband. Cameron has been criticized for a perceived lack of campaign passion, while Miliband is seen as more enthusiastic. The article also mentions that some voters believe Nicola Sturgeon, leader of the Scottish National Party, is enjoying the campaign more than anyone else.

A man accused of assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov has told a court he was beaten and pressured into confessing to the murder. Zaur Dadaev, one of five Chechen men accused of killing Nemstov, told the court he had been abducted, beaten, and pressured into confessing. Dadaev previously confessed to the murder but now says he was beaten and pressured into making that statement. Dadaev is being held with his cousins, Anzor and Shagid Gubahsev, and is accused of involvement in Nemstov's murder. The outspoken politician was shot in the back four times as he crossed a bridge near the Kremlin and Red Square in Moscow. More than 20, 000 people marched through the capital city in protest of his murder, holding posters of his face and signs saying 'I am not afraid'.

A 4-month-old baby boy named Sonit Awal was pulled from the rubble of a Nepal earthquake that killed over 5,000 people. His father, Shyam Awal, frantically searched for him amid the debris for 22 hours before the soldiers found him. Sonit's face was covered in dust, but he was uninjured and taken to Bhaktapur Hospital. The rescue provides hope to a country devastated by the disaster.

A Church of Scientology-backed organization, Narcocon, is attempting to convert a historic property near Camp David into a drug rehabilitation center. The property, Trout Run, is currently classified for resource conservation and does not permit any medical purpose. Narcocon claims that placing the property on the county register of historic places would allow them to conduct their program. The rehabilitation program, founded in 1966, is based on the teachings of Scientology's founder L. Ron Hubbard and claims to eliminate addiction cravings through a regimen of exercise, sauna, and mega doses of the vitamin Niacin.

The article describes the aftermath of the U.S. military withdrawal from Afghanistan, focusing on the challenges faced by expatriates and locals in Kabul. Despite the city's population increasing due to the influx of refugees, many expatriates have lost their jobs and are now blacklisted, leading to isolation and fear of retaliation. The article highlights the changing landscape of Kabul, with many areas abandoned and others reclaimed by locals, and the impact of the U.S. military withdrawal on the city's infrastructure and economy.

Two Navy SEALs died and one was critically injured while training in a pool at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story in Virginia on Friday. The incident occurred when the SEALs were swimming in lap lanes without wearing gear. One SEAL died and another was listed in critical condition at a civilian hospital. The investigation into the incident is ongoing.

NBC, the broadcasting giant holding live rights to the Premier League in the United States, is set to show more than one in ten Americans watching Premier League matches live in the US than in Britain. NBC has transported their entire Premier League production from their HQ in Connecticut to England for this weekend's matches, with star anchor Rebecca Lowe presenting Burnley's match against Arsenal. The move aims to enhance coverage and influence football choices among young Americans.

Ed Miliband, the younger brother of former Labour leader David Miliband, clashed with London Mayor Boris Johnson on the Andrew Marr Show, with Johnson accusing Miliband of damaging the country more than his brother did. Johnson claimed that Labour could not take power without the support of the SNP, and that Miliband would do more damage to the country than his brother did. The exchange ended with both men trying to laugh off the attack.

A 26-year-old prisoner in Oregon was slapped with an extra 30 days behind bars for dropping his trousers and flashing a judge during a court hearing. The incident occurred when Dustin Irons, who was appearing via video-link, became disgruntled with the proceedings and exposed himself despite being in handcuffs. The judge sentenced him to an additional 30 days in jail for contempt of court. Sheriff's officers quickly covered him up and bundled him back to his cell. Captain Stewart Harp, who witnessed the incident, expressed admiration for Irons' creativity. Irons, who had been in prison since December for trashing a hotel room and assaulting people inside, faces another disciplinary investigation and could be placed in a segregation unit.

Jenson Button believes McLaren has improved significantly since their slow start to the Formula One season, with Fernando Alonso and Button discovering the car was competitive alongside other midfield runners. The team is now comparing themselves with the Red Bulls, Saubers, and Lotuses, and Button acknowledges the entire team still has a long way to go. McLaren's improvement in Malaysia, compared to Australia, was due to the cooler temperatures, which could affect tyre temperature and lap times. Button is excited to see the team's progress and looks forward to further improvements.

A hospital in Western Australia, Fiona Stanley Hospital, was found to have blood and bone fragments on supposedly sanitized medical instruments, leading to the hospital being stripped of its medical service provider Serco. The hospital has been fined $60,000 and is subject to Department of Health workers auditing its staff. The incident has damaged the hospital's public image and generated a loss of morale within its workforce.

Becca Litchfield and her partner Dale, from Nottingham, decided to give up their dream wedding to pay for fertility treatment and IVF. A young Shiba Inu puppy at an American Kennel Club center in the US was filmed barking at a husky dog, causing laughter and confusion among onlookers. The video shows the Shiba Inu attempting to bark at the husky, which responds with a high-pitched whine. Liam Plunkett, an experienced English fast bowler, is preparing to lead England in a Test series against the West Indies. He aims to use his pace to challenge the opposition and has returned to the England team after a minor injury. Paul Smith, a boxer from Liverpool, is set to face Andre Ward in a unification fight for the WBA super-middleweight title. Tyrus Byrd, the first African American mayor of Parma, Missouri, was sworn in last week, but her election victory was overshadowed by the departure of the majority of the city's police force, city attorney, clerk, and water treatment supervisor. Manchester City midfielder Yaya Toure will not be forced out of the club, but the team is set to make him available this summer. Toure, who has played a major role in City's recent trophy-laden period, is content with his life at the Etihad Stadium and is not in a rush to leave. City will resist any attempt by Valencia to pull out of a £24 million deal for Alvaro Negredo to fund a move for Radamel Falcao.

A new study suggests that more than two-thirds of people taking antidepressants may not actually have depression, as they do not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder. The study, published in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, found that 38% of those taking antidepressants did not meet the criteria for obsessive compulsive disorder, panic disorder, social phobia, or generalised anxiety disorder. The researchers concluded that antidepressants are commonly used in the absence of clear evidence-based indications. The study was conducted by U.S. investigators who looked at those taking selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), the most commonly prescribed type of antidepressant. SSRIs are usually the first choice medication for depression and other psychiatric conditions because they generally have fewer side effects than most other types of antidepressant. Doris Fuller, the mother of a mentally ill daughter who died by suicide, has revealed how her daughter's bipolar disorder and psychosis led to her death. A 10-year-old boy named Koby Hodder suffered a cardiac arrest while playing British Bulldog, a game involving running from one side of a field to another without being caught. Baroness Hale of Richmond, Britain's most senior female judge, has proposed reforms to divorce laws in England and Wales. She wants to remove the need for allegations of adultery and blame in most matrimonial disputes, aiming to reduce bitterness and encourage couples to resolve issues such as children and money before obtaining a divorce. The proposed changes include a one-year cooling off period after declaring that the marriage has permanently broken down, during which couples would be required to sort out arrangements for children and money. Lady Hale, who was behind the move for 'no fault' divorce in England and Wales 20 years ago, argues that the current system, which often encourages quick divorces, is unfair and undermines the concept of marriage.

Tottenham Hotspur is considering building a state-of-the-art stadium in London that could accommodate an NFL franchise, potentially becoming the home of a new NFL team. The stadium, estimated to cost £400 million, would feature a retractable pitch with an NFL-style synthetic surface. The design includes extra-large changing rooms to accommodate NFL squad sizes. The new stadium could be more suitable for NFL games than Wembley, which has hosted NFL matches since 2007.

U.S. lawmakers have written to FIFA, urging them to remove Russia from hosting the 2018 World Cup due to its involvement in the Ukraine crisis and occupation of Crimea. FIFA president Sepp Blatter has announced Russia as the host nation for the 2018 World Cup. Universal announced the release date for the sequel to "Fifty Shades of Grey" on February 10, 2017, and February 9, 2018. The first film earned $568.8 million worldwide and stars Dakota Johnson and Jamie Dornan.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis will receive a hero's welcome when he returns to Crystal Palace, but his overall record as a Premier League manager is one of the worst of any long-serving manager. Pulis has a history of success with Stoke City and Palace, but his record as a Premier League manager is poor. Pulis has never managed to guide a team into the top half of the Premier League, and he is currently in a relegation battle with West Bromwich Albion.

Fenerbahce, a Turkish football club, has called for the suspension of the Turkish championship following a gun attack on their team bus during a match against Caykur Rizespor. The attack occurred on Saturday night as the bus drove to the airport after the match. The injured driver was taken to the hospital, and there were no reports of injuries to other passengers. A massive snow avalanche struck Everest Base Camp on Saturday, trapping hundreds of climbers and rescuers in the freezing cold. The avalanche killed at least 17 people, injured dozens more, and buried several others under the snow. Gregory Margolin, a 16-year-old Jewish recruit in the Soviet Red Army during World War II, found himself again in the middle of war in Ukraine. The Reverend Al Sharpton delivered a sermon and addressed the Walter Scott situation on Sunday morning in North Charleston, South Carolina. Brendan Rodgers will remind Raheem Sterling of his responsibilities after the Liverpool youngster hit the headlines for the wrong reasons before scoring the opener in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United. Union barons gave more than £1 million to Labour in the second week of the election campaign, boosting the party's war chest and exposing the type of government Ed Miliband would lead as Prime Minister. Passengers on a Qatar Airways flight diverted to Birmingham Airport in the UK after severe winds caused delays to its planned landing at Manchester Airport, leading to a series of incidents. Canadian pop star Justin Bieber will be accompanying Floyd Mayweather Jr. into the ring for their $300 million fight against Manny Pacquiao on Saturday in Las Vegas. Corinthian Colleges Inc., a for-profit career college, announced its decision to close all 28 of its remaining campuses. Pep Guardiola has denied a dispute with former Bayern Munich club doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit the club after being blamed for a Champions League defeat by Porto. Wladimir Klitschko, the reigning heavyweight champion, has recalled his dramatic rise to the top, including his Olympic gold medal win in 1996, which changed his life. Jeremy Clarkson, who was fired from Top Gear in March after attacking a producer during filming, has finally spoken out about his dismissal. In a bizarre incident during Barcelona's 1-0 La Liga victory against Celta Vigo, Fabian Orellana, Celta Vigo's striker, threw a lump of grass at Sergio Busquets, leading to Orellana being shown a red card. In 2013, three people died and over 200 were injured when a pair of bombs went off within 12 seconds of each other at the Boston Marathon finish line. This year, federal Judge George A. Tens of millions of Chinese people marked the annual Qingming Festival this weekend by traveling home to their ancestral villages, cleaning tombs, and burning fake paper money to ensure their loved ones are not poor or hungry in the afterlife. The festival, also known as Tomb Sweeping Day, is celebrated in China to mark the start of spring and honor the Yellow Emperor, considered the ancestor of the Qing dynasty. The festival is one of the 24 Chinese solar terms and falls in the first week of April every year.

Paul Simon, 73, has returned to the top of the UK album chart with his latest release, The Ultimate Collection, which outsold more youthful musicians like Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. Iker Casillas, a 33-year-old Spanish goalkeeper, has stated his intention to remain at Real Madrid until the end of his contract, despite speculation that Manchester United's David de Gea may be linked with a move to the Bernabeu. Britain was hailed as a "job-creating machine" last night as the number of people in work soared to its highest level in history. SsangYong, a Korean automaker, is launching a new sports utility vehicle (SUV) called Tivoli in the UK, priced under £13,000. It features a 1.6-liter engine, six-speed manual or automatic transmission, and comes in three trim levels with seven airbags and a five-year unlimited mileage warranty. A chef, Sam Longhurst, created a 10-inch, half-kilogram burger at the Splendid Kitchen restaurant in Manchester, England, containing six forms of three different meats and 2,000 calories. Yeo Valley, a dairy company in North Somerset, has opened its staff canteen to the public, offering a high-quality meal for £2 to £4 per person, prepared by Michelin-starred chef Paul Collins. The canteen, praised as the world's best staff canteen, has quirky light fittings and high tables and stools, and is open to the public at higher prices.

Blues legend B.B. King was hospitalized for dehydration, but he is now feeling much better and has left the hospital. On Easter Sunday, Manhattan's Fifth Avenue was transformed into a sea of bizarre hats as people celebrated the holiday. Chelsea players Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake, along with their teammates Loic Remy and Willian, participated in a football challenge organized by Audi. Rachel Riley, Countdown's co-presenter, was embarrassed on a recent episode when contestants offered up the eight-letter word "erection" as their answer to the word game. A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, was arrested after attempting to buy deadly poison online. Australian Olympian Jana Pittman, a seven-year-old mother of a little girl named Emily, gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Emily, just days after a video surfaced of the athlete training while eight months pregnant. A powerful storm capsized several sailboats participating in a regatta in Dauphin Island, Alabama, resulting in at least one death and missing persons. The storm rolled through the area around 4 p.m. and a man was plucked from the waters by the Coast Guard around 9 p.m. The storm caused significant damage and loss of life, with at least one person confirmed dead. The regatta was part of the 57th iteration of the race, with more than 100 sailboats and as many as 200 people participating.

Roseanne Barr, 62, revealed she is going blind due to macular degeneration and glaucoma, two eye diseases that get progressively worse over time and can steal vision. Her doctors haven't provided a timeline, but her symptoms are worsening. Macular degeneration is a breakdown of the retina that allows us to see fine details in the center of vision, while glaucoma damages the nerve that connects the retina to the brain, often caused by fluid build-up and pressure in the eyes. The combination of the two is terrible, as it takes away her central vision and peripheral vision. The American Academy of Ophthalmology recommends getting a baseline eye exam when you turn 40, and there are treatments that may delay the progression of early-stage glaucoma and halt further vision loss in advanced cases of macular degeneration.

A 17-year-old Oklahoma teenager, Chancey Luna, was convicted of first-degree murder in the 2013 shooting death of Australian college baseball player Christopher Lane, who was killed while jogging in Duncan. The jury recommended that Luna be sentenced to life in prison without parole. Luna was found guilty of shooting Lane from a passing car, but his defense attorney argued that he meant only to scare Lane. Arsene Wenger insists his record of 12 losses against Jose Mourinho will not affect Arsenal's match against Chelsea on Sunday. Wenger has drawn five and lost seven of their 12 encounters. Manny Pacquiao, a Filipino boxer, has become one of the most recognizable figures in the world of sports after a series of major fights, including a bout against Floyd Mayweather, which is scheduled to take place on Saturday night at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. Manchester University in Indiana was in lockdown late on Friday night after a 'likely prank call' about an armed person near the main administration building. Edinson Cavani, a key player for Paris Saint-Germain, prepares to face Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals. Justin Rose, a 34-year-old English golfer, has been struggling with his game recently, falling outside the world's top 10 after a bruising Florida swing. A Mayfair mansion, once a milking parlour, has gone on the market for £25 million. Bayern Munich, chasing three titles this season, are without key players Arjen Robben, Franck Ribery, Bastian Schweinsteiger, and David Alaba for their Champions League quarter-final match against Porto. Mercedes team-mates Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton visited their team's base in Brackley to discuss strategies for the upcoming Chinese Grand Prix. Oklahoma Governor Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to perform executions with nitrogen gas if lethal injection is ruled unconstitutional or unavailable. The bill, signed on Friday, states that the person will become unconscious within eight to 10 seconds and die a few minutes later from lack of oxygen. The move comes as the U.S. Supreme Court reviews the use of lethal injections. Fallin reaffirmed her support for the death penalty, stating that Oklahoma executes murderers whose crimes are especially heinous.

Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice in Swansea's 3-1 win over Hull on Saturday, earning a Game Index score of 52.9 this week. The Frenchman, who made a slow start to his career in south Wales, has scored four goals in his last six Premier League games. Gomis tops this week's EA Sports' Performance Index, which measures a player's contribution to the success of his team. The EA Sports PPI is the official player rating index of the Premier League, removing any opinion bias and only working with proven statistical measurements.

A massive freezer trawler sank in the Sea of Okhotsk off the coast of Russia, killing at least 56 crew members. The ship, carrying 132 crew members, sank in just 15 minutes after an empty fuel tank and lack of ballast caused it to tip over. The sinking occurred when a 80-ton fishing net was pulled in, likely hitting an object in the sea. Over 1,300 people are involved in the rescue operation, with 63 survivors rescued so far. The incident occurred at 4am local time, and temperatures in the water can drop to as low as -2 degrees Celsius, making rescue efforts challenging.

A new study suggests that a drug originally developed for women with breast cancer could also help men with advanced prostate cancer. Clinical trials show that olaparib, an inhibitor of PARP proteins, can delay the progression of prostate cancer in men with genetic mutations. The drug has been granted approval for use in ovarian cancer and is now being tested for prostate cancer. The study found that 16 out of 49 men with advanced prostate cancer responded to the drug, with improved responses in medical scans and lower tumour cell counts in the blood. The drug works by blocking the cancer cell's ability to repair damage, targeting only tumour cells with genetic defects. The study suggests that men with detectable DNA repair mutations may benefit from the drug, and that genomic testing could identify patients most likely to respond.

Travel photographer Rhiannon Taylor, 29, from Australia, has turned her passion for photography and globetrotting into a successful business by reviewing and photographing the best hotels, beds, pools, and room service around the world. With more than 12,000 followers on Instagram, she has built relationships with hotels and PR companies, allowing her to stay at exclusive properties and generate further income from featuring them on her site. Her unique concept of "In Bed With" has gained popularity, and she has traveled to various countries to document luxurious accommodations, including private plunge pools, idyllic spas, and sumptuous rooms.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was mauled to death after getting caught up in a fight between two adult hippos in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park in eastern South Africa. The mother hippo watched in horror as the calf was flung into the air before being dragged along the surface of the water. The calf's mother stayed with her herd, possibly believing it safer to remain out of harm's way. The baby stood no chance against the two adults as they brawled in the muddy waters of the nature reserve.

The Football Association is investigating an incident where Branislav Ivanovic, a QPR player, was struck on the head by a cigarette lighter thrown from a section of home supporters at Loftus Road. Chelsea players celebrated the winning goal, and objects were thrown onto the pitch. QPR is reviewing CCTV footage and banning those involved. The club is appealing to witnesses to come forward and is awaiting communication from the FA. The incident occurred during a west London derby contest on Sunday.

A young mother and her three children were found murdered in their home in Tisdale, Saskatchewan. The suspect in the case was found dead hours later, and while police did not confirm it was a homicide, they did say the suspect had a six-month-old baby with him who was unharmed. The victim's sister, Laura Gross, described the discovery as "very, very devastating." The family is now trying to raise money for their funeral services and has started a GoFundMe page.

Emily Thornberry, a senior Labour politician, was forced to resign from the shadow cabinet after tweeting a photo of a house covered in England flags and with a white van outside, which was seen as hypocrisy in the context of her opposition to the right to buy policy. The article highlights the controversy surrounding Thornberry's stance on right to buy and her ownership of expensive properties, including a £3 million home in north London.

Mike Lane, a huntsman, was attacked by protesters armed with iron bars during a hunt in Wiltshire, England. Despite evidence pointing to the identity of the attacker, police dropped the investigation three months later. Lane, who suffered severe injuries, is disappointed with the decision and believes the police could have done more. The incident, which took place in January 2023, involved protesters using citronella to distract hounds and attacking Lane with iron bars. The case has sparked controversy and concerns about the effectiveness of police investigations in such situations.

Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes, 21, has stated his intention to remain at the club this summer, despite interest from Premier League teams Manchester United and Chelsea. Gomes, who has netted four times in 25 La Liga appearances, has denied being contacted by Chelsea and insists he is happy to stay in Spain, particularly in La Liga.

An Australian teenager, Audrey Pekin, was raped twice on Christmas Eve in Bali while holidaying with her family. The alleged attacker, Henry Alafu, lured her to his remote home and then assaulted her in a taxi as she tried to flee. The Indonesian police failed to arrest Alafu, who is from Nigeria. Ms Pekin described the attack as "a monster" and said she felt "shocked and scared" during the ordeal.

Ashley James, a former Made in Chelsea star, has joined forces with animal rights group PETA to campaign against fur fashion at Harvey Nichols, a department store that previously had a ten-year anti-fur policy. The campaign, titled "Harvey Nichols: Here's the Rest of Your Fur Coat," features a fake skinned fox and aims to raise awareness about the cruelty involved in the fur industry. Harvey Nichols has since re-introduced its fur-free policy, but PETA is still in talks with billboard companies to mount the campaign outside their stores.

Chile has joined several South American neighbors in recognizing civil unions between people of the same sex, with President Michelle Bachelet enacting a new law on Monday. The new law will take effect in six months and will give legal weight to cohabiting relationships between two people of the same sex and between a man and a woman. The law is intended to end discrimination faced by common-law couples and gives them greater rights in the realms of property, health care, pensions, and inheritance.

Chelsea are on course to become the most dominant title-winners in Premier League history, having led the table for 230 days as of April 10, 2023. They are currently leading by seven points with a game in hand on their title rivals. The team's next three games could be crucial in their pursuit of the record.

Cape Verde, a small Portuguese former colony with a population of 500,000, is known for having more musicians per square kilometer than any other country in the world. The country's diverse cultural heritage, shaped by the transatlantic slave trade, piracy, and Jewish exiles, has given rise to unique musical styles such as batuque, morna, and funana. Despite being resource-poor, Cape Verde is exploring the economic potential of its rich musical heritage, aiming to boost its economy through the creative sector. The Kriol Jazz Festival, which celebrated its seventh edition, brought artists from the United States, Luxembourg, Brazil, and Cape Verde to the capital city of Praia, showcasing the island's musical talent and fostering cultural exchange.

An old hoax video showing a wave rider surfing in front of the Sydney Opera House has gone viral for the second time, with some users referencing the heavy storms that hit Sydney overnight as the trigger for the strange phenomenon. The video, originally posted by Sydney resident Darren Johnson in June 2012, was quickly debunked by wave experts and YouTube commenters, who pointed out inaccuracies in the video, such as the appearance of rocks around the Opera House and the cardboard-esque appearance of the man in the final shot.

Reading, the beaten FA Cup semi-finalists, lost to Birmingham in a 1-0 Championship game at the Madejski Stadium. Although Reading dominated most of the match, they wasted several chances in the closing stages. Birmingham's Clayton Donaldson scored the winning goal in the 78th minute, and Reading's Adam Federici was retained for the match. Reading's Federici had fumbled a ball that led to Arsenal's winning goal in the last four of the Cup at Wembley.

David Luiz, a key player for Paris Saint-Germain (PSG), has been ruled out of the Champions League quarter-final against Barcelona due to a hamstring injury sustained during a match against Marseille. The 27-year-old Brazilian defender will miss at least four weeks, potentially impacting PSG's title defense and their upcoming match against Barcelona.

The return of Game of Thrones has led to a significant increase in internet piracy, with more than 100,000 illegal downloads per day reported by anti-piracy firm Irdeto. The most downloaded episodes were from Brazil, followed by France, the US, Canada, and the UK. HBO has announced plans to launch a new streaming service, HBO Now, in an attempt to curb piracy and recapture revenue.

Leicester City will host West Ham United in a Premier League match on Saturday. Leicester's Matt Upson is out with an Achilles injury, while West Ham's Winston Reid is back after a hamstring problem. Leicester has won just one of their last 10 home matches, while West Ham has won their last seven away games against the Foxes.

A statue of Lucille Ball, the beloved comedian from "I Love Lucy," has sparked controversy in Celoron, New York, due to its unflattering depiction. The statue, based on a moment from the show where Ball is drunk and pitches a health tonic, has attracted over 600 likes on a Facebook page called "We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue." The anonymous creator of the page, who describes Ball as "an amazing comedienne and a stunning beauty," argues that the statue should be replaced with more "beautiful" statues of Ball. The statue, which costs an estimated $8,000 to $10,000 to recast, has been criticized for not accurately representing Ball's appearance.

A 43-year-old woman, Sharon Smith, from Halesowen, West Midlands, shed nearly half her body weight of 20st after being forced to stand during an 11-hour flight due to her fear of crushing the woman in the seat next to her. She had been a size 26 before the trip and now weighs 9st 9lb, and is due to run a 10k race on Sunday. Her weight loss began when she joined Weight Watchers Online and started running, which helped her shed 4st and then another 4.5 stone after quitting her job to work from home.

Nicola Bonn, a 34-year-old mother of a 14-month-old daughter named Poppy, started a blog called Upfront Mama to share her experiences and advice on raising a baby for the first time. Her candid account of bringing up a baby for the first time went viral, and she shared a post called "Why We Need to Stop Justifying Ourselves" that highlighted the challenges of being a new mother. The post discusses the overwhelming amount of opinions and advice that new mothers receive, which can be overwhelming and often judgmental.

Two teenage boys, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, from Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, are feared to have crossed into Syria to join ISIS. Hassan is believed to be related to Hammaad Munshi, who was arrested at 15 for his role in a terrorist plot. The families are in shock and worried about their safety. The boys, who were on a school trip, used the Easter holidays to flee Britain.

Stephanie Scott, a beloved school teacher from Leeton, New South Wales, was brutally murdered just days before her much-anticipated wedding. Her father, Robert Scott, has opened up about the grief his family is feeling as they struggle to come to terms with their daughter's death. Stephanie was a bubbly and thoughtful person who had put a great deal of time and thought into making her wedding day perfect. The wedding was supposed to take place on Saturday, but the day before, police were led to the place where Stephanie's remains were found. The venue, decorated with yellow balloons and flowers, was a reminder of the wedding, but instead of a wedding, the Scott family must prepare for Stephanie's funeral.

Southampton is reportedly interested in signing Tonny Vilhena, a 20-year-old winger from Feyenoord, who is eager to leave the club this summer. The Saints are also monitoring Jordy Clasie, a £10m-rated midfielder, and are considering making Eljero Elia's loan move from Werder Bremen permanent. Koeman, the Southampton manager, is keen to bolster his squad ahead of possible European qualification. The club is currently seventh in the Premier League table and is exceeding expectations given the mass exodus of key players last summer.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture with beanbags in the library of Ickworth House, Suffolk, in an experiment designed to encourage visitors to "dwell and take in the atmosphere." The move was met with outrage from heritage experts who called it "misguided" and "patronising nonsense." The Trust has since announced that similar experiments will take place at nine other venues around the country. The beanbag experiment was described as a short-term arrangement that would not necessarily continue for the whole year.

Former Australian Prime Minister John Howard was photographed standing on the footpath outside the Sydney Conservatorium of Music with a flat tyre, while his driver changed it. Felicity Waterford, who was waiting for her daughter at the Conservatorium, approached Howard and offered assistance. Howard, who was a complete gentleman, agreed to a selfie and took care of the tyre change himself. This incident came just weeks after Liberal MP Christopher Pyne was challenged to change a tyre on national television after boasting he was a 'fixer'.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has admitted that midfielder Joey Barton "probably had a point" about the team's performance during a 2-0 defeat to Queens Park Rangers earlier this season. Pulis, who was leading the team when they were 2-0 up, said that Barton's comments about the players "s*** themselves" were justified. Pulis also recalled his own experience of being 2-0 up but losing in a play-off final in 1999, which he believes is relevant to the current situation. Pulis praised the team's performances and hopes to continue that success in their upcoming match against QPR.

A rare monkey species, the Bouvier's red colobus monkey, has been rediscovered in the Democratic Republic of Congo after being thought extinct for over 50 years. Researchers captured the first-ever photograph of the monkey, which was previously only known from three specimens. The discovery proves that the species is not extinct and is now being studied to learn more about it. The monkey, which was first discovered in 1887, is known for its distinctive appearance, including a white penis, and is now being monitored to understand its behavior and habitat.

Kim Kardashian and her family, including her husband Kanye West and daughter North, visited Armenia for an eight-day trip to explore the country, which is the birthplace of their late father Robert Kardashian. The family stayed at the Armenia Marriott Hotel Yerevan, which is located in the capital city of Yerevan. The city is known for its rich history and cultural landmarks, including the Opera House and the Zvartnots International Airport. The visit was a chance for the family to experience Armenia's culture and landmarks, and they were accompanied by bodyguards and police to ensure their safety.

A British couple, Patrick and Valerie Jubb, are facing legal battles in southern Spain over a luxury bed and breakfast they once operated. The couple, who purchased the property in 2008, are attempting to sell it but are now facing the possibility of losing it to the local town hall due to illegal alterations made by a previous owner. The couple, who are retired and plan to move back to the UK, are currently locked in a dispute over the property, which is located in Los Alcornocales Natural Park in the Andalusian province of Cadiz.

Apple reported strong sales of its iPhone in the first quarter of 2015, with more than 61 million units sold, accounting for over two-thirds of its $58 billion in revenue and $13.6 billion in profit. The company's iPad revenue fell 29% to $5.4 billion, while Mac computer revenue rose 2% to $5.6 billion. The iPhone's sales growth in China was particularly notable, with a 72% increase over the previous quarter. Despite the strong performance, the company's Mac and iPad revenues declined, and the new Apple Watch was not yet reported.

A 3-year-old girl named Elisa, whose mother Natali Castellanos-Tyler died in a car crash, has been having disturbing nightmares and daytime visions about a white van. Her father believes this may be related to the crash. The van is described as a plain white delivery-style box truck, which has been linked to multiple hit-and-run incidents in the area.

Researchers at New York University have discovered that the brain can remember 'neutral' or boring events more easily when they are tied to an emotion. This finding suggests that the brain has the ability to store information that seems inconsequential at the time in case it becomes useful later on. The study focused on how the brain stores memories for emotionally neutral events, such as neutral events like a lunch date, and how emotion affects memory retention. Emotion increases the strength of our memory over time, a process called consolidation. Strong emotion can strengthen memory for positive events, such as a surprise birthday party, and for negative events, such as making an embarrassing faux pas.

Jahnae Jackson, the girlfriend of a teenager with a life-threatening brain tumour, has raised over $80,000 for his life-saving surgery. The 18-year-old has put her psychology studies on hold to care for her boyfriend, who is paralysed and unable to dress himself. The surgery is scheduled for Wednesday, and Jahnae and her girlfriend are overwhelmed by the community support from the small town of Casino in northern NSW.

Nedum Onuoha, a QPR centre-back, is being targeted by Hull City, Everton, and West Ham United, among other clubs, as the club considers streamlining its squad. Onuoha, who has 15 months left on his contract, has played regularly under Chris Ramsey and was part of QPR's crucial 4-1 win over West Bromwich Albion at the Hawthorns. Stoke manager Mark Hughes, who signed Onuoha for QPR, is also interested in the player. Additionally, Hull City is showing interest in West Bromwich Albion's striker Victor Anichebe, who is likely to be sold this summer.

Researchers at Yale University have created an interactive map that reveals the subtle differences in sentence structure across the US, with each state having its own unique phrases. The map allows users to click on a location marker to hear common phrases for that region. The study, which focuses on the US, also includes data for the UK, with sentences such as 'yer lugs needs washed' used in Scotland and 'Ne mon nule don hum no good' in Aylesbury. The overall pattern was clear; in the South, presentative sentences like 'Here's you a water bottle' were found to be completely normal, while in the North, it was almost unheard of.

A Canadian man named Kalman Kallai took a rocking chair on a nine-day journey across Canada from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia. He used the chair to enjoy the scenery and took videos of himself rocking and making gestures. The trip was part of his work, and he traveled with his dad. The video shows him posing, dancing, and waving at cows along the way.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood revealed a 'win bonus' to a six-year-old fan Charlie Pye who applied for the club's hotseat after Paul Lambert was sacked. Sherwood joked that the win bonus would be sweets and chocolate, and revealed a Twix multi-pack to the assembled media.

Kell Brook, a world boxing champion, enjoyed a night out at the Premier League Darts in his home town of Sheffield. Dave Chisnall, who won both of his games in week 10, moved onto 17 points in second place. Chisnall said he felt comfortable throughout the night and got a great start by defeating Gary Anderson. He also beat James Wade 7-1 in his second loss of the night. Chisnall is second in the Premier League table behind Michael van Gerwen, who snatched a 7-5 victory against Stephen Bunting. Raymond van Barneveld beat Phil Taylor 7-2 to inflict Taylor's fourth defeat in five.

Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Marco Verratti has praised Zlatan Ibrahimovic for his essential role in the club's Ligue 1 goals, stating that his off-pitch contributions are just as important. Ibrahimovic, who has scored 17 goals for the team this season, will be available for selection for the Champions League quarter-final second leg against Barcelona.

The Ministry of Defence accidentally published a secret RAF aerodrome manual containing vital details of the Falklands Islands' main base, including GPS coordinates and runway depth, on their website. This information could be used by Argentina to plan an invasion, as the manual was accessible online. The MoD acknowledged the mistake but denied it was particularly sensitive. The Falklands Islands are defended by modern Eurofighter Typhoon aircraft, and the incident highlights the ongoing sovereignty dispute between Britain and Argentina.

Paul Anderson, Huddersfield Giants' coach, aims to boost his team's offensive performance to match their defensive efficiency as they seek to climb back up the Super League ladder. The Giants have fallen from third to ninth after losing all three games over the Easter period, but Anderson believes his team can improve with a focus on offense. If Huddersfield wins their next game, they could leapfrog Catalans Dragons, who have the best defensive record in the league. The Yorkshire team can also climb to a season-high fourth if they win three games in a row.

Planners in Windsor have allowed two Costa coffee shops to open less than 500 yards apart, with one replacing a cycle shop and the other a HSBC branch. This has led to concerns from some residents who believe it's overcrowding the area with fast food and coffee shops. Costa's planning application states that the new shop would be a "significant driver to local trade," and planners said there was no legal reason to refuse.

The British Veterinary Association (BVA) has withdrawn its support for the controversial shooting of free-running badgers in two four-year pilot culls in Somerset and Gloucestershire. The BVA concluded that controlled shooting of badgers was not effective and humane. The Environment Secretary promised to roll out more culls across the country if the Tories win the election, with the Government's strategy including cattle movement controls, vaccination, and culling. The BVA's support for cage-trapping and shooting is seen as regrettable by animal welfare campaigners.

Portishead founder Geoff Barrow accused streaming services of giving his band's music away for free, saying his band received just £1,700 in royalties despite 34 million plays. Barrow, who also runs the Invada record label, wants musicians to be paid more and says streaming is hurting young talent, stopping them from establishing themselves. Artists have long railed against low royalties paid from streaming companies, leading to Jay-Z launching his own Tidal service, promising bigger returns for musicians.

Game of Thrones fans who did not want to wait and legally watch HBO's hit series premiere its fifth season tonight have leaked the first four episodes online. The episodes began appearing on torrent download sites on Saturday night, and are thought to have leaked from review copies given to the press. Fans of the show, which follows the ambitions and betrayals of competing noble factions and families in the fantasy world of Westeros, now face the daunting task of avoiding spoilers online as the first four episodes are released over the course of the month.

A 25-year-old singer named Daniel Buccheri composed an emotional song to use as his brother's best man's speech at his brother's wedding. The unique speech, performed by Daniel, was composed to the tune of Stay With Me and included tributes to his brother and his bride. The speech was viewed over 100,000 times online and included stories about Daniel's brother's love for his new wife.

Zara Phillips, the Queen's granddaughter, has revealed her fitness routine after giving birth to her daughter Mia. She started hitting the exercise bike every morning before her daughter woke up, aiming to regain her fitness after pregnancy. Phillips, who is vying for a place on Team GB at the Rio Olympics, is committed to a strict exercise and diet regime to get back in shape.

Raheem Sterling's interview on social media regarding his readiness to sign a new contract at Liverpool was met with criticism, leading to a shift in fan opinion. The article discusses Sterling's recent training session and his potential move to Arsenal, while also addressing the ongoing frustration among Liverpool fans regarding the player's situation.

The article discusses a series of images from Barcelona's training sessions featuring former and current coaches, including Jose Mourinho, Pep Guardiola, Luis Enrique, Laurent Blanc, and Julen Lopetegui. The images reveal a pattern of managers from the same club and era working together, with some of them going on to manage their own teams. The article also mentions the 1996 Spanish Super Cup-winning Barcelona team, which included players who later became managers, such as Albert Ferrer, Sergi Barjuan, and Guillermo Amor.

Former Manchester United striker Eric Cantona has claimed that Paris Saint-Germain forward Javier Pastore is the best player in the world, stating that he is the "most creative" player due to his ability to pass and surprise opponents. Cantona, who was third in the Ballon d'Or in 1993, believes that Pastore's skills are unique and that he is the most creative player in the world today. Despite being overlooked by other top players like Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, Cantona's assessment has sparked debate and controversy, particularly regarding Spain's World Cup victory.

Lorenzo Simon, a 34-year-old landlord, was found guilty of murder for killing his tenant Michael Spalding and dismembering his body. Simon forced Spalding to decorate his flat before attacking him and then dismembering his body using a hacksaw. The body parts and tools were stuffed into two suitcases and dumped in a canal. A jury took 15 hours to decide Simon's guilt by unanimous verdict at Birmingham Crown Court. Bird, Simon's girlfriend, was cleared of murder but admitted assisting an offender. The case involved a 4-week trial, and Simon moved to Derby to evade police.

Local councils in Essex and Gloucestershire have created "loneliness maps" to identify areas where elderly and other vulnerable residents are most at risk of social isolation. The maps are based on factors such as age, living alone, mental health issues, lack of transportation, and income. The maps are used to target "danger zones" of loneliness and to identify residents who need help. The Campaign to End Loneliness recommends the use of these maps across the country as a way to treat the problem.

Dedicated waitress Judy Eddingfield, 65, celebrated her 50th anniversary working at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, where she has been employed for half a century. She credits her love for the job to the classic burger restaurant's warm atmosphere and the satisfaction of serving customers. Eddingfield, who started working there at age 15, has been married to her true love for 18 months after meeting him at the restaurant.

Former England captain Mike Gatting believes Kevin Pietersen should not walk straight back into the international set-up, even if he piles on the runs for Surrey this season. Pietersen has returned to the LV= County Championship in a bid to stake a claim for an England recall, although the 34-year-old only managed 19 runs against Glamorgan on Sunday. Gatting believes that if Gary Ballance, Ian Bell, and Joe Root play well, there might not be a place for Pietersen in the team. Gatting also suggests that Pietersen should not just come straight back into the team, as it would be unfair on the players currently in the team. Pietersen is keen to play for England again after being sacked in 2014, and he is hoping to get runs against West Indies.

A 17-year-old college student, Caleb Benn, developed an app called "Uploader for Instagram" that allows users to upload photos directly from their computer to the popular photo-sharing platform Instagram. The app, which is priced at $4.99, has been generating revenue for Benn, but Instagram is now taking legal action against him, claiming that his app violates the company's terms of service. Benn has responded by stating that he was aware of the legal gray area and that he was prepared to fix the app if he was given a chance.
