The controversy highlights the challenges faced by social media platforms in regulating the use of their APIs and the potential for abuse.

South Korean companies often hold hoesik dinners with their employees, where participants consume multiple rounds of alcohol at various venues. Foreign business travelers may feel pressured to participate, as drinking etiquette is a significant aspect of Korean culture. Koreans view drinking as a way to get to know people and are often generous with alcohol. To avoid offending others, it's important to follow the seven rules of drinking etiquette in Korea, such as identifying the "higher" person in the relationship and not having an empty glass.

The Duke of Kent, 79, was admitted to Aberdeen Royal Infirmary after suffering a dislocated hip during an Easter trip to the Royal Family's Balmoral estate. He was successfully treated and is expected to leave hospital later today. The Duke, who became the Duke of Kent at age six, is the son of Prince George and is best known for his royal duties and involvement with Freemasonry.

Meter Maids, a 50-year-old tradition of Surfers Paradise, Queensland, have been criticized by local business owners who believe the outdated and outdated practice of young women dressed in gold bikinis walking the main tourist strip and placing money into expired meters is no longer relevant due to advancements in parking meter technology. The controversy has led to a split in the Gold Coast community, with business leaders calling for the end of the era, while local business owners label the group as outdated and no longer providing a public service.

Greece has denied it will miss a repayment of £330 million to the International Monetary Fund, claiming it will make the payment on time. The country is due to repay a £330 million loan to the International Monetary Fund on April 9, but there were concerns it would default on the payment. Deputy finance minister Dimitris Mardas said Greece will in fact make the payment on time. Greece has denied it will miss a repayment of £330 million to the International Monetary Fund after reports it had drawn up plans to introduce a parallel drachma currency to pay its bills.

Turkey has blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after refusing to remove pictures of a prosecutor held during an armed siege last week. The prosecutor, Mehmet Selim Kiraz, died in hospital after being taken hostage by the Revolutionary People's Liberation Party-Front. The government blocked access to social media platforms because the images were "deeply upset" the prosecutor's family.

A young Star Wars fan, Colin Gilpatric, wrote a heartfelt letter to George Lucas asking if Jedi Knights could marry. Lucasfilm responded positively, stating that marriage would not lead to becoming a Sith, and that it would be a good path for a Jedi. Colin was overjoyed to receive the letter and was able to receive a package of Star Wars merchandise.

Wisconsin defeated Kentucky in the NCAA Tournament semi-finals, ending Kentucky's unbeaten streak of nearly 40 years. Wisconsin's Frank Kaminsky scored 20 points and 11 rebounds, while Bronson Koenig made 7 of 8 free throws in the final seconds. The Badgers will face Duke in the final, while Kentucky finishes the season at 38-1.

The article discusses the controversy surrounding famous performers' renditions of the American national anthem, highlighting incidents where their performances were either praised or criticized. Key points include:

- Vince Neil, Mötley Crüe, and other performers have been criticized for their renditions of the national anthem.
- Whitney Houston set a modern standard for the national anthem at the Super Bowl.
- Roseanne Barr's rendition at a Padres game was booed, and President George H. W. Bush called it "disgraceful. "
- Jimi Hendrix's psychedelic take on the national anthem was a hit with the Woodstock generation.
- Michael Bolton's rendition at the American League Championship Series was praised, but the words were criticized.

A video of a violent altercation between Irish brothers, Barry and Patrick Lyttle, has been released for the first time. The video shows Patrick pushing his brother Barry, who then retaliates with a single punch that causes his brother to fall to the ground. Barry is charged with grievous bodily harm and has pleaded guilty. Magistrate Graeme Curran suggested a jail sentence, but the brothers' family has called for the charges to be dropped. The brothers were reunited for a holiday in Australia when the fight occurred, and Patrick was treated by paramedics at the scene. The matter is set to return to court for a possible sentencing hearing.

The family of conjoined twin sisters Faith and Hope Howie, who died 19 days after birth due to a rare condition, were devastated to find their gravesite stripped of mementos and flowers after cemetery staff cleared the baby section. The Howies had built a small shrine at the site, but when they returned to retrieve their daughters' belongings, everything had been removed, leaving only a few items. The family confronted cemetery staff, who claimed they were notified of the cleaning process, but the Howies found their daughters' belongings in nearby rubbish bins. The couple maintained the site, but by the time they returned, everything had been laid out for collection.

Lord Neuberger, the President of the Supreme Court in Britain, suggested that Muslim women should be allowed to wear a full-face veil while appearing in court, as it shows respect towards different customs. He emphasized the need for judges and courtrooms to be sensitive to the cultural and social habits of those facing them. This suggestion comes amid uncertainty over the place of Muslim traditional dress in the legal system.

Andre Cole, a 52-year-old Missouri inmate, was executed for the 1998 murder of his ex-wife and her friend, Anthony Curtis, in a fit of rage over child support payments. Cole was the third convicted killer executed in Missouri this year. He was executed by lethal injection at the Eastern Reception, Diagnostic and Correctional Center in Bonne Terre, Missouri, at 10:15 pm on Tuesday. The execution was carried out despite appeals from Cole's family and the U.S. Supreme Court, which turned down several appeals, including one claiming Cole was mentally ill and unfit for execution.

Prince Harry will fly out of the UK to Australia without seeing his new niece or nephew, as the Duchess of Cambridge is several days overdue for the birth of her second child. Harry, who will be bumped down to fifth in the line of succession, had returned briefly to hand out prizes at the London Marathon after engagements in Turkey. He is now on a month-long placement with the army and a week-long tour of New Zealand, unable to meet the new royal baby until mid-May.

An alleged fraudster named Justin Jackson has been accused of posing as Oprah Winfrey, former Obama aide Reggie Love, and Madonna's manager in an attempt to trick people into giving him jobs, clothes, free food, and jewelry worth $2.4 million. Jackson is being sued by Oprah's TV network and Love, and has been convicted for grand theft over a ruse where he tricked a jeweler into lending him items worth $2.4 million. He has been accused of sending letters purporting to be from Oprah and her representatives, as well as posing as Oprah and her representatives to recommend him for jobs.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini has placed a €50 million (£36 million) price tag on Paulo Dybala, claiming he is the "new Lionel Messi." Dybala is being tracked by Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, Juventus, and Paris Saint-Germain. Inter Milan manager Roberto Mancini was spotted watching Dybala play against Parma. Palermo is determined to sign Dybala despite PSG's interest, with Zamparini demanding a €50 million fee.

In Brazil, thousands of protesters are taking to the streets in a series of demonstrations against President Dilma Rousseff, who is facing an economic downturn and a bribery scandal at the state-run oil company Petrobras. Rousseff's supporters are holding rallies in her support, while her opponents are calling for her impeachment. The Petrobras scandal involves a multimillion-dollar kickback scheme at the company, which has led to widespread protests and a plummeting approval rating for Rousseff. The country is already sharply divided, and the protests have grown in size and breadth, with some groups calling for a military intervention to oust the President.

Former Manchester United midfielder Eric Cantona has refuted claims he starred in a soft porn film, insisting that "You and the Night" is a "piece of art." The French film, which includes a scene with Cantona on his hands and knees in just his underwear, has been both praised and criticized. Cantona, 48, defended the film, saying it is "a work of art" and "beautiful," and not a porn film as some have said.

Psychologists have found that certain types of music can enhance the enjoyment of a fish and chip supper, according to a study. The research suggests that specific music can bring out different flavors in food and drink, such as sweet, salty, and bitter. The intensity of Nessun Dorma, performed by Luciano Pavarotti, is said to be the perfect accompaniment to dark mouse or coffee, while the high-pitched piano in Billie Holiday's Autumn in New York can help emphasize the autumnal flavor of a pumpkin pudding. The study also found that people enjoyed their wine more while listening to 'paired' music, rather than while being sat in silence. Professor Charles Spence, a behavioral psychologist from Oxford University, believes that music can draw attention to certain notes in a wine or food that are competing in the mind, and that humans tend to match the same sounds to the same tastes.

Raheem Sterling, 20-year-old England player, has been offered a £100,000-a-week contract by Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers, but negotiations have ended in stalemate. Sterling has insisted he is not a 'money grabber' and Taylor, chief executive of the Professional Footballers' Association, believes waiting until the season is over before resuming talks could be a wise move. Sterling has been linked with moves to Arsenal and leading clubs in Spain. Sterling scored for England in their Euro 2016 qualifier with Lithuania on Friday evening. Taylor added that Sterling is aware of what he owes to Liverpool and Rodgers has put his faith in him.

Ohio woman La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark discovered her biological mother, Francine Simmons, who works at the same call-center operation company as her, after the Ohio Department of Health released birth records for people born between January 1, 1964, and September 18, 1996. The two met after connecting on Facebook, and Simmons called Mitchell-Clark, who had been searching for her biological mother for almost her entire life. The reunion brought Mitchell-Clark and her biological sisters, Kamala and Maisha Cummings, together, and the family is now relieved and amazed by the connection.

Oscar "Papoo" Hernandez Jr., a convicted gun trafficker, was "awed" by New England Patriots star Aaron Hernandez and sent him an assault rifle and a pair of handguns a month before Odin Lloyd's killing. Hernandez pleaded guilty to weapons charges in connection to his namesake's murder case. Hernandez was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole for first-degree murder of the semi-professional football player in 2013.

A 33-year-old man named Joel Parker was arrested in Florida for throwing a Snickers bar at a bus driver's head after threatening him and being disruptive during the ride. The driver was not injured, but Parker was arrested for battery and issued a trespass warning. He is also never allowed to use the bus again.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has discussed pre-season plans with Saido Berahino, indicating that the striker will remain at the club beyond the summer transfer window. Berahino, who has expressed a desire to play in the Champions League, is likely to be included in England's under-21 squad for the upcoming European Championships. Pulis praised Berahino's performance and commitment, emphasizing the importance of professional footballers' longevity.

Giovanni Lo Porto, a 53-year-old Italian who had worked with the German aid organization Welthungerlife on a reconstruction project in Pakistan following deadly flooding, was abducted by four armed men on January 19, 2012, and later killed by a U.S. drone strike in Afghanistan and Pakistan. Lo Porto, who had previously studied at London Metropolitan University and was passionate about helping others, was a project manager with the aid group's clean water and sanitation program in Pakistan.

A photographer captured an image of a swarm of sharks off the coast of south Florida, with hundreds of sharks seen just 100 feet from the beach. The photographer, John Massung, flew for about a mile down the shore and saw the same scene. The sharks were thought to be Blacktips or Spinners, which migrate this time of year to breed. The image was shared more than 2,000 times on Facebook.

An 11-year-old retired K-9 officer, Zeus, was honored in a grand procession in Ridgefield, Connecticut, before he was put down due to a severe degenerative hip disorder and declining health. Zeus, who worked with the Ridgefield Police Department for eight years as a K-9 officer, was deeply missed by his fellow officers and residents. The tribute was held on Wednesday, and Zeus was taken to Ridgefield Veterinary Hospital for euthanasia.

Child sexual abuse reports have surged since Operation Yewtree, which was sparked by Jimmy Savile's assaults on dozens of children. Since 2011, thousands of people have contacted police with allegations of abuse, with nearly 9,000 reports filed in 2014. Despite a 60% increase in reports, the number of arrests fell by 9%, prompting critics to accuse the Government of failing victims. The South Yorkshire force saw a 577% increase in reported cases over the last five years. The NSPCC helpline has seen a 81% increase in calls about sexual abuse since Operation Yewtree was launched in 2012.

Iceland has become a popular filming location for TV series and Hollywood blockbusters, with Thingvellir National Park, Svartalfheim, Reykjanes Peninsula, Skaftafell National Park, and Vatnajokull glacier being some of the most favored filming locations. The country's stunning waterfalls and breathtaking glaciers have been featured in films such as Game of Thrones, Interstellar, Thor: The Dark World, and Prometheus.

A blue and yellow bathing box on Brighton Beach in Melbourne sold for a staggering $276,000, making it the most expensive bathing box ever sold. The grey-fronted building in Paddington, Sydney, was sold for $1.2 million to be converted into a home. A couple in Victoria has put the Old Kilmore Gaol up for sale after renovating it 18 years ago, with 6m bluestone walls and a history of being a maximum security prison.

Samantha Rawcliffe, a 40-year-old mother-of-two from Morecambe, was diagnosed with functional neurological disorder (FND) after a car accident in May 2022. FND is an umbrella term for a range of neurological symptoms that cannot be explained, including uncontrollable shaking, loss of bladder control, and difficulty with motor function. The condition is rare and debilitating, with no known cure and limited treatment options. Mrs. Rawcliffe is now confined to her house, unable to walk and relies on a mobility scooter. She has to take 32 different drugs each day to manage her symptoms.

A controversial statue of Lucille Ball, known for her iconic role in the TV show "I Love Lucy," has been criticized for its unflattering depiction. Sculptor Dave Poulin, who created the statue, admitted to being "disappointed" with the final outcome and pledged to make a new one. The statue, based on a moment from the show, has been called "monstrous" and "frightening" by some residents of Celoron, New York. Poulin offers to remove the current statue and create a new one for free, but the cost is estimated at $8,000 to $10,000.

Bayern Munich's versatile left-back David Alaba, who was out for three months after a knee injury, will be sidelined for around seven weeks with a torn knee ligament. Alaba, 22, is set to start rehabilitation work in about a month. The 22-year-old is out for the closing stages of the season. Alaba, who had been in superb form for Bayern, helped the club stay on track for a treble of titles. Bayern, who are top of the Bundesliga, will face Porto in the Champions League quarter-finals later this month.

Beatrice Nokes, the daughter of two solicitors and a Scotland Yard detective, appeared in court on charges of running an upmarket prostitution ring with her father and a police officer. Nokes, a university student, is accused of grooming three young women to sell their bodies for sex. The two defendants, along with the police officer, are facing multiple charges including inciting prostitution, controlling prostitution, and misconduct in a public office.

Diana Doyle, a whistleblower, revealed that a firm linked to the sale of NHS patient data offered details of eating disorder sufferers, stress, hair loss, dandruff, impotence, snoring, dieters, and those with plastic surgery for just 12p a head. The firm, Sequester, is offering to sell information on 43 different health conditions, including sensitive teeth, credit card information, and health insurance. The revelations prompted probes by the Information Commissioner's Office and the Direct Marketing Commission, and a third investigation by the General Pharmaceutical Council into Pharmacy2U, the UK's biggest online pharmacy.

Jordan Spieth, the 21-year-old golfer who won the 2017 Masters tournament, expressed his thoughts on his autistic sister Ellie, who was not able to attend the event. Spieth said he misses his sister and wishes she could have been there to share in his victory. He also mentioned that his sister has shaped his upbringing and provided him with perspective. Spieth's victory was described as "even better" than his dreams, and he expressed his hope to be finishing his final Masters appearance in 50 years' time.

Dick Advocaat, the Dutch manager of Sunderland, will not underestimate the significance of the Old Firm derby against Newcastle, unlike his previous experience in 1998 when he lost to Celtic. Advocaat, who has won six points ahead of Celtic this season, insists that every game is crucial and that the fans' support will be a significant factor in the match. The Sunderland midfielder Will Buckley, who was recently arrested on suspicion of sexual activity with an under-age girl, is expected to play for the first time in the derby.

A heated argument erupted between a young woman and a butcher in Sydney's Bondi area over a chicken purchase for a Game of Thrones-themed dinner. Belinda Bartholomew, the girlfriend of Roosters star Aidan Guerra, claimed she was racially abused and told to go to an "Aussie butcher" when she tried to change her chicken selection. The butcher, however, denied the claims, stating that he was the one being rude and that she was the troublemaker. The incident highlights tensions between immigrants and locals in Sydney's eastern suburbs.

Cadbury has reduced the size of its Freddo Frogs chocolate amphibians by 20% from 15g to 12g, while keeping the price the same. The change was made due to manufacturing cost increases. The Freddo Frogs were previously 20g, but now weigh 12g. The company's profit increased by 46% from $87 million to $127 million in 2013. The change has caused anger among chocolate lovers, with some calling it a "complete & utter baloney."

Hillary Clinton's campaign-in-waiting met in Brooklyn on Saturday, outlining their values statement and goals for the upcoming presidential campaign. The document, distributed by Robby Mook, outlines the campaign's purpose, avoiding mistakes from Clinton's 2008 campaign. The campaign aims to give every family, small business, and American a path to prosperity and is described as humble, disciplined, and united. The campaign will be called "Hillary for America" and Clinton plans to launch her candidacy through a video message on social media shortly after her announcement.

A 29-year-old woman, Kyli Wilfson, revealed her 18-month-long battle with chronic pancreatitis, a rare condition that left her unable to eat anything for a year and a half despite feeling extremely hungry. Initially misdiagnosed as acute pancreatitis, she underwent a series of hospital visits and a potentially life-threatening procedure to diagnose her condition. Kyli, who is a self-confessed "food person," had to rely on a feeding tube to maintain her nutrition, leading to rapid weight loss and a significant impact on her fiancé's relationship.

The article discusses memes posted in reference to the leaders' debate, including images of the five party leaders superimposed over characters from TV shows and films, as well as a meme showing Nicola Sturgeon posing with a sceptical face. The memes were inspired by the debate, which saw Labour leader Ed Miliband warn Prime Minister David Cameron and his deputy Nick Clegg that they would not get into power without lurching left, and the Scottish National Party leader Nicola Sturgeon told him she was "not strong enough" to win power on her own. The images were also inspired by a debate that saw Miliband appear with the SNP leader, Ukip's Nigel Farage, Green leader Natalie Bennett, and Plaid Cymru's Leanne Wood, but David Cameron and Nick Clegg stayed away.

Amir Khan, the British boxer, is set to face Manny Pacquiao in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, after Mayweather declined the opportunity to fight. Khan, who has been waiting for Mayweather for two years, is now looking forward to a fight with Pacquiao. The fight is expected to be a huge draw, with Khan being a hero to the Muslim world.

A tiny two-bedroom home in Islington, London, has sold for £750,000, despite being only 5ft wide in some areas and 8ft 8in wide at its widest. The property, which is sandwiched between two other properties, has a narrow 'galley kitchen' and is described as 'well proportioned' by the estate agency. The home has two bedrooms, a tiny study, reception room, shower room, cloakroom, kitchen, and a garden. At its widest, it stretches across 8ft 8in. The property was put on the market with Foxtons for £750,000, almost double the price it sold for in 2001. The buyer will have to pay £27,000 in stamp duty, the same as a second-hand narrow boat which is 50ft long.

Scottish First Minister Nicola Sturgeon is launching an extraordinary bid to lead the UK, unveiling a manifesto that includes policies tailored for a power-sharing deal with Labour. Several of her election pledges overlap with Labour policy, such as slashing tuition fees in England and rolling back competition in the English NHS. The SNP aims to build a 'progressive alliance' for people 'right across the UK' and is positioning itself as a major force in the upcoming election, with polls suggesting the SNP could win as many as 50 seats and hold the balance of power at Westminster. The surge in support for the SNP could trigger constitutional turmoil similar to the 1910 election, which saw Irish Nationalists surge and end up with more than 70 seats, leading to bitter conflict and the eventual secession of Ireland.

Celtic secured the Glasgow Cup for the fourth time in eight seasons, defeating Rangers 2-0, with Josh Kerr scoring the opening goal. The match was played behind closed doors at Hampden Park, with Rangers taking the game to Celtic but failing to score. Celtic's victory was celebrated by their U17 players, with Ronny Deila and Stuart McCall both expressing happiness.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis, who previously played for Crystal Palace, led his team to a 2-0 victory over the former club. Pulis insists on wearing his cap, track suit, and shiny white trainers during every game, stating he would never take it off during a match. The victory moved West Brom to 36 points, securing their survival in the Premier League.

Jameela Jamil, a 29-year-old television presenter and former model, spent £3,000 on having all her amalgam fillings removed and replaced with white fillings after experiencing health problems for nearly seven years. She believed the fillings were causing her to wake up with a puffy, swollen face, feeling hungover, and experiencing exhaustion and fainting. Tests revealed high levels of mercury, and after ruling out other potential causes, she was diagnosed with mercury poisoning from her fillings. The dental amalgam, made from a mixture of metals including silver, tin, and copper, is used for robust fillings on back teeth. While the amounts taken in from fillings are minuscule, the review by the EU Commission's Scientific Committee in 2008 concluded there was no risk from amalgam.

Suge Knight, the co-creator of Death Row Records, was refused an appeal to have his bail reduced from $10 million to $5 million as he awaits trial for murder and attempted murder. Despite walking confidently into court, he had to be carted out in a wheelchair as Judge Ronald Coen rejected his pleas. However, Knight believes his close friend, the undefeated professional boxer Floyd Mayweather, will bail him out when he wins on Saturday. Mayweather, an undefeated professional worth $420 million, is set to land a record pay check after going head-to-head with Manny Pacquiao on Saturday.

In an interview with Puss Puss magazine, TV chef Gizzi Erskine revealed that her British shorthair cat, Kimchi, has a discerning palate and loves crunchy human food, such as poppadoms, tortilla chips, and taramasalata. The cat also enjoys caviar, salmon roe, jellied fish heads, and a seafood sculpture made of octopus, lobster, and prawns. Erskine, who lives in a foodie household, has had to put Kimchi on a diet due to her excessive weight gain.

A father in Japan took a photograph of his daughter standing near a rocky outcrop in July 2014. The photograph, which showed a pair of black boots behind the girl, sparked controversy online. The father, Martin Springall, said he had no idea what the boots could be and that he had no one else in the vicinity. The photograph has been the subject of debate on Reddit, with some believing it was modified or a trick of the light, while others argue it was real. Springall insisted the photograph was 100% untouched and that he could not explain the boots' origin.

The UK government plans to introduce new immigration policies that will require foreign workers to pay an average of £22,000 in tax and national insurance before they can claim benefits. The changes will ban EU migrants from receiving state support for four years and limit access to benefits for those in work. The Home Secretary, Theresa May, said the plans aim to curb the appeal of coming to Britain from poorer parts of the EU and make the immigration system fairer and more effective. The policies will be part of a renegotiation with the EU and will be published in the upcoming Tory manifesto.

A severely disabled boy, Cody Neatis, from Preston, England, has been sleeping on a mattress on the floor in hospital for seven nights due to a lack of a suitable bed for him. Cody, who has Down's syndrome, epilepsy, autism, and is fed by a tube, has been without a hospital bed because staff do not have the special cot he needs to keep him safe in his sleep. His mother, Lynne Neatis, 48, has had to sleep with Cody, who has a developmental age of around 12 months, on the mattress. The hospital does not have the specialist high-sided cot he must sleep in, to prevent him from injuring himself in the night. Lynne Neatis is now demanding answers from the local health trust as she claims she has waited two years for the high-sided bed needed for Cody and other disabled children.

Ahead of the Masters golf tournament, Derek Lawrenson from Sportsmail will provide daily updates on the tournament's behind-the-scenes activities. The article highlights several key points: Ian Poulter forgot his golf clubs before the tournament, Henrik Stenson is recovering from flu, Tiger Woods will play in the traditional par-three tournament with his children, and the 16th hole is a practice-round tradition where players try to skip their golf balls across the water.

Juventus have ruled out a move for Manchester United loan star Radamel Falcao after claiming the Colombia striker's wages are 'beyond their means'. Falcao has scored only four goals and failed to force his way into Louis van Gaal's starting XI at Manchester United. Juventus general manager Beppe Marotta has claimed that Falcao wanted to come to Turin last summer but the Serie A champions have now taken themselves out of the race to sign him. Juventus are interested in striker Paulo Dybala and Edinson Cavani, with Dybala rated at £35m.

David Cameron plans to sell Lloyds Bank shares worth up to £4 billion if he wins the election, offering them at a discount and encouraging shareholders to hold onto their shares. This is the largest privatisation since the Thatcher era, with a loyalty bonus of one free share for every ten held for at least a year. The sale is part of a Conservative policy to hark back to the 1980s, with a focus on efficiency and tax revenues.

Living near congested roads with high levels of air pollution can cause 'silent strokes' that increase the risk of dementia, according to a study by researchers at Boston University School of Medicine. The microscopic particles, mostly from traffic fumes and factory emissions, alter the structure of the brain and contribute to the deaths of 29,000 people every year in Britain. The study involved more than 900 people aged 60 and over who did not have dementia or a history of strokes. The researchers found that increases in PM2.5 in towns and cities were linked with a 46% higher risk of silent strokes.

Jessica Ainscough, a 30-year-old wellness warrior who died from a rare and aggressive form of cancer, revealed in an emotional letter that she was undergoing radiation treatment in her final weeks. Despite her decision to fight the cancer with controversial Gerson Therapy, which lacks scientific support, she embraced a course of targeted radiation. Her partner, Tallon Pamenter, described her as a "wellness warrior" who displayed courage and grace, and he expressed his love for her. The radiation successfully managed to shrink the tumour but caused complications, leading to her death.

Ten people, including four children, were involved in a multi-vehicle crash on the Brisbane Valley Highway in Brisbane's west on Wednesday afternoon. Three vehicles collided, resulting in chest and shoulder injuries for a 40-year-old man and a five-year-old boy, as well as arm and abdominal pain for a 27-year-old woman and a six-year-old girl. The incident occurred near Fernvale, with six others, including an infant and two young girls, being taken to Ipswich Hospital with minor injuries or for further assessment. The affected stretch of the highway was closed off, with diversions in place south of Fernvale.

A 34-year-old man named Jason McDonald, who volunteers at a Colorado alligator farm, walked a thin rope over a pool containing more than 50 hungry alligators. McDonald, who has been involved with alligators for over ten years and has taken handling classes, thought this would be an interesting new way of interacting with the fearsome creatures. The gators were surprisingly ok with the slackline, and McDonald said he thought this would be an interesting new way of interacting with the fearsome creatures.

The son of a Syrian imam who was shot dead on a London street may have met his father's killer just days before the murder. Abdul Hadi Arwani, an opponent of Syrian President Bashar Al-Assad, had visited the area where he was killed with his son days before his death. Arwani, 48, was shot and killed in his car on a quiet street in North West London after being called there last Tuesday, apparently to provide a quote for building work. The man, who has not been otherwise identified, also told the imam that there was no need for his son to accompany him again when he did come back. The imam's children are in little doubt that their father was killed by the man asking for the building quote.

Hong Kong's Jenny's cookies, a popular buttery treat, have become a major tourist attraction, with people lining up for hours to purchase them. The cookies, priced at $9 each, have sparked a black market, with bakeries producing knockoffs and locals hiring others to stand in line and resell the goods at a higher price. The frenzy has drawn comparisons to other food manias around the world, such as cronuts and ramen burgers.

A mother-of-one, Kira Hollis, who was diagnosed with borderline personality disorder and anorexia, has overcome her struggles by becoming a bodybuilder. At the age of 6st, she was deemed clinically underweight and self-harming. After being ordered to go to the gym by doctors, she turned her life around and is now a healthy 9. 5st. The experience has given her the confidence to overcome her depression and has changed her life. She has been helped by the Cherry Orchard Clinic in Tamworth and medication from her doctor. Her daughter Olivia has also been a huge help in her recovery.

Lewis Ferguson, a 18-year-old jockey, survived a spectacular fall from Merrion Square during a race at Wincanton on Wednesday. Despite the fall, Ferguson was able to get back on the horse and said he was undeterred from getting back in the saddle. The incident has been watched by hundreds of thousands of people online and has led to Ferguson gaining a few hundred Twitter followers. Ferguson's parents were worried about his safety, but he was able to reassure them that he was fine. The incident has not put Ferguson off riding, and he has expressed a desire to ride at the Cheltenham Festival and Aintree every year.

Hillary Clinton launched her campaign in a unique and unconventional way, using a video, new logo, and a road trip to "rebrand" herself and reframe her message. Critics, including Ruth Marcus and Jon Stewart, dismissed her efforts as "relentlessly, insultingly vapid" and "boring as s---." However, from a marketing perspective, the campaign may have been more successful than expected. The campaign's strategy of flipping Clinton's message from self-absorbed to empathetic and simple, with a bit of the upstart feel of Apple, may have been effective in creating an empathetic relationship with voters. The campaign's use of everyday Americans and fast-food chains, such as ordering at Chipotle, may have reinforced the "everyday Americans" campaign theme.

More than 1,700 Chinese high school students from Yichuan, Shaanxi province, took an exam in their school's playground on Saturday. The unusual move was made possible due to a lack of indoor space. The students organized the exam themselves, with a regular radio announcement instructing them to turn their chairs and desks from time to time to avoid being dazzled by the sun. The school believes that this outdoor exam could be a test of the students' organizing capacity and a way to broaden their horizons and encourage relaxation.

Sportsmail has partnered with Gillette to offer a unique chance for one lucky reader to win a pair of Nike Magista Obra boots signed by Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart. The prize includes a new Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor with Flexball technology and a shave gel. The competition closes on April 19.

Kecil, a baby orangutan, was rejected by his natural mother and a surrogate mother, but found love with Maggie, an experienced surrogate mother at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo. Maggie has now been raising Kecil for the past 10 months, and the two have an inseparable bond. Kecil is set to make his first public outing this weekend, where he will be displayed for two hours slots between 10am and midday, allowing him to nap in the afternoons.

A 61-year-old woman named Noelle Baynham died suddenly and was eaten by her two dogs after being locked in the house for days. The dogs, a Jack Russell and a Staffordshire Bull Terrier, initially tried to wake her but became desperate for food and started eating her remains. The most likely cause of death was an accidental overdose of medication, but the exact cause could not be determined due to the dogs' consumption of her organs. The incident was described as "the most horrifying thing" the friend who discovered her body had ever seen.

French handball star Nikola Karabatic, along with his brother Luka and 15 other players, has been accused of match fixing in an illegal betting case involving their Montpellier club. Karabatic, who was briefly detained, now plays for Barcelona in the Spanish league. The trial is expected to take place within months, with Karabatic facing up to five years in prison and a fine.

A gang of six men, including Ahmed Hassan-Sule, 21, and Mohamed Saleh, 22, were convicted of a string of sexual offenses against teenage girls in Banbury, Oxfordshire. The offenses occurred in cars, woods, and at the defendants' homes from 2009 to 2014. The victims, aged between 13 and 16, were targeted at under-18s parties organized by Hassan-Sule. The judge sentenced the men to between three and nine years in jail. The gang used social media to lure victims and abused them from 2009 to 2014.

Former New England Patriots star Aaron Hernandez faces multiple trials for murder and other charges in the death of Odin Lloyd, including a potential third trial for a 2012 shooting in Boston. Hernandez is also being sued by the families of Odin Lloyd and Daniel de Abreu/Furtado, as well as by Alexander Bradley for a 2013 shooting in Miami. Hernandez's lawyers argue he couldn't defend himself properly in Massachusetts.

The Emirates Airline has signed a historic deal to sponsor the FA Cup, rebranding it as the Emirates FA Cup. The deal, worth £30 million over three years, will add to Emirates' existing portfolio of sporting sponsorships. The deal includes naming rights to Arsenal's Emirates Stadium, the Emirates Cup, and sponsorship of AC Milan and Hamburg. Emirates' sponsorship of football clubs in the UK and Italy has been ongoing for several years, with the latest deal extending until the 2019-20 season.

Michael Phelps, the 18-time Olympic champion, is aiming to compete in the Rio Olympics next year but won't swim at the world championships in Russia this summer. He was suspended by USA Swimming after a second drunken driving arrest and is now back in Arizona for inpatient alcohol rehabilitation.

Gareth Bale, a key player for Real Madrid, is doubtful for the Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid due to a calf injury. The Welsh forward limped off during Real's 3-1 home victory over Malaga on Saturday. Real Madrid also lacks Croatian midfielder Luka Modric, who is expected to be unavailable for six weeks due to a knee ligament strain. Real Madrid's coach, Carlo Ancelotti, hopes to have striker Karim Benzema fit for the match after the Frenchman missed Saturday's encounter with a knee injury.

Scientists warn that older people are more susceptible to emotions when making decisions about their retirement, particularly during financial crises. A study of 1,204 retired people found that those with better cognitive abilities were less likely to panic and sell investments during market downturns. The study, published in the Journal of Consumer Affairs, suggests that cognitive decline with age can affect an investor's ability to control emotional responses to losses. The reforms announced by Chancellor George Osborne allow people turning 55 to take income from their pension, but they can also keep their investments in the stock market to boost profits.

Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini is under pressure to turn around the club's fortunes, with Pearce believing the 61-year-old should be given more time to do so. The team's recent poor form, particularly a defeat to Manchester United, has contributed to the manager's challenges. Pearce suggests that the club should consider refreshing its squad in the summer, while also emphasizing the importance of maintaining Pellegrini's tenure.

Manchester United's stars, including Wayne Rooney, Ander Herrera, and Robin van Persie, were training in the sunshine ahead of their Premier League match against Manchester City on Sunday. The victory could see Manchester United move four points clear of Manchester City in fourth place. Manchester United's captain, Wayne Rooney, expressed his desire to win the derby games for Manchester United fans.

Fiorentina, a Serie A club, lost 1-0 to Verona in a match that ended in a late goal, leaving them nine points behind third-placed AS Roma. The match was played on Monday, and Fiorentina's coach, Vincenzo Montella, expressed no complaints about the result. Fiorentina, currently in sixth place with 49 points, will host Dynamo Kiev in the Europa League quarter-finals on Thursday.

Miley Cyrus, 22, attended the 30th Annual Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony in Cleveland, Ohio, where she posed for a social media snap with somewhat bushy underarm hair. This sparked controversy on social media, with some users advising Cyrus to shave her armpits and others defending her choice. Cyrus is not the first, and probably won't be the last, to shun her razor in favor of the fuzz.

Barcelona's Lionel Messi, Neymar, and Luis Suarez have scored 102 goals in all competitions this season, taking them five points clear in La Liga. Messi has 49 goals, Neymar has 32, and Suarez has 21. The trio's dominance is due to their ability to score inside the box, with Messi having 30 left-footed and 15 right-footed goals, plus four headers. Barcelona's emphatic win boosts their Liga goal difference to +78, putting pressure on Real Madrid ahead of their match with Almeria.

A 44-year-old pedestrian named Andrea McVeigh was struck by a cyclist while walking on the pavement in Bermondsey, South London. The cyclist fled the scene, chased by McVeigh's husband. McVeigh suffered two three-inch gashes to her forehead and other facial and hand injuries. The cyclist initially stopped after the impact but then sped off. McVeigh is now scarred for life and off work sick with facial injuries. The police have issued CCTV footage of the cyclist they want to speak to and have launched a hunt for the cyclist.

Paul Gregory, a 51-year-old man from Bedford, was fined £795 for having a blue badge, claiming he could only walk 200 meters, when in fact he was a keen walker. He was exposed when Bedford Borough Council staff noticed a newspaper report describing his exploits on a 191-mile hike. Gregory was found guilty of two counts of dishonestly obtaining a blue badge by misrepresenting his physical abilities and was ordered to carry out 150 hours of unpaid work, pay a £60 victim surcharge, and undergo 19 sessions of 'thinking skills'.

Apple has filed a patent for a new method of unlocking its devices using facial recognition. The patent details a system that would automatically unlock a device when the user moves their face into a certain position and matches a previously taken photo. This would replace current methods of unlocking a device, which are "inconvenient and time consuming." The system would track the movement of the phone to determine whether it is being used or placed flat on a table, and would only unlock if the angle of the face matches. This would be different from Android's 'Trusted face' feature, which relies on the user pressing the power button to enable the screen.

Elizabeth Sedway, a 51-year-old mother of two battling cancer, was ejected from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California due to her lack of a doctor's note clearing her to fly. The incident occurred when an airline representative noticed her wearing a surgical mask and asked if she needed anything. After being asked a second time, she indicated she might require extra time to board the plane due to her condition. The family was eventually removed from the flight, and Sedway's husband and sons had to help her and their other children out of their seats. The airline was concerned she might collapse during the flight, and after being asked to leave, she emailed her oncologist for a note.

A vintage 1973 E-Type Jaguar was involved in a head-on collision with a 1973 Toyota Kluger on Easter Sunday night in Frenchs Forest, Sydney. The Jaguar, worth over $120,000, was completely written off, while all three adults involved were taken to hospital for precautionary measures. The crash occurred on Warringah Road, and the incident has sparked sympathy from car enthusiasts. The incident comes after police warned of increased risks during the Easter long weekend.

Google has set up a team dedicated to boosting the lifespan of phones, tablets, and electric cars, according to reports. The team, consisting of four men, focuses on developing and testing various battery technologies, including flexible and wearable options. Google has been working on similar projects since 2012, when Dr. Ramesh Bhardwaj led a testing team. The company has also collaborated with experts at AllCell Technologies to develop batteries that function at subfreezing temperatures, which is crucial for its Project Loon balloons. The team's work is part of a broader effort to improve battery technology across various devices.

The 223ft Explorer is a luxury superyacht designed by British yacht designer Tony Castro, featuring a helipad, infinity pool, and space for 12 guests. It is equipped with a climate-controlled garage for storing helicopters, jetskis, and submarines, as well as a variety of water toys. The yacht is expected to cost approximately 40 million euros to build, making it a costly addition to the ultra-rich. The layout includes a large carrying capacity for toys and tenders, ensuring a comfortable and luxurious experience for the 12 guests.

Ed Miliband, the leader of the Labour Party, has announced his intention to implement rent controls, despite warnings from experts that the plans will backfire and lead to more tenants being evicted. The controversial measures, demanded by the militant Unite union, would cap rents and offer three-year tenancies, but critics argue that they will give landlords an incentive to evict tenants and suppress house building. The proposal has been met with mixed reactions, with some senior Tories calling it "drivel" and the Confederation of British Industry warning that it could discourage investment and push rents up in the long term.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town fan was removed from his role as a mascot for Reading in the FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal after a video emerged of him backing Arsenal. The young supporter, Ryan Dearnley, said he hoped Arsenal would win, sparking outrage from Reading fans. The Football Association moved him to be a mascot for England instead.

A giant supervoid, 1.8 billion light-years across, may be responsible for a mysterious "Cold Spot" in the universe, according to astronomers. The supervoid is thought to be causing a "less-dense" region of the universe, which has about 20% less matter than other regions of the universe. The supervoid is the largest single structure ever found by humanity. The supervoid appears to be "roughly spherical" and may even contain a "significant substructure" at its center. The supervoid is thought to be causing a "less-dense" region of the universe, which has about 20% less matter than other regions of the universe. The supervoid is the largest single structure ever found by humanity.

The Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, will display Abraham Lincoln's chair where he was shot in 1865 as part of its observance of the 150th anniversary of the assassination. The chair, which has a dark stain on the back, is believed to be oil from other people's heads who sat in the chair before Lincoln. The museum has been housing the chair since its founding 85 years ago.

A 19-year-old vlogger named Jake Boys surprised his girlfriend Emily Canham with tickets to see One Direction perform in Cardiff, but mistakenly booked plane tickets to the Republic of Ireland instead. The couple is now planning to buy new train tickets to Cardiff for the band's show in June.

A new device called the Roboscan 2M Aeria has been created by Romanian company MB Telecom. It can scan entire planes for contraband, bombs, and weapons using a cone of radiation. The device is accurate enough to find a filament in a light bulb and is already being used to check trucks at borders in Eastern Europe. The device can scan planes from small private jets to medium-sized commercial airplanes and can be used to detect weapons and other contraband in low-security airports. The device can scan an entire plane in about 20 minutes.

A 54-year-old convicted paedophile, Stephen Munden, has gone on the run after vanishing from a psychiatric unit. Munden, who suffers from learning difficulties, was detained under the Mental Health Act after sexually touching a three-year-old girl. He is described as about 5ft 8ins tall, of a heavy build, and has dark hair. Officers believe he may have shaved off his beard before leaving the hospital in Winchfield. Munden was previously convicted of sexually touching a child under the age of 13.

Middlesbrough are currently top of the Championship table, having held the position for 101 days. The division is highly competitive, with just four weeks remaining and seven points separating the top eight teams. Middlesbrough's advantage is that their match against Watford is a lunchtime kick-off, which could give them a psychological advantage. The promotion race is extremely tight, with Watford and Norwich potentially securing a top-two finish if they win their upcoming matches. Jonathan Woodgate, Middlesbrough's experienced captain, is hoping to continue playing through the pain of his broken toe.

The latest hair trend is grey hair, with women embracing the look on social media under the hashtag #grannyhair. The trend has gained popularity on platforms like Instagram, with users sharing images of themselves with grey locks. The trend has been embraced by both men and women, with some using it as a statement of defiance, while others see it as a fashion statement. The trend has been traced back to a catwalk show earlier this month featuring silver-haired models, and has been popularized by fashion icons like Rihanna, Lady Gaga, and Dame Judi Dench.

A couple from Bellefontaine, Ohio, who were struggling with chronic conditions and financial difficulties, died from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning after leaving their beloved pet cats outside. The couple, Randy and Jodi Speidel, had created online fundraisers but failed to draw any donations. Their meager funds were stretched thin, and they had limited food and water. The couple had removed their cats to spare their lives, and they were found wandering outside. The couple left behind two daughters, Randa and Kira Speidel.

Liberal Democrat leader Nick Clegg vowed to continue as leader even if the party is reduced to fewer than 30 MPs, despite previous indications that he would quit if the party is left out of power. Clegg emphasized his commitment to serving the country and his party, despite the potential risks of losing the center ground and undoing the sacrifices made over the past five years. His comments came as Business Secretary Vince Cable expressed hope for another deal with the Conservatives.

A pensioner in Somerset, England, was saved from a large badger by his Jack Russell dog. The badger, which was about the size of a pig and had six-inch teeth, attacked the dog but not the pensioner. The pensioner, who was sitting in his garden with his dog, was dragged back indoors by the dog. The pensioner was left badly shaken and fears he could have been attacked if his dog had not been there. The National Farmers' Union has issued advice for residents on protecting their property from invading badgers.

Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose to Porto U21s on Wednesday, while the Blues were knocked out of the Champions League. Mourinho visited Fulham's Motspur Park with his son Jose Junior. Fulham's Liam Donnelly was sent off, but Porto's Leandro Silva scored a hat-trick to progress to the Premier League International Cup final. Chelsea are closing in on the Premier League title with six games to play, 10 points above Arsenal.

Andreas Christopheros, a 29-year-old property developer, was severely injured when corrosive liquid was thrown in his face outside his home in Truro, Cornwall. Nicole Phillips, 45, from Hastings, was charged with perverting the course of justice and is due to appear at Bodmin Magistrates Court on April 30. Her husband, David Phillips, 48, was already charged with grievous bodily harm with intent. Christopheros, a father-of-one, suffered life-changing injuries, including a loss of vision and facial scars, after the attack last December.

A Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route has erected signs warning pilgrims not to defecate along the famous path, as angry residents complain about the frequent nature calls. The signs, which show a squatting figure defecating within a red circle with a diagonal line across it, have become an attraction for pilgrims and other visitors. The pilgrimage attracts thousands of pilgrims every year, but there are few places to relieve themselves along the 500-mile route.

A massive fire consumed a building that was once home to a Michigan strip club on Wednesday afternoon, according to local media reports. The blaze took place at a Flint intersection and started at about 1pm, destroying only the building itself and a few nearby power lines. The site was not a vacant facility, and an investigation into what was behind the blaze continues.

A woman of Arab and Jewish descent, Shoshana Hebshi, who was strip-searched at a Detroit-area airport on the 10th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks, has reached a settlement of $40,000 in a lawsuit filed on her behalf. The settlement is the result of a lawsuit filed by the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) against the federal government, Frontier Airlines, the Transportation Security Administration (TSA), and the Wayne County Airport Authority. The settlement comes after Hebshi was humiliated and strip-searched during a security check at Detroit Metropolitan Airport. The incident occurred on September 11, 2011, when she was seated next to two Indian-American men, whom crew members had said spent a lot of time in the plane's bathroom. Hebshi was held for hours before being released. The settlement sends a message that discrimination and profiling are unacceptable, and it will help protect future passengers from similar experiences.

An Asiana Airlines flight OZ162 crashed and skidded off the runway at Hiroshima Airport in Japan, resulting in 20 injuries. The plane, which had departed from Incheon International Airport in Seoul, South Korea, crashed at 8pm local time and overran the runway. Local media reported that the plane spun 180 degrees after impact and was left facing the wrong way on the runway. The crash injured 20 people, and the airport was closed as a result.

Mark-Francis Vandelli, a wealthy reality star from Made in Chelsea, has opened up his watch collection to the Evening Standard, showcasing 16 expensive timepieces. The 26-year-old, privately educated and the son of a multimillionaire industrialist and model, has been collecting watches since his teens, with his most expensive watch costing £32,000. The collection includes a Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42, a Cartier Tortue Collection Privée, and a Rolex yellow gold Oyster Perpetual. Vandelli's most expensive watch is a Cartier white gold Moonphase, which he bought from a shop on Sloane Street in Chelsea earlier this year.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy, known for his roles in "All Creatures Great and Small" and "Winston Churchill," is selling his extensive collection of antiques in a £100,000 auction. The collection includes a 3D diorama of the Battle of Agincourt, a longbow made from yew, and a portrait of Hardy holding the bow. The auction, held by Dominic Winter auctioneers in South Cerney, Gloucestershire, features dozens of books, furniture, swords, flintlock rifles, silverware, and crystal chandeliers. Hardy, 89, is downsizing and is selling his collection, which he built up through his interest in classic literature and military history.

A Brazilian commuter, Nelson Felippe, took a photo of a woman hugging another woman on a train platform and posted it on Facebook, expressing his disapproval of the scene. The image quickly went viral, with over 100, 000 views in 24 hours. Felippe's post, which cleverly mocks conservative attitudes, warns against public displays of affection and challenges social conventions. The incident highlights the tension between personal freedom and public safety, with Felippe warning against the normalization of such behavior.

A young English cricket fan, Jonathan Stevenson, wrote a letter to Richie Benaud, the legendary Australian cricket player, asking for tips on left-handed leg spin. Benaud, who was 68 at the time, responded with a detailed letter that included advice on different deliveries and how to deliver them. Stevenson shared the letter on Twitter as a tribute to Benaud, who passed away in 2018. The letter, dated September 27, 1996, was signed by Benaud and included a full page of notes on spin bowling for left-hand bowlers.

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg predicts that virtual reality will revolutionize travel, allowing users to experience destinations from multiple viewpoints and even change their perspectives. The company purchased Oculus, a virtual reality headset maker, and promised to support virtual reality on its newsfeed, enabling users to explore locations with VR headsets. Marriott hotels have also trialled Oculus Rift for a tour of destinations.

A 22-year-old woman in China was diagnosed with bone cancer and admitted to the hospital, preventing her from getting married on her birthday. Her boyfriend, Guo Kai, arranged for professional photographers to take wedding photos for her, despite her condition requiring frequent medical attention. The couple's love story, which began after a mutual friend introduced them, highlights their commitment to each other and their shared experiences.

A 34-year-old man, Blaine Boudreaux, was charged with intoxication manslaughter, intoxicated assault, and failure to stop and render aid involving death after three separate DUI collisions in Houston that killed a 6-year-old boy and injured his mother. Boudreaux, who has an extensive DUI record in Louisiana, was allegedly drunk when he ran a red light on Lockwood Drive and slammed his Dodge pickup truck into a Honda Civic, killing the boy and injuring his mother. The incident occurred within three hours of another collision that killed a homeless man and injured a woman and her toddler.

Microsoft has launched a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions within the company, with positions based at its Redmond campus in Washington and run in partnership with Specialisterne, a Danish nonprofit. The program aims to expand opportunity and represent customers, with Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella apologizing for comments about women needing to trust the system to pay them well.

Two deputies involved in the fatal shooting of Eric Harris in Tulsa, Oklahoma, have been reassigned due to threats against them and their families. The shooting occurred when Reserve Deputy Robert Bates shot Harris, who was trying to arrest him. The deputies are not charged with a crime but have faced criticism for their actions. The sheriff's office has suspended operations of the drug unit pending a review of the April 2 shooting. The FBI has cleared the agency of any civil rights violations. The shooting has led to allegations of forgery and unqualified training, with the sheriff denying these claims. The family of Eric Harris has demanded justice and changes in policy.

Katie Prager, a 24-year-old woman with cystic fibrosis who needs a life-saving lung transplant, is in a race against time as her health continues to decline. Her husband, Dalton, is pleading for help, but her insurance company, Kentucky Medicaid, will not pay for the out-of-state treatment she needs at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. Dalton is desperate to save his wife, Katie, and has already received new lungs. The couple is running out of options and needs help to save Katie's life.

The Sleep Cycle app analyzed data from over two million users to determine the best and worst days of the week for sleep quality worldwide. The study found that the earliest wake-up time is on Mondays in South Africa, while Americans wake up at 7am and are in the worst mood all week. Slovakia topped the list for national average sleep quality, while the UK was in 45th place and the US was in 49th. The best sleep quality occurs on Wednesdays, with China recording the highest sleep quality that night. Users in the Middle East sleep the longest on Thursdays, and Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and UAE report the best mood on Thursdays. Americans typically don't rise until 8:24am on Fridays and report the best wake-up mood.

A series of unpublished love letters from Mexican artist Frida Kahlo to her lover Jose Bartoli are expected to fetch upwards of $120,000 when the passionate missives go up for auction later this year. The letters, written between 1946 and 1949, were saved by Jose until his death in 1995 and comprise more than 100 pages. Frida signed her letters to Jose 'Mara', which biographer Hayden Herrera explained is probably short for 'Maravillosa', a name Jose would call her. The collection also includes an original drawing of a sleeping cat, pressed flowers, ribbon, beads, and drafts of a few of Jose's responses.

Trade union leader Len McCluskey, known for his militant stance, is popular with Labour activists but is seen as a "potent, sinister force" in British politics due to his influence over Labour candidates and his socialist policies. McCluskey, who once presided over more strikes than any other union boss, is open about his desire to return Britain to the "dark days" of the 1970s, when unions held the government to ransom. His union, Unite, has a claimed membership of 1.42 million and remains addicted to failed socialist policies, including a major expansion in the public sector, higher taxation, and state spending.

A zookeeper at the Zoological Center in Tel Aviv, Elad Hershkowitz, captured footage of various animals drinking water in their enclosures using a GoPro camera placed at the bottom of their troughs. The footage, totaling 30 hours, revealed unique drinking behaviors among the animals, including a rhino that almost kisses the surface of the water and a lemur that delicately licks it. The zookeeper, who had the idea while walking around the enclosures, was surprised by the animals' reactions, which ranged from skepticism to complete acceptance of the camera. The footage, which was cut down to four minutes, offers a unique perspective on animal drinking habits and showcases the diverse behaviors of the animals.
Just a quarter of voters think David Cameron is hungriest to win the election, according to a poll, as the Prime Minister tries to boost his campaign passion.

A man, Zaur Dadaev, has confessed to assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov, claiming he was beaten and pressured into making the statement. Dadaev was previously convicted but now denies the murder. He was accused of being involved in the shooting of Nemstov in February, along with four other Chechen men. The incident sparked a massive protest march in Moscow.

A 4-month-old baby boy named Sonit Awal was pulled from the rubble of a Nepal earthquake that killed over 5,000 people. His father, Shyam Awal, frantically searched for him amid the debris for 22 hours before soldiers found him and lifted him out of the rubble. Sonit's face was exposed during the rescue, but he was uninjured. The rescue provides hope to a country devastated by the disaster.

A Church of Scientology-backed organization, Narcocon, is facing a land use battle over plans to turn a patch of secluded land near the presidential retreat Camp David into a drug rehab center. Narcocon, a drug rehab network affiliated with the Church of Scientology, is trying to prove that the property, Trout Run, is historic enough to change its designation and build a center for twelve patients. The property, which includes stone cottages, is currently classified for resource conservation and does not permit any medical purpose. The rehabilitation program, founded in 1966, is based on the teachings of Scientology's founder L. Ron Hubbard and claims to eliminate addiction cravings through a regimen of exercise, sauna, and mega doses of the vitamin Niacin.

The article discusses the aftermath of the U.S. military withdrawal from Afghanistan, focusing on the challenges faced by expatriates and locals in Kabul. Five men who once spoke English fluently due to their work with NATO have been fired and blacklisted, leading to isolation and fear of retaliation. They sleep in market stalls and avoid traveling to see their families. The city has transformed, with neighborhoods emptying out and new residents reclaiming streets. The U.S. Embassy and NATO declined to comment.

One US Navy SEAL died and another was critically injured while training in a pool at a Virginia military base, according to a Navy spokesman. The incident occurred on Friday at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story, where the two members of the Navy's elite sea, air, land teams were found at the bottom of the pool by another service member around 3pm local time. The names of the SEALS were withheld pending notification of next of kin. Both were assigned to Naval Special Warfare Group Two, which contains SEAL teams. The sailors were swimming in lap lanes and were not wearing gear at the time. One was pronounced dead, and the second is listed in critical condition.

NBC, the broadcasting giant holding live rights to the Premier League in the United States, is set to show all Premier League matches in the country for the first time this weekend, reflecting a significant increase in US interest in English football. NBC has transported their entire production from Connecticut to England, with hosts including Rebecca Lowe, Robbie Earle, and Kyle Martino, who are also based in Los Angeles. The move aims to enhance coverage and influence American football choices, with Lowe now helping to shape the preferences of young Americans.

Ed Miliband will do "more damage to the country than he did to his brother," Boris Johnson said during a live TV debate, accusing him of potentially stabbing the country in the back by forming a deal with the SNP to gain power.

A 26-year-old prisoner in Oregon, Dustin Irons, was slapped with an extra 30 days behind bars for dropping his trousers and flashing a judge during a court hearing. The incident occurred when Irons, who was in handcuffs, became disgruntled with the proceedings and exposed himself to the judge via video-link. The judge sentenced him to an additional 30 days in jail for contempt of court. Irons, who has been in prison since December for trashing a hotel room and assaulting people inside, faces another disciplinary investigation and could be placed in a segregation unit.

Jenson Button believes McLaren has improved significantly since their slow start to the Formula One season, with both Button and Fernando Alonso discovering the car was competitive alongside other midfield runners. Although Button and Alonso retired during the race at the Sepang International Circuit, the team's progress was noted, and they are now hoping to continue improving their position in the championship. McLaren's improvement in Malaysia, compared to Australia, was attributed to the cooler temperatures, which could affect tyre performance. Button acknowledges that while the team still has a long way to go, they are making progress and are excited to be racing against other strong teams.

A hospital in Western Australia, Fiona Stanley Hospital, was found to have blood and bone fragments on supposedly sanitized medical instruments, leading to the hospital being stripped of its medical service provider Serco and fined $60,000. The hospital has been found to continue operating with poorly sanitized instruments, raising concerns about patient safety.

Becca Litchfield and Dale, a couple from Nottingham, decided to give up their dream wedding to pay for fertility treatment and IVF. After weeks of waiting, they won a wedding competition and discovered that their fertility treatment had worked. The couple, who had given up on their dream wedding, were overjoyed to welcome twins, Darci-Mai and Stanley, and found a way to say their "I do's" in a white wedding.

A family-friendly coffee shop in Omaha, Nebraska, had its Facebook page hacked and flooded with pornography after an employee clicked on a malicious link in an email. The hack lasted for 24 hours, with the page being replaced with adult cartoons similar to those posted on other brands. The company issued an apology and removed the content, but it was not until a day later that Facebook was contacted to regain control of the account.

A young Shibu Inu puppy at an American Kennel Club center in the United States was filmed barking at a young husky dog, causing laughter and confusion among onlookers. The video shows the Shibu Inu attempting to bark at the husky, which responds with a high-pitched whine. The dogs continue to vocalize at one another, and the video ends with the husky losing interest and chewing on its handler's sleeve.

Liam Plunkett, an experienced English seamer, is set to return to the West Indies batting lineup after a comeback from injury. Plunkett, who managed 18 wickets in four Tests prior to his injury, is eager to use his pace to lead England to victory in the upcoming Test series against the West Indies. He is competing for a place in the England Test side with Chris Jordan and Mark Wood, who are both familiar with the West Indies' conditions. Plunkett is determined to earn his place in the team and prove his worth by bowling well in practice and warm-up games.

Paul Smith, a boxer from Liverpool, is set to face Andre Ward in a unification fight for the WBA super-middleweight title. The bout is seen as a warm-up for Ward's rematch with Carl Froch, who is ranked among the top five pound-for-pound boxers in the world. The WBA has ordered Ward and Froch to meet in a unification fight, with Froch declaring willingness if Ward returns the compliment by traveling to the UK. Smith is the ideal opponent for Ward, and the WBA is granting the Son of God licence to Froch to shake off the ring rust in his hometown of Nottingham.

Tyrus Byrd, the first African American mayor of Parma, Missouri, was sworn in last week but faced a sudden departure of five of her six police officers and several other top officials after her election victory. The resignations were attributed to "safety concerns," with the outgoing mayor stating that the departures were not due to any harm to the town. The city has a population of 713, with 57% white and 41% black residents. The town has experienced a surge in crime, and despite a large police force, residents reported seeing few police officers on the streets. The new mayor's father, who was defeated in the election, stated that his daughter had a good relationship with the police department.

Manchester City midfielder Yaya Toure will not be forced out of the club but is set to become available this summer. The Ivorian, who has played a major role in City's recent trophy-winning period, is content with his life at the Etihad Stadium and is not in a rush to leave. However, his wages are a stumbling block towards a potential move. Inter Milan, managed by Roberto Mancini, is interested in Toure but given his huge salary, there are doubts over whether they would be able to afford it. City, meanwhile, will resist any attempt by Valencia to pull out of a £24 million deal for Alvaro Negredo to fund a move for Radamel Falcao, currently on loan at Manchester United.

A new study claims that more than two-thirds of people taking antidepressants may not actually have depression, challenging the common belief that these drugs are prescribed for clinical depression. The research, published in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, found that 69% of antidepressant users did not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder. The study, conducted by U.S. investigators, examined patients taking selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), the most commonly prescribed type of antidepressant. The researchers concluded that many individuals prescribed antidepressants may not have met the criteria for mental disorders. The study also noted a significant increase in antidepressant prescriptions since 1998, with the highest rates in countries like Iceland and Australia.

Doris Fuller, the mother of a mentally ill daughter who killed herself, has revealed how her daughter's bipolar disorder and psychosis led to her death. Fuller wrote about her daughter's life in a long article for the Washington Post, describing how her illness went undiagnosed until her early 20s and how her daughter lived with an incurable disease that filled her head with devils that eventually drove her to suicide. Fuller said her daughter was the bravest person she had ever known and that her suicide doesn't change that.

A 10-year-old boy named Koby Hodder nearly died after suffering a cardiac arrest in the school playground while playing British Bulldog, a game involving running from one side of a field to another without being caught. He was diagnosed with the same heart condition as footballer Fabrice Muamba, who had a similar cardiac arrest in 2012. Koby's heart stopped for 12 minutes, and he collapsed and lost consciousness. Teachers performed CPR until paramedics arrived, who used a defibrillator to save his life. The incident led to calls for the game to be banned, as it is considered dangerous and can lead to injuries.

Baroness Hale of Richmond, Britain's most senior female judge, has proposed reforms to divorce laws in England and Wales to remove the need for allegations of adultery and blame, aiming to reduce bitterness in matrimonial disputes. The current system requires couples to cite one of five reasons for divorce, with unreasonable behavior being the most widely used. Lady Hale suggests a one-year cooling off period after declaring that the marriage has permanently broken down, during which couples would be encouraged to resolve arrangements for children, money, and the home before obtaining a divorce. This overhaul aims to make the process more equitable and less reliant on fault-based claims.

Tottenham Hotspur is considering building a state-of-the-art stadium with a retractable pitch that could accommodate an NFL franchise. The stadium, set to be completed for the 2018-19 season, would feature a synthetic surface beneath a NFL-style pitch and could house up to 70 players. The NFL is expected to have a permanent franchise in London within five years, and teams are testing logistics for their three games at Wembley this autumn. Tottenham's new stadium, with a capacity of 65,000, is seen as more suitable for NFL requirements than Wembley's 90,000 seats. The NFL is keeping its options open, but Tottenham's proposed design could be a significant blow to the Football Association, which also sees the NFL as a lucrative partner for Wembley.

U.S. lawmakers have written to FIFA, urging the organization to remove Russia from hosting the 2018 World Cup due to its involvement in the Ukraine crisis and occupation of Crimea. The senators, including John McCain, have called for economic sanctions against Russia and the condemnation of its regime.

Universal announced the release date for the sequel to "Fifty Shades of Grey" on February 10, 2017, and February 9, 2018. The husband of the author, Erika Leonard, will write the script for the second film, while Sam Taylor-Johnson is no longer directing the sequel. The first film earned $568.8 million worldwide and stars Dakota Johnson and Jamie Dornan.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis will receive a hero's welcome upon his return to Crystal Palace, but he faces a challenging season as he struggles to avoid relegation from the Premier League. Pulis has never managed to guide a team into the top half of the league, and his current record of finishing in the bottom three is the worst of any long-serving Premier League manager. Pulis has a history of success with Stoke City and Palace, but his overall record is poor, and he is currently in danger of being relegated from the top flight.

Fenerbahce, a Turkish football club, has called for the suspension of the Turkish championship following a gun attack on their team bus during a match against Caykur Rizespor. The attack occurred on Saturday night as the bus drove to the airport after a match in Turkey's Super Lig. The injured driver, who was taken to hospital, is seeking medical attention. Fenerbahce believes the attack is not being solved in a way that satisfies the club and public opinion, leading to the call for a championship suspension. The incident followed a 5-1 win for Fenerbahce against Rizespor.

A massive snow avalanche struck Everest Base Camp on Saturday, killing at least 17 people and injuring dozens. The avalanche, which occurred during the Nepal earthquake, left hundreds of climbers stranded at higher camps, with helicopters rescuing around 200 people. The avalanche was caused by aftershocks in the Khumbu Icefall, making the route impassable.

Gregory Margolin, a 16-year-old Jewish recruit in the Soviet Red Army during World War II, found himself again in war in Ukraine. Margolin, who survived one war, was able to survive another, even as a stray missile hit his house, killing his daughter. He and his family fled to Israel, where they are now living in a refugee center set up by the International Fellowship of Christians and Jews.

John Carver, a former assistant to Ruud Gullit, is eager to take charge of Newcastle United against Sunderland on Sunday. Gullit, who managed Newcastle between 1998 and 1999, controversially decided not to start star players Duncan Ferguson and Alan Shearer in a 1999 derby match, leading to Newcastle's defeat. Carver's memories of Gullit's downfall remind him of the potential consequences of his own decisions. The match is significant for Newcastle's manager, as a positive result could aid his chances of winning the head coach position beyond the end of the season.

The Revered Al Sharpton delivered a sermon and addressed the Walter Scott situation on Sunday morning in North Charleston, South Carolina. He praised Mayor Keith Summey for firing the officer who killed Scott and called for reform in policing. Sharpton is expected to attend a vigil near the scene of the Scott shooting on Sunday afternoon. Scott, a black driver, was fatally shot by a white police officer after he fled a traffic stop.
