Brendan Rodgers will remind Raheem Sterling of his responsibilities after the Liverpool youngster hit the headlines for the wrong reasons before scoring the opener in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United. Sterling, who is unwilling to sign a new contract at Anfield, has been videoed passing out after allegedly inhaling nitrous oxide, also known as 'hippy crack', and on Sunday was pictured puffing on a shisha pipe. The 20-year-old faces a club investigation and potential disciplinary action over his behaviour, and Liverpool manager Rodgers now says he will take time to talk to his rising star about what being a professional entails.

Labour received more than £1 million in union donations between April 6 and April 12, boosting their election war chest. The donations, worth £105,420.80 a day, came from Unison, USDAW, and Unite, with Unite's donations being the largest. The union donations are seen as a blow to David Cameron and a potential wedge for Ed Miliband to gain support.

Police were called to Manchester Airport after passengers on a Qatar Airways flight became disruptive and kicked off during a delay caused by strong winds, leading to a second call for officers two hours later. The flight was diverted to Birmingham Airport, where passengers were stranded for five hours. Qatar Airways apologized for the delay, which occurred due to the aircraft's operating crew exceeding their legal flying hours.

Canadian pop sensation Justin Bieber will carry Floyd Mayweather's championship belts into the ring ahead of his $300 million mega-fight with Manny Pacquiao on Saturday. Bieber, who has been close friends with Mayweather for years, will join the fighter on stage during a recent press conference and will be asked to lead out the American's entourage at the MGM Grand. Mayweather, who has a 47-0 record on the line, is expected to be the biggest fight in history and the most lucrative, with Bieber confirming he will be part of Mayweather's entourage for the mega-fight.

Corinthian Colleges Inc., a for-profit career college, announced its intention to close all 28 of its remaining campuses, marking a significant victory in efforts to hold for-profit colleges accountable. Corinthian, which once enrolled over 70,000 students, is one of the worst "predator colleges" due to its dubious degrees, high student debt, and reliance on federal student aid. The closure comes after the U.S. Department of Education curtailed Corinthian's access to federal student aid last summer. Corinthian's aggressive recruitment tactics, including leaving 100 messages per day, have led to high student debt and default rates, with for-profit college students having worse default rates than subprime borrowers during the financial crisis. The closure of Corinthian marks a new chapter in the fight against for-profit colleges, with the Department of Education signaling a willingness to forgive loans of Corinthian graduates who have crushing debt and no job prospects.

Pep Guardiola has denied claims of a dispute with former Bayern Munich club doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit the club on Thursday after 'being blamed' for the defeat by Porto. Muller-Wohlfahrt claimed the bond of trust was damaged, but Guardiola has played down the feud. Bayern Munich lost 2-1 to Porto in the Champions League quarter-final, with Guardiola appearing to blame injuries and lack of available players. Muller-Wohlfahrt, a 72-year-old world leader in his field, quit the club after the defeat.

Wladimir Klitschko, the reigning heavyweight champion, is set to make his return to Madison Square Garden in New York for a world title defense against Bryant Jennings. Klitschko, who won Olympic gold in 1996, has been reminiscing about his rise to fame and the power of sport to change lives. Despite being just a year short of his 40th birthday, Klitschko believes age has no bearing on his ability to continue dominating the boxing world.

Jeremy Clarkson, who was fired from Top Gear in March after attacking a producer during filming, has finally spoken out about his dismissal. Clarkson, 54, said he would "miss" fronting the BBC2 show, while former presenter Angela Rippon, who first presented the show 38 years ago, said she would be keen to return to the motoring show if invited back. Lord Hall, the director-general of the BBC, announced that the corporation would not be renewing Clarkson's contract, citing his "crossing of the line."

In a bizarre incident during a La Liga match, Barcelona's Sergio Busquets was given a straight red card for throwing a lump of grass at Celta Vigo's Fabian Orellana during the closing stages of the match. The incident led to Orellana being shown the red card, and Busquets was able to grab his eye despite the turf striking him. Barcelona earned a crucial three points, while Real Madrid won 9-1 against Granada earlier in the day.

In 2013, three people died and over 200 were injured when a pair of bombs went off within 12 seconds of each other at the Boston Marathon finish line. This year, federal Judge George A. O'Toole warned jurors not to attend the Boston Marathon or any events related to the anniversary or the current running of the marathon. The jury convicted Dzhokhar Tsarnaev on all 30 charges, including using weapons of mass destruction, bombing a place of public use, conspiracy, and aiding and abetting. The sentencing phase is expected to last four weeks, with the maximum penalty for several charges being death.

Millions of Chinese people marked the Qingming Festival, a three-day holiday in China, by watching parades and traveling home. The festival, which celebrates the start of spring and outdoor celebrations, includes a grand and colourful ceremony in Huangling County, Shaanxi Province, honoring the Yellow Emperor Huangdi.

Paul Simon, 73, has returned to the top of the UK album chart with his latest release, The Ultimate Collection, which outsold more youthful musicians like Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. The album, featuring 19 tracks from Simon's 50-year career, including hits from his solo career, reached number one for the first time since 1990. Simon's recent tour with Sting is believed to have been the catalyst in helping him reach the top of the charts.

Iker Casillas, a 33-year-old Spanish goalkeeper, has stated his intention to remain at Real Madrid until the end of his contract, despite speculation that Manchester United's David de Gea may be linked with a move to the Bernabeu. Casillas, who has been at the club since breaking into the team as a 16-year-old, claims he will fight for the No. 1 jersey and earn it through hard work and dedication. Real Madrid is determined to defend their Champions League title, having reached the semi-finals with a 1-0 aggregate victory over local rivals Atletico Madrid.

Britain was hailed as a "job-creating machine" last night as employment rose to its highest level in history, with the International Monetary Fund praising Chancellor George Osborne's economic strategy. The number of people in work soared above 31 million in the three months to February, up 557,000 from a year before. Rolls-Royce announced its biggest-ever order, worth more than £6 billion, to power passenger jets for the Middle Eastern airline Emirates. David Cameron said the Conservatives had overseen a "jobs miracle" and Britain had created more jobs in the last five years than the rest of the EU put together. IMF chief Christine Lagarde and German finance minister Wolfgang Schaeuble praised Mr Osborne's "wonderful job" of handling the economy. The plan had reduced the deficit from a record £153 billion under Labour in 2009-10 to £90 billion last year.

SsangYong, a Korean automaker, is launching a new sports utility vehicle (SUV) called Tivoli in the UK, priced from £12,950. The SUV is designed to appeal to thrifty motorists by offering value for money and a European name inspired by the Italian town of Tivoli. It comes in three trim levels, with a choice of front-wheel drive or 4x4, and features a five-year unlimited mileage warranty. The Tivoli aims to double SsangYong's annual UK sales from 2,000 to 4,000 vehicles.

A chef, Sam Longhurst, created a 10-inch, half-kilogram burger at the Splendid Kitchen restaurant in Manchester, England, containing six forms of three different meats and 2,000 calories. The burger, called "The Whole Damn Farm," was inspired by a customer's disappointment with a "Cow & Chicken" burger and was designed to be a show-stopping meal. The burger features two beef patties, homemade bacon jam, ham chunks, a whole chicken thigh, barbequed pulled pork, and bacon rashers, all sandwiched between two brioche buns. The creation was met with enthusiasm from diners, who were impressed by the sheer size and variety of the meat.

Yeo Valley, a dairy company in North Somerset, has opened its staff canteen to the public, offering a gourmet menu of organic and locally sourced dishes at a subsidised price. The canteen, praised as the world's best staff canteen, features quirky light fittings and high tables and stools, and offers meals such as organic sourdough with Yeo Valley salted butter and a dessert of apple and rhubarb crumble with ice cream or creme fraiche. The canteen's menu changes daily based on the available produce.

Blues legend B.B. King was hospitalized for dehydration, but he is now much better and is back home resting with his grandchildren. King, 89, has used various models of Gibson guitars over the years, and named each one of them Lucille. He has 30 Grammy nominations and has won his first Grammy in 1970 for "The Thrill Is Gone." King suffered from dehydration and exhaustion after a show in Chicago last year, but he is now recovering and touring again.

On Easter Sunday, Manhattan's Fifth Avenue was transformed into a sea of bizarre hats as people celebrated the holiday. The event, known as the 2015 Easter Parade, featured a diverse range of headwear, including ship-shaped hats, elaborate dioramas, and floral bonnets. The parade, which has been held annually since the 1880s, drew participants from various religious backgrounds, including Christians, Jews, Hindus, agnostics, and atheists. The event was organized by the New York City Department of Parks and Recreation and was attended by thousands of people.

Emergency crews in Essex received a prank call from a woman who reported feeling ill after eating too much takeaway food, while another man reported that his feet were hurting after wearing shoes that were too tight. The East of England ambulance service revealed a list of 1,248 inappropriate call outs, with half of them attended by front-line crews, potentially putting lives at risk.

Chelsea players Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake, along with their teammates Loic Remy and Willian, participated in a football challenge organized by Audi. The challenge involved shooting balls into the boot of a car from close range and sinking them from long range into a convertible Audi. Hazard and Ake won the first round, followed by Hazard and his partner Ake winning the final round. The final challenge involved shooting at cars from long range, with Willian and Remy winning but causing damage to the Audi's wing mirrors.

Brendan Rodgers criticized Raheem Sterling's advisor, Aidy Ward, for allegedly being manipulated by outside forces, suggesting Sterling would stay at Liverpool if left to make a decision alone. Sterling rejected a contract extension worth £100,000 a week and has just two years left on his deal at the end of the season. Rodgers sat down with Sterling to discuss his future, stating Liverpool Football Club is the best place for him and that his enjoyment of playing for Liverpool and loving the opportunity to improve as a footballer outweighs the market's interest.

Rachel Riley, Countdown's co-presenter, was embarrassed on a recent episode when contestants offered up the eight-letter word "erection" as their answer to the word game. Host Nick Hewer struggled to stifle his laughter as the blushing Ms Riley spelled out the word. The incident is not the first time Hewer has struggled to contain himself when a rude word has popped up on the show.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, who attempted to buy deadly poison on the internet and was later arrested, was spared jail after pleading guilty to trying to commit suicide. The teenager, who cannot be named for legal reasons, was unaware his online requests were being tracked by covert counter-terrorism officers. He was sentenced to a 12-month referral order. The dark web, a subsection of the deep web, was used for the transaction.

Three hours after giving birth to her long-awaited baby girl, Lianne Hindle, a 37-year-old mother-of-four, died at the scandal-hit North Manchester General Hospital in December. The death occurred just months after three babies and one mother died at the same maternity unit. The deaths prompted an investigation, and Lianne's partner, Chris Barnes, has called for action to prevent further tragedies at the hospital.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman, a seven-year-old mother of a little girl named Emily, gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Emily, just days after a video surfaced of the athlete training while eight months pregnant. Pittman, who plans to compete in both the Beijing World Championships and the 2016 Rio Olympics, continued to train while pregnant with her son Cornelis, who was born seven months after his mother's first child. The athlete's coach, Mike Hurst, said that Pittman trained every second day and was careful to monitor her core temperature throughout her training program. The new addition to Pittman's family is the result of an IVF donor, and she is currently four months pregnant with her second child.

A powerful storm capsized several sailboats participating in a regatta in Alabama, resulting in at least one death and missing persons. The storm rolled through the area around 4 p.m. and a man was plucked from the waters by the Coast Guard around 9 p.m. The storm caused significant damage to the boats and resulted in scattered boats across Mobile Bay. At least one person was confirmed dead, but the cause of death is unknown.

Roseanne Barr, 62, has revealed she is going blind due to macular degeneration and glaucoma, two eye diseases that get progressively worse over time and can steal vision. Her doctors haven't provided a timeline, but her symptoms are worsening. Macular degeneration is a breakdown of the part of the retina that allows us to see fine details in the center of vision, while glaucoma damages the nerve that connects the retina to the brain, often caused by fluid build-up and pressure in the eyes. The American Academy of Ophthalmology recommends getting a baseline eye exam when you turn 40, and certain people, especially African Americans, are at higher risk in their 40s. There is no cure for either disease, but treatments can delay the progression of early-stage glaucoma and halt further vision loss in advanced cases of macular degeneration.

A 17-year-old Oklahoma teenager, Chancey Luna, was convicted of first-degree murder in the 2013 shooting death of Australian college baseball player Christopher Lane, who was killed while jogging in Duncan. Luna was found guilty of the crime after a jury recommended a life sentence without parole. Luna's defense attorney argued that he meant to scare Lane but was unaware he was shooting at him. The case highlights the complexities of teenage criminal behavior and the challenges of holding young offenders accountable.

Arsene Wenger insists his record of 12 losses against Jose Mourinho will not affect Arsenal's match against Chelsea at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday. Wenger has drawn five and lost seven of their 12 encounters. Chelsea's strengths include efficient counter-attacks and set-pieces, while Arsenal's recent form and belief are highlighted. Wenger emphasizes the importance of the game's outcome rather than the managers' relationship.

Manny Pacquiao, a Filipino boxer, has become one of the most recognizable figures in sports after a series of major fights, including a bout against Floyd Mayweather, which is scheduled for Saturday night at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. Pacquiao, who was born into poverty in the Philippines, spent his early career fighting in the Far East before gaining recognition in 2001 when he fought against Lehlo Ledwaba in an IBF world super-bantamweight title fight in Las Vegas. He has since become a global superstar, facing some of the biggest fighters in the world, including Mayweather, who is set to face Pacquiao in the Fight of the Century on Saturday night.

A talented young footballer, Jack Grealish, has been photographed inhaling nitrous oxide, a drug that is considered illegal but still used by some athletes. Grealish, who played for Aston Villa in their FA Cup semi-final against Liverpool, has become the third top-flight starlet to be caught using the substance. Grealish's performance against Liverpool was impressive, but he has not yet achieved the level of success he needs to maintain his status as a top athlete. Wenger, the manager of Arsenal, has emphasized the importance of athletes taking care of their bodies and avoiding substances that can slow down their performance.

Sam Barton, a 22-year-old man who underwent £55,000 in cosmetic surgery to resemble reality star Joey Essex, was attacked by a group of men on Easter Monday in Sutton Coldfield, West Midlands. The attack, which included pelted with eggs, followed online abuse and forced Barton to move house. The incident highlights the financial and emotional toll of pursuing a celebrity lifestyle, with Barton admitting to racking up debts of £100,000 on his champagne lifestyle.

An Indiana university was in lockdown late on Friday night after a "likely prank call" about an armed person near the main administration building. Police received a phone call from someone saying that they had stabbed their roommate at the university, was armed with a shotgun and threatening to blow up the administration building. Manchester University had issued a statement advising students to shelter in place. The university had continued reposting the shelter in place warning for hours after the original message and had not given the all clear as of 2am. No injuries have been confirmed.

Edinson Cavani, known as "El Matador," will face Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals, with the spotlight on him as PSG struggle to progress beyond the last eight despite key suspensions and injuries. Cavani, known for his prolific goals, has endured a goal drought and has faced criticism for his behavior, leading to speculation about his future in Paris.

Derry Mathews has won the interim WBA lightweight title after defeating Tony Luis in a close fight. Mathews, who was previously stripped of the belt, won the fight with a unanimous points decision of 114-112, 114-112, 115-112. The fight was notable for Luis being drafted in at the last minute and Mathews being handed a tight decision after a thrilling encounter.

Hull FC defeated St Helens 28-20 in a surprise victory, overcoming a 12-10 halftime deficit. Hull's Jamie Shaul scored the winning try, while St Helens' Jordan Turner scored a try and Tom Makinson added the conversion. The win was Hull's first since a derby loss to Hull KR on Thursday.

The United States' undocumented and documented immigrant population is projected to reach a record high of 51 million by 2023, with undocumented immigrants expected to account for 14.8% of the population. By 2060, the immigrant population could reach 78 million, representing 82% of the total population. The Center for Immigration Studies predicts that immigration will steadily increase over the next 45 years, with net immigration totaling 64 million. Without changes to current immigration policy, the immigrant population could reach 14.8% of the population by 2023, and 15.8% by 2030, 17.1% by 2040, and 18.8% by 2060. This growth has implications for workers, schools, infrastructure, congestion, and the environment.

Jack Wilshere made his long-awaited return from injury to captain Arsenal Under 21s, but the team lost 1-0 to Reading's youngsters at the Emirates Stadium. Wilshere was joined by other injured first team players, including Serge Gnabry and Abou Diaby, who managed to last 56 minutes. The Royals scored the winning goal in the opening minutes, and Martin Keown's son Niall scored the winner for Reading. Wilshere will hope to return to the first team for the season run-in and FA Cup semi-final.

Justin Rose, a 34-year-old English golfer, has fallen outside the world's top 10 after a bruising Florida swing that saw him miss three cuts and finish 55th at the Cadillac Championship. Rose, who has been a fixture in the top five for the last three years, has spent the past two weeks on the practice ground to improve his game. The Shell Houston Open saw Rose hit 17 out of 18 greens in regulation and finish with a 69, showing a welcome return to his previous form. Rose believes he has corrected the faults in his game and is going in the right direction again. Phil Mickelson, another golfer, has enjoyed his best round in months with a 66 on Thursday. Rose is focused on his game and hopes to avoid any slippage in the rankings.

A Mayfair mansion, once a milking parlour, has gone on the market for £25 million. The property, which now features modern amenities like an indoor swimming pool and a cinema room, was originally a depot before being demolished in the 19th century. The mansion, which is 8, 139 square feet, is being sold by estate agents Wetherell and Knight Frank.

Bayern Munich, chasing three titles this season, are without key players Arjen Robben, Franck Ribery, Bastian Schweinsteiger, and David Alaba for their Champions League quarter-final match against Porto. Despite the injuries, Bayern Munich's sense of unity is stronger, and Thomas Muller believes it will help them against Porto. Bayern Munich will rely heavily on the scoring prowess of Muller and Robert Lewandowski, who are expected to score goals despite the absence of Robben and Ribery. The team is confident and aims to become the first team to beat Porto in the Champions League this season.

Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton visited Mercedes' Brackley base to collaborate on a winning strategy for the upcoming Chinese Grand Prix. Sebastian Vettel's victory at the Malaysian Grand Prix, despite Mercedes' best efforts, led to concerns about the team's dominance in the upcoming season. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff admitted that the team was surprised by Vettel's victory and acknowledged that the team's aggressive set-up pushed them into a three-stop strategy, which was not as effective as Ferrari's. The race outcome highlighted the challenges faced by Mercedes in adapting to Ferrari's tactics in high-temperature conditions.

Oklahoma Governor Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to perform executions with nitrogen gas if lethal injection is ruled unconstitutional or unavailable. The bill, signed on Friday, states that the person will become unconscious within eight to 10 seconds and die a few minutes later from lack of oxygen. This follows a review by the U.S. Supreme Court of Oklahoma's use of lethal injections, which has been put on hold. Fallin reaffirmed her support for the death penalty, stating that Oklahoma executes murderers whose crimes are especially heinous.

Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice in Swansea's 3-1 win over Hull on Saturday, earning a Game Index score of 52.9 this week. The French striker, who made a slow start to his career in south Wales, has scored four goals in his last six Premier League games. Gomis tops this week's EA Sports' Performance Index, which measures a player's contribution to the success of his team.

A massive freezer trawler sank in the Sea of Okhotsk off the coast of Russia, killing at least 56 crew members and sinking in just 15 minutes. The ship, carrying 132 crew members, was unstable due to empty fuel tanks and a lack of ballast. A massive rescue operation involving more than 1,300 people is underway, with 63 survivors rescued so far. The sinking occurred when a fishing net weighing 80 tons was pulled in, and the ship tipped over. The incident happened at around 4am local time, and the trawler did not send any distress signals before it sank. The Russian Emergencies Ministry sent an Mi-8 helicopter to treat and transport rescued crew members to hospitals.

A pioneering drug originally intended for women with breast cancer, olaparib, has shown promise in clinical trials for men with advanced prostate cancer. The drug, known as Lynparza, has been found to delay the progression of the disease in up to 30% of men with prostate cancer that has genetic defects. The study, led by researchers at the Institute of Cancer Research and the Royal Marsden hospital, found that 16 out of 49 men with advanced prostate cancer responded to the drug, with lower tumour cell counts in the blood and improved responses in medical scans. This suggests that men with detectable DNA repair mutations may benefit from the drug, which could be identified through genomic testing. Olaparib is the first cancer drug to target inherited genetic mutations and is one of the first of a new class of drugs called PARP inhibitors. The drug has been granted approval for use in ovarian cancer by the European Commission and the US Food and Drug Administration.

Travel photographer Rhiannon Taylor, 29, from Australia, has turned her passion for photography and globetrotting into a successful business by launching the website "In Bed With" to review and photograph the best hotels, beds, pools, and room service around the world. With more than 12,000 followers on Instagram, Taylor has built relationships with hotels and PR companies, allowing her to stay at exclusive resorts and feature their properties on her site. The website's name, "In Bed With," is a play on her Instagram handle, and the concept is unique, as it focuses on luxurious accommodations rather than travel experiences. Taylor has photographed properties in countries such as Indonesia, the US, and Mexico, and has received payments from hotels and companies for featuring their products on her site.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was mauled to death by two adult hippos in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park in eastern South Africa. The calf's mother watched in horror as the hippo was flung into the air before being dragged along the surface of the water. The two male hippos had been fighting for some time and the mother of the calf stayed with her herd, possibly believing it safer to stay out of harm's way herself. The baby stood no chance against the two adults as they brawled in the muddy waters of the nature reserve.

The Football Association will contact QPR and Chelsea after an incident where Branislav Ivanovic was struck on the head by a cigarette lighter thrown from a section of home supporters at Loftus Road during a Chelsea victory. The incident occurred during Chelsea celebrations, and the FA will seek observations from each club, ensuring QPR and the police take necessary steps to identify the culprit via CCTV and face a banning order. QPR is reviewing CCTV footage and appealing to witnesses. Chelsea duo Nemanja Matic and Branislav Ivanovic were targeted by objects thrown from the crowd.

A young mother and her three children were found murdered in their home in Tisdale, Saskatchewan. LaTasha Gosling, 27, and her two daughters, Janyaa, 4, and Jenika, 8, and her son Landen, 7, were discovered early Wednesday. The suspect in the case was found dead hours later, and while police did not say how he died, they did not rule out homicide. The suspect had a six-month-old baby with him who was unharmed. The Goslings' family is raising money for their funeral services and has started a GoFundMe page.

Emily Thornberry, a senior Labour politician, was forced to resign from the shadow cabinet after tweeting a photo of a house covered in England flags and with a white van outside, which was seen as hypocrisy in the context of her opposition to the right to buy policy. The incident highlighted Thornberry's ownership of expensive properties, including a £3 million home in north London, which she had bought from a housing association property worth nearly £1 million.

Mike Lane, a 40-year-old huntsman, was beaten by protesters armed with iron bars during an artificial scent chase in Everleigh, Wiltshire, three months after the incident. Despite evidence pointing to the identity of the attacker, Wiltshire Police dropped the investigation, leading Lane to condemn the decision as "pathetic." The attack left Lane with concussion, broken teeth, and memory loss, and he expressed disappointment in the lack of action by the police.

Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes, 21, has stated his intention to remain at the club this summer, insisting he is happy with his performance and prefers to stay in Spain. Gomes has been linked with Premier League clubs Manchester United and Chelsea, but he denies any interest from the latter. Valencia has been performing well in La Liga, with Gomes scoring four goals in 25 appearances.

An Australian teenager, Audrey Pekin, was raped twice on Christmas Eve in Bali while holidaying with her family. The attacker, Henry Alafu, lured her to his remote home and then assaulted her in a taxi as she tried to flee. The Indonesian police failed to arrest Alafu, who is from Nigeria. The incident has sparked outrage in Australia and Indonesia, with the family of the victim calling for justice.

Animal rights activist Ashley James has teamed up with PETA to launch an anti-fur campaign against Harvey Nichols, a department store that previously abandoned its fur-free policy. James, who is known for her vegan lifestyle, poses with a fake fox image on Harvey Nichols' billboards, highlighting the cruelty of the fur industry. Harvey Nichols has previously re-introduced its fur-free policy, but PETA is seeking to mount a new campaign to raise awareness about the industry.

Chile has joined several South American neighbors in recognizing civil unions between people of the same sex, with President Michelle Bachelet enacting a new law on Monday. The new law will take effect in six months and will give legal weight to cohabiting relationships between two people of the same sex and between a man and a woman. The law is intended to end discrimination faced by common-law couples and gives them greater rights in the realms of property, health care, pensions, and inheritance.

Chelsea are on track to become the most dominant title-winners in Premier League history, having led the table for 230 days as of April 10, 2023. This would surpass Manchester United's record of 262 days from the 1993-94 season. Chelsea's current lead of seven points with a game in hand makes them the favorites to win the title. Their next three games against QPR, Manchester United, and Arsenal could be crucial in determining their final position.

Cape Verde, a small Portuguese former colony with a population of 500,000, is tapping into its rich musical heritage to boost its economy. The country, which lacks natural resources, is promoting music and culture as a key sector for growth. The Kriol Jazz Festival, which has been held in Cape Verde for seven years, has attracted international artists and has become a major event in the country. The festival has helped to showcase Cape Verde's unique musical styles and has brought people from all over the world to share in the music.

An old hoax video showing a wave rider surfing in front of the Sydney Opera House went viral again after being reposted by popular Sydney radio duo Fitzy and Wippa on Twitter. The video, originally posted by Sydney resident Darren Johnson in June 2012, was quickly debunked by wave experts and YouTube commenters, who pointed out inaccuracies such as the appearance of rocks around the Opera House and the cardboard-like appearance of the man in the final shot. The video was uploaded to Twitter on Tuesday morning and quickly gained traction, with some users referencing the heavy storms that had hit Sydney the previous night as the trigger for the strange phenomenon.

Reading, the FA Cup semi-finalists, were defeated 1-0 by Birmingham in a Sky Bet Championship game at the Madejski Stadium. Clayton Donaldson scored the winning goal in the 78th minute. Reading's Adam Federici, who had fumbled a crucial clearance against Arsenal, was retained for the match. Birmingham, who were already relegated, managed to secure a point.

David Luiz, a key player for Paris Saint-Germain (PSG), has been ruled out of the Champions League quarter-final against Barcelona due to a hamstring injury sustained during a match against Marseille. The 27-year-old Brazilian defender will miss at least four weeks, potentially impacting PSG's title defense and their upcoming match against Barcelona. Luiz's absence could force PSG to play eight matches without him.

The return of Game of Thrones has led to a significant increase in internet piracy, with more than 100,000 illegal downloads per day reported by anti-piracy firm Irdeto. The unauthorized downloads of Game of Thrones episodes, which spanned February to April, saw a 45% year-on-year increase, with Brazil and France being the top countries for illegal downloads. The unauthorized downloads of Game of Thrones episodes, which spanned February to April, saw a 45% year-on-year increase, with Brazil and France being the top countries for illegal downloads. HBO has announced that the forthcoming season will air across 170 countries at the same time, and has launched a new internet streaming service, HBO Now, in an attempt to curb piracy and recapture revenue.

Leicester City will host West Ham United in a Premier League match on Saturday. Leicester's Matt Upson is out with an Achilles injury, while West Ham's Winston Reid is back from injury. Leicester has won just one of their last 10 home matches, while West Ham has won their last seven away games against the Foxes.

For residents of Celoron, New York, a statue of Lucille Ball, the town's most famous resident, has become a source of controversy. The statue, based on a moment from Ball's show "I Love Lucy," depicts her intoxicated and unflattering face, leading to a Facebook page called "We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue" with over 600 likes. The anonymous creator, a fan of Ball, argues that the statue should be more like the statues of other comedians he admires, such as Nick at Nite's "Bewitched" and "The Honeymooners" statues and Bob Newhart. The statue, which costs an estimated $8,000 to $10,000 to recast, has been criticized for not doing justice to Ball's beauty and sense of humor.

A 43-year-old woman named Sharon Smith, who was overweight and struggled to fit into a plane seat during a 11-hour flight, lost nearly half her body weight after deciding to take up running. She joined a slimming club and started running, which helped her shed 4st. After quitting her job and working from home, she was able to exercise more and stand for the entire flight, which helped her lose another 4.5 stone. Smith's weight loss began just under two years ago when she joined Weight Watchers Online, but she did not weigh herself immediately.

A new mother, Nicola Bonn, started a blog called Upfront Mama to share her experiences of raising her 14-month-old daughter Poppy and the challenges she faced. Her candid account of bringing up a baby for the first time went viral, and she decided to stop justifying herself and apologizing for her decisions. The main hurdle she faced was the overwhelming amount of opinions and judgments from others, which can be overwhelming for a new mother.

Two teenage boys, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, from Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, are feared to have traveled to Syria to join ISIS. Hassan is believed to be related to Hammaad Munshi, who was arrested at 15 for planning to murder non-Muslims. The families are in shock and worry about their safety. The boys, who were on a school trip, boarded a Thomas Cook flight from Manchester to Dalaman, Turkey, on March 31. British authorities fear they have managed to escape.

Stephanie Scott, a beloved school teacher from Leeton, was brutally murdered just days before her much-anticipated wedding. Her father, Robert, described her as bubbly and thoughtful, and her mother and sister expressed their grief over her loss. The wedding was to be held at the picturesque Eat Your Greens venue, decorated with yellow balloons and flowers, but the family must now prepare for Stephanie's funeral instead.

Southampton is interested in signing Tonny Vilhena, a 20-year-old winger from Feyenoord, who wants to leave the club this summer. Koeman, the Southampton manager, is keen to bring Vilhena to the club, and the team is also monitoring their teammate Jordy Clasie, who has won 11 senior caps for Holland. Koeman is also looking to make Eljero Elia's loan move from Werder Bremen permanent to strengthen his squad ahead of possible European qualification.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture with beanbags in the library of Ickworth House, Suffolk, in an experiment designed to encourage visitors to "dwell and take in the atmosphere." This move was met with outrage from heritage experts who called it "misguided." The Trust has since announced similar experiments at nine other venues around the country. Art historian Bendor Grosvenor criticized the move as "patronizing nonsense," arguing that it is better to take away objects people might want to see rather than bring in new audiences. The National Trust's director of strategy, curatorship, and external affairs, Simon Murray, defended the experiment, stating that each house is different and treated appropriately, and that the beanbag seating was a short-term arrangement.

Former Australian Prime Minister John Howard was photographed standing on the side of the road with a flat tyre, but was helped by his driver to change it. Felicity Waterford, a mother waiting for her daughter at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music, noticed the flat tyre and offered assistance. Howard, who was a complete gentleman, agreed to a selfie with Waterford. This incident came weeks after Liberal MP Christopher Pyne was challenged to change a tyre on national television after boasting he was a 'fixer'.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has admitted that midfielder Joey Barton "probably had a point" about the team's performance during a 2-1 defeat to Queens Park Rangers earlier this season. Pulis, who has instilled a solid core of players at West Brom, believes Barton's criticism of the team's finishing was justified, as the club was 2-0 up but lost 3-2. Pulis also recalled his own experience of being 2-0 up but losing in a play-off final in 1999, emphasizing that West Brom's recent performances have been good. The match between West Brom and QPR is scheduled for Saturday.

A new species of monkey, the Bouvier's red colobus monkey, has been discovered in the remote rain forests of the Democratic Republic of Congo. The primate, which was thought to have been extinct for over 50 years, was first captured on camera by researchers in Ntokou-Pikounda National Park. The discovery proves that the species is not extinct and is the first ever photograph of the monkey. Researchers hope to study the monkey to learn more about it and understand its behavior. The new species, Macaca leucogenys, was officially named after the pale whiskers on its chin and the side of its face. The discovery was made after scientists set up camera traps in the remote highland forests of south-east Tibet, where the white-cheeked macaque was also discovered. The new species is vulnerable to hunters involved in the commercial bushmeat trade in the area.

Kim Kardashian and her family, including her husband Kanye West and daughter North, visited Armenia for an eight-day stay, primarily to explore the country and its cultural landmarks. The visit was a rock star welcome, and they stayed at the Armenia Marriott Hotel Yerevan, which is located on Republic Square. The city is known for its Opera House, which is a must-visit place, and its cultural, economic, and political significance. The Kardashian-West crew had the assistance of bodyguards and police to ensure their safety.

A British couple, Patrick and Valerie Jubb, are facing legal battles with the local town hall over a luxury bed and breakfast they once operated in southern Spain. The couple, who purchased the property in 2008, are attempting to sell it but are now facing the possibility of losing it due to illegal alterations made by a previous owner. The couple, who are retired and want to return to the UK, are in a difficult situation as their money is tied up in the property.

Apple reported strong sales of its iPhone in the first quarter of 2015, with more than 61 million units sold, accounting for over two-thirds of its $58 billion in revenue and $13.6 billion in profit. The company's iPad revenue fell 29% to $5.4 billion, while Mac computer revenue rose 2% to $5.6 billion. The iPhone's sales growth in China was particularly notable, with a 72% increase over the previous quarter. Analysts estimate that about 2 million Apple Watches have been sold, with early demand considered healthy but not yet a blockbuster. The iPhone's market share in the global smartphone market has been challenged by Samsung, with Apple vying for the top position.

A 3-year-old girl named Elisa, whose mother Natali Castellanos-Tyler died in a car crash, has been having disturbing nightmares and daytime visions about a white van. Her father, Craig Tyler, believes the van may be connected to the crash. The van, which is described as plain white and box-shaped, has been linked to three hit-and-run incidents in the area.

Researchers at New York University have discovered that the brain can remember 'neutral' or boring events more easily when they are tied to an emotion. This finding suggests that the brain has the remarkable ability to store information that seems inconsequential at the time in case it becomes useful later on. The study focused on how the brain stores memories for emotionally neutral events, such as neutral events like a lunch date, and how emotion affects memory retention.

Jahnae Jackson, the girlfriend of a teenager with a life-threatening brain tumour, has raised over $80,000 for his life-saving surgery to be performed by renowned neurosurgeon Dr. Charlie Teo. The 18-year-old has put her psychology studies on hold to care for her boyfriend, who is paralysed and unable to dress himself due to the tumour. The surgery is expected to save his life, but he will need rehabilitation for some time. The community in the small town of Casino, NSW, has shown overwhelming support for the couple, raising more than the initial goal.

Nedum Onuoha, a QPR centre-back with 15 months left on his contract, is being targeted by Hull City, Everton, and West Ham United, among other clubs. Onuoha played for QPR under Chris Ramsey and has been a regular starter for the club. The article also mentions other players and clubs interested in Onuoha, including Stoke's interest in Catania defender Nicolas Spolli and West Bromwich Albion's striker Victor Anichebe, who is likely to be sold this summer.

Researchers at Yale University have discovered regional variations in English sentence structure across the United States, with some states using unique phrases that are unfamiliar to others. The study, which involved nationwide surveys using an online crowdsourcing platform, found that people in the South are more likely to use presentative sentences like "Here's you a water bottle," while those in the North are less likely to use such phrases. The researchers, led by professor Larry Horn, are now creating a comprehensive guide to these regional sentence structures.

A Canadian man named Kalman Kallai took a rocking chair on a 9-day journey across Canada, from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia, to enjoy the scenery. He used an online advertisement site to find a free rocking chair and attached it to a trailer. The video shows him sitting in the chair, posing, and making gestures, including mimicking planes and waving at cows. The trip was a bonding experience for Kallai and his dad, and they met up with each other in Manitoba.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood revealed a "win bonus" of sweets and chocolate to six-year-old fan Charlie Pye, who applied for the club's hotseat after Paul Lambert's departure. Sherwood joked that Pye's win bonus would be sweets and chocolate, and revealed a Twix multi-pack under the desk.

Kell Brook, a world boxing champion, enjoyed a night out at the Premier League Darts in his home town of Sheffield. Dave Chisnall, who won both of his games in week 10, moved onto 17 points in second place. Chisnall said it was a confidence boost to beat the world champion and that he felt good up on stage. Chisnall is second in the Premier League table behind Michael van Gerwen, who snatched a 7-5 victory against Stephen Bunting. Raymond van Barneveld beat Phil Taylor 7-2 to inflict Taylor's fourth defeat in five.

Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Marco Verratti has praised Zlatan Ibrahimovic for his essential role in the club, emphasizing his off-pitch contributions. Ibrahimovic, who has scored 17 goals for the team this season, is unavailable for the Champions League quarter-final second leg against Barcelona due to suspension.

The Ministry of Defence accidentally published a secret RAF aerodrome manual containing vital GPS coordinates and runway depth information on their website, which could be used by Argentina to prepare an invasion of the Falkland Islands. The information was accidentally uploaded to a public section of the MoD's website and could have been downloaded by Argentine intelligence agents. The RAF operates from Mount Pleasant aerodrome on West Falkland, defended by modern Eurofighter Typhoon aircraft and supported by a refueling tanker. The MoD has disabled the link to the manual, but the information could still be accessed by unauthorized parties.

Paul Anderson, Huddersfield's coach, aims to revive his team's offensive performance as they prepare to face Catalans Dragons, who boast the league's best defensive record. The Giants have fallen to ninth place after losing all three games over the Easter period, while Widnes are the only team without a win away from home. Anderson attributes the team's struggles to an offensive issue and acknowledges the importance of finding their offensive rhythm.

Planners in Windsor have allowed two Costa coffee shops to open less than 500 yards apart, creating a situation where there will be three Costa stores within a mile of each other. This development has sparked controversy among residents, with some expressing concerns about the proliferation of fast food and coffee shops in the area.

The British Veterinary Association (BVA) has withdrawn its support for the controversial shooting of free-running badgers in two four-year pilot culls in Somerset and Gloucestershire, stating that controlled trapping and shooting is more humane and effective. The BVA concluded that the first two years of culling did not demonstrate conclusively that controlled shooting could be effective and humane. The Environment Secretary has promised to roll out more culls across the country if the Conservatives win the election, with the Government's strategy including cattle movement controls, vaccination in 'edge' areas, and culling where the disease is rife.

Geoff Barrow, the founder of Portishead, has accused streaming services of underpaying his band for their music, stating that he received just £1,700 in royalties despite 34 million plays. Barrow argues that younger artists are getting a poor deal, with all their rights sold away by major labels. This has led to a row between artists, music labels, and streaming companies, with Jay-Z launching Tidal, a service offering artists a better deal.

Game of Thrones fans who did not want to wait for the show's fifth season premiere leaked the first four episodes online, sparking concerns about spoilers. The episodes, titled "The Wars to Come," "The House of Black and White," "High Sparrow," and "The Sons of the Harpy," have been downloaded more than 550,000 times, making Game of Thrones the most illegally downloaded program in the world. HBO is investigating the leak, and the series is now available for streaming on HBO Now.

A 25-year-old singer named Daniel Buccheri composed an emotional song for his brother's wedding, which he performed as his best man's speech. The unique speech, which included tributes to his brother and his bride, was viewed over 100,000 times online. The speech documented Daniel's brother Adrian's love for his new wife Sarah, who he met on the internet. The speech was performed at a wedding in Melbourne, Australia, and was a touching tribute to the brother and his love.

Zara Phillips, the Queen's granddaughter, has revealed her fitness routine after giving birth to her daughter Mia. She started hitting the exercise bike every morning before her daughter woke up, aiming to regain her fitness after pregnancy. Phillips, who is vying for a place on Team GB at the Rio Olympics, is committed to a strict exercise and diet regime to get back in shape.

Raheem Sterling's interview, in which he said he was not ready to sign a new contract at Liverpool, has caused a stir among fans and the club. The interview was seen as ill-timed and did not go well, potentially changing the way fans feel about him. Sterling returned to training after the international break and shook hands with manager Brendan Rodgers. Many fans believe he has the potential to be worth more than the £100,000-a-week contract he turned down, but he is currently in the top five best young players in the world. Sterling has been linked with a move to Arsenal, and while Liverpool fans have a mantra that no player is bigger than the club, they are now of the belief that if he wants to go, he is welcome to.

In 1996, Barcelona's 1996-97 Spanish Super Cup-winning team included current PSG coach Laurent Blanc, current Porto coach Julen Lopetegui, and four of the current Champions League managers from the same club at the same time. The team featured Luis Enrique, Jose Mourinho, Pep Guardiola, and Albert Ferrer, who later became Cordoba coach.

Former Manchester United legend Eric Cantona has declared Paris Saint-Germain forward Javier Pastore as the best player in the world, challenging the opinions of Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. Cantona's assessment is based on his observation of Pastore's passing skills and creativity, which he believes surpasses that of Messi and Ronaldo. Pastore has been a key player for PSG this season, scoring three goals and providing five assists. Cantona's comments have sparked debate, with some suggesting that Spain's World Cup victory in 2010 was due to Barcelona's influence on the national team.

Lorenzo Simon, 34, was found guilty of murder for killing his tenant Michael Spalding, 39, and dismembering his body before dumping the parts into a canal. Simon, with the help of his girlfriend Michelle Bird, 35, threw the suitcases containing the body parts into the canal. The case was heard at Birmingham Crown Court, and Bird was cleared of murder and manslaughter but admitted assisting an offender. The trial lasted four weeks, and the jury took 15 hours to reach a unanimous verdict.

Local councils in Essex and Gloucestershire have created "loneliness maps" to identify areas where elderly and socially isolated residents are most vulnerable. The maps are based on factors such as age, living alone, mental health issues, lack of transportation, and low income. The maps are used to target these "danger zones" and provide support to those in need. The Campaign to End Loneliness recommends the use of these maps across the country as a way to treat the problem of loneliness.

Dedicated waitress Judy Eddingfield, 65, celebrated her 50th anniversary at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, the only job she has ever had or ever wanted. She has been working there since 1965, when she was 15 years old, and has been trained by her mother, who had been working at the establishment for 13 years. Eddingfield remembers when she spilled a shake all over a woman's fur coat and thought she would be fired, but it was forgiven after the coat was cleaned. She has been married to her first husband, Jerry Mathers, for 18 months after meeting him at Winstead's. Eddingfield's favorite memory is when Jerry Mathers and Tony Dow of the television series 'Leave It to Beaver' came to eat there in the late 1970s.

Former England captain Mike Gatting believes Kevin Pietersen should not return to the international set-up immediately, even if he scores runs for Surrey. Gatting suggests that if Gary Ballance, Ian Bell, and Joe Root play well, Pietersen might not have a place in the team. Gatting also criticizes England captain Alastair Cook for his poor performances in the recent Test series against West Indies, which has led to questions about his future in the team.

A 17-year-old college student named Caleb Benn developed an app called "Uploader for Instagram" that allows users to upload photos directly from their computer to the popular photo-sharing platform. The app, which is priced at $4.99, has been generating revenue for Benn, who is now making $1,000 a day from it. However, Instagram has filed a lawsuit against Benn, claiming that his app violated the company's terms of service. Benn has responded by saying that he was aware of the legal gray area and suspected that Facebook would find out about it. The app, called Layout, allows users to create collages of up to nine images and 11 combinations, and it has four main features: Faces, Mirroring, Photo Booth, and Previews.

Korean drinking culture, known as "hoe sik," is a significant aspect of Korean social life, involving multiple rounds of alcohol consumption at various venues. Foreign business travelers often find themselves pressured to participate, as drinking etiquette is a crucial part of the culture. Koreans view drinking as a way to get to know someone better and as a way to show respect. The article discusses the importance of following certain rules to avoid offending someone, such as identifying the "higher" person in the relationship and not having an empty glass.

The Duke of Kent, 79, was admitted to Aberdeen Royal Infirmary after suffering a dislocated hip during an Easter trip to Balmoral, the Queen's private residence in Royal Deeside, Aberdeenshire. He was successfully treated and discharged today, with his daughter driving him away. The Duke, who became the Duke of Kent at age six, is the son of Prince George and is best known for his royal duties and involvement with Freemasonry.

Meter Maids, a 50-year-old tradition of Surfers Paradise, Queensland, have been called into question by local business owners who believe the outdated and controversial practice of young women dressed in gold bikinis walking the main tourist strip and placing money into expired meters is no longer relevant due to advancements in parking meter technology. The Gold Coast Chamber of Commerce president, Peter Yared, argues that Meter Maids are now a business violating anti-touting laws and no longer perform a public service. However, Surfers Paradise Meter Maids general manager, Michael Yarwood, counters that tourists love and embrace the practice, which he claims is quintessentially part of the Gold Coast and Surfers Paradise experience.

Greece has denied it will miss a repayment of £330 million to the International Monetary Fund, claiming it will make the payment on time. Deputy finance minister Dimitris Mardas stated that Greece will in fact pay on April 9. Greece has drawn up plans to introduce a parallel drachma currency to pay domestic bills, but this has been denied by the government. The country is due to repay a £330 million loan to the International Monetary Fund on April 9, but there were concerns it would default on the payment. Greece has not received bailout funds since August last year and has resorted to measures such as borrowing from state entities via repo transactions to tide it through the cash crunch.

Turkey has blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after refusing to remove pictures of a prosecutor held during an armed siege last week, citing the images as "deeply upset" the prosecutor's wife and children. The prosecutor, Mehmet Selim Kiraz, died in hospital after being taken hostage by the Revolutionary People's Liberation Party-Front. The government imposed the blocks due to the images being shared on social media and "deeply upset" the family.

A young Star Wars fan named Colin Gilpatric wrote a heartfelt letter to George Lucas, the creator of the franchise, asking if Jedi Knights could marry. Lucasfilm responded positively, stating that marriage would not lead to the dark side and that it would be a good path for a Jedi. Colin was overjoyed to receive the letter and was able to receive a package of Star Wars merchandise.

Wisconsin defeated Kentucky in the NCAA Tournament semi-finals, ending Kentucky's unbeaten streak and advancing to the Final Four. Frank Kaminsky scored 20 points and 11 rebounds for Wisconsin, while Kentucky's 38-1 record was ended. The game was played at the Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, and Wisconsin will face Duke in the final.

Vince Neil, a member of the rock band Mötley Crüe, was criticized for his rendition of the American national anthem during a football game in Las Vegas. His performance was deemed disrespectful by many, and he was compared to other famous singers who have also been criticized for their performances of the anthem.

A video of a devastating moment in which a man, Barry Lyttle, caused his brother, Patrick, to suffer a severe head injury with a single punch has been released for the first time. The incident occurred during a sentence hearing in Sydney, Australia, where Barry was charged with grievous bodily harm. Magistrate Graeme Curran suggested a jail sentence, but the brother called for the charges to be dropped. The brothers, who had only been reunited for a holiday in Australia, had a heated argument at a bar, and Barry's punch caused Patrick to fall to the ground, resulting in his head snapping back and body crumpling. Patrick was treated by paramedics at the scene and was found in a pool of blood and vomit. The case is expected to return to court for a possible sentencing hearing.

The family of conjoined twin sisters Faith and Hope Howie, who died 19 days after birth, were devastated to find their gravesite cleared of mementos and tossed in the rubbish by cemetery staff. The Howies had built a small shrine at the site, which was stripped away without warning. The twins were buried in a pink coffin at Pinegrove Memorial Park in Sydney, and their family and friends had maintained the site, retrieving about 25% of their memorabilia. The incident highlights the challenges faced by families of critically ill children and the need for better communication and care coordination in hospitals and cemeteries.

Lord Neuberger, the President of the Supreme Court, suggested that Muslim women should be allowed to wear a full-face veil while appearing in court, as it shows respect towards different customs. He emphasized the need for judges and courtrooms to be sensitive to the cultural and social habits of those facing them. This suggestion comes amid uncertainty over the place of Muslim traditional dress in the legal system.

Andre Cole, a 52-year-old Missouri inmate, was executed for the 1998 murder of his ex-wife, Anthony Curtis, in a fit of rage over child support payments. Cole was the third convicted killer put to death in Missouri this year, following appeals that were denied. He was executed by lethal injection at the Eastern Reception, Diagnostic and Correctional Center in Bonne Terre, Missouri, at 10:15 pm on Tuesday. The execution was carried out despite concerns about Cole's mental health and the all-white jury that convicted him.

Prince Harry will fly out of the UK to Australia without seeing his new niece or nephew, as the Duchess of Cambridge is several days overdue for the birth of her second child. Harry, who will be bumped down to fifth in the line of succession, had returned briefly to hand out prizes at the London Marathon after engagements in Turkey. The prince is being forced to return to Australia for a month-long placement with the army and a week-long official tour of New Zealand. The new baby's arrival will be announced on Twitter and Instagram, with details posted on an easel outside Buckingham Palace.

An alleged fraudster named Justin Jackson has been accused of posing as Oprah Winfrey, former Obama aide Reggie Love, and Madonna's manager in an attempt to trick people into giving him jobs, clothes, free food, and jewelry worth $2.4 million. Jackson is being sued by Oprah's TV network and Love, and has been convicted for grand theft over a ruse in which he tricked a jeweler into lending him items worth $2.4 million. He is accused of sending letters purporting to be from Oprah and her representatives, as well as from Love, to recommend him for jobs and get free goods.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini has placed a €50 million price tag on Paulo Dybala, claiming he is the "new Messi" and that Paris Saint-Germain will have to spend a significant amount to sign him. Dybala is being tracked by Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, Juventus, and PSG, with Inter Milan manager Roberto Mancini reportedly watching the Serie A match between Parma and Palermo on Sunday. Zamparini claims that Dybala is worth €40 million but is willing to negotiate for €50 million, with PSG being the fiercest competition.

Hundreds of thousands of Brazilians are protesting against President Dilma Rousseff, who is struggling with an economic downturn and a bribery scandal at Petrobras. The protests are calling for Rousseff's impeachment. Petrobras was once considered Brazil's corporate jewel, but an investigation into a multimillion-dollar kickback scheme has led to widespread corruption allegations. The protests have grown in size and breadth, with some demonstrators saying they initially voted for Rousseff.

Former Manchester United midfielder Eric Cantona has refuted claims he starred in a soft porn film, insisting it is a "piece of art". The French film, "You and the Night", includes a scene in a cage with Cantona in just his underwear. Cantona, 48, says it is not pornography but a work of art and beautiful, defending the film as "a work of art" and "beautiful", and not a porn film as some have said.

A study by Oxford University researchers has found that certain types of music can enhance the enjoyment of a fish and chip supper, with the intensity of Nessun Dorma by Luciano Pavarotti being the perfect accompaniment to dark mouse or coffee, and the high-pitched piano in Billie Holiday's Autumn in New York helping to emphasise the autumnal flavour of a pumpkin pudding.

Raheem Sterling, 20, has been offered a £100,000-a-week contract by Liverpool, but negotiations have stalled. Manager Brendan Rodgers described the offer as "incredible." Sterling, who has two years left on his contract, has postponed contract talks until the end of the season. PFA Chief Executive Gordon Taylor defends Sterling, stating he is not a "money grabber" and believes waiting until the season is over could be a wise move. Sterling has been linked with moves to Arsenal and leading clubs in Spain. Sterling scored for England in their Euro 2016 qualifier with Lithuania. Taylor believes Sterling is aware of what he owes to Liverpool and Rodgers has given him his opportunity.

An Ohio woman, La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, discovered her biological mother, Francine Simmons, works at the same call-center operation company she does. After connecting the dots, she found Simmons on Facebook and realized her mother was closer than she could imagine. They eventually met after a phone call, and Mitchell-Clark found out she has three younger sisters. The reunion was a relief for the family, particularly for Simmons's daughter, Kamala Cummings.

Oscar "Papoo" Hernandez Jr., a convicted gun trafficker, was "awed" by New England Patriots star Aaron Hernandez and sent him an assault rifle and handguns a month before Odin Lloyd's murder. Hernandez pleaded guilty to weapons charges and faces up to 30 months in prison.

A 33-year-old man named Joel Parker was arrested in Florida for throwing a Snickers bar at a bus driver's head after threatening him and being disruptive during the ride. The incident occurred on a Sunshine Bus in St Johns County. Parker was not injured, but the driver called the police, and he was arrested for battery. Parker posted a $250 bond and was issued a trespass warning. He is also never allowed to use the bus again.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has discussed pre-season plans with Saido Berahino, indicating the striker will remain at the club beyond the summer transfer window. Berahino, who has expressed a desire to play in the Champions League, is likely to be included in England's under-21 squad for the upcoming European Championships. Pulis praised Berahino's performance and commitment, emphasizing the importance of professional footballers' longevity.

Giovanni Lo Porto, a Sicilian man who had been working on a reconstruction project in Pakistan following deadly flooding, was abducted by four armed men and later killed by a U.S. drone strike in 2012. He was a project manager for the German aid organization Welthungerlife, working on a clean water and sanitation program in Pakistan. Lo Porto had previously studied at London Metropolitan University and was passionate about helping others. His death was part of a larger counterterrorism operation that killed at least one al Qaeda leader, Ahmed Farouq, who was also a U.S. citizen.

A photographer captured an image of hundreds of sharks gathered off the coast of south Florida, with the scene being spotted by both the photographer and a fellow photographer. The sharks were theorized to be Blacktips or Spinners, which migrate to breed in shallower waters. The image was shared more than 2,000 times on Facebook, with experts suggesting the sharks were either Blacktips or Spinners.

An 11-year-old retired K-9 officer named Zeus, a German Shepherd who worked with the Ridgefield Police Department for eight years as a K-9 officer, was honored in a grand procession on Wednesday before he was put down due to a severe degenerative hip disorder and declining health. The tribute for Zeus began around 4:45 PM and ended at the Ridgefield Veterinary Hospital. The police department wrote an emotional message about Zeus on their Facebook, expressing their thoughts and prayers for Zeus, Officer Murray, and his family during this difficult time. During the grand procession, residents of Ridgefield lined the streets as they watched the cop cars drive by through the town. Zeus was being taken to Ridgefield Veterinary Clinic where he was to be euthanized.

Since Operation Yewtree, which was sparked by Jimmy Savile's assaults on dozens of children, reports of child sexual abuse have surged by more than 60%. Figures show that thousands of people have contacted police with allegations of abuse since 2011, with nearly 9,000 reports filed in 2014. Despite a rise in reports, the number of arrests fell by nine percent, prompting critics to accuse the Government of failing victims. The South Yorkshire force saw a 577 percent increase in reported cases over the last five years. The NSPCC helpline has seen a 81% increase in calls about sexual abuse since the launch of Operation Yewtree in 2012.

Iceland has become a popular filming location for TV series and Hollywood blockbusters, with Thingvellir National Park and Svartalfheim providing stunning settings for Game of Thrones and Thor: The Dark World, respectively. The country's natural landscapes, including Thingvellir National Park, Svartalfheim, Reykjanes Peninsula, Skaftafell National Park, and Vatnajokull glacier, have been used in films such as Interstellar, Prometheus, and Game of Thrones.

A 100-year-old mechanic's garage in Sydney has sold for $1.2 million, with the property being converted into a home. The grey-fronted building, built as a fire station in 1917, is now expected to be turned into a three-bedroom, four-storey house.

Samantha Rawcliffe, a 40-year-old mother-of-two from Morecambe, was diagnosed with functional neurological disorder (FND) after a car accident in May 2022. FND is an umbrella term for a range of neurological symptoms that cannot be explained, including uncontrollable shaking, loss of bladder control, and difficulty with motor function. Rawcliffe lost control of her body and crashed her car, leading to a series of symptoms that she initially attributed to shock. She was diagnosed with FND in September 2022, and now spends most of her time confined to her home, relying on a mobility scooter and taking 32 different drugs daily to manage her symptoms.

The artist behind a controversial statue of Lucille Ball, depicting her intoxicated pitch for a health tonic, has admitted to being "disappointed" with the work and offered to fix it for free. The statue, which was unveiled in 2009 in Celoron, New York, has been called "monstrous" and "frightening" by some residents, who have called for its removal. The artist, Dave Poulin, has pledged to create a new statue that better represents Ball's beauty and talent.

Bayern Munich's versatile left-back David Alaba, out for seven weeks with a torn knee ligament, will be sidelined for the closing stages of the season after being injured while playing for Austria. Alaba, 22, is set to start rehabilitation work in about a month and is set to miss the season finale. Bayern Munich, top of the Bundesliga, is set to face Porto in the Champions League quarter-finals later this month.

Beatrice Nokes, the daughter of two solicitors and a Scotland Yard detective, appeared in court today on charges of inciting a prostitution ring. Nokes, 21, is accused of running the ring with her father's friend Daniel Williams, who is also a detective constable. The case involves grooming three young women to sell their bodies for sex. Williams, who is suspended from duty, is accused of committing the crimes while on and off-duty. The case has led to several other charges against Williams, including controlling prostitution for gain and spying on unsuspecting hotel guests.

Diana Doyle, a whistleblower, revealed that a firm linked to the sale of NHS patient data is offering details of eating disorder sufferers, stress, hair loss, dandruff, impotence, snoring, dieters, and those with plastic surgery for just 12p a head. The firm, Sequester, is offering to sell information on 43 different health conditions, including skin problems, insomnia, migraines, and sensitive teeth. The revelations prompted probes by the Information Commissioner's Office and the Direct Marketing Commission, and a third investigation by the General Pharmaceutical Council into Pharmacy2U, the UK's biggest online pharmacy.

Jordan Spieth, the 21-year-old golfer who won the 2017 Masters tournament, expressed his feelings about his autistic sister Ellie, who was unable to attend the event. Spieth, who was named after basketball legend Michael Jordan, described Ellie as the most special part of his family and the funniest. He said that his sister's presence provided him with perspective and helped him understand the bigger picture of life. Spieth's victory was described as "even better" than his dreams, and he expressed his hope to be finishing his final Masters appearance in 50 years' time.

Dick Advocaat, the 67-year-old Dutch football manager, will not underestimate the significance of the Old Firm derby between Sunderland and Newcastle United, the home team, in the upcoming match. Advocaat, who had previously underplayed the importance of the rivalry in 1998, insists he will not make the same mistake. The match is crucial for Sunderland, who are one point above the relegation zone and could be in the bottom three by kick-off. Advocaat, who could start Adam Johnson for the first time, is considering starting him in the derby. The match is expected to be a special game for Sunderland, with the home crowd expected to provide an extra weapon for the team.

A heated argument erupted between a young woman and a butcher in Sydney's Bondi area over a chicken purchase dispute. Belinda Bartholomew, the girlfriend of Roosters star Aidan Guerra, claimed she was racially abused and called a "f***ing c***" by the butcher when she tried to change her chicken selection. The butcher, however, denied the claims, stating that he was the one being rude and that the woman was the troublemaker. The incident highlights tensions between immigrants and locals in Sydney's eastern suburbs.

Freddo Frog, a popular children's chocolate, has been reduced in size by 20% from 15g to 12g due to manufacturing cost increases. This change was spotted by a shop owner who stocks the treats. Cadbury's parent company, Mondelez International, announced the change in February, reducing the size of their family blocks from 220g to 200g. The company's profit before tax rose 46% from $87 million to $127 million in 2013. Thousands of chocolate fans expressed their anger and disappointment on Cadbury's Facebook page.

Hillary Clinton's campaign-in-waiting met in Brooklyn on Saturday, a day before her official presidential announcement, to outline their values and goals. The "values statement" includes avoiding mistakes from Clinton's 2008 campaign and emphasizes humility, discipline, and unity. The campaign aims to win by giving families and small businesses a path to prosperity. Clinton plans to launch her campaign through a video message on Sunday and will visit Iowa and New Hampshire.

A 29-year-old woman named Kyli Wilfson, who was 26 when she first experienced severe abdominal pain while eating, was diagnosed with chronic pancreatitis, a rare condition that left her unable to eat anything for a year and a half despite feeling extremely hungry. Kyli, who was from North Carolina, had been experiencing digestive problems for years but was initially misdiagnosed with acute pancreatitis. She eventually received a correct diagnosis of chronic pancreatitis after doctors performed a procedure to examine her pancreas. Kyli's condition required her to be fed through a feeding tube, and she lost a significant amount of weight, dropping to 80lbs. The disease is characterized by an inflammation of the pancreas and is often associated with a lifetime of pain and difficulty eating. Kyli found support through a Facebook group for people with chronic pancreatitis, and her fiancé, Dustin Wood, felt bad eating in front of her.

Scottish National Party leader Nicola Sturgeon posed with a sceptical face in a meme referencing the leaders' debate, while Labour leader Ed Miliband was superimposed over London rapper Plan B, issuing a call to 'come at me bruv'. The images were inspired by a debate that saw Miliband warned he would not get into power without lurching left, as Sturgeon told him he is 'not strong enough' to win power on his own. Cameron and Clegg stayed away, with the Prime Minister and his deputy superimposed over Christopher Steed and Stephen Webb from Channel 4's Gogglebox.

Amir Khan, the British boxer, is set to face Manny Pacquiao in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, after Mayweather declined the opportunity. Khan, who has been waiting for Mayweather for two years, is now considering a fight with Pacquiao. The fight, if successful, would be the richest fight in boxing history. Khan, who has been looking at an event in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, is a huge attraction in the Muslim world.

A two-bedroom home in Islington, north London, has sold for £750,000, despite being only 5ft wide in some areas and 8ft 8in wide at its widest. The property, which is described as "well proportioned" by the estate agency, has two bedrooms, a tiny study, reception room, shower room, cloakroom, kitchen, and a garden. The home, which was put on the market with Foxtons for £750,000, is said to be a "stylish two bedroom period house" with characterful touches and a pretty rear garden. The buyer will have to pay £27,000 in stamp duty, the same as a second-hand narrow boat which is 50ft long.

Scottish First Minister Nicola Sturgeon is launching an ambitious manifesto to lead the UK, aiming to form a power-sharing deal with Labour. The SNP's policies overlap with Labour's, including reducing tuition fees and rolling back NHS competition. The manifesto includes plans for spending increases funded by more borrowing, potentially totaling £180 billion over five years. The SNP aims to build a "progressive alliance" for policies across the UK, with a focus on Scotland. The surge in support for the SNP could lead to constitutional turmoil similar to the 1910 election, which resulted in bitter conflict and the secession of Ireland.

Celtic U17 team won the Glasgow Cup against Rangers, with Josh Kerr scoring twice. Rangers struggled to create chances, and Celtic's Robby McCrorie made crucial saves. The match was played behind closed doors due to fan trouble.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis, who previously played for Crystal Palace, led his team to a 2-0 victory over the former club. Pulis insists on wearing his cap, track suit, and white trainers during every game, stating he would never take it off during a match. The victory moved West Brom to 36 points, securing their survival in the Premier League.

Jameela Jamil, a 29-year-old television presenter and former model, spent £3,000 on having all her amalgam fillings removed and replaced with white fillings after experiencing health problems for nearly seven years. The fillings were removed due to high levels of mercury detected in her blood tests, which suggested they were the cause of her symptoms, including puffy faces, heavy heads, and fainting. While dental amalgam has been used for over 150 years and is still commonly used, the amounts taken in from fillings are considered minuscule and are not associated with health risks, according to experts.

Suge Knight, the co-creator of Death Row Records, was refused an appeal to have his bail reduced from $10 million to $5 million as he awaits trial for murder and attempted murder. Despite walking into court, he had to be wheeled out in a wheelchair. Judge Ronald Coen rejected his pleas. However, Knight believes his close friend, the undefeated professional boxer Floyd Mayweather, will bail him out when he wins on Saturday. Mayweather, worth $420 million, is set to land a record pay check after going head-to-head with Manny Pacquiao on Saturday. Knight's attorney Matthew Fletcher is confident that Mayweather will bail him out.

TV chef Gizzi Erskine posed for a cat magazine shoot with her shorthair cat Kimchi, who has a discerning palate and loves crunchy human food like poppadoms and tortilla chips. Kimchi is described as a fussy eater who will steal food from her owner if she's not looking, and she has a particular fondness for taramasalata. Erskine's cat family includes a new addition, Ponzu, named after her favorite Japanese dressing.
