A father in Japan discovered a pair of boots behind his daughter in a photograph he took in 2014, sparking internet speculation about their origin and meaning. The boots, which appear to be black, have since been the subject of debate on Reddit, with some suggesting they could be samurai boots or the result of a trick of light. The father, Martin Springall, insists the boots are genuine and that he has no idea what they could represent, adding that he has no recollection of anyone standing behind his daughter in the photograph.

The UK government plans to introduce new immigration policies that will require foreign workers to pay an average of £22,000 in tax and national insurance before they can claim benefits. The measures, which will be outlined in the Tory manifesto, will ban EU migrants from receiving state support for four years and will also ban the "exporting" of child benefit for children living in other EU countries. The crackdown is aimed at limiting the appeal of coming to Britain from poorer parts of the EU and is part of the government's plan to negotiate a new deal with Europe, including curbing access to benefits.

A severely disabled boy, Cody Neatis, from Preston, England, has been sleeping on a mattress on the floor in hospital for seven nights due to a lack of a suitable bed for him. Cody, who has Down's syndrome, epilepsy, autism, and is fed by a tube, has been without a hospital bed because staff do not have the special cot needed to keep him safe in his sleep. His mother, Lynne Neatis, 48, has slept with Cody for the past week, fearing he will injure himself or pull out his oxygen. The hospital does not have the specialist high-sided cot needed for Cody and other disabled children. Lynne Neatis is now demanding answers from the local health trust as she claims she has waited two years for the bed.

Ahead of the Masters golf tournament, Derek Lawrenson reports on the excitement and challenges faced by players. Rory McIlroy aims to complete his career Grand Slam, while Henrik Stenson, recovering from flu, and Tiger Woods, accompanied by his children, face the pressure of playing in the traditional par-three tournament. The tournament's history is marked by memorable shots, such as Gene Sarazen's albatross on the 15th hole, and the tradition of players attempting to skip their golf balls across the water at the 16th hole.

Juventus have ruled out a move for Manchester United loan star Radamel Falcao after claiming the Colombia striker's wages are 'beyond their means'. Falcao has scored only four goals and failed to force his way into Louis van Gaal's starting XI at Manchester United. Juventus general manager Beppe Marotta has claimed that Falcao wanted to come to Turin last summer but the Serie A champions have now taken themselves out of the race to sign him. Juventus need to reinforce their forward line with highly rated Palermo striker Paulo Dybala and Paris Saint Germain striker Edinson Cavani.

David Cameron plans to sell Lloyds Bank shares worth £4 billion if he wins the election, offering them at a discount and encouraging long-term ownership. This is the largest privatisation since Thatcher's era, with a £20 billion bailout by Gordon Brown. The sale aims to help pay down the national debt and is part of a Conservative policy revival.

Living near congested roads with high levels of air pollution can cause 'silent strokes' that increase the risk of dementia, according to a study by researchers at Boston University School of Medicine. The microscopic particles, mostly from traffic fumes and factory emissions, alter the structure of the brain and are linked to a 46% higher risk of silent strokes in towns and cities. The study, published in the journal Stroke, involved more than 900 people aged 60 and over who did not have dementia or a history of strokes.

Jessica Ainscough, a 30-year-old wellness warrior who died from a rare and aggressive form of cancer, wrote an emotional letter to her followers revealing she was undergoing radiation treatment in her final weeks. She had previously rejected chemotherapy and radiation, opting for controversial Gerson Therapy, which lacks scientific support. After discussions with experts, Ainscough began a course of targeted radiation in her final weeks, which was among the toughest for her partner, Tallon Pamenter. The radiation successfully shrunk the tumour but complications arose, leading to Ainscough's death.

Ten people, including four children, were involved in a multi-vehicle crash on the Brisbane Valley Highway in Brisbane's west on Wednesday afternoon. Three vehicles collided, resulting in chest and shoulder injuries for a 40-year-old man and a 5-year-old boy, as well as arm and abdominal pain for a 27-year-old woman and a 6-year-old girl. The incident occurred near Fernvale, with six others, including an infant and two young girls, being taken to Ipswich Hospital with minor injuries or for further assessment. A man suffered hand lacerations, and two females escaped injuries. The affected stretch of the highway was closed off, with diversions in place south of Fernvale. The Rescue 500 helicopter airlifted patients to the Princess Alexandra Hospital in Brisbane.

Jason McDonald, a 34-year-old volunteer at the Colorado Gator Farm, walked a thin slackline rope over a pool containing more than 50 hungry alligators at the farm. McDonald, who has been involved with alligators for over ten years and has taken handling classes, thought this would be an interesting new way of interacting with the fearsome creatures. The gators were surprisingly ok with the slackline, and McDonald said he wanted to take his hobby further by walking over Elvis or Morris, his two biggest gators on the farm.

The son of a Syrian imam who was shot dead on a London street may have met his father's killer just days before the murder. Abdul Hadi Arwani, an opponent of Syrian President Bashar Al-Assad, had visited the area where he was killed with his son days before his death. Arwani, 48, was shot and killed in his car on a quiet street in North West London after being called there last Tuesday, apparently to provide a quote for building work. The man, who has not been otherwise identified, also told the imam that there was no need for his son to accompany him again when he did come back. The counter-terrorism unit is investigating whether the man was a hired killer who postponed the hit because Arwani was not alone.

Hong Kong's Jenny's cookies, a popular buttery treat, have sparked a black market frenzy, with tourists and locals lining up for hours to purchase them. The original store has signs warning against buying "fake" cookies, while bakeries have started making knockoffs. The cookie's popularity has led to people being hired to stand in line and resell the goods at a 70% markup. The cookie's popularity has sparked a similar frenzy in other parts of the world, with people waiting hours to purchase foods like cronuts and ramen burgers.

A mother-of-one, Kira Hollis, overcame anorexia and depression by becoming a bodybuilder. She was diagnosed with borderline personality disorder and was underweight at 6st. Doctors ordered her to go to the gym to gain weight, which led her to become a personal trainer. Now, she is 9. 5st and says bodybuilding gave her the confidence to overcome her depression. She was helped by the Cherry Orchard Clinic in Tamworth and medication from her doctor. Her six-year-old daughter Olivia also helped her with her recovery.

Lewis Ferguson, 18, survived a spectacular fall from Merrion Square during a race at Wincanton on Wednesday, causing him to hit the fence and perform a mid-air somersault. The incident, which was captured on video and has been viewed millions of times online, has led to Ferguson gaining a reputation as an internet sensation. Despite the fall, Ferguson returned to riding and said he was undeterred from getting back in the saddle. The incident was described as the worst fall the race course clerk of the course Barry Johnson had ever seen.

Hillary Clinton launched her campaign in a unique and unconventional way, using a video, new logo, and a road trip to "rebrand" herself and reframe her message. The launch was met with mixed reactions from the media, with some criticizing it as "relentlessly, insultingly vapid" and others finding it refreshing and forward-looking. The campaign logo, which features Clinton standing in line at a fast-food chain, is expected to be the most ubiquitous element of her campaign.

More than 1,700 Chinese high school students from Yichuan, Shaanxi province, took an exam in their school's playground on Saturday, the first time the school allowed students to sit exams outdoors due to insufficient indoor space. The students organized the outdoor exam themselves, with a regular radio announcement instructing them to turn their chairs and desks from time to time to avoid being dazzled by the sun. The school approved the proposal, and many students believe sitting the exam outside is a novel way to broaden their horizons and encourage relaxation.

Sportsmail has partnered with Gillette to offer a unique chance for one lucky reader to win a pair of Nike Magista Obra boots signed by Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart. The prize includes a new Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor with Flexball technology and a shave gel. The competition closes on April 19.

Kecil, a baby orangutan, was found rejected by his natural mother and a surrogate mother, but was later adopted by Maggie, an experienced surrogate mother at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo. Maggie has now been raising Kecil for the past 10 months, and the two have formed an inseparable bond. Kecil is set to make his first public appearance this weekend, and Maggie has proven her parenting prowess once again.

A 61-year-old woman named Noelle Baynham died suddenly and was eaten by her two dogs after being locked in the house for days. The dogs, a Jack Russell and a Staffordshire Bull Terrier, partially ate her body, and the cause of death was an accidental overdose of medication. The incident occurred on January 17, 2023, in Winchester, Hampshire, and was ruled an open verdict by the coroner.

France's handball star Nikola Karabatic, along with his brother Luka and 15 other players, is facing a fraud trial for suspected match-fixing. Karabatic, who was briefly detained, competes for France in the Handball World Cup against Iceland in January. He denies placing bets on a Montpellier match that resulted in a loss. The trial is expected to take place within months, with Karabatic facing up to five years in prison and a fine.

A gang of six men, including Ahmed Hassan-Sule, 21, and Mohamed Saleh, 22, were convicted of a string of sexual offenses against teenage girls in Banbury, Oxfordshire, from 2009 to 2014. The offenses occurred in cars, woods, and at the defendants' homes. Hassan-Sule and Saleh were sentenced to nine and four years in jail, respectively. The girls, aged between 13 and 16, were targeted at under-18s parties organized by Hassan-Sule. The judge criticized the defense's argument that the girls came forward because they were victims, stating that it stops other girls from coming forward.

Former New England Patriots star Aaron Hernandez faces three more trials, including a murder trial in which he is accused of killing two men and wounding another person near a Boston nightclub in July 2012. Hernandez pleaded not guilty at his arraignment. The trial was originally slated for May 28, but was postponed and no new date has been set.

The Emirates Airline has signed a £30 million three-year deal to sponsor the FA Cup, rebranding it as the Emirates FA Cup. This deal, along with existing sponsorship deals with Arsenal, AC Milan, and Hamburg, adds to Emirates' growing portfolio of sporting sponsorships.

Michael Phelps, the 18-time Olympic champion, is aiming to compete in the Rio Olympics next year but won't swim at the world championships in Russia this summer. He was suspended by USA Swimming after a second drunken driving arrest and will compete in his first meet since the suspension. Phelps expressed his desire to return to the Olympics and acknowledged the pain of missing the world championships.

Gareth Bale, a key player for Real Madrid, is doubtful for the Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid due to a calf injury. The Welsh forward limped off during Real's 3-1 home victory over Malaga on Saturday. Real Madrid's medical staff found a muscular lesion in Bale's soleus muscle. Los Blancos are also without Croatian midfielder Luka Modric, who suffered a knee ligament strain and is expected to be unavailable for six weeks. Real Madrid's striker Karim Benzema is expected to be fit for the match after missing Saturday's encounter with a knee injury.

Scientists warn that older people are more susceptible to emotions when making decisions about their retirement, particularly during financial crises. A study of 1,204 retired individuals found that those with better cognitive abilities were less likely to panic and sell investments during market downturns. The study, published in the Journal of Consumer Affairs, suggests that cognitive decline with age can impair decision-making, especially in the face of emotional responses to market losses. The reforms announced by Chancellor George Osborne allow individuals to withdraw from their pension and take the income they need starting April 5, 2016, under final salary schemes.

Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini is criticized by Stuart Pearce for not being given enough time to turn around the club's fortunes. Pearce believes Pellegrini should stay in place, as he has been around the block long enough to realize the squad needs drastic changes this summer. The article highlights Manchester City's poor run of form, with Sergio Aguero being a rare bright spot in the squad.

Manchester United's stars, including Wayne Rooney, Ander Herrera, and Robin van Persie, are training in the sunshine ahead of their Premier League match against Manchester City on Sunday. The game is significant as it marks Manchester United's first Premier League clash against their rivals since the Sir Alex Ferguson era, and a victory could give them a four-point lead in fourth place. The match is also crucial for Manchester City, who have won their last three visits to Old Trafford.

Fiorentina, the Italian football club, lost 1-0 to Verona in a Champions League qualifying match, leaving them nine points behind third-placed AS Roma. Fiorentina's coach, Vincenzo Montella, expressed disappointment, and the team fell to sixth place on 49 points. The defeat leaves Fiorentina with a chance to qualify for the Europa League quarter-finals against Dynamo Kiev in the upcoming match.

Miley Cyrus, 22, attended the 30th Annual Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony in Cleveland, Ohio, where she posed for a social media snap with somewhat bushy underarm hair. This sparked controversy, with some users advising her to shave, while others defended her choice. Cyrus is not the first, and probably won't be the last, to choose not to shave her armpits.

Barcelona's Lionel Messi, Neymar, and Luis Suarez scored a combined 102 goals in the 2019-20 season, surpassing their previous record of 92 goals. The trio's dominance led Barcelona to a 6-0 victory over Getafe, securing a 5-point lead in La Liga. Messi, Neymar, and Suarez each have 49, 32, and 21 goals respectively, with Messi's 30 left-footed and 15 right-footed goals, and four headers. The victory boosted Barcelona's goal difference to +78, putting pressure on Real Madrid ahead of their match against Almeria.

A 44-year-old pedestrian named Andrea McVeigh was struck by a cyclist on the pavement in Bermondsey, South London, on April 14. The cyclist fled the scene, and McVeigh suffered two three-inch gashes to her forehead and other facial and hand injuries. The cyclist initially stopped after the impact but then sped off, turning around and smiling at McVeigh's husband as he chased him. McVeigh is now off work sick and has two black eyes, a swollen nose, stitches, and a feeling of being very scared to go out onto the street. The police have issued CCTV footage of the cyclist they want to speak to and have launched a hunt for the mystery cyclist.

Paul Gregory, 51, of Bedford, was fined £795 for claiming he could only walk 200 meters when he was actually a keen walker and member of a mountaineering club. He was exposed after council officials noticed a newspaper report describing his exploits on a 191-mile hike. Gregory pleaded guilty to two counts of dishonestly obtaining a blue badge by misrepresenting his physical abilities and was ordered to carry out 150 hours of unpaid work and pay a £60 victim surcharge.

Apple has filed a patent for a new method of unlocking its devices using facial recognition, which involves scanning a user's face with the front-facing camera when the handset is moved into a certain position. If the scanned face matches a previously taken photo, the phone unlocks automatically. This system is similar to Android's Trusted face feature, which relies on the user pressing the power button to enable the screen. The patent was filed by Apple in March 2011 and was awarded earlier this week.

Elizabeth Sedway, a 51-year-old mother of two battling cancer, was ejected from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California due to her lack of a doctor's note clearing her to fly. The incident occurred when an airline representative noticed her wearing a surgical mask and asked if she needed anything. After being asked a second time, she indicated she might require extra time to board the plane due to her cancer. The family was eventually removed from the flight, and Sedway's husband and sons were forced to walk towards the exit.

A vintage 1973 E-Type Jaguar was involved in a head-on collision with a 1973 Toyota Kluger on Easter Sunday night in Frenchs Forest, Sydney. The Jaguar, valued at over $120,000, was completely written off, while all three adults involved were taken to hospital for precautionary measures. The incident occurred on Warringah Road at a traffic light intersection. The crash was reported to be the result of a modern car hitting a classic car, sparking sympathy from car enthusiasts and a warning to drivers to follow road rules during the Easter long weekend.

Google has established a team focused on enhancing the longevity of electronic devices, including smartphones, tablets, and electric vehicles, through the development of flexible and wearable technologies. The team, consisting of four individuals, has been working on solid-state, thin-film batteries since 2012, with a particular interest in subfreezing temperature performance for Google's Project Loon balloons. This initiative follows Apple's recent job listings for battery-related positions, indicating a growing trend in the tech industry towards improving battery life and sustainability.

The 223-foot Explorer is a luxury superyacht designed by British yacht designer Tony Castro, featuring a helipad, infinity pool, and space for 12 guests. It is capable of carrying a helicopter, twin limousine tenders, car, submarine, jetskis, paddleboards, and inflatables. The yacht is expected to cost approximately 40 million euros to build, making it likely to cost even more to purchase. The layout includes a variety of different areas for guests to retreat to, ensuring they don't get bored while sailing around the world. However, the high cost of the yacht means that it will likely retail for even more.

Ed Miliband, the Labour leader, announced his plans to cap rents in the UK despite warnings from experts that they will backfire, leading to more tenants being evicted and investment in new housing being slashed. The controversial proposal, demanded by the militant Unite union, would give millions of "forgotten" renters a fairer deal by helping those stuck in Generation Rent by soaring house prices. However, the Generation Rent campaign group criticized the plans, saying they were "riddled with loopholes" and may make tenants' lives worse.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town fan, Ryan Dearnley, was removed from his role as a mascot for Reading in the FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal after a video emerged showing him backing Arsenal. The move was made to avoid a negative reception from Reading fans. The Football Association offered Dearnley two tickets to watch the semi-final in the Arsenal end but he declined, preferring to watch Huddersfield take on Derby in the Championship.

A giant supervoid, estimated to be 1.8 billion light-years across, may be responsible for a mysterious "Cold Spot" in the universe, which is 20% less dense than other regions. The supervoid is thought to be causing a "less-dense" region of the universe, with a temperature 70 nano-Kelvins colder than the rest of the cosmic microwave background radiation. The supervoid is the largest single structure ever found by humanity.

The Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, will display Abraham Lincoln's chair where he was shot in 1865 as part of its observance of the 150th anniversary of the assassination. The chair, which has a dark stain on the back believed to be blood from the shooting, will be removed from its enclosure and displayed in an open plaza on April 15. It will also be onstage when renowned historian and Lincoln expert Doris Kearns Goodwin delivers a sold-out lecture at The Henry Ford on April 13. The chair has been part of the museum since its founding 85 years ago and was originally housed in the theater where Lincoln was shot.

A 19-year-old vlogger named Jake Boys surprised his girlfriend Emily Canham with tickets to see One Direction perform in Cardiff, but mistakenly booked plane tickets to the Republic of Ireland instead. The couple, both popular vloggers, are now planning to buy new train tickets to Cardiff for the band's show in June.

A Romanian company has developed a mobile X-ray scanner, the Roboscan 2M Aeria, that can scan entire planes for contraband, bombs, and weapons. The device, which costs €3 million, is already being used to check trucks at borders in Eastern Europe and has helped seize 76,000 packs of illegal cigarettes. The device can scan planes from small private jets to medium-sized commercial airplanes and can be used to detect weapons and other contraband in low-security airports. The device can scan an entire plane in about 20 minutes.

A 54-year-old convicted paedophile, Stephen Munden, has gone on the run after vanishing from a psychiatric unit. Munden, described as having a 'fanatical obsession' with young girls, was last seen leaving a hospital in Hampshire. He was detained under the Mental Health Act after sexually touching a three-year-old girl. Munden, formerly of Southampton, is believed to have shaved off his beard before leaving the hospital. A court heard he admitted ten unrelated offences of possessing or attempting to possess indecent images of children. Officers are now searching for Munden, who is described as about 5ft 8ins tall, of a heavy build, and has dark hair.

Middlesbrough, currently top of the Championship, hold a significant lead over the rest of the league, with just four weeks remaining. The division is highly volatile, with seven teams separated by just one point, and Middlesbrough's advantage over second-placed Bournemouth is a point with Watford and Norwich, who are both a point behind. The match against Watford on Monday is a lunchtime kick-off, which could have a psychological effect on other teams. The promotion race is highly competitive, with Watford and Norwich having a chance to overtake Bournemouth if they win their games.

The latest hair trend is grey hair, with women sharing images on social media under the hashtag #grannyhair. The trend has gained popularity on platforms like Instagram, with over half a million views. The trend has been embraced by both professional models and everyday women, with some opting for a more dramatic look with makeup and highlights. The trend has been traced back to a catwalk show featuring silver-haired models earlier this month, and has been praised by fashion fans.

A couple from Bellefontaine, Ohio, who were struggling with chronic conditions and financial difficulties, died from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning after living without gas, water, and electricity for months. The couple, Randy and Jodi Speidel, had created online fundraisers but failed to draw any donations. Their deaths were confirmed by a note found at their residence and a note left on their GoFundMe page. The couple's daughters, Randa and Kira, were left without a father and mother.

Liberal Democrat leader Nick Clegg vowed to continue as leader even if the party is reduced to fewer than 30 MPs, despite previous indications he would quit if the party is left out of power. Clegg emphasized his commitment to serving the country and his party, despite the potential risks of losing the center ground and undoing past sacrifices. Business Secretary Vince Cable expressed hope to be made Chancellor if the Lib Dems form another coalition with the Conservatives. Clegg also appeared to lean towards another deal with the Tories, stating he deserved "credit" for forming the Coalition while enduring "five years of constant bile from the Labour Party."

A pensioner named Terry Cooper, 79, was living in fear after his Jack Russell dog saved him from a badger that was the size of a large pig with six-inch teeth. The incident occurred when Cooper was enjoying the sunshine in his garden with his dog Sam. The badger, which had two cubs, burst through a hedge and attacked Cooper's dog, which then pulled him back indoors. Cooper was left badly shaken and fears he could have been attacked if his dog had not been there. The National Farmers' Union has issued advice for residents on protecting their property from invading badgers.

Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose to Porto U21s on Wednesday, while the Blues were knocked out of the Champions League. Mourinho visited Fulham's Motspur Park with his son Jose Junior. Porto's Leandro Silva scored a hat-trick to progress to the Premier League International Cup final. Chelsea are closing in on the Premier League title with six games to play, 10 points above Arsenal.

Andreas Christopheros, a 29-year-old property developer, was severely injured when corrosive liquid was thrown in his face outside his home in Truro, Cornwall. Nicole Phillips, 45, from Hastings, was charged with perverting the course of justice and is due to appear at Bodmin Magistrates Court on April 30. Her husband, David Phillips, 48, was already charged with grievous bodily harm with intent. Mr Christopheros, a father-of-one, suffered life-changing injuries, including a loss of vision and facial scars, after the attack last December.

A Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route has erected signs warning pilgrims not to defecate along the famous path, as angry residents complain about the frequent nature calls. The signs, which show a squatting figure defecating within a red circle with a diagonal line across it, have become an attraction for pilgrims. The pilgrimage attracts thousands of pilgrims every year, but there are few places to relieve themselves.

A massive fire broke out at a former strip club in Flint, Michigan, on Wednesday afternoon, destroying the building and nearby power lines. The blaze started at about 1pm and was reported to have affected only the building itself and a few nearby power lines. The site was not a vacant facility, and local resident Terry Rauh said a fire had taken place there before. The fire was reported to be under investigation.

A woman of Arab and Jewish descent, Shoshana Hebshi, reached a settlement of $40,000 in a lawsuit against the federal government, Transportation Security Administration, and Wayne County Airport Authority after being strip-searched at a Detroit-area airport on the 10th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks. The settlement aims to protect future passengers from similar experiences.

A plane made a crash landing and skidded off the runway at Hiroshima Airport in Japan, injuring 20 people. The Airbus A320, bound from Incheon International Airport in Seoul, South Korea, reportedly missed the landing point and overran the runway. Local media reported a hard landing and no sign of the landing gear, with evacuation slides deployed. The incident occurred after the plane had a tailstrike, and the airport was closed as a result.

Mark-Francis Vandelli, a wealthy reality TV star, has opened up his watch collection to the Evening Standard, showcasing 16 expensive timepieces. The most expensive watch in his collection is a Cartier white gold Moonphase, which he bought for £32,000. Vandelli revealed his favorite items and the history behind them, including a Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42 and a Cartier Tortue Collection Privée.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy is selling his extensive collection of antiques in a £100,000 auction after deciding to downsize his home. The collection includes a 3D diorama of the Battle of Agincourt, a longbow made from yew, and a portrait of Hardy holding the bow. The auction, held by Dominic Winter auctioneers, features 238 lots of furniture, paintings, swords, and other items. Hardy, 89, is a military historian who studied with J.R.R. Tolkien and is now an expert on the medieval longbow. The sale is part of his downsizing process, and Hardy hopes the proceeds will bring joy to future owners.

A Brazilian commuter, Nelson Felippe, took a photo of two women hugging on a train platform and posted it on Facebook, expressing his disapproval of the scene. The image quickly went viral, with over 100, 000 views in 24 hours. Felippe's post, which initially appeared to be homophobic, actually revealed that he was observing a public transport safety regulation. The post has been praised for its witty way of exposing homophobia and has received thousands of comments.

A young English cricket fan, Jonathan Stevenson, wrote a letter to Richie Benaud, the legendary Australian cricket great, asking for tips on leg spin bowling almost 20 years ago. Benaud's detailed response, dated September 27, 1996, was shared on Twitter as a tribute to the "great man." The letter included notes on various deliveries and tips on how to deliver them. Benaud, who enjoyed a remarkable Test career as a wily leg-spin bowler, also provided advice on different deliveries and how to deliver them.

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg predicts that virtual reality will revolutionize travel, allowing users to experience destinations from multiple viewpoints and even change their perspectives. The company purchased Oculus, a virtual reality headset maker, and promised to support virtual reality on its newsfeed, enabling users to explore locations with multiple cameras. Marriott hotels have also trialled Oculus Rift for a tour of destinations.

A 22-year-old woman in China was diagnosed with bone cancer and admitted to the hospital, preventing her from getting married on her birthday. Her boyfriend, Guo Kai, arranged for professional photographers to take wedding photos for her, despite her condition requiring frequent medical attention. The couple met through mutual friends and have been committed to each other since the earthquake in 2008.

Blaine Boudreaux, a 34-year-old man with a history of DUIs, was arrested in Houston for three separate DUI collisions that killed a 6-year-old boy and injured his mother. Boudreaux was charged with intoxication manslaughter, intoxicated assault, and failure to stop and render aid involving death. The incidents occurred within three hours of each other, with the first collision involving a mother and her 2-year-old child, who were taken to the hospital and later released.

Microsoft has launched a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions within the company, with positions based at its Redmond campus in Washington and run in partnership with Specialisterne, a Danish nonprofit. The program aims to expand opportunity and represent customers, with Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella apologizing for comments about women needing to trust the system to pay them well.

Two Tulsa, Oklahoma, deputies involved in the fatal shooting of Eric Harris have been reassigned due to threats against them and their families. The shooting occurred when Reserve Deputy Robert Bates shot Harris, who was trying to arrest him. The deputies are not charged with a crime but have faced criticism for their actions. The sheriff's office has suspended the drug unit pending a review of the April shooting. The FBI has cleared the agency of any civil rights violations. The shooting has led to allegations of forgery and unqualified training, with the sheriff denying these claims. The family of Eric Harris has demanded justice and changes in policy.

Katie Prager, a 24-year-old woman with cystic fibrosis, is in desperate need of a life-saving lung transplant due to an infection. Her husband, Dalton, has already received new lungs but Katie is waiting for a transplant in Kentucky. Katie's insurance company, Kentucky Medicaid, will not cover the out-of-state treatment at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. Dalton is pleading for help to save his wife, who is struggling to negotiate her healthcare options from her hospital bed at the University of Kentucky.

The Sleep Cycle app analyzed data from over two million users to discover that the world's earliest wake-up time is on a Monday in South Africa, while Americans wake up at 7am and are in the worst mood all week. Slovakia topped the list for national average sleep quality, with the UK in 45th place and the US in 49th. The best sleep quality worldwide occurs on a Wednesday night, with more than half of countries surveyed reporting the most restful sleep on this day.

A series of unpublished love letters from Mexican artist Frida Kahlo to her lover Jose Bartoli are expected to fetch upwards of $120,000 when the passionate missives go up for auction later this year. The letters, written between 1946 and 1949, were saved by Jose until his death in 1995 and comprise more than 100 pages. Frida signed her letters to Jose 'Mara', which biographer Hayden Herrera explained is probably short for 'Maravillosa', a name Jose would call her. The collection also includes an original drawing of a sleeping cat, pressed flowers, ribbon, beads, and drafts of a few of Jose's responses.

Trade union leader Len McCluskey, known for his militant stance, is popular with Labour activists during an election campaign in South Wales. However, his union, Unite, is a potent force in British politics, seeking to impose socialist policies on the government. McCluskey, who once presided over more strikes than any other union boss, is open about his desire to return Britain to the dark days of the 1970s. His union's influence on Labour candidates is chilling, and his socialist policies, including a major expansion in the public sector and higher taxation, are intertwined with the Labour Party's structure and finances.

A zookeeper at the Zoological Center in Tel Aviv, Elad Hershkowitz, used a GoPro camera to capture the unique ways different animals drink water in their enclosures. The footage, totaling 30 hours, shows a variety of animal behaviors, from a rhino almost kissing the surface of the water to a lemur delicately licking it. The zookeeper initially worried that the animals would be skeptical of the foreign object, but they eventually got used to the camera's presence and drank freely. The footage offers a unique perspective on animal drinking habits and showcases the diverse behaviors of different species.
Just a quarter of voters think David Cameron is hungriest to win the election, a poll reveals, as the Prime Minister tries to step up his campaign passion.

A man charged with assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov has told a court he was beaten and pressured into confessing to the murder. Zaur Dadaev, accused of being involved in the shooting of Nemstov in Moscow on February 27, told the court he had been abducted, beaten, and pressured into confessing. Dadaev had previously confessed to the murder but now says he was beaten and pressured into making that statement. He is one of five Chechen men accused of killing Nemstov. Dadaev is being held with his cousins, Anzor and Shagid Gubahsev, and Khamzat Bakhayev and Tamerlan Eskerkhanov have also been accused of involvement in Nemstov's murder.

A 4-month-old baby boy named Sonit Awal was pulled from the rubble of a Nepal earthquake that killed over 5,000 people. His father, Shyam Awal, frantically searched for him amid the debris for 22 hours before the soldiers found him at 10 a.m. on Sunday. Sonit's face was exposed during the rescue, but he was uninjured.

A Church of Scientology-affiliated drug rehabilitation network, Narcocon, is challenging the designation of a historic site near Camp David as a way to circumvent zoning laws and build a drug rehab center. The property, Trout Run, was bought by a real estate company in 2013 and is currently classified for resource conservation, making it ineligible for a drug rehab center. Narcocon claims its program, based on Scientology teachings, can help addicts overcome cravings by flushing out stored drugs through a regimen of exercise, sauna sessions, and vitamin therapy. The case is being contested by opponents who argue the designation is a trick to circumvent current zoning laws.

The article discusses the aftermath of the U.S. military withdrawal from Afghanistan, focusing on the challenges faced by expatriates and locals in Kabul. Five men who once spoke English fluently due to their work with NATO are now blacklisted and isolated, fearing reprisals. The city has transformed, with the population swelling but the violence in the provinces causing further growth. The article highlights the empty streets, abandoned shops, and the detritus of the U.S. military presence, reflecting the changing dynamics in Kabul.

One US Navy SEAL died and another was critically injured while training in a pool at a Virginia military base, according to a Navy spokesman. The incident occurred on Friday at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story, where the two members of the Navy's elite sea, air, land teams were found at the bottom of the pool by another service member around 3pm local time. The names of the SEALS were withheld pending notification of next of kin. Both were assigned to Naval Special Warfare Group Two, which contains SEAL teams. The sailors were swimming in lap lanes and were not wearing gear at the time. One was pronounced dead, and the second is listed in critical condition. An investigation into the incident is ongoing.

NBC, the broadcasting giant, has transported their entire Premier League production from their HQ in Stamford, Connecticut, to England for this weekend's round of matches. This move reflects NBC's increased interest in the Premier League and its live rights to show matches in the United States. The move comes after NBC has more than doubled US interest in England's elite division in the past two years, with some 32 million Americans watching at least one top-flight English game live in 2012-13. The move includes NBC host Rebecca Lowe, former Wimbledon midfielder Robbie Earle, and retired MLS star Kyle Martino, who will also be at the Manchester derby at Old Trafford on Sunday and at Anfield for Liverpool-Newcastle on Monday.

Ed Miliband will do "more damage to the country than he did to his brother," Boris Johnson said during a live TV debate, accusing him of potentially stabbing the country in the back by forming a deal with the SNP to gain power.

A prisoner in Oregon, Dustin Irons, was slapped with an extra 30 days behind bars for dropping his trousers and flashing a judge during a court hearing. The judge sentenced him to an additional 30 days for contempt of court. Irons, 26, was arrested for trashing a hotel room and assaulting people inside. He was known as a difficult inmate who needed two officers and handcuffs to be moved.

Jenson Button believes McLaren has improved significantly since the Australian Grand Prix, with both he and Fernando Alonso discovering the car was competitive alongside other midfield runners. Despite Button's retirement during the Malaysian Grand Prix, the team's progress was noted, and they are now comparing themselves with the Force Indias, Saubers, and Lotuses. Button acknowledges that the entire team, including Honda, still has a long way to go, but he is pleased with the team's basic car and the progress made.

A hospital in Western Australia, Fiona Stanley, was found to have blood and bone fragments on supposedly sanitized medical instruments, leading to its medical service provider, Serco, being stripped of its contract and fined. The hospital has been found to continue operating with poorly sanitized instruments, raising concerns about patient safety.

Becca Litchfield and Dale, who chose to forgo their dream wedding to pay for IVF, have welcomed twins and found a way to say their "I do's." The couple, from Nottingham, won a wedding competition and were able to have the white wedding they had always wanted.

A family-friendly coffee shop in Omaha, Nebraska, had its Facebook page hacked and flooded with pornography after an employee clicked on a malicious link in an email. The hack lasted for 24 hours, with the page being replaced with adult cartoons similar to those posted on other brands. The company issued an apology and removed the content, but it was not until a day later that Facebook was contacted to regain control of the account.

A young Shibu Inu puppy at an American Kennel Club center in the United States was filmed squeaking and squawking after meeting a young husky dog, attempting to bark at its new companion. The video shows the puppies being held in the air by their respective handlers and one of the dogs making a high-pitched whining sound. The Shibu Inu then begins vocalising with a yappy bark before the husky responds. The video ends with the husky losing interest slightly and chewing on its handler's sleeve.

Liam Plunkett, an experienced English seamer, is preparing to lead England in a Test series against the West Indies. He has returned to the England fold after a minor injury and is determined to use his pace to win the series. Plunkett is competing for a place in the team with Barbados-born Chris Jordan and the uncapped Mark Wood. He aims to bowl fast and ruffle batsmen, and is confident that he can earn his place in the team.

Paul Smith, a boxer from Liverpool, is set to face Andre Ward in a unification fight for the WBA super-middleweight title. Smith, who has lost two previous title defenses to Arthur Abraham, is seen as a potential warm-up opponent for Carl Froch, who is ranked among the top five pound-for-pound boxers. The WBA has ordered Ward and Froch to meet in a unification fight, with Froch willing to travel to the UK if Ward returns the favor by coming to the US. Smith is the preferred opponent for Ward, who sees him as the ideal warm-up for a rematch with Carl Froch.

Tyrus Byrd, the first African American mayor of Parma, Missouri, was sworn in last week but faced a significant departure of city employees, including five police officers, the city attorney, clerk, and water treatment supervisor. The resignations were attributed to "safety concerns," and residents rallied behind Byrd, who believes the election of an African American mayor should be celebrated rather than focusing on the departures. The town, with a population of 713, has experienced a surge in crime, and the police force, despite being larger than needed, rarely patrols the streets.

Manchester City midfielder Yaya Toure will not be forced out of the club but is set to become available this summer. The Ivorian, who has played a major role in City's recent trophy-winning period, is content with his current contract and is fully committed to the team. Inter Milan is interested in Toure, but his huge wages make a move difficult. City will resist any attempt by Valencia to pull out of a £24 million deal for Alvaro Negredo to fund a move for Radamel Falcao.

A new study claims that more than two-thirds of people taking antidepressants may not actually have depression, challenging the common belief that these drugs are prescribed for clinical depression. The study, published in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, found that 69% of antidepressant users did not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder. Researchers also discovered that 38% of those taking antidepressants did not meet the criteria for other psychiatric disorders such as obsessive compulsive disorder, panic disorder, social phobia, or generalized anxiety disorder. The study, conducted by U.S. investigators, concluded that many individuals prescribed antidepressants may not have met the criteria for mental disorders. The findings raise questions about the effectiveness and appropriateness of antidepressant use, especially in the absence of clear evidence-based indications.

Doris Fuller, the mother of a mentally ill daughter who killed herself, has revealed how her daughter's bipolar disorder and psychosis led to her death. Fuller wrote about her daughter's life in a long article for the Washington Post, describing how her illness went undiagnosed until her early 20s and how her daughter lived with an incurable disease that filled her head with devils that eventually drove her to suicide. Fuller said her daughter was the bravest person she had ever known and that her suicide doesn't change that.

A 10-year-old boy named Koby Hodder nearly died after suffering a cardiac arrest during a game of British Bulldog at his school playground. He collapsed and lost consciousness after his heart stopped for 12 minutes. Koby was later diagnosed with the same heart condition as footballer Fabrice Muamba, who had a similar cardiac arrest in 2012. Teachers at Koby's school performed CPR until paramedics arrived, who used a defibrillator to save his life. The incident has led to calls for the game to be banned as it is considered dangerous and can lead to injuries.

Baroness Hale of Richmond, Britain's most senior female judge, has proposed reforms to England and Wales' divorce laws, aiming to remove the need for allegations of adultery and blame in most matrimonial disputes. She wants to see bitterness taken out of most disputes, encouraging couples to sort out arrangements for children and money before obtaining a divorce. The reforms would involve a one-year "cooling off period" after declaring that their marriage has permanently broken down, during which they would be encouraged to resolve these issues. This proposal aims to make the divorce process more equitable and less reliant on fault-based claims.

Tottenham Hotspur is considering building a state-of-the-art stadium with a retractable pitch that could accommodate an NFL franchise. The stadium, set to be completed for the 2018-19 season, would feature a synthetic surface beneath a NFL-style pitch and could house up to 70 players. The NFL is expected to have a permanent franchise in London within five years, and teams are testing logistics for their three games at Wembley this autumn. Tottenham's new stadium, with a capacity of 65,000, is seen as more suitable for NFL requirements than Wembley's 90,000 seats. The NFL is keeping its options open, but Tottenham's proposed design could be a significant blow to the Football Association, which also sees the NFL as a lucrative partner for Wembley.

U.S. senators have written to FIFA, urging the organization to remove Russia as host of the 2018 World Cup due to its role in the Ukraine crisis and occupation of Crimea. The senators, including John McCain, have called for economic sanctions against Russia and the condemnation of its regime. FIFA president Sepp Blatter announced Russia as the host nation for the 2018 World Cup. England is planning a bid to host the 2028 World Cup, while the FA has decided not to bid for FIFA tournaments while Blatter is still in power.

Universal announced that the sequel to the box office blockbuster "Fifty Shades of Grey" will hit theaters on February 10, 2017, and February 9, 2018. Niall Leonard, married to the author of the "Fifty Shades" trilogy, will write the script for the second film. James, who has been credited with keeping a strong amount of creative control, is no longer directing the sequel.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis will receive a hero's welcome when he returns to Crystal Palace, but he must wonder if he'll ever be successful at the right end of the Premier League, given his poor overall record as a Premier League manager. Pulis has never finished in the top half of the Premier League, and if Swansea City doesn't drop lower than 10th, he will be the only manager in the Premier League with more than 12 months experience who has never finished higher than 11th. Pulis has a proud record of never being relegated, but his current record of 33 points is still seven points above the bottom three, and his final five fixtures after the weekend come against Liverpool, Manchester United, Chelsea, and Arsenal, which may not be enough to secure his place in the top half of the Premier League.

Fenerbahce, the Turkish football club, has called for the suspension of the Turkish championship following a gun attack on their team bus during a match against Caykur Rizespor. The bus was attacked as it drove to the airport after a match in Turkey's Super Lig. The injured driver, who had a head wound, was taken to hospital. Fenerbahce believes the attack is not solved and a suspension of the championship is inevitable. The club has posted pictures of the damaged bus, including shattered windows and blood on the driver's seat and steering wheel.

A massive snowstorm swept over Everest Base Camp, trapping climbers and locals in a deadly avalanche that killed at least 17 people and injured dozens. The disaster occurred on Saturday, with aftershocks complicating rescue efforts and leaving hundreds stranded in higher camps. Helicopters rescued climbers and Sherpas from Camp 1, with estimates of 200 people trapped in the higher camps.

Gregory Margolin, a 16-year-old Jewish recruit in the Soviet Red Army during World War II, survived the war and later settled in Ukraine. Now, decades later, he finds himself in the middle of a new war in Eastern Ukraine. Margolin, who had survived one war, was able to survive another, even as a stray missile hit his house, killing his daughter. He and his family fled to Israel, where they are now living in a refugee center set up by the International Fellowship of Christians and Jews. Margolin's granddaughter, Liora, says they felt safe in Donetsk, but they prayed for their safety. The article highlights the ongoing conflict in Eastern Ukraine and the impact of war on individuals and families.

John Carver, Newcastle United's assistant manager, is eager to take charge of the club against Sunderland on Sunday, following a loss to the team in a previous derby match. Gullit, Newcastle's former manager, made controversial decisions in 1999, including leaving out star players Duncan Ferguson and Alan Shearer, which led to the team's defeat. Carver believes a positive result could help him secure the head coach position beyond the season.

The Reverend Al Sharpton delivered a sermon and addressed the Walter Scott situation on Sunday morning in North Charleston, South Carolina. He spoke at Charity Missionary Baptist Church and addressed the Scott case and the need for reform around national policing legislation. Elected officials and police from North Charleston were in attendance, including Mayor Keith Summey, Sheriff Al Cannon, Senator Marlon Kimpson, and SCLC Leader Michael Steele. Sharpton wrote on Facebook that he joined Mayor Summey, Sheriff Al Cannon, Senator Marlon Kimpson, SCLC Leader Michael Steele, North Charleston Police Chief Eddie Driggers, and Assistant Police Chief Reggie Burgess. He said that when an officer is wrong, they should protest, but when they are right, they should have the same courage to say they are right. He also said that North Charleston, known as a place of intolerance, could be the place that could set a new tone in policing all over the United States.

Brendan Rodgers will remind Raheem Sterling of his responsibilities after the Liverpool youngster hit the headlines for the wrong reasons before scoring the opener in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United. Sterling, who is unwilling to sign a new contract at Anfield, has been videoed passing out after allegedly inhaling nitrous oxide, also known as 'hippy crack', and on Sunday was pictured puffing on a shisha pipe. The 20-year-old faces a club investigation and potential disciplinary action over his behaviour, and Liverpool manager Rodgers now says he will take time to talk to his rising star about what being a professional entails.

Labour received more than £1 million in union donations between April 6 and April 12, boosting their election war chest, while the Conservatives received £492,512. Unions gave more than £700,000 to Labour, with Unison and Unite contributing the most. The Liberal Democrats received £50,000, and Ukip £8,000. This financial support is seen as a potential threat to David Cameron and Ed Miliband's campaign.

West Midlands Police were called to Manchester Airport after passengers on a Qatar Airways flight became disruptive and kicked off during a delay caused by strong winds, leading to a second call for officers two hours later. The flight was diverted to Birmingham, where passengers were stranded for five hours before being allowed to disembark and bused to Manchester. Qatar Airways apologized for the delay, which occurred due to strong winds preventing the aircraft from landing at Manchester.

Canadian pop star Justin Bieber will accompany boxing legend Floyd Mayweather Jr. into the ring for their $300 million fight against Manny Pacquiao on Saturday in Las Vegas. Bieber, who has been Mayweather's friend for years, has been asked to lead out the American's entourage at the MGM Grand. Mayweather, who has a 47-0 record, is expected to be the biggest draw of the fight, with the fight being billed as the biggest in history.

The article discusses the closure of Corinthian Colleges Inc., a for-profit college that has been struggling to hold accountable. Corinthian, which once enrolled over 70,000 students, is one of the worst "predator colleges" due to its dubious degrees, high student debt, and reliance on federal student aid. The closure is seen as a positive development in the fight against for-profit colleges. Corinthian's closure will help transition students into legitimate postsecondary schools and reduce the default rate of for-profit college students. The article also mentions the aggressive tactics used by for-profit colleges to enroll students, such as recruiting low-income students and making them take tens of thousands of dollars in federal student loans.

Pep Guardiola has denied a dispute with former Bayern Munich club doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit the club after being blamed for a Champions League defeat by Porto. Muller-Wohlfahrt claimed the bond of trust was damaged, while Guardiola played down the feud, stating it was his decision and injuries were part of football. Muller-Wohlfahrt had worked at Bayern for almost 40 years.

Wladimir Klitschko, the reigning heavyweight champion, is set to make his return to Madison Square Garden in New York for a world title defense against Bryant Jennings. Klitschko, who won Olympic gold in Atlanta in 1996, recalled how the Olympic victory changed his life and inspired him to become a champion. Despite being just a year short of his 40th birthday, Klitschko believes age has no bearing on his ability to continue dominating the heavyweight division.

Jeremy Clarkson, who was fired from Top Gear in March after attacking a producer during filming, has finally spoken out about his dismissal. Clarkson, 54, said he would "miss" fronting the BBC2 show. Former presenter Angela Rippon, who first presented the show 38 years ago, said she would be keen to return to the motoring show if invited back. Lord Hall, the director-general of the BBC, announced that the corporation would not be renewing Clarkson's contract, citing his "crossing of the line."

In a La Liga match, Fabian Orellana of Celta Vigo threw a lump of grass at Sergio Busquets during the closing stages, leading to Orellana being shown a red card. Busquets, angered by the incident, grabbed his eye despite the turf striking him. Referee Inaki Vicandi Garrido awarded a straight red card to Orellana and gave him his marching orders. Barcelona, led by Dani Alves, secured a crucial 1-0 victory against Celta Vigo, while Real Madrid won 9-1 against Granada.

In 2013, three people died and over 200 were injured when a pair of bombs went off within 12 seconds of each other at the Boston Marathon finish line. This year, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, one of the suspects, was convicted of using weapons of mass destruction, bombing a place of public use, conspiracy, and aiding and abetting. The sentencing phase of his trial began on April 21, and the judge warned jurors not to attend the Boston Marathon or any events related to the anniversary. The maximum penalty for several of the charges is death.

Tens of millions of Chinese people marked the Qingming Festival, a three-day holiday, by traveling home to their ancestral villages to clean tombs, burn fake paper money, and leave food and drink for the deceased. The festival, which celebrates the start of spring and the beauty of nature, is one of the 24 Chinese solar terms and falls in the first week of April.

Paul Simon, 73, has topped the UK album chart for the first time in 25 years with his latest release, The Ultimate Collection. The album, which includes 19 tracks from his 50-year career, including hits like "Mrs Robinson" and "50 Ways to Leave Your Lover," has outsold more youthful musicians like Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. Simon's recent tour with Sting is believed to have been the catalyst in helping him reach the top of the charts. This marks his first number one album since The Rhythm of the Saints in 1990.

Iker Casillas, the 33-year-old goalkeeper for Real Madrid, insists he will stay at the club even if David de Gea, a Manchester United player, joins as his replacement. Casillas, who has been at the Bernabeu since 1996, claims he is willing to fight for the No. 1 jersey, despite criticism in recent seasons. The Spanish giants have linked with a move for de Gea, who is also a Manchester United player. Casillas hopes to fulfill his contract and earn the starting position, stating that he will strive and fight for it. Real Madrid is determined to defend their Champions League title, having reached the semi-finals with a 1-0 aggregate victory over Atletico Madrid.

Britain's employment hit a record high of 31 million in the three months to February, with the Conservatives' economic strategy winning international praise from the International Monetary Fund and German finance minister. Rolls-Royce announced its biggest-ever order, worth over £6 billion, for Emirates. Chancellor George Osborne praised the plan, reducing the deficit from £153 billion under Labour in 2009-10 to £90 billion last year, and forecast the UK could return to the black in 2018-19.

SsangYong, a Korean automaker, is launching a new sports utility vehicle (SUV) called Tivoli in the UK, priced under £13,000. The SUV is named after the Italian town of Tivoli, known for its Renaissance architecture and garden. It features a 1.6-liter engine, six-speed manual or automatic transmission, and comes in three trim levels with seven airbags and a five-year unlimited mileage warranty. The Tivoli aims to compete with the Nissan Juke and is expected to double SsangYong's annual UK sales from 2,000 to 4,000 vehicles.

A chef, Sam Longhurst, created a 10-inch, half-kilogram burger at the Whole Damn Farm restaurant in Manchester, England, containing six forms of three different meats and 2,000 calories. The burger, priced at £13. 50, was inspired by a customer's disappointment with a "Cow & Chicken" burger and features two beef patties, homemade bacon jam, ham chunks, a whole fried chicken thigh, barbequed pulled pork, and bacon rashers. The restaurant, Splendid Kitchen, is known for experimenting with cooking at home and creating unusual dishes.

Yeo Valley, a dairy company in North Somerset, has opened its staff canteen to the public, offering a gourmet menu of organic and locally sourced dishes at a subsidised price. The canteen, praised as the world's best staff canteen, features quirky light fittings and high tables and stools, and offers meals such as organic sourdough with Yeo Valley salted butter and a dessert of apple and rhubarb crumble with ice cream or creme fraiche. The canteen's menu changes daily based on the available produce.

Blues legend B.B. King was hospitalized for dehydration, but he is now much better and is back home resting with his grandchildren. King, 89, has used various models of Gibson guitars over the years, and named each one of them Lucille. He was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1987 and has 30 Grammy nominations.

On Easter Sunday, Manhattan's Fifth Avenue was filled with bizarre hats as people celebrated the holiday. The parade featured a mix of conservative and outlandish attire, with some wearing elaborate dioramas inspired by local politicians. The event attracted a diverse crowd, including Christians, Jews, Hindus, agnostics, and atheists. The parade, which has been held since the 1880s, was a departure from its earlier strolling display, with more modern and creative headwear.

Emergency crews in Essex received a call about a person being run over by a car in Epping Forest, but the caller revealed the "victim" was actually a squirrel. This incident is part of a list of 1,248 inappropriate calls received by the East of England ambulance service in the last two years, with front-line crews attending almost half of them. The service advises people to use common sense when calling 999 and to stop and think about the potential consequences of making a prank call.

Chelsea players Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake, along with their teammates Loic Remy and Willian, participated in a football challenge organized by Audi. The challenge involved shooting balls into the boot of a car from close range and sinking them from long range into a convertible Audi. Hazard and Ake won the first round, followed by Hazard and his partner Ake winning the final round. The final challenge involved shooting at cars from long range, with Willian and Remy winning but Remy damaging an Audi with a long-range effort.

Brendan Rodgers criticized Raheem Sterling's advisor, Aidy Ward, for allegedly being manipulated by outside forces, suggesting Sterling would stay at Liverpool if left to make a decision alone. Rodgers sat down with Sterling to discuss the situation, stating that the player's best interest would be served by staying at the club. Sterling rejected a contract extension worth £100,000 a week and has just two years left on his deal at the end of the season.

Rachel Riley, Countdown's co-presenter, was embarrassed on a recent episode when contestants offered up the eight-letter word "erection" as their answer to the word game. Host Nick Hewer struggled to stifle his laughter, while celebrity guest Dr Phil Hammond provided the correct answer. This incident is not the first time Hewer has struggled to contain himself, as he has previously struggled with words like "todgers" and "m*nges." The Countdown show has been running since 1982 and has reached its 6,000th episode.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, who attempted to buy deadly poison on the internet, was spared jail after pleading guilty to trying to commit suicide. The teenager, who cannot be named for legal reasons, was arrested during an anti-terror operation and was sentenced to a 12-month referral order. The case highlights the dangers of the dark web and the importance of vigilance in law enforcement.

Three hours after giving birth to her long-awaited baby girl, Lianne Hindle, a 37-year-old mother-of-four, died at the scandal-hit North Manchester General Hospital in December. The death occurred just months after three babies and one mother died at the same maternity unit. The deaths prompted an investigation, and Lianne's partner, Chris Barnes, has called for action to prevent further tragedies at the hospital.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman, a seven-year-old mother of two, gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Emily, just days after a video surfaced of her training while eight months pregnant. Pittman, who plans to compete in the Beijing World Championships and the 2016 Rio Olympics, continued to train while pregnant with her son Cornelis, who was born seven months after his father. The athlete's coach, Mike Hurst, said she trained every second day and monitored her core temperature throughout her program. Pittman's new daughter was conceived with an IVF donor and is described as her "little miracle."

At least one person died and multiple sailboats capsized during a storm that swept through Dauphin Island, Alabama, during the 57th iteration of the Dauphin Island Regatta. The storm, which rolled through the area around 4 p.m., caused at least four people to go missing. The Coast Guard responded to the capsized vessels and searched through the night. Mayor Jeff Collier confirmed at least one death, but the cause was unknown. The storm was described as severe, with boats becoming distressed and scattered across a wide area of Mobile Bay.

Roseanne Barr, 62, has been diagnosed with macular degeneration and glaucoma, two eye diseases that are getting progressively worse over time and can steal vision. Her doctors haven't provided a timeline, but her symptoms are worsening. Barr said in an interview that she helps relieve the pressure by using marijuana. Macular degeneration is a breakdown of the part of the retina that allows us to see fine details in the center of vision, while glaucoma damages the nerve that connects the retina to the brain. The American Academy of Ophthalmology recommends getting a baseline eye exam when you turn the big 4-0, even if you have perfect vision. There is no cure for either disease, but treatments can delay the progression of early-stage glaucoma and halt further vision loss in advanced cases of macular degeneration.

An Oklahoma jury convicted 17-year-old Chancey Luna of first-degree murder in the 2013 shooting death of Australian college baseball player Christopher Lane, who was killed while jogging in Duncan. Luna was found guilty of the fatal shooting from a passing car, and the jury recommended a life sentence without parole. Luna's defense attorney argued that he meant to scare Lane, but the judge denied a second-degree murder conviction. Luna did not testify, and the defense called only his mother as a witness.

Arsene Wenger insists his record of 12 losses against Jose Mourinho will not affect Arsenal's match against Chelsea at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday. Wenger has drawn five and lost seven of their 12 clashes. Chelsea's strengths include efficient counter-attacks and set-pieces. Arsenal, 10 points behind Chelsea, are on a good run and want to beat Chelsea at home.

Manny Pacquiao, a Filipino boxer, has become one of the most recognizable figures in sports after a series of major fights, including a bout against Floyd Mayweather on Saturday night at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. Pacquiao, who was born into poverty in the Philippines, spent his early career boxing in the Far East before gaining recognition in 2001 when he fought against Lehlo Ledwaba in an IBF world super-bantamweight title fight in Las Vegas. Despite facing challenges, Pacquiao has risen to become a global superstar, having won 10 professional bouts in 1995 and 1996.

A talented young footballer, Jack Grealish, has been photographed inhaling nitrous oxide, a drug that is considered legal but harmful to athletes. The incident, which occurred during a match against Liverpool, highlights the need for athletes to prioritize their health and well-being. Grealish, who has shown exceptional talent, has not yet achieved the level of success he deserves. Wenger's advice to professional athletes to focus on their bodies and avoid substances that slow them down, such as alcohol, is echoed by Grealish's coach.

Sam Barton, a 22-year-old man who underwent £55,000 in cosmetic surgery to resemble reality star Joey Essex, was attacked by a group of men on Easter Monday in Sutton Coldfield, West Midlands. The attack, which included pelted with eggs, followed online abuse and forced Barton to move house. The incident highlights the pressures faced by individuals pursuing a celebrity lifestyle, with Barton admitting to racking up debts of £100,000 on his champagne lifestyle.

An Indiana university was in lockdown late on Friday night after a 'likely prank call' about an armed person near the main administration building. Police said they received a phone call from someone saying that they had stabbed their roommate at the university, was armed with a shotgun and threatening to blow up the administration building. Manchester University had issued a statement advising students at its North Manchester campus, some 36 miles west of Fort Wayne, to shelter in place. The university had continued reposting the shelter in place warning for hours after the original message and had not given the all clear as of 2am.

Edinson Cavani, known as "El Matador," prepares to face Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals at the Parc des Princes. Despite PSG's suspension issues and injuries, Cavani must overcome Barcelona's star-studded lineup to progress beyond the last eight. His goal drought and recent altercation with Laurent Blanc have raised questions about his future in Paris.

Derry Mathews has won the interim WBA lightweight title after defeating Tony Luis in a unanimous points decision at the Echo Arena in Liverpool. Mathews, who saw Richar Abril and Ismael Barroso both pull out of the fight, showcased his relentless style and landed a decent uppercut in the second round. Luis, who was drafted in at the last minute, showed aggression but was deducted points for low blows and head use. Mathews was handed a 114-112, 114-112, 115-112 decision, and the fight was described as thrilling.

Hull FC defeated St Helens 28-20 in a surprise victory, overcoming St Helens' Good Friday exertions. Hull's Jamie Shaul scored the winning try, while St Helens' Jordan Turner scored a try and Tom Makinson added the conversion. The win was Hull's first since their derby defeat to Hull KR on Thursday.

The U.S. Census predicts that the undocumented and documented immigrant population could reach a record high of 51 million by 2023, with immigrants accounting for 14.8% of the U.S. population by 2060. The Center for Immigration Studies reports that immigration will steadily increase over the next 45 years, totaling 64 million immigrants. Without changes to current immigration policy, the total immigrant population in the United States will reach 14.8% of the population by 2023, and immigration will grow almost four times faster than the native-born population. The growth in immigrant population has important implications for workers, schools, infrastructure, congestion, and the environment.

Jack Wilshere made his long-awaited return from injury for Arsenal U21 but could not prevent a 1-0 defeat by Reading's youngsters at the Emirates Stadium. Wilshere was joined by other injury-plagued first-team players including Serge Gnabry and Abou Diaby, who managed to last 56 minutes. However, Reading's Martin Keown's son Niall scored the eventual winner with a header in the opening minutes.

Justin Rose, the English golfer, has fallen outside the world's top 10 after a bruising Florida swing, but he has since made a comeback with a 69 at the Shell Houston Open. Rose hit 17 out of 18 greens in regulation and signed for a 69, the same score as his playing partner, the ever- consistent Jordan Spieth. Rose believes he has done some good work over the past two weeks and feels like he is going in the right direction again. Phil Mickelson enjoyed his best round in months with a 66 on Thursday.

A Mayfair mansion, once a milking parlour, has gone on the market for £25 million. The property, which was built in 2011 after the original structure was demolished, features modern amenities such as an indoor swimming pool, gym, and cinema room. The mansion, which is 8, 139 square feet, is being sold by estate agents Wetherell and Knight Frank.

Bayern Munich's squad is weakened by injuries, but the team's sense of unity is stronger, according to Thomas Muller. The Bavarians, chasing three titles this season, are without key players Arjen Robben, Franck Ribery, Bastian Schweinsteiger, and David Alaba for the Champions League quarter-final against Porto. Muller believes the team's recent games with a decimated squad have helped build a strong unit. Bayern Munich will rely heavily on the scoring prowess of Muller and Robert Lewandowski, who are expected to score goals despite the injuries. The team will face Porto in the Champions League quarter-final, first leg on April 15, followed by a second leg on April 18.

Mercedes team-mates Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton visited the team's Brackley base to discuss strategies for the upcoming Chinese Grand Prix. After being beaten by Sebastian Vettel at the Malaysian Grand Prix, they aimed to collaborate with their team to ensure victory in Shanghai. Rosberg tweeted a picture of him and Hamilton on a flight back from Brackley. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff admitted that Vettel's victory was unexpected and that Ferrari's tactics were spot-on in the hot conditions. The race results showed Vettel winning by 8.5 seconds, with Hamilton and Rosberg finishing third and fourth, respectively. Mercedes now faces the challenge of analyzing why Ferrari's strategy was more effective in the high-temperature conditions.

Oklahoma Governor Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to perform executions with nitrogen gas if lethal injection is ruled unconstitutional or unavailable. The bill, signed on Friday, states that the person will become unconscious within eight to 10 seconds and die a few minutes later from lack of oxygen. This follows a review by the U.S. Supreme Court of Oklahoma's use of lethal injections, which has been put on hold. Fallin reaffirmed her support for the death penalty, stating that Oklahoma executes murderers whose crimes are especially heinous.

Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice in Swansea's 3-1 win over Hull on Saturday, leading the EA Sports' Performance Index with a 52.9 score after another thrilling Premier League match. Gomis, who made a slow start to his career in south Wales, has scored four goals in his last six games. Chelsea's Eden Hazard scored for the Blues, and Manchester United's Ander Herrera scored twice, completing a top four performance in the EA Sports' index.

A Russian freezer trawler sank in the Sea of Okhotsk, killing at least 56 crew members and sinking in just 15 minutes. More than 1,300 people are involved in the massive rescue operation, with 63 survivors rescued so far. The ship, carrying 132 crew members, was unstable due to empty fuel tanks and a lack of ballast. The sinking is believed to have been caused by a fishing net weighing 80 tons being pulled in, which tipped the ship over. The emergency services sent a Mi-8 helicopter to treat and transport rescued crew members to hospitals.

Men with advanced prostate cancer could benefit from a pioneering drug originally meant for women, according to new clinical trials. Olaparib, already used to treat women with breast cancer, showed promise in delaying the progression of prostate cancer in men with genetic defects within their tumours. The drug, known as Lynparza, extended the length of time that patients with advanced prostate cancer lived without their disease getting worse.

Travel photographer Rhiannon Taylor, 29, from Australia, has turned her passion for photography and globetrotting into a successful business by launching the website "In Bed With" to review and photograph the best hotels, beds, pools, and room service around the world. With more than 12, 000 followers on Instagram, Taylor has built relationships with hotels and PR companies, allowing her to stay at exclusive properties and generate further income from featuring them on her site. Taylor has photographed and reviewed hotels in locations such as Indonesia, the US, and Mexico, documenting everything from the best pies to the biggest beds.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was mauled to death by two adult hippos in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park in eastern South Africa. The calf's mother watched in horror as the hippo was flung into the air before being dragged along the surface of the water. The two male hippos had been fighting for some time, and the mother of the calf stayed with her herd, possibly believing it safer to stay out of harm's way herself. The baby stood no chance against the two adults as they brawled in the muddy waters of the nature reserve.

The Football Association will contact QPR and Chelsea after an incident where Branislav Ivanovic was struck on the head by a cigarette lighter thrown from a section of home supporters at Loftus Road. Chelsea players celebrated the winning goal, but objects were thrown onto the pitch, marred by the incident. QPR is reviewing CCTV footage and banning those involved, while Chelsea has a zero-tolerance approach to such behavior.

A young mother and her three children were found murdered in their home in Tisdale, Saskatchewan. The suspect, who had a six-month-old baby with him, was found dead hours later. Police have not released much information, but they say the suspect and victim knew each other. The family's sister described them as "hard working, young family." The family is raising money for their funeral services and has exceeded their initial goal on a GoFundMe page.

Emily Thornberry, a senior Labour politician, lost her frontbench job after tweeting a photo of a house covered in England flags and with a white van outside, while renting out a property she bought from a housing association for £1 million. The incident highlighted Thornberry's hypocrisy in opposing right to buy but not "right to buy to let."

Mike Lane, a 40-year-old huntsman, was beaten by protesters armed with iron bars during an attack on his hunt near Amesbury, Wiltshire. Despite evidence pointing to the identity of the attacker, police dropped the investigation three months later, angering Lane and other hunt supporters. The attack, which took place on January 24, involved protesters spraying hounds with citronella and then attacking Lane with iron bars. The incident has led to calls for the police to be held accountable for not identifying and prosecuting the attackers.

Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes, 21, insists he has no intention of leaving the club this summer. He says remaining at the Mestalla is his preferred option.
