Gomes has netted four times in 25 La Liga appearances since leaving Benfica last summer, helping Valencia to fourth place in the table. Reports have linked Gomes with a move to Premier League duo Manchester United and Chelsea, but he denies being contacted by Chelsea. Gomes says he just thinks about spending the next season in Spain, and his agent is not aware of any opportunity.

An Australian teenager, Audrey Pekin, has accused a man named Henry Alafu of raping her twice in Bali while on holiday with her family. Alafu allegedly lured Pekin to his remote home and then attacked her in a taxi as she tried to flee. Pekin claims that Alafu locked the door and forced her to the bed, where he allegedly attacked her. The incident occurred at the Bounty Bar in Kuta, where Pekin and Alafu had previously met. Pekin's family believes Alafu is from Nigeria, but the Indonesian police have not yet arrested him.

PETA has teamed up with Ashley James, a former Made in Chelsea star, to launch an anti-fur campaign against Harvey Nichols, a department store that previously abandoned its ten-year anti-fur policy. The campaign features James holding a fake skinned fox, with the slogan "Harvey Nichols: Here's the Rest of Your Fur Coat." Harvey Nichols, which has 12 locations worldwide, previously reintroduced its fur-free policy last year. The store's current range includes coyote fur from Canada Goose, raccoon fur from Charlotte Simone, and rabbit pelts from Vince. Ashley James, who leads a mostly vegan lifestyle, believes that people should make informed decisions about their purchases. Harvey Nichols claims to be committed to sustainable and responsible practices, including ethical trading.

Chile's President Michelle Bachelet signed a law on Monday allowing civil unions between people of the same sex, joining several South American neighbors in recognizing the unions. The new law, which will take effect in six months, will give legal weight to cohabiting relationships between two people of the same sex and between a man and a woman. The Chilean government estimates that around 2 million people will be able to benefit from the change, which aims to end discrimination faced by common-law couples.

Chelsea are on track to become the most dominant title-winners in Premier League history, leading the table for 257 days as of April 10, 2005/06, surpassing Manchester United's record of 262 days. The Blues are currently seven points ahead of their title rivals, with their next three games against QPR, Manchester United, and Arsenal crucial to their chances.

Cape Verde, a small Portuguese former colony with a population of 500,000, is tapping into its rich musical heritage to boost its economy. The country, which lacks natural resources, is promoting music and culture as a key sector for growth. The Kriol Jazz Festival, celebrating its seventh edition, has attracted international artists and brought people from around the world to share in the music. The festival has become a symbol of Cape Verde's cultural identity and economic potential.

An old hoax video showing a wave rider surfing in front of the Sydney Opera House went viral again after being reposted by other sources. The video, originally uploaded by Sydney radio duo Fitzy and Wippa on Tuesday morning, was quickly pointed out by YouTube commenters for inaccuracies such as the appearance of rocks around the Opera House and the cardboard-like appearance of the man in the final shot. Wave experts vowed it was a sham, and Ben Macartney, a swell forecaster, stated that it was theoretically impossible for ocean swells to break that far inside the Harbour.

Reading, the beaten FA Cup semi-finalists, lost to Birmingham in a 1-0 Championship match at the Madejski Stadium. Clayton Donaldson scored the winning goal in the 78th minute. Reading's Adam Federici, who made a costly mistake against Arsenal, was retained for the match. Birmingham, aiming to improve on their poor recent record, dominated the game but could not capitalize on their chances.

David Luiz, a key player for Paris Saint-Germain (PSG), has been ruled out of the Champions League quarter-final against Barcelona due to a hamstring injury sustained during a match against Marseille. The 27-year-old Brazilian defender will miss at least four weeks, potentially impacting PSG's title defense and their upcoming match. Luiz's absence could force the team to play eight matches without him. PSG currently leads Ligue One with a one-point advantage over Lyon.

The return of Game of Thrones has led to a significant increase in internet piracy, with more than 100,000 illegal downloads per day reported by anti-piracy firm Irdeto. The unauthorized downloads of the show's episodes, which span from seasons one to four, have surged by 45% year-on-year, with Brazil and France being the top countries for illegal downloads. The unauthorized downloads of Game of Thrones episodes have prompted HBO to announce a new internet streaming service, HBO Now, in an attempt to curb piracy and recapture revenue.

Leicester City will host West Ham United in a Premier League match on Saturday. Leicester's Matt Upson is out with an Achilles injury, while West Ham's Winston Reid is back after a hamstring issue. Leicester has won just one of their last 10 home matches, while West Ham has won their last seven away games against the Foxes.

A controversial statue of Lucille Ball, the beloved comedian from "I Love Lucy," has sparked outrage in Celoron, New York, where locals have called for its removal due to its unflattering depiction. The statue, based on a moment from the show, has attracted over 600 likes on a Facebook page titled 'We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue.' The anonymous creator, who describes Ball as "an amazing comedienne and stunning beauty," argues that the statue should be more like those created for other iconic comedians. Artist Dave Poulin, who created the statue, has declined to comment, stating that it looks like a "monster" and is frightening at night. The town has tried to honor Ball with other memorials, but this statue has become a source of controversy.

A 43-year-old woman named Sharon Smith, who was overweight and struggled to fit into a plane seat during a 11-hour flight, lost nearly half her body weight after deciding to take up running. She joined a slimming club and started running, which led to her weight loss. Smith's weight loss began just under two years ago when she joined Weight Watchers Online, but she did not weigh herself immediately. After six months of following the plan, she was 18st 6lb, and she estimates that when she started, she was 'way over 20st' and a size 26. Smith's weight loss continued after quitting her job to go freelance and work from home, and she started standing for the entire flight with her iPod in.

One new mother, Nicola Bonn, started a blog called Upfront Mama to share her experiences of becoming a first-time mother and the challenges she faced. Her candid account of raising her 14-month-old daughter, Poppy, went viral, and she wrote about the overwhelming opinions and self-doubt new mothers often experience. Bonn decided to stop justifying herself and apologizing for her decisions, believing that everyone has an opinion and it can be overwhelming for new mothers.

Two teenage boys, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, from Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, are feared to have traveled to Syria to join ISIS. Hassan is believed to be related to Hammaad Munshi, who was arrested at 15 for his role in a terrorist plot. The families are in shock and worry about their safety. The boys, who were on a school trip, used the Easter holidays to flee Britain.

Stephanie Scott, a beloved school teacher from Leeton, was brutally murdered just days before her much-anticipated wedding. Her father, Robert Scott, described the grief as especially painful due to the joy she had brought to others. The wedding was originally scheduled for Saturday, but the day before, her body was found in nearby bushland. The venue, decorated with yellow balloons and flowers, was a stark contrast to the planned wedding. The family is now preparing for Stephanie's funeral, with many of the wedding plans and decorations left behind.

Southampton is interested in signing Dutch winger Tonny Vilhena, who is eager to leave Feyenoord this summer. Southampton's boss, Ronald Koeman, is also considering bringing in midfielder Jordy Clasie and looking to make Eljero Elia's loan from Werder Bremen permanent. Koeman is aiming to bolster his squad ahead of potential European qualification.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture with beanbags in the library of Ickworth House, Suffolk, in an experiment designed to encourage visitors to "dwell and take in the atmosphere." This move was met with outrage from heritage experts who called it "misguided." The Trust has since announced that similar experiments will take place at nine other of its venues around the country. Art historian Bendor Grosvenor criticized the move as "patronizing nonsense," arguing that it is not the best way to attract new audiences. The National Trust's director of strategy, curatorship, and external affairs, Simon Murray, defended the experiment, stating that each house is treated appropriately and that the Trust presents each in context.

Former Prime Minister John Howard was photographed standing on the footpath outside the Sydney Conservatorium of Music with a flat tyre, while his driver changed it. Felicity Waterford, who was waiting for her daughter at the Conservatorium, offered assistance and took a selfie with Howard. This incident occurred weeks after Liberal MP Christopher Pyne was challenged to change a tyre on national television.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has admitted that midfielder Joey Barton "probably had a point" about the team's performance during a 2-0 defeat to Queens Park Rangers earlier this season. Pulis, who was leading Gillingham in the Second Division play-off final in 1999, recalled his own experience of being 2-0 up but losing on penalties. Pulis praised the team's performances and hopes to continue that success in their upcoming match against QPR.

A new species of monkey, the Bouvier's red colobus monkey, has been discovered in the remote rain forests of the Democratic Republic of Congo. The primate, which was previously thought to be extinct, was captured on camera in Ntokou-Pikounda National Park. The discovery proves that the species is not extinct and researchers hope to study the monkey to learn more about it.

Kim Kardashian and her family, including her husband Kanye West and daughter North, visited Armenia for an eight-day stay, primarily to explore the country and its cultural landmarks. The visit was a rock star welcome, and they stayed at the Armenia Marriott Hotel Yerevan, which is located on Republic Square. The city is known for its Opera House, which is a must-visit place, and its cultural and economic significance. The Kardashian-West crew had the assistance of bodyguards and police, and the visit was documented by camera crews.

A British couple, Patrick and Valerie Jubb, are facing legal battles in southern Spain over a luxury bed and breakfast they once operated. The couple, who purchased the property in 2008, are attempting to sell it but are now trapped in the property due to illegal alterations made by a previous owner. The town hall claims the first floor, kitchen, and pool were illegally built in 1994, despite the couple obtaining a certificate stating there were no infractions when they bought the property. The Jubbs, who are retired and want to return to the UK, are facing the potential loss of their property and are seeking legal advice.

Despite expectations, Apple's iPhone sales in the first quarter of 2015 surpassed analysts' forecasts, with the company reporting a 40% increase from the previous year, totaling over 61 million units sold. This marks a 72% growth in China, where the company has ambitious expansion plans. The iPhone's dominance in the market, driven by strong sales and customer response, has propelled Apple to a $200 billion cash balance, up from $150 billion a year ago.

A 3-year-old girl, Elisa Tyler, has been plagued by disturbing nightmares and daytime visions about a white van, which her father believes may have something to do with the crash that killed her mother, Natali Castellanos-Tyler, in an SUV accident. The girl's father, Craig Tyler, said she has been having nightmares and daytime visions about the accident, and he believes that the white van in her dreams 'hurt' her and her car. The crash occurred in Virginia two months ago, and the driver of the white box truck briefly slowed down and turned his head back to look at the damaged car, but then took off without waiting for police to arrive.

Researchers at New York University have discovered that the brain can remember 'neutral' or boring events more easily when they are tied to an emotion. This finding suggests that the brain has the ability to store information that seems inconsequential at the time in case it becomes useful later on. The study focused on how the brain stores memories for emotionally neutral events, such as neutral events like a lunch date, and how emotion affects memory retention.

Jahnae Jackson, the girlfriend of a teenager with a life-threatening brain tumour, has raised over $80,000 for his life-saving surgery. The 18-year-old has put her psychology studies on hold to care for her boyfriend, who is paralysed and unable to dress himself. The surgery, performed by renowned neurosurgeon Dr. Charlie Teo, is expected to save his life, but he will need rehabilitation for some time. The community in the small town of Casino, NSW, has shown overwhelming support for the couple, with Jahnae raising the funds through a GoFundMe page.

Nedum Onuoha, a 28-year-old QPR centre-back, is being targeted by Hull City, Everton, and West Ham United, among other clubs, as the club considers streamlining its squad. Onuoha, who has 15 months left on his contract, played in QPR's crucial 4-1 win over West Bromwich Albion at the Hawthorns. Onuoha is also being considered by Stoke manager Mark Hughes and West Ham. Additionally, Hull City is showing interest in West Bromwich Albion's Victor Anichebe, who is likely to be sold this summer.

Researchers at Yale University have discovered regional variations in English sentence structure across the United States, with some states using phrases like "here's you a piece of pizza" or "this glass needs washed" that are not commonly used elsewhere. The study, which involved nationwide surveys, found that people in the South are more likely to use presentative sentences, while those in the North are less likely to do so. The researchers hope that this information can help improve communication across the country.

A Canadian man named Kalman Kallai took a rocking chair on a 9-day journey across Canada, from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia, to enjoy the scenery and see more of his country. He used an online advertisement site to find a free rocking chair and attached it to a trailer. The video shows him sitting in the chair, posing, and making gestures, including mimicking planes and waving at cows. The journey was a bonding experience for Kallai and his dad, and they met with their dad's youth stories.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood revealed a "win bonus" of sweets and chocolate to six-year-old fan Charlie Pye, who applied for the club's hotseat after Paul Lambert was sacked. Sherwood joked that Pye's win bonus would be sweets and chocolate, and revealed a Twix multi-pack under the desk.

Kell Brook, a world boxing champion, enjoyed a night out at the Premier League Darts in his home town of Sheffield. Dave Chisnall won both of his games in week 10 to move onto 17 points in second place. Chisnall said it was a confidence boost to beat the world champion and that he felt good up on stage. Chisnall is second in the Premier League table behind Michael van Gerwen, who snatched a 7-5 victory against Stephen Bunting. Raymond van Barneveld beat Phil Taylor 7-2 to inflict Taylor's fourth defeat in five.

Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Marco Verratti has praised Zlatan Ibrahimovic for his essential role in the club, emphasizing his off-pitch contributions. Ibrahimovic, who has scored 17 goals for the team this season, is unavailable for the Champions League quarter-final second leg against Barcelona due to suspension.

The Ministry of Defence accidentally published a secret RAF aerodrome manual containing vital GPS coordinates and runway depth information on their website, which could be used by Argentina to prepare an invasion of the Falkland Islands. The information was accessible to anyone and could cripple Britain's ability to defend the islands. The MoD admitted the manual was available on the internet but disabled the link. The Falkland Islands are defended by modern Eurofighter Typhoon aircraft, supported by Rapier surface-to-air missiles and 1,200 troops.

Paul Anderson, Huddersfield Giants coach, hopes to improve his team's offensive performance to match their defensive efficiency as they aim to climb back up the Super League ladder. The Giants have fallen from third to ninth after losing all three games over the Easter period. Anderson attributes the team's poor start to the fast-paced nature of the season and acknowledges the need to find their offensive groove. If Huddersfield wins their next game, they could leapfrog Catalans Dragons, who have the best defensive record in the league.

Planners in Windsor have approved two Costa coffee shops, one of which is less than 500 yards from the other, in a residential area. This has led to concerns from residents who believe it will lead to an overabundance of coffee shops in the area.

The British Veterinary Association (BVA) has withdrawn its support for the controversial shooting of free-running badgers in two four-year pilot culls in Somerset and Gloucestershire, stating that controlled trapping and shooting is more humane and effective. The BVA still supports badger culling to tackle tuberculosis in cattle. The Environment Secretary has promised to roll out more culls across the country if the Conservatives win the election, with the Government's strategy including cattle movement controls, vaccination, and culling.

Geoff Barrow, the founder of Portishead, has accused streaming services of giving his band's music away for free, saying his band received just £1,700 in royalties despite 34 million plays. Barrow, who also runs the Invada record label, believes younger artists are getting a poor deal and wants musicians to be paid more. The ongoing row between artists, music labels, and streaming companies has led to Jay-Z launching his own service, Tidal, which aims to give musicians a better deal. Tidal streams at 1,411 kilobytes per second and offers a higher share of the revenue compared to Spotify.

Game of Thrones fans who did not want to wait for the show's fifth season premiere leaked the first four episodes online, which are scheduled to debut tonight. The episodes, titled "The Wars to Come," "The House of Black and White," "High Sparrow," and "The Sons of the Harpy," have been downloaded more than 550,000 times as of early Sunday morning, making it the most illegally downloaded program in the world. HBO is actively investigating how the breach occurred, and the series is the most pirated in the world, with Brazil and France being the top two countries by illegal downloads.

A best man at his brother's wedding in Melbourne composed an emotional song to use as his speech, touching the guests and being viewed over 100,000 times online. Daniel Buccheri, 25, sang "Stay With Me" to his brother Adrian, who met his love on the internet. The unique speech, performed at Poet's Lane in Sherbrooke, was dedicated to his brother and his new wife Sarah, touching the audience with stories of their love and life journey.

Zara Phillips, the Queen's granddaughter, has revealed her fitness routine after giving birth to her daughter Mia. She started hitting the exercise bike every morning before her daughter woke up, aiming to regain her fitness after pregnancy. Phillips, who is vying for a place on Team GB at the Rio Olympics, is committed to a strict exercise and diet regime to get back in shape.

Raheem Sterling's interview, in which he said he was not ready to sign a new contract at Liverpool, has angered fans and potentially changed their opinion of him. The interview was seen as ill-timed and unprofessional, and it has been speculated that Sterling's agent may have engineered the situation. Sterling returned to training ahead of the weekend's game against Arsenal and was linked with a move to Arsenal. Liverpool fans have a popular mantra that no player is bigger than the club, but they are now of the belief that if Sterling wants to go, he is welcome to.

In 1996, Barcelona's 1996-97 Spanish Super Cup-winning team included current PSG coach Laurent Blanc, current Porto coach Julen Lopetegui, and four of the current Champions League managers from the same club at the same time. The team featured Luis Enrique, Jose Mourinho, Pep Guardiola, and Albert Ferrer, who later became Cordoba coach.

Former Manchester United legend Eric Cantona has declared Paris Saint-Germain forward Javier Pastore the best player in the world, challenging the opinions of Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. Cantona, who won the Ballon d'Or in 1993, praised Pastore's creativity and passing skills, stating that he can do things that other players don't know. Despite statistics showing Pastore's goals and assists, Cantona's assessment is based on his personal observation of Pastore's performances.

Lorenzo Simon, 34, was found guilty of murder for killing his tenant Michael Spalding, 39, by dismembering his body and disposing of the parts in a canal. The trial took 15 hours and involved a jury that decided unanimously. Simon, with girlfriend Michelle Bird, 35, was cleared of murder but found guilty of manslaughter. The case involved dismembering the body with a hacksaw and stuffing the parts into suitcases, which were later found in the canal.

Two county councils, Essex and Gloucestershire, have implemented "loneliness maps" to identify areas where residents are most vulnerable to social isolation. The maps are based on public health factors linked to loneliness, such as age, living alone, mental health issues, lack of a car, and low income. Gloucestershire's council surveyed residents to identify those who rarely speak to their neighbors, are unsatisfied with their social life, and say they don't have someone to talk to. The maps are used to target local people who need help the most. The Campaign to End Loneliness recommends the maps as a way to treat the problem across the country.

Dedicated waitress Judy Eddingfield, 65, celebrated her 50th anniversary at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, the only job she has ever had or ever wanted. She remembers when French fries and a classic Coca-Cola cost just 65 cents, and her first day on the job when she spilled a shake all over a woman's fur coat. Eddingfield has been providing top-notch service for 60 years, and her favorite memory was when Jerry Mathers and Tony Dow of the television series 'Leave It to Beaver' came to eat there in the late 1970s.

Former England captain Mike Gatting believes Kevin Pietersen should not return to the international set-up immediately, even if he scores runs for Surrey. Pietersen, who returned to the LV= County Championship, scored 19 runs against Glamorgan but has been criticized for not playing well in recent matches. Gatting suggests that England's other top players, Gary Ballance, Ian Bell, and Joe Root, should play well before Pietersen is considered for an England recall. Gatting also expresses concern that Pietersen might not get a chance to play if Cook, England's captain, fails to score runs against West Indies.

A 17-year-old college student, Caleb Benn, developed an app called "Uploader for Instagram" that allows users to upload photos directly from their computer to the popular photo-sharing platform. The app, which is priced at $4.99, has been generating $1,000 a day in revenue. However, Instagram has filed a lawsuit against Benn, claiming that his app violates the company's terms of service. Benn has until Monday to fix the app, but he believes doing so would make it pointless. The app, called Layout, allows users to create collages with up to nine images and 11 combinations, and it has four main features: Faces, Mirroring, Photo Booth, and Previews.

Most companies in South Korea have hoesik (dinner with co-workers) at least once a month, sometimes weekly. Foreign business travelers find it challenging to participate due to intense pressure to drink. Koreans view drinking as a way to get to know someone, and it's considered rude to refuse. Drinking etiquette varies, with seniors pouring first and everyone saying "Gunbae!" to chug the entire glass. Avoiding offense involves identifying the "higher" person in the relationship and following rules like not having an empty glass.

The Duke of Kent, 79, was admitted to Aberdeen Royal Infirmary after suffering a dislocated hip during an Easter trip to Balmoral, the Queen's private residence in Royal Deeside, Aberdeenshire. He was successfully treated and is expected to leave hospital later today. The Duke, who became the Duke of Kent at age six, is the son of Prince George, the younger brother of King George VI and King Edward VIII. He is the country's top Freemason and has performed numerous royal engagements.

Meter Maids, a 50-year-old tradition of Surfers Paradise, Queensland, have been called into question by local business owners who believe the outdated and outdated practice of young women dressed in gold bikinis walking the main tourist strip and placing money into expired meters is no longer relevant due to advancements in parking meter technology. The Gold Coast Chamber of Commerce president, Peter Yared, argues that Meter Maids are now a business and not a public service, while local business owners claim the group is no longer providing a service and is violating anti-touting laws. The controversy has split the Gold Coast community, with some calling for the end of the tradition, while others defend it as a quintessentially part of the Gold Coast and Surfers Paradise experience.

Greece has denied it will miss a repayment of £330 million to the International Monetary Fund, claiming it will make the payment on time. Deputy finance minister Dimitris Mardas stated that Greece will in fact pay on April 9. Greece has drawn up plans to introduce a parallel drachma currency to pay domestic bills, but this has been denied by the country. The International Monetary Fund is due to repay a £330 million loan on April 9, and there are concerns that Greece may default on the payment.

Turkey has blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after refusing to remove pictures of a prosecutor held during an armed siege last week, citing the images as "deeply upset" the hostage's family. The prosecutor, Mehmet Selim Kiraz, died in hospital after being taken hostage by the Revolutionary People's Liberation Party-Front. The DHKP-C is considered a terrorist group by Turkey, the European Union, and the US.

A young Star Wars fan named Colin Gilpatric wrote a heartfelt letter to George Lucas, the creator of the franchise, asking if Jedi Knights could marry. Lucasfilm responded positively, stating that marriage would not lead to becoming a Sith and that it would be a good path for a Jedi. Colin was overjoyed to receive the letter and was able to receive a package of Star Wars merchandise.

Wisconsin defeated Kentucky in the NCAA Tournament semi-finals, ending Kentucky's unbeaten streak and advancing to the Final Four. Frank Kaminsky scored 20 points and 11 rebounds for Wisconsin, while Kentucky's unbeaten season was brought to an end. The Badgers will face Duke in the final.

Vince Neil, a member of the rock band Mötley Crüe, was criticized for his rendition of the American national anthem at a football game in Las Vegas. His performance was deemed disrespectful by some, while others praised his ability to perform the song. The incident highlights the controversy surrounding the national anthem and the various interpretations of its meaning.

A video of a man hitting his brother unconscious with a single punch has been released for the first time, with the brother facing potential prison time. The incident occurred during a sentence hearing in Sydney, Australia, where the brother pleaded guilty to grievous bodily harm. The video shows the brothers arguing in a bar before a fight escalated, with the brother hitting his brother unconscious. The brother is now facing potential jail time, and the court is considering whether to suspend a full-time jail term.

The family of conjoined twin sisters Faith and Hope Howie, who died 19 days after birth due to a rare condition, were devastated to find their gravesite cleared of mementos and thrown in the rubbish by cemetery staff. The Howies had built a small shrine at the site, but when they returned to retrieve their daughters' belongings, everything had been removed apart from a bunch of flowers. The staff had not been notified of the cleaning process, and the Howies were only able to retrieve about 25% of their memorabilia.

Lord Neuberger, the President of the Supreme Court, suggested that Muslim women should be allowed to wear a full-face veil while appearing in court, as it shows respect towards different customs. This suggestion comes amid uncertainty over the place of Muslim traditional dress in the legal system. Lord Neuberger emphasized the need for judges and courtrooms to be sensitive to the cultural and social habits of those facing them.

Andre Cole, a 52-year-old Missouri inmate, was executed for the 1998 murder of his ex-wife, Anthony Curtis, in a fit of rage over child support payments. Cole was the third convicted killer executed in Missouri this year. The execution took place on Tuesday night at the Eastern Reception, Diagnostic and Correctional Center in Bonne Terre, Missouri. The inmate declined to order a last meal and received the day's inmate tray meal. Governor Jay Nixon expressed condolences to the victims' families.

Prince Harry will fly out of the UK to Australia without seeing his new niece or nephew, as the Duchess of Cambridge is several days overdue for the birth of her second child. Harry, who will be bumped down in the line of succession, had returned briefly to hand out prizes at the London Marathon after engagements in Turkey. The prince is now on a month-long placement with the army and a week-long tour of New Zealand, unable to meet the new royal baby until he returns to the UK in mid-May.

An alleged fraudster named Justin Jackson has been accused of posing as Oprah Winfrey, former Obama aide Reggie Love, and Madonna's manager in an attempt to trick people into giving him jobs, clothes, free food, and jewelry worth $2.4 million. Jackson is being sued by Oprah's TV network and Love, and has been convicted for grand theft over a ruse in which he tricked a jeweler into lending him items worth $2.4 million. He is accused of sending letters purporting to be from Oprah and her representatives, as well as from former Obama aide Reggie Love, to recommend him for jobs and get free goods.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini has placed a €50 million price tag on Paulo Dybala, telling Paris Saint-Germain they will have to spend big to sign the "new Messi." A bidding war is set to break out over Dybala, with Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, Juventus, and PSG all interested. Inter Milan manager Roberto Mancini was spotted watching Dybala at a Serie A match. Zamparini told Telefoot that Dybala is the new Messi and that he would be a good investment for PSG. Dybala is wanted by some of Europe's biggest clubs, and Palermo is determined to cash in on him.

Hundreds of thousands of Brazilians are protesting against President Dilma Rousseff, who is struggling with an economic downturn and a massive bribery scandal. The protests are calling for Rousseff to be impeached. Petrobras, the state-run oil company, is the center of the corruption investigation, with construction companies paying bribes to secure lucrative contracts. Rousseff has defended Brazilians' right to protest and acknowledged the need to clean up corruption at Petrobras, but her supporters say the position is merely a figurehead. The country was already sharply divided during presidential elections, and the protests have grown bigger and broader, with many demonstrators saying they initially voted for Rousseff.

Former Manchester United midfielder Eric Cantona has refuted claims he starred in a soft porn film, insisting it is a "piece of art." The French film, "You and the Night," includes racy scenes, with Cantona on his hands and knees in just his underwear. Cantona, 48, says it is not pornography but a work of art, praising its beauty and calling it "superb artistic orgy."

Psychologists have found that certain types of music can enhance the enjoyment of a fish and chip supper, according to a study. The research suggests that specific music can bring out different flavors in food and drink, such as sweet, salty, and bitter. The intensity of Nessun Dorma, performed by Luciano Pavarotti, is said to be the perfect accompaniment to dark mouse or coffee, while the high-pitched piano in Billie Holiday's Autumn in New York can help emphasize the autumnal flavor of a pumpkin pudding.

Raheem Sterling, 20, has been offered a £100,000-a-week contract by Liverpool, but negotiations have stalled. Sterling, who has two years left on his contract, has postponed contract talks until the end of the season. Taylor, the PFA chief executive, believes waiting until the season is over could be a wise move. Sterling has been linked with moves to Arsenal and leading clubs in Spain. Sterling scored for England in their Euro 2016 qualifier with Lithuania. Taylor is confident Sterling is aware of what he owes to Liverpool and Rodgers.

An Ohio woman, La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, discovered her biological mother, Francine Simmons, works at the same call-center operation company she does. After connecting the dots, she found Simmons on Facebook and realized her mother was closer than she could imagine. They eventually met after a phone call, and Mitchell-Clark found out she has three younger sisters. The reunion was a relief and amazing for the family, particularly for Simmons's daughter, Kamala Cummings.

Oscar "Papoo" Hernandez Jr., a convicted gun trafficker, pleaded guilty to weapons charges in connection with his namesake's murder case. He was sentenced to up to 30 months in prison for transporting firearms across state lines and lying to a federal grand jury. Hernandez, 24, was arrested in April 2014 and charged with weapons offenses after shipping three guns, including a Hungarian rifle, to Aaron Hernandez, the NFL player who was sentenced to life in prison for Odin Lloyd's 2013 murder.

A 33-year-old man named Joel Parker was arrested in Florida for throwing a Snickers bar at a bus driver's head after threatening him and being disruptive during the ride. Parker was arrested for battery and issued a trespass warning, with a $250 bond and a ban on using the bus again.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has discussed pre-season plans with Saido Berahino, indicating the striker will remain at the club beyond the summer transfer window. Berahino, who has expressed a desire to play in the Champions League, is likely to be included in England's under-21 squad for the upcoming European Championships. Pulis praised Berahino's performance and commitment, suggesting he would be a valuable asset to the club.

Giovanni Lo Porto, a Sicilian man who worked with the German aid organization Welthungerlife to help rebuild Pakistan after flooding, was killed by a U.S. drone strike in 2012. Lo Porto, who had previously studied at London Metropolitan University, was abducted by four armed men in Pakistan and later died along with his colleague Bernd Muehlenbeck. The incident occurred during a major flood in Pakistan in 2010, which affected one-fifth of the country and left over 1,500 people dead.

A photographer captured an image of hundreds of sharks swimming near a beach in south Florida, prompting speculation that the sharks were Blacktips or Spinners migrating to breed. The incident was shared more than 2,000 times on social media.

An 11-year-old retired K-9 officer named Zeus, a German Shepherd who worked with the Ridgefield Police Department for eight years as a K-9 officer, was honored in a grand procession on Wednesday before he was put down due to a severe degenerative hip disorder and declining health. The tribute for Zeus began around 4:45 PM and ended at the Ridgefield Veterinary Hospital. The police department wrote an emotional message about Zeus on their Facebook, expressing their thoughts and prayers for Zeus, Officer Murray, and his family during this difficult time. During the grand procession, residents of Ridgefield lined the streets as they watched the cop cars drive by through the streets of the town.

Since Operation Yewtree, the number of child sex abuse reports has surged by more than 60%, with thousands of new allegations filed since 2011. Despite a 9% decrease in arrests, critics accuse the government of failing to protect victims. The South Yorkshire force saw a 577% increase in reported cases, with 501 investigations in 2014. Thames Valley Police made 191 arrests in relation to child sex abuse, up from 13 in 2011. The NSPCC helpline has seen a 81% increase in calls about sexual abuse since the operation's launch.

Iceland has become a popular filming location for TV series and Hollywood blockbusters, with Thingvellir National Park and Svartalfheim providing stunning settings for films such as Game of Thrones, Thor: The Dark World, and Interstellar. The country's natural beauty, including its waterfalls and glaciers, has attracted filmmakers from around the world.

A 100-year-old mechanic's garage in Sydney has sold for $1.2 million, with the grey-fronted building being converted into a three-bedroom, four-storey home. The grey-fronted building, built as a fire station in 1917, was used as a mechanic's garage for three generations before being converted into a home.

Samantha Rawcliffe, a 40-year-old mother-of-two from Morecambe, was diagnosed with functional neurological disorder (FND) after a car accident in May 2021. FND is an umbrella term for a range of neurological symptoms that cannot be explained, including uncontrollable shaking, loss of bladder control, and paralysis. Rawcliffe lost control of her body and crashed her car, leading to a series of symptoms that she initially attributed to shock. Tests revealed she had FND, which is a rare brain disorder. She is now confined to her house, unable to walk, and relies on a mobility scooter. The condition is debilitating and has no effective treatment plans, with physical therapy and cognitive behavior therapy being the most common treatments.

A controversial statue of Lucille Ball, depicting her intoxicated pitch for a health tonic, has been called "monstrous" and "frightening" by residents of Celoron, New York. Sculptor Dave Poulin, who created the statue, has admitted to being "disappointed" in his work and offered to fix it for free. The statue, based on a famous moment from Ball's show "I Love Lucy," has been the subject of a social media campaign to have it removed. Poulin, who believes the statue should never have been cast in bronze and made public, has pledged to create a new one. The statue, which is currently located in Celoron, is estimated to cost $8,000 to $10,000 to recast.

Bayern Munich's versatile left-back David Alaba, out for seven weeks with a torn knee ligament, will miss the season's final matches after being ruled out for another seven weeks. Alaba, 22, is set to begin rehabilitation in about a month. He had been in excellent form for Bayern, helping them stay on track for a treble of titles. Bayern Munich will face Porto in the Champions League quarter-finals later this month.

Beatrice Nokes, the daughter of two solicitors and a Scotland Yard detective, appeared in court today on charges of inciting prostitution and running an upmarket vice ring. Nokes, 21, is accused of grooming three young women to sell their bodies for sex. Daniel Williams, a 37-year-old Met police officer, faces multiple charges including voyeurism and hiding profits in socks stuffed up the chimney of his home. Both Williams and Nokes are suspended from duty and are accused of running the prostitution ring while on and off-duty.

Diana Doyle, a whistleblower, revealed that a firm linked to the sale of NHS patient data is offering details of eating disorder sufferers, stress, hair loss, dandruff, impotence, snoring, dieters, and those with plastic surgery for just 12p a head. The firm, Sequester, is offering to sell information on 43 different health conditions, including skin problems, insomnia, migraines, and sensitive teeth. The data is a goldmine for unscrupulous firms and criminals, who can use it to target vulnerable individuals and scam them over the phone.

Jordan Spieth, the 21-year-old golfer who won the 2017 Masters tournament, expressed his feelings about his autistic sister Ellie, who was unable to attend the event. Spieth said he misses his sister and hopes to bring her a present from the tournament. The article also mentions that Spieth's 14-year-old sister provides him with perspective and that she is the most special part of their family.

Dick Advocaat, the 67-year-old Dutch manager of Sunderland, will not underestimate the significance of the Old Firm derby against Newcastle, unlike his 1998 performance when he said the match was just another game, leading to a humiliating loss. Advocaat, who has won just twice at home this season, is considering starting Adam Johnson, who was recently arrested on suspicion of sexual activity with an under-age girl, in the derby. The Sunderland manager believes that the home crowd will provide an extra weapon for the team, and the match is expected to be a special game for both teams.

A heated argument erupted between a young woman and a butcher in Sydney's Bondi area over a chicken purchase dispute. Belinda Bartholomew, the girlfriend of Roosters star Aidan Guerra, claimed she was racially abused and called a "f***ing c***" by the butcher when she tried to change her chicken selection. The butcher, however, denied the claims, stating that he was the one being rude and that she was the troublemaker. The incident highlights tensions between immigrants and locals in the area.

Freddo Frogs, a popular children's chocolate, has been reduced in size by 20% from 15g to 12g, despite maintaining the same retail price. This change was spotted by a shop owner and is part of a broader trend of declining confectionery sales. Cadbury's parent company, Mondelez International, announced the change due to increased manufacturing costs. The company's profit before tax rose 46% from $87 million to $127 million in 2013. Thousands of chocolate fans expressed anger and disappointment, with some accusing Cadbury of being greedy and unaffordable.

Hillary Clinton's campaign-in-waiting met in Brooklyn on Saturday, a day before officially announcing her presidential bid. Robby Mook, her soon-to-be campaign manager, distributed a "values statement" outlining the campaign's goals and strategies. The document mentions issues that plagued Clinton's 2008 campaign, emphasizing humility, discipline, and unity. The campaign aims to avoid mistakes and focus on winning in states, with a focus on family prosperity. Clinton plans to launch her campaign through a video message on social media shortly after her announcement.

A 29-year-old woman, Kyli Wilfson, revealed details about her 18-month-long battle with chronic pancreatitis, a rare condition that left her unable to eat anything for a year and a half despite feeling extremely hungry. Initially diagnosed with acute pancreatitis, Wilfson was later diagnosed with chronic pancreatitis, which only worsened over time. She lost 30 pounds and had to rely on a feeding tube due to the condition's permanent damage.

Scottish National Party leader Nicola Sturgeon posed with a sceptical face in a meme referencing the leaders' debate. Prime Minister David Cameron and his deputy Nick Clegg were superimposed over Christopher Steed and Stephen Webb, two men from Brighton who appear on Channel 4 series Gogglebox. The images were inspired by a debate that saw Labour leader Ed Miliband warn the Prime Minister he would not get into power without lurching left, as SNP leader Nicola Sturgeon told him she is 'not strong enough' to win power on her own.

Amir Khan, the British boxer, is set to face Manny Pacquiao in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, after Mayweather declined the opportunity. Khan, who has been waiting for Mayweather for two years, is now considering a fight with Pacquiao. The fight could be a dream come true for Khan, who has been looking forward to fighting in the Middle East.

A tiny two-bedroom home in Islington, London, has sold for £750,000, despite being only 5ft wide in some areas and 8ft 8in wide at its widest. The property, which has a narrow galley kitchen, is described as "well proportioned" by the estate agency. The home, which has two bedrooms, a tiny study, reception room, shower room, cloakroom, kitchen, and a garden, is said to be garnering a lot of interest. The property was put on the market with Foxtons for £750,000, almost double its price in 2001. The buyer will have to pay £27,000 in stamp duty, the same as a second-hand narrow boat which is 50ft long.

Scottish First Minister Nicola Sturgeon is launching an ambitious manifesto to lead the UK, aiming to form a power-sharing deal with Labour. The SNP's policies overlap with Labour's, including reducing tuition fees and rolling back NHS competition. The manifesto includes plans for spending increases funded by more borrowing, potentially totaling £180 billion over five years. The SNP aims to build a "progressive alliance" for policies across the UK, with a focus on Scotland. The surge in support for the SNP could lead to constitutional turmoil similar to the 1910 election, which resulted in bitter conflict and the secession of Ireland.

Two mistakes from Rangers goalkeeper Robby McCrorie led to Celtic winning the Glasgow Cup 2-0, marking their fourth victory in eight seasons. Celtic's Josh Kerr scored the opening goal, and Robby McCrorie missed a penalty. The match was played behind closed doors due to previous fan trouble.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis, who previously played for Crystal Palace, led his team to a 2-0 victory over the former club. Pulis insists on wearing his cap, track suit, and white trainers during every game, stating he would never take it off during a match. The victory moves West Brom to 36 points, virtually guaranteeing their Premier League survival.

Jameela Jamil, a 29-year-old television presenter and former model, spent £3,000 on having all her amalgam fillings removed and replaced with white fillings after experiencing health problems for nearly seven years. The fillings were removed due to high levels of mercury detected in her blood tests, which suggested they were the cause of her symptoms, including puffy faces, heavy heads, and fainting. The dental amalgam, made from a mixture of metals including silver, tin, and copper, is used for robust fillings on back teeth and has been in use for more than 150 years. While the amounts taken in from fillings are minuscule, the review by the EU Commission's Scientific Committee in 2008 concluded there was no risk from amalgam.

Suge Knight, the co-creator of Death Row Records, was refused an appeal to have his bail reduced from $10 million to $5 million as he awaits trial for murder and attempted murder. Despite walking into court, he had to be wheeled out in a wheelchair. Knight believes his close friend, the undefeated professional boxer Floyd Mayweather, will bail him out when he wins his next fight. Mayweather, worth $420 million, is set to land a record pay check after going head-to-head with Manny Pacquiao on Saturday. Knight's attorney Matthew Fletcher is confident that Mayweather will bail him out.

In an interview with Puss Puss magazine, TV chef Gizzi Erskine discusses her fussy feline, Kimchi, who loves crunchy human food like poppadoms, tortilla chips, and taramasalata. Kimchi, a British shorthair, is described as having a discerning palate and will steal food from her plate if not watched. Erskine, who lives in a foodie household, has had to put Kimchi on a diet due to her excessive weight gain. Kimchi is also known for her love of cheese, caviar, and fish, and occasionally indulges in cat food. Erskine recently added a new addition to her cat family, Ponzu, named after her favorite Japanese dressing.

A father in Japan took a photograph of his young daughter standing near a rocky outcrop in July 2014, which later sparked controversy online. The photograph, featuring a pair of black boots behind the girl, has been the subject of debate, with some suggesting it could be a trick of the light or a paranormal phenomenon. The father, Martin Springall, 38, said he has no idea what the boots could be and that he does not recall a person standing behind his daughter. The photograph has become a topic of discussion on Reddit, with some viewing it as a prank, while others believe it to be genuine.

The UK government plans to introduce new immigration policies that will force EU migrants to pay tax and national insurance for four years before they can claim benefits, as part of a crackdown on net migration. The proposals include banning EU migrants from receiving state support and deporting those who do not find work within six months of arrival. The Home Secretary, Theresa May, said the changes would act to limit the appeal of coming to Britain from poorer parts of the EU.

A severely disabled boy, Cody Neatis, has been sleeping on a mattress on the floor in a hospital bed because the hospital does not have a suitable bed for him to sleep in. Cody has Down's syndrome, epilepsy, autism, and is fed by a tube. His mother, Lynne Neatis, has been sleeping with him for the past week, fearing he will injure himself or pull out his oxygen. The hospital does not have the specialist high-sided cot needed for Cody to sleep safely. Lynne Neatis is demanding answers from the local health trust about why they still do not have a suitable bed for disabled children.

Ahead of the Masters golf tournament, Derek Lawrenson reports on the excitement and challenges faced by players. Ian Poulter forgot his golf clubs, Henrik Stenson is recovering from flu, Tiger Woods will play with his children, and Gene Sarazen's albatross on the 15th hole is remembered as the most impressive shot in tournament history.

Juventus have ruled out a move for Manchester United loan star Radamel Falcao, claiming his wages are "beyond their means." Falcao, who scored only four goals since arriving at Manchester United from Monaco, is unlikely to remain at the club. Juventus general manager Beppe Marotta stated that Falcao wanted to come to Turin last summer but the club has now taken themselves out of the race to sign him. Juventus are interested in striker Paulo Dybala and Edinson Cavani, with Dybala rated at £35m.

David Cameron plans to sell Lloyds Bank shares worth up to £4 billion if he wins the election, offering them at a discount and encouraging long-term ownership. This is the largest privatisation since Thatcher's era, with a £20 billion bailout by Gordon Brown. The sale aims to help pay down the national debt and is part of a Conservative policy revival.

Living near congested roads with high levels of air pollution can cause 'silent strokes' that increase the risk of dementia, according to a study by researchers at Boston University School of Medicine. The study found that exposure to small, sooty particles, mostly caused by traffic fumes and factory emissions, alters the structure of the brain. The microscopic particles have previously been shown to cause lung damage and harmful changes in blood vessels and clotting, and are thought to contribute to the deaths of 29,000 people every year in Britain.

Jessica Ainscough, a 30-year-old wellness warrior who chose unconventional Gerson Therapy over conventional chemotherapy and radiation, died in February after a seven-year-long battle with epithelioid sarcoma. Her partner, Tallon Pamenter, revealed that Ainscough began a course of targeted radiation in her final weeks, which was a risky and tough decision. The radiation successfully managed to shrink the tumour but caused complications, leading to Ainscough's death. Ainscough's partner expressed her courage and grace, and the couple's love was deeply felt by their followers.

Ten people, including four children, were involved in a multi-vehicle crash on the Brisbane Valley Highway near Fernvale on Wednesday afternoon. Three vehicles collided, resulting in chest and shoulder injuries for a 40-year-old man and a 5-year-old boy, as well as arm and abdominal pain for a 27-year-old woman and a 6-year-old girl. The incident occurred at 2 km south of Fernvale, and the affected stretch of the highway was closed off with diversions in place. The Rescue 500 helicopter airlifted several patients to the Princess Alexandra Hospital in Brisbane.

Jason McDonald, a 34-year-old volunteer at the Colorado Gator Farm, walked a thin slackline rope over a pool containing more than 50 hungry alligators at the farm. McDonald, who has been involved with alligators for over ten years and has taken handling classes, thought this would be an interesting new way of interacting with the fearsome creatures. The gators were surprisingly ok with the slackline, and McDonald said he wanted to take his hobby further by walking over Elvis or Morris, his two biggest gators on the farm.

The son of a Syrian imam who was shot dead on a London street may have met his father's killer just days before the murder. Sources close to the investigation, which is being led by the counter-terrorism unit, told the Sunday Times that Abdul Hadi Arwani, an opponent of Syrian President Bashar Al-Assad, had visited the area where he was killed with his son days before his death. Arwani, 48, was shot and killed in his car on a quiet street in North West London after being called there last Tuesday, apparently to provide a quote for building work.

Hong Kong's Jenny's cookies, a popular buttery treat, have sparked a black market, with tourists and locals lining up for hours to purchase them. The original store warns against buying "fake" cookies, while bakeries produce knockoffs and locals hire others to stand in line. The frenzy has spread to other parts of the world, with similar food manias occurring.

A mother-of-one, Kira Hollis, has overcome anorexia and depression by becoming a bodybuilder. She was diagnosed with borderline personality disorder and depression at the age of 27, but her journey to fitness changed her life. Doctors ordered her to go to the gym to gain weight, but it led to a newfound hobby and focus. Now, she is a personal trainer and has a healthy weight of 9. 5st. Her story has gone viral, and she has been helped by the Cherry Orchard Clinic and medication. Her daughter Olivia has also been a huge help in her recovery.

Lewis Ferguson, 18, survived a spectacular fall from Merrion Square during a race at Wincanton on Wednesday, causing him to perform a mid-air somersault. The incident, which was captured on video and viewed by hundreds of thousands of people online, has led to Ferguson gaining a cut on his nose and gaining a few hundred Twitter followers. Despite the fall, Ferguson is undeterred and plans to continue riding at the Cheltenham Festival and Aintree every year. The incident was described as the worst fall the race course clerk of the course, Barry Johnson, had ever seen.

Hillary Clinton launched her campaign with a video, new logo, and road trip, aiming to rebrand herself and frame her as an empathetic candidate. Critics, including Ruth Marcus and Jon Stewart, dismissed the launch as vapid and boring. However, marketing experts argue that the campaign's strategy of flipping Clinton's message from self-absorbed to empathetic may be more successful than initially thought. The campaign's logo, introduced last week, is expected to become the most ubiquitous element of Clinton's campaign.

More than 1,700 Chinese high school students from Yichuan, Shaanxi province, took an outdoor exam on Saturday, the first attempt by the school to allow pupils to sit exams in the open. The unusual move was made due to a lack of indoor space, and the students organized the exam themselves, including turning their desks and chairs to avoid being dazzled by the sun. The school said the outdoor exam could be a test of the students' organizing capacity and that it could help prevent cheating.

Sportsmail has partnered with Gillette to offer a unique chance for one lucky reader to win a pair of Nike Magista Obra boots signed by Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart. The prize includes a new Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor with Flexball technology and a shave gel. The competition closes on April 19.

Kecil, a baby orangutan, was found rejected by his natural mother and a surrogate mother at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo. After a tough start, Kecil was adopted by Maggie, a 53-year-old surrogate mother who had already raised four of her own children. Maggie proved her parenting skills by helping Kecil for the past 10 months, and the two now have an inseparable bond. Kecil, who had to be moved from his birthplace at Toledo Zoo 14 months ago due to his natural mother's failure to bond with him, will have his first public outing this weekend in two hours slots between 10am and midday.

A 61-year-old woman named Noelle Baynham died suddenly and was eaten by her two dogs after being locked in the house for days. The dogs, a Jack Russell and a Staffordshire Bull Terrier, partially ate her body, and the cause of death was an accidental overdose of medication. The incident occurred on January 17, 2023, in Winchester, Hampshire, and the dogs' behavior, including scratch marks on her chest, suggested they tried to wake her before becoming desperate for food. The inquest ruled that there was no evidence of suicide or an accidental fall, but the coroner believed she may have had a stroke.

France's handball star Nikola Karabatic, along with his brother Luka and 15 others, is facing trial for suspected match-fixing. Karabatic, a multiple world and Olympic gold medalist, was banned by the French league for betting on a match in which his Montpellier club lost to a struggling team. He is now playing for Barcelona in the Spanish league. The trial is likely to take place within months, and Karabatic faces up to five years in prison and a fine.

Thames Valley Police launched Operation Reportage after receiving a tip-off about the men's activities and eventually tracked down numerous teenager girls who had been molested. The gang of six men, including Ahmed Hassan-Sule, 21, and Mohamed Saleh, 22, were found guilty of a string of sexual offenses against teenage girls in Banbury, Oxfordshire, ranging from inciting sexual activity with a child to rape. The defendants were sentenced to a total of 31 years in jail, with Hassan-Sule receiving nine years and Saleh four years and nine months. The victims, who were described as "emotionally immature" and "vulnerable," were targeted at under-18s parties organized by the gang.

Former New England Patriots star Aaron Hernandez faces three more trials, including a murder trial in which he is accused of killing two men and wounding another person near a Boston nightclub in July 2012. Hernandez pleaded not guilty at his arraignment. The trial was originally slated for May 28, but was postponed and no new date has been set.

The Emirates Airline has signed a £30 million three-year deal to sponsor the FA Cup, renaming it the Emirates FA Cup. This deal, along with existing sponsorship deals with Arsenal, AC Milan, and Hamburg, adds to Emirates' portfolio of sporting sponsorships.

Michael Phelps, the 18-time Olympic champion, is aiming to compete in the Rio Olympics next year but won't swim at the world championships in Russia this summer as part of a six-month suspension by USA Swimming. Phelps, who had already qualified in three events before being banned, said he enjoys participating in international meets but is disappointed not to compete at the worlds. He has been in rehab for alcohol addiction since a second DUI arrest last fall and has enrolled in Alcoholics Anonymous.

Gareth Bale, a key player for Real Madrid, is doubtful for the Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid due to a calf injury. The Welsh forward limped off during Real's 3-1 home victory over Malaga on Saturday. Real Madrid's medical staff found a muscular lesion in Bale's soleus muscle. Los Blancos are also without Croatian midfielder Luka Modric, who suffered a knee ligament strain and is expected to be unavailable for six weeks. Real Madrid coach Carlo Ancelotti hopes striker Karim Benzema will be fit for the match.

Scientists warn that older people are more susceptible to emotions when making decisions about retirement investments, particularly during financial crises. A study at Texas Tech University found that more than 50% of pensioners who sold their investments during the 2007-2008 global financial crisis lost significant amounts of money. The study, published in the Journal of Consumer Affairs, analyzed 1,204 retired people with investments between 2006 and 2008. The researchers found that those with better cognitive abilities were less likely to make emotional investment decisions. The reforms announced by Chancellor George Osborne allow British retirees to take income from their pensions, with the option to keep their investments in the stock market.

Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini is criticized by Stuart Pearce for not giving him more time to turn around the club's fortunes. Pearce believes Pellegrini should stay in place, as he has been around the block long enough to realize the squad needs freshening up this summer. The article also mentions that Manchester City's poor run of form is attributed to the fading influence of Ivorian Yaya Toure.

Manchester United's stars, including Wayne Rooney, Ander Herrera, and Robin van Persie, are training in the sunshine ahead of their Premier League derby against Manchester City on Sunday. The match is significant as it marks Manchester United's first game against their rivals since the Sir Alex Ferguson era, and a victory could give them a four-point lead in the league. The game is also crucial for Manchester City, who have won their last three visits to Old Trafford.

Fiorentina lost 1-0 to Verona at home, leaving them nine points behind third-placed AS Roma. Fiorentina's coach, Vincenzo Montella, said his team paid dearly for failing to convert their dominance into goals. Verona's Mounir Obbadi scored the winning goal in the 90th minute, and Fiorentina's Alessandro Diamanti missed a penalty. Fiorentina is now in sixth place with 49 points, one point behind Sampdoria.

Miley Cyrus, 22, attended the 30th Annual Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony in Cleveland, Ohio, where she posed for a social media snap with somewhat bushy underarm hair. This sparked controversy, with some users advising her to shave, while others defended her choice. Cyrus is not the first, and likely won't be the last, to choose not to shave her armpits.

Barcelona's Lionel Messi, Neymar, and Luis Suarez have scored 102 goals collectively this season, taking them five points clear in La Liga. Messi has 49 goals, Neymar has 32, and Suarez has 21. The trio's dominance has boosted Barcelona's goal difference to +78, putting pressure on Real Madrid ahead of their match against Almería.

A 44-year-old pedestrian named Andrea McVeigh was struck by a cyclist who was riding on the pavement in Bermondsey, south London. The cyclist fled the scene after hitting McVeigh, who suffered two three-inch gashes to the middle of her forehead and other facial and hand injuries. The cyclist initially stopped after the impact but then sped off. McVeigh's husband chased the cyclist, who turned around and smiled at him as he disappeared. The police have issued CCTV footage of the cyclist they want to speak to in connection with the crash. McVeigh is currently off work sick with facial injuries and is seeking justice for the incident.

Paul Gregory, 51, of Bedford, was fined £795 for claiming he could only walk 200 meters when he was actually a keen walker and member of a mountaineering club. He was exposed after council officials noticed a newspaper report recounting his exploits on a 191-mile hike. Gregory pleaded guilty to two counts of dishonestly obtaining a blue badge by misrepresenting his physical abilities and was ordered to carry out 150 hours of unpaid work and pay a £60 victim surcharge.

Apple has filed a patent for a new method of unlocking its devices using facial recognition, which involves scanning a user's face with the front-facing camera when the handset is moved into a certain position. If the scanned face matches a previously taken photo, the phone unlocks automatically. This system would track the movement of the phone to determine whether it is being used or placed flat on a table, and would not require the screen to be enabled.

Elizabeth Sedway, a 51-year-old mother of two battling cancer, was ejected from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California due to her lack of a doctor's note clearing her to fly. The incident occurred when an airline representative noticed her wearing a surgical mask and asked if she needed anything. Mrs. Sedway initially denied needing assistance, but the representative insisted she needed a doctor's note. After being ejected, she posted an emotional video on Facebook, detailing her ordeal and the emotional toll it took on her family.

A vintage 1973 E-Type Jaguar was involved in a head-on collision with a 1973 Toyota Kluger on Easter Sunday night in Frenchs Forest, Sydney. The Jaguar, worth over $120,000, was completely written off, while all three adults involved were taken to hospital for precautionary measures. Police are investigating the incident, and the Jaguar's owner expressed sympathy and admiration for classic car enthusiasts. The crash occurred on Warringah Road, and the incident comes after police warned of increased enforcement during the Easter long weekend.

Google has established a team focused on enhancing the longevity of electronic devices, including phones, tablets, and electric vehicles, through the development of flexible and wearable technologies. The team, consisting of four individuals, has been working on solid-state, thin-film batteries since 2012, with a particular interest in subfreezing temperature performance for Google's Project Loon balloons. This initiative is part of a broader effort to improve battery technology across various industries.

The 223-foot Explorer superyacht, designed by British yacht designer Tony Castro, offers a luxurious and versatile experience for its ultra-rich owners. Equipped with a helipad, an infinity pool, and ample space for storage of luxury vehicles and water toys, the yacht is described as the "Range Rover of the seas." The yacht's cost to build is approximately 40 million euros, making it a significant investment for its owners. The layout includes various areas for guests to relax and entertain, ensuring a comfortable and enjoyable experience for the 12 guests and 15 crew. However, the high cost of the yacht means that its retail price is likely to be even higher.

Ed Miliband, the leader of the Labour Party, announced his intention to implement rent controls despite warnings from experts that the plans would backfire. Labour's proposals, which include three-year tenancies and rent caps, are criticized for potentially leading to more evictions and higher rents. The plans are opposed by senior Tories, the Confederation of British Industry, and former Labour minister Tessa Jowell, who warns against unintended consequences.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town fan who said he hoped Arsenal would win in a video was removed from his role as a mascot for Reading in the FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal. The young supporter was offered the chance to be a mascot for England instead.

A giant supervoid 1.8 billion light-years across may be responsible for a mysterious 'Cold Spot' in the universe, according to astronomers seeking to understand the anomaly. The supervoid is thought to be causing a 'less-dense' region of the universe, with a temperature 70 nano-Kelvins colder than other regions. The research, published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, was carried out by the Institute for Astronomy at the University of Hawaii at Manoa.

The Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, will display Abraham Lincoln's chair where he was shot in 1865 as part of its observance of the 150th anniversary of the assassination. The chair, which has a dark stain on the back, is part of the museum's collection and has been housed in various locations since its founding.

A 19-year-old vlogger named Jake Boys surprised his girlfriend Emily Canham by booking tickets for One Direction to perform in Cardiff. However, he mistakenly booked plane tickets to the Republic of Ireland instead of Wales, where the concert was actually taking place. The couple is now planning to buy new train tickets to Cardiff for the band's show in June.

A Romanian company has unveiled the Roboscan 2M Aeria, a mobile X-ray scanner that can detect contraband, bombs, and weapons on airplanes. The device, costing €3 million, is already being used to inspect trucks at borders in Eastern Europe, where it has seized 76,000 packs of illegal cigarettes. The company claims it can scan entire planes in about 20 minutes, but the radiation emitted is not safe for passengers yet.

A 54-year-old convicted paedophile, Stephen Munden, has gone on the run after vanishing from a psychiatric unit. Munden, described as having a 'fanatical obsession' with young girls, was detained under the Mental Health Act after sexually touching a three-year-old girl. He is believed to have shaved off his beard before leaving the hospital in Winchfield. Munden, formerly of Marchwood, near Southampton, was convicted of sexually touching a child under the age of 13 and is subject to a hospital order. A manhunt is underway to find Munden, who is described as about 5ft 8ins tall, of a heavy build, and has dark hair.

Middlesbrough, led by Aitor Karanka, are currently top of the Championship table with a 7-point lead over second-placed Bournemouth. The division is highly competitive, with only four weeks remaining, and Boro know they cannot be caught if they keep winning. The match against Watford on Monday is a lunchtime kick-off, which could have a psychological effect on other teams. Watford's Odion Ighalo, who scored against Bournemouth, is eager to play in the Premier League. The promotion race is highly precarious, with a potential change in the top two if Watford and Norwich win and Bournemouth fail to secure three points against Birmingham. Jonathan Woodgate, Karanka's experienced captain, is expected to play through a broken toe.

The latest hair trend is grey hair, with women sharing images on social media under the hashtag #grannyhair. The trend has gained popularity on platforms like Instagram, with users posting images of themselves with grey hair, often with makeup or accessories to enhance the look. The trend has been embraced by both men and women, with some seeing it as a feminist statement, while others view it as a fashion fad. The trend can be traced back to fashion designer Jean Paul Gaultier's catwalk show at Paris Fashion Week earlier this month, which featured silver-haired models.

A couple from Bellefontaine, Ohio, who were struggling with chronic conditions and financial difficulties, died from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning after leaving their charcoal grills in their bedroom. The couple, Randy and Jodi Speidel, had created online fundraisers but failed to receive any donations. Their landlord discovered a note warning of carbon monoxide and found the couple dead, with their pets outside. The couple had been living without gas, water, and electricity, and had limited their food intake to one meal a day. Their daughters, Randa and Kira, were left without a father and mother.

Liberal Democrat leader Nick Clegg vowed to continue as leader even if the party is reduced to fewer than 30 MPs, despite previous indications he would quit if the party is left out of power. Clegg emphasized his commitment to serving the country and his party, despite the potential risks of losing the center ground and undoing past sacrifices. Business Secretary Vince Cable expressed hope to be made Chancellor if the Lib Dems form another coalition with the Conservatives. Clegg also appeared to lean towards another deal with the Tories, saying he deserved "credit" for forming the Coalition while enduring "five years of constant bile from the Labour Party."

A pensioner in Somerset, England, was saved from a large badger by his Jack Russell dog, which dragged him back indoors. The badger, which was described as the size of a pig with six-inch teeth, attacked the dog but not the pensioner. The incident has led to the National Farmers' Union issuing advice for residents to protect their property from badgers.

Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose to Porto U21s at Motspur Park on Wednesday, while the Blues were knocked out of the Champions League by PSG. Mourinho's son Jose Junior accompanied him. Chelsea is closing in on their first Premier League title since 2010, with six games remaining.

Andreas Christopheros, a 29-year-old property developer, was severely injured in a December 2014 acid attack on his home in Truro, Cornwall. Nicole Phillips, 45, from Hastings, was charged with perverting the course of justice and is due to appear in court. Christopheros, who works in the event and property management industries, has suffered life-changing injuries including a loss of vision and facial scars.

A Spanish town near the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route has erected signs warning pilgrims not to defecate along the trail, sparking controversy. The signs, which show a squatting figure within a red circle with a diagonal line, have become an attraction, with pilgrims posing for photos with them. The mayor of the town says there are no public facilities for pilgrims along the route.

A massive fire destroyed a building that once housed a strip club in Flint, Michigan, on Wednesday afternoon. Flames consumed the structure and nearby power lines, with only the building and a few power lines remaining. The fire started at about 1pm and was reported to have taken place on a Flint intersection. Local officials stated that the site was not a vacant facility. The incident is under investigation, and the cause of the fire remains unclear.

Shoshana Hebshi, a woman of Arab and Jewish descent who was strip-searched at a Detroit-area airport on the 10th anniversary of 9/11, has reached a settlement of $40,000 in a lawsuit filed on her behalf. The federal government will compensate her for being humiliated and traumatized. The settlement sends a message about protecting constitutional rights and will help prevent future passengers from enduring similar experiences.

An Asiana Airlines flight OZ162 crashed and skidded off the runway at Hiroshima Airport in Japan, injuring 20 people. The plane, which had departed from Incheon International Airport in South Korea, reportedly missed the landing point and overran the runway. Local media described the incident as a crash landing, with images showing evidence of a hard landing and no sign of the landing gear. The flight had 74 passengers and seven crew members on board. The airport was closed, and emergency services were at the scene, with injured passengers being taken to hospital.

Mark-Francis Vandelli, a wealthy reality star, has opened up his watch collection to the Evening Standard, showcasing 16 expensive timepieces. He revealed his favorite items and the history behind them, including a Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42, a Cartier Tortue Collection Privée, and a Rolex yellow gold Oyster Perpetual. His most expensive watch is a Cartier white gold Moonphase, which he bought for £32,000.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy is selling his extensive collection of antiques in a £100,000 auction after deciding to downsize his home. The collection includes a 3D diorama of the Battle of Agincourt, a longbow made from yew, and a portrait of Hardy holding the bow. The auction, held by Dominic Winter auctioneers, features 238 lots of furniture, paintings, swords, and other items. Hardy, 89, is a military historian who studied with J.R.R. Tolkien and is now an expert on the medieval longbow. The sale is part of his downsizing process, and Hardy hopes the proceeds will bring joy to future owners.

A Brazilian commuter, Nelson Felippe, took a photo of two women hugging on a train platform and shared it on Facebook, expressing his disapproval of the scene. The image quickly went viral, with over 100, 000 views in 24 hours. Felippe's post, which initially appeared to be homophobic, actually revealed that he was observing a public transport safety regulation. The image sparked controversy and led to thousands of comments, with many praising Felippe's witty way of exposing homophobia.

A young English cricket fan, Jonathan Stevenson, wrote a letter to Richie Benaud, the legendary Australian cricket great, asking for tips on left-handed leg spin. Benaud's detailed response, dated September 27, 1996, was shared on Twitter as a tribute to the "great man." The letter included notes on spin bowling for left-hand bowlers, explaining the difference in coaching between right-handed and left-handed bowlers. Benaud, who enjoyed a remarkable Test career as a wily leg-spin bowler, also provided advice on different deliveries and how to deliver them.

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg predicts that virtual reality will revolutionize travel, allowing users to experience destinations from multiple viewpoints and even change their perspectives. The company purchased Oculus, a virtual reality headset maker, and promised virtual reality gaming would be available "this year." Zuckerberg mentioned that users will be able to explore locations with multiple cameras, creating even more immersive experiences. Marriott hotels have also trialled Oculus Rift for a tour of hotels across America.

A 22-year-old woman in China was diagnosed with bone cancer and admitted to the hospital, preventing her from getting married on her birthday. Her boyfriend, Guo Kai, arranged for professional photographers to take wedding photos for her, despite her condition requiring frequent medical attention. The couple met a year ago and have been committed to each other since.
