A 34-year-old man, Blaine Boudreaux, was charged with intoxication manslaughter, intoxicated assault, and failure to stop and render aid involving death after three separate DUI collisions in Houston that killed a 6-year-old boy and injured his mother. Boudreaux, who has an extensive DUI record in Louisiana, was allegedly drunk when he ran a red light on Lockwood Drive and slammed his Dodge pickup truck into a Honda Civic, killing the boy and injuring his mother. The suspect was arrested at the scene after failing a field sobriety test.

Microsoft announced a new pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions within the company, with positions based at its Redmond campus in Washington and run in partnership with Specialisterne, a Danish nonprofit. The program aims to expand opportunity and represent customers, with Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella previously apologizing for comments suggesting women don't need to ask for raises.

Two Tulsa deputies involved in the fatal shooting of Eric Harris have been reassigned due to threats against them and their families. The shooting occurred when Reserve Deputy Robert Bates shot Harris, who was trying to arrest him. The deputies are not charged with a crime but have faced criticism for their actions. The sheriff's office has suspended the drug unit pending an investigation into the April shooting of Harris. The FBI has cleared the agency of any civil rights violations.

Katie Prager, a 24-year-old woman with cystic fibrosis, is in desperate need of a life-saving lung transplant due to an infection that doctors predicted she would not survive without new lungs. Her husband, Dalton, has already received new lungs, but Katie is waiting for a transplant at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center, which her insurance company, Kentucky Medicaid, will not cover. Katie's insurance company, Kentucky Medicaid, will not pay for the out-of-state treatment she needs at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center, and her health continues to decline. Dalton is pleading for help, saying that his wife is being turned into a number, a statistic, and a dollar sign by her insurance company.

The Sleep Cycle app data reveals that the world sleeps the least on Tuesdays, with Americans waking up at 7am and feeling the worst mood all week. The best sleep quality occurs on Wednesdays, with China recording the highest sleep quality that night. The data also shows that the world sleeps the most on Saturdays, with Finland getting the most hours of sleep (8 hours and 2 minutes on average). Users in the Middle East wake up the latest and happiest on Thursdays, and in Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and UAE, users report the best mood on Thursdays. Americans typically don't rise until 8:24am on Fridays and report the best wake-up mood.

Mexican artist Frida Kahlo's unpublished love letters to her lover Jose Bartoli, written during their secret three-year romance while she was married to Diego Rivera, are expected to fetch upwards of $120,000 when they go up for auction at Doyle New York on April 15. The letters, written in Spanish between August 1946 and November 1949, were saved by Jose until his death in 1995 and comprise more than 100 pages. Frida signed her letters to Jose as 'Sonja' to make it seem like they were from a woman if Diego came across them.

Trade union leader Len McCluskey, known for his militant stance, is popular with Labour activists during an election campaign in South Wales. However, his union, Unite, is a potent force in British politics, seeking to impose socialist policies on the government. McCluskey, who once presided over more strikes than any other union boss, is open about his desire to return Britain to the dark days of the 1970s. His union's influence on Labour candidates is a concern, as it is intertwined with the Labour Party's structure and finances.

Zoologist Elad Hershkowitz captured footage of various animals drinking water in their enclosures using a GoPro camera, revealing unique and humorous drinking methods. The footage, totaling 30 hours, shows a rhino almost kissing the water surface, a lemur delicately licking, and a herd of zebras drinking humorously. Hershkowitz filmed the animals for four minutes, noting the significant differences in drinking methods among carnivores and herbivores. The experiment was conducted with the camera secured above the troughs to ensure the animals' comfort.
Just a quarter of voters think David Cameron is hungriest to win the election, a poll reveals as the Prime Minister tries to step up his campaign passion.

A man charged with assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov has told a court he was beaten and pressured into confessing to the murder. Zaur Dadaev, accused of being involved in the shooting of Nemstov in Moscow on February 27, told the court he had been abducted, beaten, and pressured into confessing. Dadaev previously confessed to the murder but now says he was beaten and pressured into making that statement. He is one of five Chechen men accused of killing Nemstov. The incident sparked a protest march in Moscow, and Dadaev is being held with his cousins, Anzor and Shagid Gubahsev.

A 4-month-old baby boy named Sonit Awal was pulled from the rubble of a Nepal earthquake that killed over 5,000 people. His father, Shyam Awal, frantically searched for him amid the debris for 22 hours before soldiers found him alive at 10 a.m. on Sunday. Sonit's face was exposed during the rescue but was uninjured.

A Church of Scientology-backed organization is facing a land use battle over plans to turn a historic property near the presidential retreat Camp David into a drug rehab center. Narcocon, a drug rehab network affiliated with the Church of Scientology, argues that the property has historic significance due to President Herbert Hoover's fishing trip there. Opponents view the proposed designation as a trick to circumvent current zoning laws and create a dangerous program. Narcocon, which uses sauna sessions and Scientology teachings, has been sued for wrongful deaths. The Maryland center would house 12 patients, with eight staff living there and eight off-site. The property is currently classified for resource conservation and does not permit any medical purpose.

The article describes the aftermath of the U.S. withdrawal from Afghanistan, focusing on the challenges faced by expatriates and locals in Kabul. Five men who once spoke English due to their work with NATO are now blacklisted and isolated, sleeping in market stalls and avoiding family visits due to threats. The city has transformed, with neighborhoods emptying out and roads being reclaimed by Afghans. The U.S. Embassy and NATO declined to comment.

One US Navy SEAL died and another was critically injured while training in a pool at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story in Virginia, a Navy spokesman said. The two members of the Navy's elite sea, air, land teams were found at the bottom of the pool by another service member around 3pm local time. The names of the SEALS were withheld pending notification of next of kin.

NBC, the broadcasting titan holding live rights to the Premier League in the United States, is set to show all Premier League matches in the country for the first time this weekend, reflecting a significant increase in US interest in English football. NBC has transported their entire production from Connecticut to England, with hosts including Rebecca Lowe, Robbie Earle, and Kyle Martino, who are joined by pitchside analysts Lee Dixon and Robbie Mustoe. The move aims to enhance coverage and influence young American football fans, who are now more likely to see replica Premier League shirts.

Ed Miliband will do "more damage to the country than he did to his brother," Boris Johnson said during a live TV debate, accusing him of potentially stabbing the country in the back by forming a deal with the SNP to gain power. Johnson insisted that Miliband would be more damaging to the country than his brother, who won the Labour leadership in 2010.

A prisoner in Oregon was slapped with an extra 30 days behind bars for dropping his trousers and flashing a judge during a court hearing. The judge sentenced him to an additional 30 days for contempt of court. The incident occurred when Dustin Irons, 26, appeared via video-link to a court in Oregon. He was handcuffed but managed to pull down his pants for a lewd gesture, which angered the judge. Irons was arrested for trashing a hotel room and assaulting people inside. He faces another disciplinary investigation and could be placed in a segregation unit.

Jenson Button believes McLaren has improved significantly since the Australian Grand Prix, with both he and Fernando Alonso discovering the car was competitive alongside other midfield runners. Despite retiring during the Malaysian Grand Prix, Button is hopeful for further progress in Shanghai, where the cooler weather could affect tyre performance. McLaren acknowledges the team still has a long way to go, but Button expresses satisfaction with the team's basic car and progress made with the power unit.

A hospital in Western Australia, Fiona Stanley, was found to have blood and bone fragments on supposedly sanitized medical instruments, leading to its medical service provider being stripped of its contract and fined. The hospital has been found to continue operating with poorly sanitized instruments, raising concerns about patient safety.

Becca Litchfield and Dale, who chose to forgo their dream wedding to pay for IVF, have welcomed twins and found a way to say their "I do's." The couple, from Nottingham, won a wedding competition and were able to finally get married, despite their age and previous failures with IVF.

A family-friendly coffee shop in Omaha, Nebraska, had its Facebook page hacked and flooded with pornography after an employee clicked on a malicious link in an email. The hack lasted for 24 hours, with the page being replaced with adult cartoons similar to those posted on other brands. The company issued an apology and removed the content, but it was not until a day later that Facebook was contacted to regain control of the account.

A young Shibu Inu puppy at an American Kennel Club center in the United States caused confusion and laughter when it attempted to bark at a nearby husky dog, resulting in a series of vocal exchanges that included squeaking, squawking, and yapping. The video, captured on camera, shows the Shibu Inu attempting to bark at the husky, which then responded with a high-pitched whine. The incident, which was captured on video, caused people to laugh and mimic the dogs' vocalizations, with one person even asking, "What is that noise?" The video concludes with the husky losing interest and the Shibu Inu settling down after being rubbed by its handler.

Liam Plunkett, an experienced English seamer, is set to return to the West Indies batting lineup and aims to use his pace to lead England to victory in the upcoming Test series. Plunkett, who managed 18 wickets in four Tests prior to his injury, is now looking to make a name for himself in the Caribbean, where he has a reputation for being a fast bowler. He is competing for a place in the England Test side with Chris Jordan and Mark Wood, who are both familiar with the conditions in their homeland.

Paul Smith, a boxer from Liverpool, is set to face Andre Ward in a unification fight for the WBA super-middleweight title. Smith, who has lost two previous title defenses to Arthur Abraham, is seen as a potential warm-up opponent for Ward, who is ranked among the top five pound-for-pound boxers. The fight is part of the WBA's plan to unify the super-middleweight division, with Ward and Carl Froch set to meet in a rematch.

Tyrus Byrd, the first African American mayor of Parma, Missouri, was sworn in last week but faced a sudden departure of five of her six police officers and several other top officials after her election victory. The resignations were attributed to "safety concerns," with the outgoing mayor stating that the police force was overwhelmed by the new mayor's election. The town, with a population of 713, has experienced a surge in crime, and residents rallied behind Byrd, believing she should be celebrated for her election rather than the departures of city employees.

Manchester City midfielder Yaya Toure will not be forced out of the club but is set to become available this summer. The Ivorian, who has played a major role in City's recent trophy-winning period, is content with his current contract and is fully committed to the team. Inter Milan is interested in Toure, but his huge wages make it uncertain whether they can afford to sign him. City will resist any attempt by Valencia to pull out of a £24 million deal for Alvaro Negredo to fund a move for Radamel Falcao.

A new study claims that more than two-thirds of people taking antidepressants may not actually have depression, as they do not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder. The study, published in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, found that 38% of those taking antidepressants did not meet the criteria for obsessive compulsive disorder, panic disorder, social phobia, or generalised anxiety disorder. The researchers concluded that antidepressants are commonly used in the absence of clear evidence-based indications. The study was conducted by U.S. investigators who looked at those taking selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), the most commonly prescribed type of antidepressant. The study found that prescriptions for anti-depressants have more than trebled since 1998 in the world's richest countries, with a particular rise in the use of SSRIs like Prozac and Seroxat.

Doris Fuller, the mother of a mentally ill daughter who killed herself, has revealed how her daughter's bipolar disorder and psychosis led to her death. Fuller wrote about how her daughter's illness, which went undiagnosed until her early 20s, eventually drove her to suicide. Fuller's daughter, Natalie, suffered from bipolar disorder and psychosis and died when she stepped in front of a train in Baltimore, Maryland. Fuller described her daughter as the bravest person she had ever known and said that her suicide doesn't change that. Despite receiving proper treatment, Natalie eventually decided to stop taking her meds, which brought her troubles back, even more acute than before.

A 10-year-old boy named Koby Hodder suffered a cardiac arrest while playing British Bulldog at his school playground, collapsing for 12 minutes before being revived by paramedics. His condition was similar to that of footballer Fabrice Muamba, who also suffered a cardiac arrest during a match. The incident led to calls for the game to be banned, with teachers praising Koby's survival as a testament to the importance of CPR.

Baroness Hale of Richmond, Britain's most senior female judge, has proposed reforms to divorce laws in England and Wales to remove the need for allegations of adultery and blame, aiming to reduce bitterness in matrimonial disputes. The proposed changes include a one-year cooling-off period after declaring that a marriage has permanently broken down, encouraging couples to resolve arrangements for children and money before obtaining a divorce. Lady Hale, who is deputy president to the Supreme Court and the only woman among the 12 Supreme Court justices, wants to overhaul the current system, which requires couples to cite one of five reasons for divorce, including adultery, unreasonable behavior, desertion, two years' separation with consent, or five years' separation without consent. The reforms aim to make the process of obtaining a divorce more lengthy and to encourage couples to resolve issues before the divorce is finalized.

Tottenham Hotspur is considering building a state-of-the-art stadium with a retractable pitch that could accommodate an NFL franchise, potentially becoming their home. The stadium, set to open in 2018-19, would feature a synthetic surface beneath a retractable grass pitch, allowing for NFL-style games. The NFL is expected to have a permanent franchise in London within five years, and teams are testing logistics for their three games at Wembley this autumn. Tottenham's new stadium, with a capacity of 65,000, is seen as more suitable for NFL requirements than Wembley's 90,000 seats. The NFL sees the new stadium as advantageous, despite concerns about the national stadium's status and seating capacity.

U.S. senators have written to FIFA, urging the organization to remove Russia as host of the 2018 World Cup due to its role in the Ukraine crisis and occupation of Crimea. The senators, including John McCain, are calling for economic sanctions against Russia and a condemnation of the Putin regime.

Universal announced the release date for the sequel to "Fifty Shades of Grey" on February 10, 2017, and February 9, 2018. Niall Leonard, married to the author Erika Leonard, will write the script for the second film. The second film, titled "Fifty Shades Darker," is set to release over Valentine's Day weekend of this year, earning a massive $568.8 million worldwide.

West Brom manager Tony Pulis will receive a hero's welcome when he returns to Crystal Palace, but he must wonder if he'll ever be successful at the right end of the Premier League, given his overall record of never finishing in the top half of the table. Pulis has never managed to guide a team into the top half of the Premier League, and he is currently the only manager in the league with more than 12 months experience who has never finished higher than 11th. Pulis has a proud record of never being relegated, but his current record of 33 points leaves him with four of his final five fixtures coming against Liverpool, Manchester United, Chelsea, and Arsenal, which may not be enough to prevent relegation. Pulis has a history of turning around teams, but his current record is not as impressive as some of his peers.

Fenerbahce, the Turkish football club, has called for the suspension of the Turkish championship following a gun attack on their team bus during a match against Caykur Rizespor. The bus was attacked as it drove to the airport after a match, resulting in the driver being wounded and taken to hospital. Fenerbahce believes the attack is not being solved in a way that satisfies them and public opinion, leading to the suspension of the championship.

A massive snow avalanche struck Everest Base Camp on Saturday, killing at least 17 people and injuring dozens. The avalanche, which occurred during the Nepal earthquake, left hundreds of climbers stranded at higher camps, with helicopters rescuing around 200 people. The disaster highlights the dangers of climbing in the Himalayas and the need for better infrastructure and rescue systems.

Gregory Margolin, a 16-year-old Jewish recruit in the Soviet Red Army during World War II, survived the war and later settled in Ukraine. Now, in 2023, he finds himself in the middle of a new conflict in Eastern Ukraine. Margolin, who had survived one war, was able to survive another, even as a stray missile hit his house, killing his daughter. He and his family fled to Israel, where they are now living in a refugee center set up by the International Fellowship of Christians and Jews. Margolin's granddaughter, Liora, says they felt safe in Donetsk, praying for their safety. The article highlights the ongoing conflict in Eastern Ukraine and the impact of war on individuals, including Margolin's struggle with Alzheimer's disease.

John Carver, Newcastle United's assistant manager, is eager to take charge of the team against Sunderland on Sunday, knowing that a victory could boost his chances of winning the manager's position beyond the season. Gullit, who was Newcastle's manager in 1999, controversially decided not to start star players Duncan Ferguson and Alan Shearer, leading to a 2-1 defeat. Carver's memories of Gullit's downfall remind him of the potential consequences of such decisions.

The Reverend Al Sharpton delivered a sermon and addressed the Walter Scott situation on Sunday morning in North Charleston, South Carolina, where a white police officer fatally shot a black driver. Sharpton called for reform in national policing legislation and urged the community to use this opportunity to change policing practices. He also attended a vigil near the scene of the Scott shooting on Sunday afternoon.

Brendan Rodgers will remind Raheem Sterling of his responsibilities after the Liverpool youngster's recent controversies, including allegedly inhaling nitrous oxide and puffing on a shisha pipe. Sterling scored the opener in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United, and Rodgers will speak to him about being a professional. Liverpool forward Sterling could have had more goals, and Rodgers praised his skill and ability for the first goal.

Labour received more than £1 million in union donations between April 6 and April 12, more than twice as much as the Conservative party, with £700,000 coming from Ed Miliband's party. This boost to Labour's election war chest is seen as a significant financial advantage, with most of the Tory cash coming from wealthy individuals.

Police were called to Manchester Airport after passengers on a Qatar Airways flight in Birmingham became disruptive and refused to disembark, causing a delay. The flight was diverted to Birmingham due to strong winds, and passengers were stranded for five hours. The airline arranged for the passengers to be bused to Manchester, where they were eventually allowed to disembark.

Canadian pop sensation Justin Bieber will carry Floyd Mayweather's championship belts into the ring ahead of his $300 million mega-fight with Manny Pacquiao on Saturday. The 21-year-old performer has been close friends with Mayweather for years and has accompanied him into the ring on numerous occasions. Bieber is set to lead Mayweather's entourage at the MGM Grand, with his daughter's support. The fight is being billed as the biggest in history, with Mayweather having a 47-0 record on the line.

Corinthian Colleges Inc., a for-profit career college, announced its decision to close all 28 of its remaining campuses, marking a significant victory in efforts to hold for-profit colleges accountable. The closure follows a curtailment of federal student aid access, affecting about 1.3 million students enrolled in for-profit colleges. The article highlights the predatory nature of these institutions, which enroll only 13% of college students but account for nearly half of all student loan defaults. The closure is seen as a step towards ending the exploitation of students and ending the multibillion-dollar industry of for-profit colleges.

Pep Guardiola has denied claims of a dispute with former Bayern Munich club doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit the club after being blamed for the defeat by Porto. Muller-Wohlfahrt claimed the bond of trust was damaged, while Guardiola played down the feud, stating it was his decision and injuries were part of football. Muller-Wohlfahrt had worked at Bayern for almost 40 years and was a world leader in his field.

Wladimir Klitschko, the reigning heavyweight champion, is set to make his return to Madison Square Garden for a world title defense against Bryant Jennings. Klitschko, who won Olympic gold in 1996, recalls how the sport has the power to change one's life, and believes age is not a barrier to his continued success in boxing.

Jeremy Clarkson, who was fired from Top Gear, has admitted he will miss fronting the show. Former presenter Angela Rippon expressed interest in returning to the motoring show if invited back. Lord Hall, the director-general of the BBC, announced that the corporation will not be renewing Clarkson's contract.

In a La Liga match, Fabian Orellana of Celta Vigo threw a lump of grass at Sergio Busquets during the closing stages, leading to Orellana being shown a red card. Busquets, in retaliation, grabbed his eye with the turf. Barcelona won 1-0 against Celta Vigo, earning crucial three points.

In 2013, three people died and over 200 were injured when bombs went off at the Boston Marathon finish line. This year, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the man convicted of the bombings, faces sentencing. Judge George A. O'Toole warned jurors not to attend the Boston Marathon or any events related to the race, stressing the importance of avoiding prejudicial information. The sentencing phase is expected to last four weeks, with the maximum penalty for several charges being death.

The annual "Tomb Sweeping Festival" in China, also known as Qingming Festival, is observed by millions of people marking the start of spring and honoring their ancestors. Families travel to ancestral graves to clean tombs, burn fake paper money, and leave food and drink to ensure their loved ones are not hungry or poor in the afterlife. The festival, which falls in the first week of April, is celebrated with parades, outdoor celebrations, and traditional dances. The festival is one of the 24 Chinese solar terms and is considered a significant time for preparing the land for planting.

Paul Simon, 73, has topped the UK album chart for the first time in 25 years with his latest release, The Ultimate Collection. The album, which includes hits from his 50-year career, outsold more youthful musicians like Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. Simon's recent tour with Sting is believed to have been the catalyst in helping him reach the top of the charts.

Iker Casillas, the 33-year-old Spanish goalkeeper, insists he will stay at Real Madrid even if David de Gea arrives to displace him as first choice keeper. Casillas claims he is willing to fight for the jersey he went on to make his own after breaking into the side as a 16-year-old in 1996. Real Madrid has repeatedly linked to a move for Manchester United's David de Gea, but Casillas insists he will continue to fight for the No. 1 jersey.

The UK's employment rate hit a record high of 31 million in the three months to February, with the International Monetary Fund praising Chancellor George Osborne's economic strategy. The Conservative government has overseen a "jobs miracle," with two million more people in work than in 2010. Rolls-Royce announced its biggest-ever order, worth over £6 billion, for Emirates. IMF chief Christine Lagarde and German finance minister Wolfgang Schaeuble praised Osborne's handling of the economy. The UK has reduced its deficit from a record £153 billion under Labour in 2009-10 to £90 billion last year, and the Chancellor has pledged to return Britain to the black in 2018-19.

SsangYong, a Korean automaker, is launching a new sports utility vehicle (SUV) called the Tivoli, priced under £13,000, targeting thrifty motorists. The SUV is named after the Italian town of Tivoli, known for its Renaissance architecture and garden, and features a European name. It offers a range of engines, transmissions, and safety features, including a five-year unlimited mileage warranty. The Tivoli aims to double SsangYong's annual UK sales from 2,000 to 4,000 vehicles.

A chef, Sam Longhurst, created a 10-inch, half-kilogram burger at the Whole Damn Farm restaurant in Manchester, containing six forms of three different meats and 2,000 calories. The burger, costing £13. 50, was inspired by a customer's request for a burger with three kinds of meat. The meal features two beef patties, homemade bacon jam, ham chunks, a whole fried chicken thigh, barbequed pulled pork, and bacon rashers, all sandwiched between two brioche buns. The creation was met with enthusiasm from diners, who praised its size and variety of meats.

Yeo Valley, a dairy company in North Somerset, has opened its staff canteen to the public, offering a gourmet menu of organic and locally sourced dishes at a subsidised price. The canteen, praised as the world's best staff canteen, features quirky light fittings and high tables and stools, and offers meals such as organic sourdough with Yeo Valley salted butter and a dessert of apple and rhubarb crumble with ice cream or creme fraiche. The canteen's menu changes daily based on the available produce.

Blues legend B.B. King was hospitalized for dehydration due to his Type II diabetes, but he is now much better and is back home resting with his grandchildren. King, 89, has used various models of Gibson guitars over the years, including a custom-made Lucille guitar. He has won multiple Grammy nominations and has released hits like "The Thrill Is Gone" and "When Love Comes to Town."

On Easter Sunday, Manhattan's Fifth Avenue was filled with bizarre hats as people celebrated the holiday. The parade featured a mix of conservative and outlandish headwear, including ship-shaped hats, elaborate dioramas, and floral bonnets. The event attracted a diverse crowd, including Christians, Jews, Hindus, agnostics, and atheists. The parade, which started in the 1880s, was a departure from its original strolling display and featured a wide range of headwear.

Emergency crews in Essex received a prank call about a squirrel being run over in Epping Forest, leading to the dispatch of two ambulances. This incident, along with others like a man calling to say he was locked out of his house and a woman reporting she felt ill after eating too much takeaway, highlights the need for people to use common sense when calling 999. The East of England ambulance service has received 1,248 inappropriate calls in the past two years, with front-line crews attending almost half of them. The service urges people to stop and think before making prank calls, as they can affect the lives of real emergency responders.

Chelsea players Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake, along with their teammates Loic Remy and Willian, participated in a football challenge organized by Audi. In the first round, Hazard and Ake secured a 5-3 win by firing balls into the boot of a car from close range. In the second round, they took on their teammates in a challenge to sink balls from long range, with Hazard and Ake winning the decider with a 6-0 lead. The final challenge involved shooting from long range, with Willian and Remy winning the game. However, Willian's long-range effort damaged an Audi car, leading to a humorous reaction from Remy.

Brendan Rodgers criticizes Raheem Sterling's advisor, Aidy Ward, for allegedly being manipulated by outside forces, suggesting Sterling would stay at Liverpool if left to make a decision alone. Rodgers sat down with Sterling to advise him to stay at the club, despite the player rejecting a contract extension worth £100,000 a week and having just two years left on his deal. Sterling has also rejected a contract extension worth £100,000 a week and has just two years left on his deal at the end of this season.

Rachel Riley, Countdown co-presenter, was embarrassed on a recent episode when contestants offered the same eight-letter double entendre, causing host Nick Hewer to struggle to stifle his laughter. Dr Phil Hammond, a celebrity guest, saved the day with the word "recondite." This incident is not the first time Hewer has struggled to contain himself, as he has also faced similar situations with other rude words. The Countdown show, which has been running since 1982, recently picked up a Guinness world record for reaching its 6,000th episode.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, who attempted to buy deadly poison on the internet and was later arrested, was spared jail after pleading guilty to trying to buy the toxin. The teenager, who cannot be named for legal reasons, expressed an interest in buying the poison and showed awareness of its toxicity and potential for use in causing harm. He was arrested during a raid on two homes in Tameside on February 16. The case highlights the dangers of the dark web and the importance of vigilance in law enforcement.

Three hours after giving birth, Lianne Hindle, 37, died at North Manchester General Hospital in December, prompting calls for action to prevent further tragedies at the maternity unit. Her death, along with those of three babies and one mother at the hospital, led to an investigation. The family of Lianne Hindle, whose partner died three hours after giving birth to their daughter Poppy, has called for changes to prevent similar incidents.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman, a seven-time world champion hurdler, gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Emily, just days after a video surfaced of her training while eight months pregnant. Pittman, who plans to compete in the Beijing World Championships and the 2016 Rio Olympics, continued to train while pregnant with her son Cornelis, who was born at 3.1 kilograms on Monday. The athlete's coach, Mike Hurst, praised her careful training and monitoring of her core temperature. Emily was conceived with an anonymous sperm donor and Pittman expressed her happiness and luck in having a second child.

A powerful storm capsized several sailboats participating in a regatta on Dauphin Island, Alabama, resulting in at least one death and missing persons. The storm caused widespread damage and forced crews to search through the night. The incident occurred around 4 p.m. and was confirmed to have killed at least one person. The storm was described as severe, with winds reaching up to 70 mph, and was expected to cause significant damage to the boats and surrounding area.

Roseanne Barr, 62, revealed she is going blind due to macular degeneration and glaucoma, two eye diseases that get progressively worse over time and can steal vision. Her doctors haven't provided a timeline, but her symptoms are worsening. Barr said in the interview that she helps relieve the pressure by using marijuana. Macular degeneration is a breakdown of the part of the retina that allows us to see fine details in the center of vision, while glaucoma damages the nerve that connects the retina to the brain. The American Academy of Ophthalmology recommends getting a baseline eye exam when you turn 40, and certain people are genetically predisposed to these diseases. There is no cure for either disease, but treatments can delay the progression of early-stage glaucoma and halt further vision loss in advanced cases of macular degeneration.

An Oklahoma jury convicted 17-year-old Chancey Luna of first-degree murder in the 2013 shooting death of Australian college baseball player Christopher Lane, who was killed while jogging in Duncan. Luna was found guilty of the fatal shooting from a passing car, and the jury recommended life in prison without parole. Luna's defense attorney argued that he meant to scare Lane, but the judge denied a second-degree murder conviction. Luna did not testify, and the defense called only his mother as a witness.

Arsene Wenger insists his record of 12 losses against Jose Mourinho will not affect Arsenal's match against Chelsea at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday. Wenger has drawn five and lost seven of their 12 clashes. Chelsea's strengths include efficient counter-attacks and set-pieces, while Arsenal's recent form and belief are highlighted. Wenger emphasizes the importance of the performance on Sunday.

Manny Pacquiao, a Filipino boxer, has become one of the most recognizable figures in sports after a series of major fights, including a bout against Floyd Mayweather, which is scheduled for Saturday night at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. Pacquiao, who was born into poverty in the Philippines, spent his early career boxing in the Far East before gaining recognition in 2001 when he fought against Lehlo Ledwaba in an IBF world super-bantamweight title fight in Las Vegas. Despite facing challenges, Pacquiao has risen to become a global superstar, and Mayweather's upcoming fight against him is expected to be a significant event.

Jack Grealish, a talented young footballer, has been photographed inhaling nitrous oxide, a drug that can be used recreationally but is also illegal. Grealish, who starred for Aston Villa in their FA Cup semi-final win over Liverpool, has been caught on camera using the drug. This incident, which could help keep Grealish grounded, comes after Arsenal's Arsene Wenger emphasized the importance of professional athletes' health and well-being. Grealish's performance and future in the sport are discussed, with the emphasis on making the right choices to ensure he remains on the back pages rather than the front.

Sam Barton, a 22-year-old man who underwent £55,000 in cosmetic surgery to resemble reality star Joey Essex, was attacked by a group of men with eggs on Easter Monday while enjoying drinks at a pub. The attack followed online abuse about his appearance and forced him to move house. Barton, who has spent £20,000 on teeth treatment, £5,000 on Botox, £2,000 on waxing, and £2,500 on tanning, has also spent £10,400 on two nose jobs, with one free on the NHS. He is the grandson of Aston Villa's European Cup-winning boss Tony Barton and is friends with Benefits Street star White Dee.

An Indiana university was in lockdown late on Friday night after a "likely prank call" about an armed person near the main administration building. Police received a phone call from someone saying that they had stabbed their roommate at the university, was armed with a shotgun and threatening to blow up the administration building. Manchester University had issued a statement advising students to shelter in place. Barricades were set up, and the university continued to post shelter in place warnings for hours after the original message. No injuries have been confirmed, and the university's peace studies program is located there.

Edinson Cavani, a key player for Paris Saint-Germain, prepares to face Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals. Cavani, known as "El Matador," must overcome the challenges posed by Barcelona's strong defense and the absence of key players like Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Marco Veratti. His goal drought, which lasted seven matches, has led to speculation about his future in Paris.

Derry Mathews has won the interim WBA lightweight title by a unanimous points decision over Tony Luis in a Liverpool fight. Mathews, who was drafted in at the last minute, outperformed Luis in the closing rounds but Luis showed aggression and landed a good uppercut in the sixth round. Mathews' relentless style and superior jab control gave him the victory, with Luis being deducted points for low blows and head use.

Hull FC defeated St Helens 28-20 in a surprise victory, overcoming St Helens' Good Friday exertions and forcing a third straight defeat for the league leaders. Jamie Shaul's long-distance try sealed the win, while Hull's Jordan Rankin added the extras. The game was marked by a tactical switch at the break, with Hull taking the lead and St Helens falling behind. The match was described as a to-and-fro affair, with Hull scoring twice in the second half and St Helens managing to get back within 12 points.

The United States' undocumented and documented immigrant population is projected to reach a record high of 51 million by 2023, with immigrants accounting for 14.8% of the population by 2060. This growth is expected to continue, with immigration population growing almost four times faster than the native-born population. The Center for Immigration Studies predicts that by 2060, immigrants could make up 82% of the population. This trend has significant implications for workers, schools, infrastructure, congestion, and the environment.

Jack Wilshere made his long-awaited return from injury as Arsenal's Under 21s lost 1-0 to Reading's Under 21s at the Emirates Stadium. Wilshere was joined by other injured players including Serge Gnabry and Abou Diaby. Reading's Martin Keown scored the only goal in the 8th minute, and the Gunners struggled to find an equalizer. Wilshere impressed in the second half, but Arsenal ultimately lost the match.

Justin Rose, the English golfer, has fallen outside the world's top 10 after a poor performance in Florida. Rose, who has been a fixture in the top five for the last three years, has been struggling with his form, resulting in three missed cuts and a 55th-place finish at the Cadillac Championship. To improve his game, Rose has been spending time on the practice ground, hitting 17 out of 18 greens in regulation and signing for a 69 at the Shell Houston Open. Rose believes that his recent performance is a welcome return to his previous form, and he is confident that he will finish well at the Masters. Phil Mickelson, another golfer, has also been struggling with his form, but he is focused on his game and does not worry about the rankings changing fast when he is playing well.

A £25 million mansion built on the site of a former milking parlour in Mayfair, London, has gone on the market. The property, which features modern amenities like an indoor swimming pool and a cinema room, was once a milking parlour and a depot before being demolished in the 19th century. The mansion, which has four bedrooms, is decorated with modern furnishings and luxurious features such as a private lift and a 14-piece dining table. It was constructed in 2011 after developers demolished the original structure. The property is being sold by estate agents Wetherell and Knight Frank.

Bayern Munich's squad is stronger despite injuries, according to Thomas Muller, as the team looks to reach the Champions League quarter-finals. Muller believes the team's unity will help them against Porto. Bayern Munich will rely on Muller and Robert Lewandowski, who are expected to score, despite the absence of key players like Arjen Robben, Franck Ribery, Bastian Schweinsteiger, and David Alaba. The team is confident and aims to become the first team to beat Porto in the Champions League this season.

Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton visited Mercedes' Brackley base to collaborate on a winning strategy for the upcoming Chinese Grand Prix. After Sebastian Vettel's victory at the Malaysian Grand Prix, Mercedes was surprised by Vettel's performance, which led to concerns about their dominance in the championship. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff admitted that the team's aggressive set-up pushed them into a three-stop strategy, which was not ideal in the high-temperature conditions. The visit to Brackley was seen as a crucial step in preparing for the upcoming race.

Oklahoma Governor Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to perform executions with nitrogen gas if lethal injection is ruled unconstitutional or unavailable. The bill, signed on Friday, states that the person will become unconscious within eight to 10 seconds and die a few minutes later from lack of oxygen. This follows a review by the U.S. Supreme Court of Oklahoma's use of lethal injections, which has been put on hold. Fallin reaffirmed her support for the death penalty, stating that Oklahoma executes murderers whose crimes are especially heinous and that capital punishment must be performed effectively and without cruelty.

Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice in Swansea's 3-1 win over Hull, leading the EA Sports' Performance Index with a score of 52.9 after another thrilling Premier League match. Gomis, who made a slow start to his career, has scored four goals in his last six games. Chelsea's Eden Hazard scored for the Blues, and Manchester United's Ander Herrera scored twice, placing him in the top four with a Game Index score of 51.7.

A freezer trawler sank in the Sea of Okhotsk, killing at least 56 crew members and sinking in just 15 minutes. More than 1,300 people are involved in the massive rescue operation, with 63 survivors rescued so far. The sinking was reportedly caused by an empty fuel tank and lack of ballast, and the ship hit an object in the sea. The incident occurred at around 4am local time, and temperatures in the water can drop to as low as -2 degrees Celsius.

Men with advanced prostate cancer could benefit from a pioneering drug originally meant for women, according to new clinical trials. Olaparib, already used to treat women with breast cancer, showed promising results in men with genetic faults within their prostate cancer tumors. Up to 30% of men with advanced prostate cancer have tumours that respond particularly well to olaparib, which can extend the length of time that a prostate cancer patient lives with the disease without it getting worse. The drug is the first cancer drug to target inherited genetic mutations and is one of the first of a new class of drugs called PARP inhibitors.

Travel photographer Rhiannon Taylor, 29, from Australia, has turned her passion for photography and globetrotting into a successful business by launching the website "In Bed With" to review and photograph the best hotels, beds, pools, and room service around the world. With more than 12, 000 followers on Instagram, she has built relationships with hotels and PR companies, allowing her to stay at exclusive resorts and feature their properties on her site. The website's name, "In Bed With," is a play on her Instagram handle, and the concept is unique, as she has been documenting her experiences in various parts of the world for seven years.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was mauled to death by two adult hippos in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park in eastern South Africa. The calf's mother watched in horror as the hippo was flung into the air before being dragged along the surface of the water. The two male hippos had been fighting for some time, and the mother of the calf stayed with her herd, possibly believing it safer to stay out of harm's way herself. The baby stood no chance against the two adults as they brawled in the muddy waters of the nature reserve.

The Football Association will contact QPR and Chelsea after an incident where Branislav Ivanovic was struck on the head by a cigarette lighter thrown from a section of home supporters at Loftus Road. Chelsea players celebrated the winning goal, and objects were thrown onto the pitch. QPR is reviewing CCTV footage and banning those involved, while Chelsea has a zero-tolerance policy towards such behavior.

A young mother and her three children were found murdered in their home in Tisdale, Saskatchewan. The suspect was found dead hours later, and police did not say how he died. The victim, LaTasha Gosling, and her two daughters, Janyaa and Jenika, and her son Landen, were discovered early Wednesday. The family had been missing for one day. The suspect and victim knew each other, and the family was described as quiet and hardworking. The Goslings' sister said the family was very difficult to deal with. A memorial has been set up outside their home.

Emily Thornberry, a senior Labour politician, lost her frontbench job after tweeting a photo of a house covered in England flags and with a white van outside, while renting out a property she bought from a housing association eight years ago. The incident highlighted Thornberry's hypocrisy in opposing right to buy but not "right to buy to let."

Mike Lane, a huntsman, was beaten by protesters armed with iron bars during an artificial scent chase, despite evidence pointing to the identity of the attackers. Wiltshire Police dropped the investigation three months later, despite the victim's claims that the police could have made more effort. The incident has angered hunt supporters and led to calls for the police to identify and prosecute the attackers.

Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes insists he has no intention of leaving the club this summer, stating he prefers to stay at the Mestalla. Gomes has been linked with Premier League teams Manchester United and Chelsea, but he denies being contacted by Chelsea. The 21-year-old has netted four times in 25 La Liga appearances and is happy to stay with Valencia in Spain.

An Australian teenager, Audrey Pekin, was raped twice by a man named Henry Alafu while on a Christmas holiday to Bali with her family. Alafu lured her to his remote home and then attacked her in a taxi as she tried to flee. The incident was reported to Indonesian police, who let Alafu escape back to Nigeria. The teenager, who is 19 years old, has accused the police of letting her attacker go.

PETA has teamed up with animal rights activist Ashley James to launch an anti-fur campaign against Harvey Nichols, a department store that previously abandoned its ten-year anti-fur policy. The campaign features James posing with a fake skinned fox, with the slogan "Harvey Nichols: Here's the Rest of Your Fur Coat." Harvey Nichols has since re-introduced its fur-free policy, with a range of fur products including coyote, raccoon, and rabbit pelts. James, who is vegan, advocates for informed purchasing decisions and criticizes the cruelty of the fur industry.

Chile has joined several South American neighbors in allowing civil unions between people of the same sex, with President Michelle Bachelet enacting a new law on Monday. The new law will take effect in six months and will give legal weight to cohabiting relationships between two people of the same sex and between a man and a woman. The law is intended to end discrimination faced by common-law couples and gives them greater rights in the realms of property, health care, pensions, and inheritance.

Chelsea are on track to become the most dominant title-winners in Premier League history, leading the table for 257 days as of April 10, 2005/06, surpassing Manchester United's record of 262 days. The Blues face QPR, Man Utd, and Arsenal in their final three games.

Cape Verde, a small Portuguese former colony with a population of 500,000, is known for having more musicians per square kilometer than any other country in the world. The country's diverse cultural heritage, shaped by the transatlantic slave trade, piracy, and Jewish exiles, has given rise to unique musical styles like batuque, morna, and funana. Cape Verde is now seeking to tap into the economic potential of its rich musical heritage, which includes the Kriol Jazz Festival, to help its economy flourish.

An old hoax video showing a wave rider surfing in front of the Sydney Opera House went viral again after heavy storms hit Sydney, with some users linking the phenomenon to the weather. The video, originally posted by Darren Johnson in June 2012, was quickly debunked by wave experts and YouTube commenters, who pointed out inaccuracies and the impossibility of such waves breaking inside Sydney Harbour.

Reading, the beaten FA Cup semi-finalists, lost to Birmingham in a 1-0 Championship game at the Madejski Stadium. Clayton Donaldson scored the winning goal in the 78th minute. Reading's Adam Federici, who made a costly mistake against Arsenal, was retained for the match. Birmingham, aiming to improve on their poor recent record, dominated the game but could not capitalize on their chances.

David Luiz, a key player for Paris Saint-Germain (PSG), will miss the Champions League quarter-final against Barcelona due to a hamstring injury sustained during a match against Marseille. The 27-year-old Brazilian defender, who is currently sidelined for at least four weeks, will miss both legs of the upcoming match, potentially impacting PSG's title defense.

The return of Game of Thrones has led to a significant increase in internet piracy, with more than 100,000 illegal downloads per day reported by Irdeto. The most downloaded episodes were from Brazil, followed by France, the US, Canada, and the UK. HBO has announced plans to launch a new streaming service, HBO Now, in an attempt to curb piracy and recapture revenue.

Leicester City will host West Ham United in a Premier League match on Saturday, with Leicester's Matt Upson out due to an Achilles injury. West Ham's Winston Reid is expected to return from injury. Leicester has won just one of their last 10 home matches, while West Ham has not lost in their last seven league games against Leicester.

For six years, a statue of Lucille Ball in Celoron, New York, has been a source of controversy. The statue, based on a moment from her show "I Love Lucy," depicts her as drunk and pitchy for a health tonic, which locals find unflattering. A Facebook page called "We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue" has gained over 600 likes, with the anonymous creator claiming the statue is "monstrous" and "nothing like the beautiful Lucy we all know." The town has tried to honor its most famous resident, but the statue has become a source of tension.

A 43-year-old woman, Sharon Smith, shed nearly half her body weight of 20st after being forced to stand during an 11-hour flight due to her fear of crushing the woman in the seat next to her. She had been a size 26 and weighed 18st 6lb when she started her business trip in December 2012. After joining Weight Watchers Online and running a 10k race, she lost 4st through slimming and another 4.5 stone after taking up running. Her weight loss began just under two years ago when she joined Weight Watchers Online, but she did not weigh herself immediately.

Nicola Bonn, a 34-year-old mother of 14-month-old Poppy, started a blog called Upfront Mama to share her experiences and advice for new mothers. Her candid account of raising a baby has gone viral, and she has shared a post titled "Why We Need to Stop Justifying Ourselves," which has been widely read. The post discusses the challenges of being a new mother, including the pressure to justify decisions and the overwhelming opinions of others. Bonn believes that one of the main hurdles for new mothers is the constant questioning of their decisions, which can be overwhelming and irritating.

Two teenage boys, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, from Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, are feared to have traveled to Syria to join ISIS. Hassan is believed to be related to Hammaad Munshi, who was arrested at 15 for planning to murder non-Muslims. The families are in shock and worry about their safety. The boys, who were on a school trip, used the Easter holidays to flee Britain.

Stephanie Scott, a beloved school teacher from Leeton, was brutally murdered just days before her much-anticipated wedding. Her father, Robert, described her as a bubbly and thoughtful person who gave so much joy to others. The wedding was originally scheduled for Saturday, but the day before, Stephanie's body was found in nearby bushland. The family is struggling to come to terms with the loss and the fact that their daughter's life was cut short when she had so much to look forward to.

Southampton is interested in signing Tonny Vilhena, a 20-year-old winger from Feyenoord, who wants to leave the club this summer. Koeman, the Southampton manager, is also considering bringing Jordy Clasie, a £10m-rated midfielder, to the south coast. Koeman is also looking to make Eljero Elia's loan move from Werder Bremen permanent. Southampton is currently seventh in the Premier League table and is in with a chance of qualifying for the Europa League.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture with beanbags in the library of Ickworth House, Suffolk, to encourage visitors to "dwell and take in the atmosphere," but this experiment has angered heritage experts who believe it is patronizing. The Trust has announced similar experiments at nine other venues around the country. Art historian Bendor Grosvenor criticized the move, calling it "misguided" and "patronizing nonsense." The National Trust's director of strategy, curatorship and external affairs, Simon Murray, defended the experiment, stating that each house is different and treated appropriately.

Former Prime Minister John Howard was photographed standing on the side of the road with a flat tyre, while his driver changed it. Felicity Waterford, who was waiting for her daughter at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music, noticed the vehicle and offered assistance. The former PM, who was a complete gentleman, agreed to a selfie with Ms Waterford. This incident came weeks after Liberal MP Christopher Pyne was challenged to change a tyre on national television.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis acknowledges that Joey Barton "probably had a point" about the team's performance during a 2-0 lead against Queens Park Rangers, leading to a 3-2 loss. Pulis, who was 2-0 up in a Second Division play-off final in 1999, believes Barton's criticism was justified given the circumstances. Pulis also praises the team's recent performances, stating they have not conceded after scoring first in a game.

A Bouvier's red colobus monkey, thought to be extinct for over 50 years, has been rediscovered in the remote rain forests of the Democratic Republic of Congo. Researchers captured the first-ever photograph of the monkey, which was previously known only from three specimens. The discovery proves the species is not extinct and highlights the vulnerability of these primates to hunters involved in the commercial bushmeat trade.

Kim Kardashian and her family, including her daughter North, visited Armenia for an eight-day trip, primarily to explore the country and its cultural landmarks. The visit was a surprise for the Kardashian family, who had expressed excitement about the opportunity to visit their father's homeland. The family stayed at the Armenia Marriott Hotel Yerevan, which is located in the heart of the city. The trip was well-received, with the family visiting notable landmarks such as the Opera House and the Zvartnots International Airport.

British expats Patrick and Valerie Jubb are trapped in southern Spain, attempting to sell their four-bedroom property in Jimena de la Frontera, Spain, but it is now on the brink of being torn down. The couple, who purchased the bed and breakfast in 2008, are facing legal battles with the local town hall over illegal additions made by a previous owner. The Jubbs claim they have done nothing wrong and are seeking to return to the UK, but their money is tied up in the property.

Despite expectations, Apple's iPhone sales in the first quarter exceeded analysts' forecasts, with more than 61 million units sold, accounting for two-thirds of its $58 billion in revenue and $13.6 billion in profit. Sales in China outpaced those in the US. The company's iPad revenue fell 29%, while Mac computer revenue rose 2%. Analysts estimate about 2 million Apple Watches have been sold, with early demand considered healthy but not blockbuster. Apple shares have risen more than 50% over the past year, making it the world's most valuable company.

A 3-year-old girl, Elisa Tyler, has been plagued by disturbing nightmares and daytime visions about a mysterious white van after her mother, Natali Castellanos-Tyler, died in a one-car SUV crash in Virginia. The girl's father, Craig Tyler, believes the recurring nightmares may be linked to the crash, which he suspects involved a white van. The incident, which occurred two months ago, has led to a series of hit-and-run accidents involving a white box truck in nearby communities.

Researchers at New York University have discovered that the brain can more easily remember neutral or boring events when they are tied to an emotion. This finding suggests that the brain has the ability to store information that seems inconsequential at the time in case it becomes useful later on. The study, which focused on how the brain stores memories for emotionally arousing stimuli, found that emotion affects activity in brain regions involved in emotional processing and encoding new experiences. The researchers noted that we often take for granted that we remember highly emotional events better than we remember neutral events, such as a lunch date. Emotion increases our ability to remember by affecting activity in certain brain regions and also strengthens memory for positive and negative events.

Jahnae Jackson, the girlfriend of a teenager with a life-threatening brain tumour, has raised over $80,000 for his life-saving surgery. The 18-year-old has put her psychology studies on hold to care for her boyfriend, who is paralysed and unable to dress himself due to the tumour. The surgery, performed by renowned neurosurgeon Dr. Charlie Teo, is expected to save his life, but he will need rehabilitation for some time. The community in the small town of Casino, NSW, has shown overwhelming support, raising more than the initial goal.

Nedum Onuoha, a QPR centre-back with 15 months left on his contract, is being targeted by Hull City, Everton, and West Ham United, among other clubs. Onuoha played in QPR's crucial 4-1 win over West Bromwich Albion at the Hawthorns. QPR are also interested in signing Catania defender Nicolas Spolli, while Hull City are showing interest in West Bromwich Albion striker Victor Anichebe, who is likely to be sold this summer.

In a study by Yale University researchers, they have documented the subtle differences in sentence structure across the US, revealing that each state has its own set of phrases that can seem bizarre to the rest of the English-speaking world. The study uses an interactive map to show common phrases for each state, with examples such as "I'm so totally over this" in New York and "I ain't never had no trouble with none of 'em" in Florida. The researchers found that presentative sentences like "Here's you a water bottle" were completely normal in the South, while in the North, it was almost unheard of.

A Canadian man named Kalman Kallai took a rocking chair on a 9-day journey across Canada, covering 2,796 miles from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia. He used the chair to enjoy the scenery and interact with various landmarks, including planes, boats, and wildlife. The journey was documented in a video, and Kallai's father joined him for part of the trip, sharing stories and bonding.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood revealed a "win bonus" of sweets and chocolate to six-year-old fan Charlie Pye, who applied for the club's hotseat after Paul Lambert was sacked. Sherwood joked that Pye's win bonus would be sweets and chocolate, and revealed a Twix multi-pack under the desk.

Kell Brook, the world boxing champion, enjoyed a night out at the Premier League darts event in his hometown of Sheffield. Dave Chisnall, who won both of his games in week 10, moved onto 17 points in second place in the table. Chisnall praised his performance, saying it was a confidence boost to beat the world champion. The event was part of Brook's preparations for his second title defence against Frankie Gavin on May 30.

Marco Verratti of Paris Saint-Germain praises Zlatan Ibrahimovic for his essential role off the pitch, despite the striker's suspension for the Champions League quarter-final first leg against Barcelona. Ibrahimovic helps young players progress and exerts confidence in the team.

The Ministry of Defence accidentally published a secret RAF aerodrome manual containing vital GPS coordinates and runway depth information on their website, which could be used by Argentina to prepare an invasion of the Falkland Islands. The MoD admitted the manual was available online but disabled the link. The Falkland Islands are defended by modern Eurofighter Typhoon aircraft, and the UK is considering leasing 12 Russian Sukhoi SU-24 bombers from Argentina.

Paul Anderson, Huddersfield Giants coach, hopes to improve his team's offensive performance to match their defensive efficiency as they aim to climb back up the Super League ladder. The Giants have fallen from third to ninth after losing all three games over the Easter period, but Anderson believes his team can improve with better offensive play. If Huddersfield wins their next game, they could leapfrog Catalans Dragons, who have the best defensive record in the league. The article also mentions that Widnes are the only team yet to take a point from their travels, and Vikings coach Denis Betts expects a tough test against Castleford.

Planners in Windsor have approved two Costa coffee shops, one of which is less than 500 yards from the other, in a residential area. This has led to concerns from residents who believe it will lead to an overabundance of coffee shops in the area.

The British Veterinary Association (BVA) has withdrawn its support for the controversial pilot culls of free-running badgers, stating that the first two years of culling have not demonstrated conclusively that "controlled shooting" of badgers can be effective and humane. The BVA still supports badger culling to tackle tuberculosis in cattle. The Environment Secretary has promised to roll out more culls across the country if the Conservatives win the election, with critics arguing that the culls have been criticized and that the low numbers in Gloucestershire and Somerset reflect challenges from unlawful protest and intimidation.

Geoff Barrow, founder of Portishead, accused streaming services of underpaying his band for their music, stating he received £1,700 in royalties for 34 million plays. Barrow argues that younger artists are getting poor deals due to streaming, and calls for better compensation for musicians. Streaming companies defend their practices, offering artists a fair price and providing exclusive content. Jay-Z launched Tidal, a subscription-based streaming service, offering artists a better deal and charging £20 per month.

Game of Thrones fans who did not want to wait for the show's fifth season premiere leaked the first four episodes online, which are scheduled to debut tonight. The episodes, titled "The Wars to Come," "The House of Black and White," "High Sparrow," and "The Sons of the Harpy," have been downloaded more than 550,000 times, making it the most illegally downloaded program in the world. HBO is actively investigating the breach, and the series is the most pirated in the world, with Brazil and France being the top two countries by illegal downloads.

A 25-year-old singer named Daniel Buccheri composed an emotional song to use as his brother's best man's speech at his brother's wedding. The unique speech, performed on the keyboard, was composed to the tune of "Stay With Me" and included tributes to his brother and his new wife. The speech was viewed over 100, 000 times online and included anecdotes about his brother's love for his new wife.

Zara Phillips, the Queen's granddaughter, has revealed how she regained her fitness after giving birth to her daughter Mia. She started exercising every morning, hitting the exercise bike at her home before her daughter wakes up. Phillips, who is vying for a place on Team GB at the Rio Olympics, aims to qualify for the eventing team that goes to the Olympics in 2016.

Raheem Sterling's interview, in which he said he was not ready to sign a new contract at Liverpool, has angered fans and potentially changed their opinion of him. The interview was seen as ill-timed and unprofessional, and it has fueled speculation about Sterling's future. Liverpool fans are divided, with some hoping he will leave the club, while others want him to stay. Sterling has been linked with a move to Arsenal, and the club's stance on his potential departure is uncertain.

Barcelona's 1996 Spanish Super Cup-winning team, led by Bobby Robson and Pep Guardiola, is now breeding managers. Luis Enrique, Laurent Blanc, Julen Lopetegui, and Albert Ferrer are among those who have taken up coaching positions, including former teammates Luis Enrique and Julen Lopetegui.

Former Manchester United legend Eric Cantona has declared Paris Saint-Germain forward Javier Pastore the best player in the world, praising his creativity and ability to pass the ball. Cantona, who won the Ballon d'Or in 1993, believes Pastore's unique skills make him the most creative player in the world. Despite statistics showing Messi and Ronaldo as the top scorers, Cantona's assessment is based on his personal observation of Pastore's performances.

Lorenzo Simon, 34, was found guilty of murder for killing his tenant Michael Spalding, 39, by dismembering his body and disposing of the parts in a canal. The case involved Simon forcing Spalding to decorate his flat and then attacking him, leading to his murder. The trial took 15 hours and resulted in a unanimous verdict. Michelle Bird, Simon's girlfriend, was cleared of murder but admitted assisting in the crime.

Local councils in Essex and Gloucestershire are using "loneliness maps" to identify areas where elderly and socially isolated residents are most vulnerable. The maps are based on public health factors such as age, living alone, mental health issues, and low income. The maps are used to target "danger zones" of loneliness and provide targeted help to those in need. The Campaign to End Loneliness recommends the use of these maps across the country as a way to treat the problem.

Dedicated waitress Judy Eddingfield, 65, celebrated her 50th anniversary at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, the only job she has ever had or ever wanted. She remembers when French fries and a classic Coca-Cola cost just 65 cents, and her first day on the job when she spilled a shake all over a woman's fur coat. Eddingfield has been providing top-notch service for 60 years, and her favorite memory was when Jerry Mathers and Tony Dow of the television series 'Leave It to Beaver' came to eat there in the late 1970s.

Former England captain Mike Gatting believes Kevin Pietersen should not return to the international set-up immediately, even if he scores runs for Surrey. Gatting suggests that if Gary Ballance, Ian Bell, and Joe Root play well, Pietersen might not have a place in the team. Gatting also mentions that England captain Alastair Cook has struggled with poor performances and may face questions if he fails to score runs against West Indies.

A 17-year-old college student, Caleb Benn, developed an app called "Uploader for Instagram" that allows users to upload photos directly from their computer to the popular photo-sharing platform. The app, which is priced at $4.99, has reportedly made Benn $1,000 a day. However, Instagram has filed a lawsuit against Benn, claiming that his app violates the company's terms of service. Benn has until Monday to fix the issue, but he believes doing so would make the app pointless. The controversy highlights the tension between social media platforms and developers who want to expand their user base.

South Korean companies frequently hold hoesik dinners, where employees drink alcohol together. Foreign business travelers may feel pressured to participate, but drinking etiquette is crucial. Koreans view drinking as a way to get to know people. To avoid offending others, follow these seven rules: identify the higher person in the relationship, defer to them, and turn your body away from senior figures when drinking.

The Duke of Kent, 79, suffered a dislocated hip during an Easter trip to Balmoral and was admitted to Aberdeen Royal Infirmary. He was successfully treated and discharged today, with his daughter driving him away. The Duke, who became the Duke of Kent at age six, is the son of Prince George and is known for his royal duties and involvement with Freemasonry.

Meter Maids, a 50-year-old tradition of Surfers Paradise, Queensland, have been called into question by local business owners who argue that advancements in parking meter technology have made the practice obsolete. The initiative, started in 1965 by Gold Coast developer Bernie Elsey, involved young women in gold bikinis walking the main tourist strip and placing money into expired meters. However, local business owners claim the group is no longer providing a public service and are violating anti-touting laws by promoting branded merchandise. The Gold Coast Chamber of Commerce president, Peter Yared, argues that the group is now a business and no longer performs any service for the community. Despite this, Surfers Paradise Meter Maids general manager Michael Yarwood maintains that the tourists love and embrace the practice, which he believes is quintessentially part of the Gold Coast and Surfers Paradise experience.

Greece has denied it will miss a repayment of £330 million to the International Monetary Fund, claiming it will make the payment on time. Deputy finance minister Dimitris Mardas stated that Greece will in fact pay on April 9. Greece has drawn up plans to introduce a parallel drachma currency to pay domestic bills, but this has been denied by the country. The International Monetary Fund is due to repay a £330 million loan on April 9, and there are concerns that Greece may default on the payment.

Turkey has blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after refusing to remove pictures of a prosecutor held during an armed siege last week, citing the images as "deeply upset" the hostage's family. The prosecutor, Mehmet Selim Kiraz, died in hospital after being taken hostage by the Revolutionary People's Liberation Party-Front. The DHKP-C is considered a terrorist group by Turkey, the European Union, and the US.

A young Star Wars fan named Colin Gilpatric wrote a letter to George Lucas, the creator of the Star Wars franchise, asking if Jedi Knights could marry. Lucasfilm responded positively, stating that marriage would not lead to becoming a Sith and that it would be a path of the light. Colin was ecstatic to receive the letter and was able to receive a package of Star Wars merchandise.
Wisconsin defeated Kentucky 71-64 in the NCAA Tournament semi-finals, ending Kentucky's unbeaten streak. Wisconsin advances to the Final Four, while Kentucky finishes the season at 38-1.

Vince Neil, a member of Mötley Crüe, was criticized for his rendition of the American national anthem at a football game, which was seen as disrespectful by some. This incident highlights the potential consequences of performing the anthem in a way that is perceived as inappropriate or offensive.

A video of a devastating moment in which a man, Barry Lyttle, caused his brother, Patrick, to fall to the ground and have his head snap back after a single punch has been released for the first time. The video shows the brothers arguing at a bar in Sydney, with Patrick pushing Barry and then retaliating with a punch. Barry is charged with grievous bodily harm and has pleaded guilty. Magistrate Graeme Curran suggested a jail sentence, but the brother called for the charges to be dropped. The brothers, who had only been reunited for a holiday, are now facing legal consequences.

The family of conjoined twin sisters Faith and Hope Howie, who died 19 days after birth, were devastated to find their gravesite cleared of mementos and thrown in the rubbish by cemetery staff. The Howies had built a small shrine at the site, but when they returned to retrieve their daughters' belongings, everything had been removed apart from a bunch of flowers. The staff had not been notified of the cleaning process, and the Howies were only able to retrieve about 25% of their memorabilia.

Lord Neuberger, the President of the Supreme Court, suggested that Muslim women should be allowed to wear a full-face veil while appearing in court, as it shows respect towards different customs. He emphasized the need for judges and courtrooms to be sensitive to the cultural and social habits of those facing them. This suggestion comes amid uncertainty over the place of Muslim traditional dress in the legal system.

Andre Cole, a 52-year-old Missouri inmate, was executed for the 1998 murder of his ex-wife and her friend, Anthony Curtis, in a fit of rage over child support payments. Cole was the third convicted killer executed in Missouri this year, following appeals that were denied. He was executed by lethal injection at 10:15 pm on Tuesday at the Eastern Reception, Diagnostic and Correctional Center in Bonne Terre, Missouri. The execution was carried out despite a clemency petition that raised concerns about Cole's race and the all-white jury that convicted him.

Prince Harry will fly out of the UK to Australia without seeing his new niece or nephew, as the Duchess of Cambridge is several days overdue for the birth of her second child. Harry, who will be bumped down in the line of succession, had returned briefly to hand out prizes at the London Marathon after engagements in Turkey. He is now on a month-long placement with the army and a week-long tour of New Zealand, unable to meet the new royal baby until mid-May.

An alleged fraudster named Justin Jackson has been accused of posing as Oprah Winfrey, former Obama aide Reggie Love, and Madonna's manager in an attempt to trick people into giving him jobs, clothes, free food, and jewelry worth $2.4 million. Jackson is being sued by Oprah's TV network and Love, and has been convicted for grand theft over a ruse in which he tricked a jeweler into lending him items worth $2.4 million. He is accused of sending letters purporting to be from Oprah and her representatives, as well as from former Obama aide Reggie Love, to recommend him for jobs and get free goods.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini has placed a €50 million price tag on Paulo Dybala, claiming he is the "new Messi" and demanding PSG pay at least €50 million for the player. Dybala is being tracked by Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, Juventus, and Paris Saint-Germain, with Inter Milan manager Roberto Mancini reportedly watching the Serie A match between Parma and Palermo on Sunday. Zamparini is seeking a significant sum for Dybala, with some suggesting he could be sold to PSG if they meet his demands.

Hundreds of thousands of Brazilians are protesting against President Dilma Rousseff, calling for her impeachment over an economic downturn and a massive bribery scandal involving Petrobras. The protests are fueled by allegations of a multimillion-dollar kickback scheme at the state-run oil company, with Petrobras considered Brazil's corporate jewel. Rousseff's supporters defend her, while opponents argue she should be impeached for failing to address corruption. The protests have grown in size and breadth, with some calling for a military intervention to oust the President.

Former Manchester United midfielder Eric Cantona has refuted claims he starred in a soft porn film, insisting it is a "piece of art". The French film, "You and the Night", includes a scene with Cantona on his hands and knees in just his underwear. Cantona, 48, says it is not pornography but a work of art, praising its beauty and calling it "superb artistic orgy".

Psychologists have found that certain types of music can enhance the enjoyment of a fish and chip supper, with specific music types being the perfect accompaniment to different flavors in food and drink. The study suggests that the intensity of Nessun Dorma, performed by Luciano Pavarotti, is the perfect accompaniment to dark mouse or coffee, while the high-pitched piano in Billie Holiday's Autumn in New York can help emphasise the autumnal flavor of a pumpkin pudding.

Raheem Sterling, 20, has been offered a £100, 000-a-week contract by Liverpool, but negotiations have stalled. Manager Brendan Rodgers described the offer as "incredible." Sterling, who has two years left on his contract, has postponed contract talks until the end of the season. PFA Chief Executive Gordon Taylor defends Sterling, stating he is not a "money grabber" and believes waiting until the season is over could be a wise move. Sterling has been linked with moves to Arsenal and leading clubs in Spain. Taylor emphasizes that Sterling is aware of what he owes to Liverpool and that the club has looked after him.

An Ohio woman, La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, discovered her biological mother, Francine Simmons, who works at the same call-center operation company as her, after the Ohio Department of Health released birth records for people born between January 1, 1964, and September 18, 1996. Mitchell-Clark found out about her mother's job and found her on Facebook, leading to a phone call and eventual meeting.
