The reunion led to the discovery of three younger sisters, Kamala and Maisha Cummings, and a sense of relief for the family.

Oscar "Papoo" Hernandez Jr., a convicted gun trafficker, was "awed" by New England Patriots star Aaron Hernandez and sent him an assault rifle and handguns a month before Odin Lloyd's murder. Hernandez pleaded guilty to weapons charges and faces up to 30 months in prison.

A 33-year-old Florida bus passenger named Joel Parker was arrested for throwing a Snickers bar at the driver's head after threatening him and being disruptive during the ride. The driver was not injured, but Parker was charged with battery and issued a trespass warning.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has discussed pre-season plans with Saido Berahino, indicating the striker will remain at the club beyond the summer transfer window. Berahino, who has expressed a desire to play in the Champions League, is likely to be included in England's under-21 squad for the upcoming European Championships. Pulis praised Berahino's performance and commitment, suggesting he would not be influenced by agents.

Giovanni Lo Porto, a Sicilian man who worked with the German aid organization Welthungerlife to help rebuild Pakistan after flooding, was killed by a U.S. drone strike in 2012. He was abducted by four armed men in 2011 and died along with his colleague Bernd Muehlenbeck in the same incident. Lo Porto was a project manager for the clean water and sanitation program with Welthungerlife, working with 8 to 10 international staffers and 100 to 200 locals. His work and life came to a halt on January 19, 2012, when he was abducted and killed by armed men.

A photographer captured an image of hundreds of sharks gathered off the coast of south Florida near Sebastian Inlet, with the scene being described as a "worst nightmare" by the photographer. The sharks were seen swimming just 100 feet from the beach and were theorized to be Blacktip or Spinner sharks, which migrate to breed in shallower waters. The incident has been shared more than 2,000 times on social media.

An 11-year-old retired K-9 officer named Zeus, a German Shepherd who worked with the Ridgefield Police Department for eight years as a K-9 officer, was honored in a grand procession before he was put down due to a severe degenerative hip disorder and declining health. The tribute was held on Wednesday, and Zeus's final ride was in a cop patrol car. The police department wrote an emotional message about Zeus, expressing their deep regret at his passing. The grand procession was attended by officers from the department and police departments across the state, and residents held signs and waved a flag at half staff next to a draped black cloth at the department. Zeus was a beloved officer and friend who assisted with more than 250 narcotics arrests and helped track down 50 missing or wanted individuals during his eight-year career.

Since Operation Yewtree, reports of child sexual abuse have surged by more than 60%, with thousands of new cases filed in 2014. Despite a 9% drop in arrests, critics accuse the Government of failing to protect victims. The number of reported cases has increased in South Yorkshire by 577%, with 501 cases investigated in 2014 compared to 74 in 2011. The NSPCC helpline has seen a 81% increase in calls about sexual abuse since the operation was launched in 2012.

Iceland has become a popular filming location for TV series and Hollywood blockbusters, with Thingvellir National Park, Svartalfheim, Reykjanes Peninsula, Skaftafell National Park, and Vatnajokull glacier being featured in various productions. Icelandair's infographic highlights the stunning landscapes of the country, such as Thingvellir National Park, Svartalfheim, Reykjanes Peninsula, and Vatnajokull glacier, which have been used in films like Game of Thrones, Thor: The Dark World, Interstellar, and Prometheus. The article also mentions that Europe's most powerful waterfall, the Dettifoss, was used in the opening scenes of Prometheus.

A 100-year-old mechanic's garage in Sydney has sold for $1.2 million, with the property being converted into a home. The grey-fronted building, originally a fire station, was used as a mechanic's garage for three generations.

Samantha Rawcliffe, a 40-year-old mother-of-two from Morecambe, was diagnosed with functional neurological disorder (FND) after losing control of her body and crashing her car. The rare condition, an umbrella term for a range of neurological symptoms that doctors cannot explain, has left her unable to walk and relies on a mobility scooter. She is now confined to her house and takes 32 different drugs daily to manage symptoms.

The sculptor of a controversial statue of Lucille Ball, dubbed "Scary Lucy," has admitted to being "disappointed" with the work and offered to fix it for free. The statue, based on a moment from Ball's show "I Love Lucy," has been called "monstrous" and "frightening" by some residents of Celoron, New York. The sculptor, Dave Poulin, pledged to create a new statue that would be "beautiful and charming" and cost an estimated $8,000 to $10,000 to recast.

Bayern Munich's versatile left-back David Alaba will miss the rest of the season after being ruled out for around seven weeks with a torn knee ligament. Alaba, who was out for three months earlier this season, was injured while playing for Austria against Bosnia. He is set to start rehabilitation work in about a month and will miss the closing stages of the season. Bayern Munich, who are top of the Bundesliga, will face Porto in the Champions League quarter-finals later this month.

Beatrice Nokes, the daughter of two solicitors and a Scotland Yard detective, appeared in court on charges of running an upmarket prostitution ring with her father's friend Daniel Williams. Nokes, 21, is accused of inciting prostitution and grooming young women for sex. Williams, 37, is facing multiple charges including voyeurism and hiding profits. The case has sparked controversy over the use of police computers and hidden equipment for surveillance.

Diana Doyle, a whistleblower, revealed that a firm linked to the sale of NHS patient data is offering details of eating disorder sufferers, stress, hair loss, dandruff, impotence, snoring, dieters, and those with plastic surgery for just 12p a head. The firm, Sequester, is also offering to supply names of those who have had plastic surgery, smoke, wear glasses or contact lenses, have sensitive teeth, and have wills or health insurance. The revelations prompted probes by the Information Commissioner’s Office and the Direct Marketing Commission, and a third investigation by the General Pharmaceutical council into Pharmacy2U, the UK’s biggest online pharmacy.

Jordan Spieth, the 21-year-old golfer who won the 2017 Masters tournament, expressed his love for his autistic sister Ellie, who was unable to attend the event. Spieth, who equaled Tiger Woods' 1997 record winning score of 18 under par, became the second-youngest winner of the tournament, behind only Woods, who was 155 days younger. Ellie, who is 14 years old, provides Spieth with perspective and support, helping him understand the bigger picture of life. Spieth's victory was described as "even better" than his dreams, and he expressed his hope to be finishing his final Masters appearance in 50 years' time.

Dick Advocaat, the 67-year-old Dutch manager of Sunderland, will not underestimate the significance of the Old Firm derby against Newcastle, unlike his 1998 performance when he said the match was just another game, leading to a humiliating loss. Advocaat, who has won just twice at home this season, believes the home crowd will provide an extra weapon for Sunderland to win the game.

A dispute erupted between a young woman and a butcher in Sydney over a chicken purchase for a Game of Thrones-themed dinner. Belinda Bartholomew, the girlfriend of Roosters star Aidan Guerra, claims she was racially abused and told to go to an "Aussie butcher" when she tried to change her chicken selection. The butcher, Sam the Butcher, denies the claims, stating that he was slow with his eftpos machine and that Bartholomew was the one being rude.

Freddo Frogs, a popular children's chocolate, have been reduced in size by 20% from 15g to 12g, despite maintaining the same retail price. This change was spotted by a shop owner and is part of a broader trend of declining confectionery sales. Cadbury's parent company, Mondelez International, announced the change due to increased manufacturing costs, though the company's profit before tax rose 46% from $87 million to $127 million in 2013. The change has led to backlash from consumers, with some calling it a "thief" and others expressing disappointment.

Hillary Clinton's campaign-in-waiting held a meeting in Brooklyn on Saturday, distributing a "values statement" that outlines the campaign's goals and strategies. The document, obtained by CNN, includes ideas from Clinton's soon-to-be staffers and advisers, emphasizing humility, discipline, and unity. The campaign aims to avoid mistakes from Clinton's 2008 campaign and will be called "Hillary for America." Clinton plans to launch her presidential candidacy on Sunday with a video message on social media, followed by visits to Iowa and New Hampshire.

A 29-year-old woman, Kyli Wilfson, revealed her 18-month-long battle with chronic pancreatitis, a rare condition that left her unable to eat anything for a year and a half despite feeling extremely hungry. Initially diagnosed with acute pancreatitis, she was later confirmed with chronic pancreatitis, which only worsened over time. Wilfson, who had previously experienced digestive problems, was eventually diagnosed at the age of 26. Despite her condition, she maintained an appetite but could not eat without experiencing excruciating pain. Her weight dropped to 80 pounds, and she had to postpone her wedding. Wilfson found solace in a support group for people with chronic pancreatitis, and her story highlights the challenges faced by those with this rare condition.

Scottish National Party leader Nicola Sturgeon poses with a sceptical face in this meme, referencing Labour leader Ed Miliband's direct message to Prime Minister David Cameron, saying: 'David, if you think this election is about leadership, then debate me one-on-one.' The images were inspired by a debate that saw Miliband warned he would not get into power without lurching left, as Sturgeon told him he is 'not strong enough' to win power on his own. Cameron and Clegg stayed away, with the Prime Minister and his deputy superimposed over Christopher Steed and Stephen Webb from Channel 4 series Gogglebox.

Amir Khan, the British boxer, is set to face Manny Pacquiao in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, after Mayweather declined the opportunity. Khan, who has been waiting for Mayweather for two years, is now considering a fight with Pacquiao. The fight could take place in November or December, and Khan hopes to fight in the Middle East.

A tiny two-bedroom home in Islington, London, priced at £750,000, has sold for £750,000, despite being only 5ft wide in some areas and 8ft 8in wide at its widest. The narrow house, with a 'galley kitchen' and a garden, has attracted a lot of interest and is now under offer. The home, which was put on the market with Foxtons for £750,000 in 2001, is described as a 'stylish two bedroom period house' with characterful touches and a pretty rear garden. The buyer will have to pay £27,000 in stamp duty, the same as a second-hand narrow boat which is 50ft long.

The SNP leader Nicola Sturgeon is launching an extraordinary bid to lead the UK, unveiling a manifesto including policies tailored for a power-sharing deal with Labour. Several of her election pledges overlap with Labour policy, such as slashing tuition fees in England and rolling back competition in the English NHS. The SNP aims to build a 'progressive alliance' for people 'right across the UK' and aims for 'modest' spending increases funded by more borrowing. The SNP is on course for a landslide victory, potentially triggering constitutional turmoil similar to the 1910 election.

Two mistakes by Rangers goalkeeper Robby McCrorie led to Celtic winning the Glasgow Cup 2-0, clinching the trophy for the fourth time in eight seasons. Celtic's Josh Kerr scored the opening goal, and Robby McCrorie missed a penalty kick. The match was played behind closed doors due to fan trouble, and Celtic's victory was celebrated by their U17 players.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis, who previously played for Crystal Palace, announced he will continue wearing his distinctive cap, track suit, and white trainers at all matches, despite his former club's victory. Pulis, who led West Brom to a 2-0 win over Crystal Palace, stated he will return to the stadium in suit and tie after the match to address the press. The win moved West Brom to 36 points, securing their survival in the Premier League.

Jameela Jamil, a 29-year-old television presenter and former model, spent £3,000 on having all her amalgam fillings removed and replaced with white fillings after experiencing health problems for nearly seven years. The fillings were removed due to high levels of mercury detected in her blood tests, which suggested they were the cause of her symptoms, including puffy faces, heavy heads, and fainting. The dental amalgam, made from a mixture of metals including silver, tin, and copper, is used for robust fillings on back teeth but can release mercury vapour when being placed or removed, potentially causing health issues.

Suge Knight, the co-creator of Death Row Records, was refused an appeal to have his bail reduced from $10 million to $5 million as he awaits trial for murder and attempted murder. Despite walking into court, he had to be carted out in a wheelchair. Knight believes his close friend, the undefeated professional boxer Floyd Mayweather, will bail him out when he wins his next fight. Mayweather, worth $420 million, is set to land a record pay check after going head-to-head with Manny Pacquiao on Saturday.

In an interview with Puss Puss magazine, stylish chef Gizzi Erskine discusses her fussy feline, Kimchi, who loves poppadoms, tortilla chips, and taramasalata. The cat, described as having a discerning palate, prefers crunchy human food and considers taramasalata as his "death row dish." Erskine, who lives in a foodie household, has had to put Kimchi on a diet due to her cat's obesity. Kimchi is also known for his love of cheese, caviar, and fish, and has even indulged in cat food. Erskine recently added a new addition to her cat family, Ponzu, named after her favorite Japanese dressing.

The father of a little girl who appeared in a photograph of a mysterious pair of boots in Japan has no idea what the boots could be. The photograph, taken in 2014, sparked debate online about the boots' origin and meaning. The father insists there was no one else in the vicinity and that the boots were not Photoshopped.

The UK government plans to introduce new immigration policies that will require foreign workers to pay an average of £22,000 in tax over four years before they can claim benefits. The measures, outlined in the Tory manifesto, will ban EU migrants from receiving welfare support for four years and limit access to benefits for those in work. The changes are part of efforts to curb net migration to the UK and are expected to be unveiled this week.

A severely disabled boy, Cody Neatis, has been sleeping on a mattress on the floor at Royal Preston Hospital for seven nights due to a lack of a suitable bed for him. Cody, who has Down's syndrome, epilepsy, autism, and is fed by a tube, has been without a hospital bed because staff do not have the special cot needed to keep him safe in his sleep. His mother, Lynne Neatis, 48, has had to sleep with Cody, who has a developmental age of around 12 months, on the mattress. The hospital does not have the specialist high-sided cot needed for Cody to sleep in, and the local health trust has not provided a suitable bed. Lynne Neatis is demanding answers from the trust as she claims she has waited two years for the bed.

Ahead of the Masters golf tournament, Derek Lawrenson reports on the excitement and challenges faced by players, including Ian Poulter forgetting his golf clubs, Henrik Stenson recovering from flu, Tiger Woods playing with his children, and the tradition of skipping golf balls across water at the 16th hole.

Juventus have ruled out a move for Manchester United loan star Radamel Falcao, claiming his wages are 'beyond their means'. Falcao, who scored only four goals since arriving at Old Trafford, is unlikely to remain at the club. Juventus general manager Beppe Marotta stated that Falcao wanted to come to Turin last summer but the club has now taken themselves out of the race to sign him. Juventus are interested in striker Paulo Dybala and Edinson Cavani, with Dybala rated at £35m.

David Cameron plans to sell Lloyds Bank shares worth £4 billion if he wins the election, offering them at a discount and encouraging long-term ownership. This is the largest privatisation since the Thatcher era, with a £20 billion bailout by Gordon Brown. The sale aims to help pay down the national debt and is part of a Conservative policy to hark back to the 1980s.

Living near congested roads with high levels of air pollution can cause 'silent strokes' that increase the risk of dementia, according to a study by researchers at Boston University School of Medicine. The microscopic particles, mostly from traffic fumes and factory emissions, alter the structure of the brain and are linked to a 46% higher risk of silent strokes in towns and cities. The study, published in the journal Stroke, found that increases in PM2.5 exposure were associated with a 46% higher risk of silent strokes.

Jessica Ainscough, a 30-year-old wellness warrior who died from a rare and aggressive form of cancer, wrote an emotional letter to her followers revealing she was undergoing radiation treatment in her final weeks. She had previously rejected chemotherapy and radiation, opting for controversial Gerson Therapy, which lacks scientific support. After discussions with experts, Ainscough began a course of targeted radiation in her final weeks, which successfully managed to shrink the tumour but caused complications. Her partner, Tallon Pamenter, described her as a "wellness warrior" who displayed courage and grace, and her death has stripped him of the magic that once brought joy to his life.

Ten people, including four children, were involved in a multi-vehicle crash on the Brisbane Valley Highway in Brisbane's west on Wednesday afternoon. Three vehicles collided, resulting in chest and shoulder injuries for a 40-year-old man and a 5-year-old boy, as well as arm and abdominal pain for a 27-year-old woman and a 6-year-old girl. The incident occurred near Fernvale, with six others, including an infant and two young girls, being taken to Ipswich Hospital with minor injuries or for further assessment. A man suffered hand lacerations, and two females escaped injuries. The affected stretch of the highway was closed off, with diversions in place south of Fernvale.

Jason McDonald, a 34-year-old volunteer at the Colorado Gator Farm, walked a thin slackline over a pool containing more than 50 hungry alligators, including some measuring up to ten feet in length. McDonald, who has been involved with alligators for over ten years and has taken handling classes, thought this would be an interesting new way of interacting with the fearsome creatures. The gators were surprisingly ok with the slackline, and McDonald plans to take his hobby further by walking over Elvis or Morris, his two biggest gators on the farm.

The son of a Syrian imam who was shot dead on a London street may have met his father's killer just days before the murder. Abdul Hadi Arwani, an opponent of Syrian President Bashar Al-Assad, visited the area where he was killed with his son days before his death. The man, who has not been otherwise identified, also told Arwani that there was no need for his son to accompany him again when he did come back. The counter-terrorism unit is investigating whether the man was a hired killer who postponed the hit because Arwani was not alone.

Hong Kong's Jenny's cookies, a popular buttery treat, have sparked a black market frenzy, with tourists and locals lining up for hours to purchase them. The original store warns against buying "fake" cookies, while bakeries produce knockoffs and resell them at a markup. The cookie's popularity has led to a surge in demand, with people hired to stand in line and resell the goods. This phenomenon, which has occurred in other parts of the world, highlights the allure of foodmania and the lengths people will go to for a taste.

A mother-of-one, Kira Hollis, overcame anorexia and depression by becoming a bodybuilder. She was diagnosed with borderline personality disorder and was underweight at 6st. Doctors ordered her to go to the gym to gain weight, which led her to become a personal trainer. Now, at 9. 5st, she says bodybuilding gave her the confidence to overcome her depression. Her story went viral after she uploaded a video online, which has been viewed over 2 million times.

Lewis Ferguson, 18, survived a spectacular fall from Merrion Square during a race at Wincanton on Wednesday, causing him to perform a mid-air somersault. The incident, which was captured on video and viewed by hundreds of thousands of people online, has led to Ferguson gaining a cut on his nose and gaining a few hundred Twitter followers. Despite the fall, Ferguson is undeterred and plans to continue riding at the Cheltenham Festival and Aintree every year. The incident was described as the worst fall the race course clerk of the course, Barry Johnson, had ever seen.

Hillary Clinton launched her campaign with a video, new logo, and road trip, aiming to rebrand herself and frame her as an empathetic candidate. Critics dismissed her efforts as vapid and boring, but marketing experts argue her strategy may be more successful than initially thought. The campaign's rebranding and reframing efforts, including her road trip and new logo, aim to change how voters perceive her and her campaign.

More than 1,700 Chinese high school freshmen took an exam outdoors in their school playground for the first time, as the school lacked indoor space. The students organized the outdoor exam themselves, with a regular radio announcement instructing them to turn their desks and chairs periodically to avoid being dazzled by the sun. The school approved the proposal, and many students believe it is a novel way to broaden their horizons and encourage relaxation.

Sportsmail has partnered with Gillette to offer a unique chance for one lucky reader to win a pair of Nike Magista Obra boots signed by Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart. The prize includes a new Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor with Flexball technology and a shave gel. The competition closes on April 19.

Kecil, a baby orangutan, has been raised by Maggie, an experienced surrogate mother at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo, after his natural mother and another surrogate rejected him. Maggie has now successfully raised Kecil for the past 10 months, and the two are inseparable. Kecil is set to make his first public appearance this weekend at the zoo.

A 61-year-old woman died suddenly and was eaten by her pet dogs after lying undiscovered in the house for days. The dogs, initially thought to have tried to wake her before becoming desperate for food, ate parts of her vital organs. The most likely cause of death was an accidental overdose of medication, but the exact cause of death could not be determined due to the dogs' consumption of her organs.

France's handball star Nikola Karabatic, along with his brother Luka, will stand trial for suspected match-fixing in an illegal betting case involving their Montpellier club. Karabatic, who was briefly detained, now plays for Barcelona in the Spanish league. The trial is likely to take place within months, with Karabatic facing up to five years in prison and a fine.

A gang of six men, including Ahmed Hassan-Sule, 21, and Mohamed Saleh, 22, were convicted of a string of sexual offenses against teenage girls in Banbury, Oxfordshire. The offenses occurred in cars, woods, and at the defendants' homes from 2009 to 2014. Hassan-Sule and Saleh were sentenced to nine and four years in jail, respectively. The girls, aged between 13 and 16, were targeted at under-18s parties organized by Hassan-Sule. The judge criticized the defendants for using charity events to gain popularity among young people and for exploiting emotionally immature victims.

Former New England Patriots star Aaron Hernandez faces three more trials, including a murder trial in which he is accused of killing two men and wounding another person near a Boston nightclub in July 2012. Hernandez pleaded not guilty at his arraignment.

The Emirates Airline has signed a £30 million three-year deal to sponsor the FA Cup, renaming it the Emirates FA Cup. This deal, along with existing sponsorship deals with Arsenal, AC Milan, and Hamburg, adds to Emirates' growing portfolio of sporting sponsorships.

Michael Phelps, the 18-time Olympic champion, is aiming to compete in the Rio Olympics next year but won't swim at the world championships in Russia this summer as part of a six-month suspension by USA Swimming. Phelps, who had already qualified in three events before being banned, expressed his desire to return to the pool and emphasized his enjoyment of international competitions. He also acknowledged the challenges of rehabilitating his alcohol addiction and taking responsibility for his actions.

Gareth Bale, a key player for Real Madrid, is doubtful for the Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid due to a calf injury. The Welsh forward limped off during Real's 3-1 home victory over Malaga on Saturday. Real Madrid also lacks Croatian midfielder Luka Modric, who is expected to be out for six weeks with a knee ligament strain. Real's striker Karim Benzema is expected to be fit for the match after missing Saturday's encounter with a knee injury.

Scientists warn that older people are more susceptible to emotions when making decisions about retirement investments, particularly during financial crises. A study found that 50% of pensioners who sold their investments during the 2007-2008 global financial crisis lost 30% of their value, while those who held on saw their investments grow. The study, published in the Journal of Consumer Affairs, suggests that cognitive ability declines with age, making older people more prone to emotional decision-making. The UK government is implementing reforms allowing 55-year-olds to withdraw from their pension and take the income they need, with the option to keep the money invested in the stock market.

Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini should be given more time to turn around the club's fortunes, according to Stuart Pearce, who believes the team is at a stage where it needs significant squad changes. Pearce, who has managed the club, suggests Pellegrini, who has been with the team for many years, should stay in place to understand the squad's needs.

Manchester United's stars, including Wayne Rooney, Ander Herrera, and Robin van Persie, are training in the sunshine ahead of their Premier League derby against Manchester City on Sunday. The match is significant as it marks Manchester United's first game against their rivals since the Sir Alex Ferguson era, and a victory could give them a four-point lead in the league. The game is also crucial for Manchester City, who have won their last three visits to Old Trafford.
Fiorentina lost 1-0 to Verona, leaving them nine points behind third-placed AS Roma, as Fiorentina's fading hopes of qualifying for the Champions League all but disappeared.

Miley Cyrus, 22, attended the 30th Annual Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony in Cleveland, Ohio, where she posed for a social media snap with somewhat bushy underarm hair. This sparked controversy, with some users advising her to shave, while others defended her choice. Cyrus is known for her controversial sartorial choices, and her armpit hair caused a stir on social media.

Barcelona's Lionel Messi, Neymar, and Luis Suarez have scored 102 goals collectively this season, taking them five points clear in La Liga. Messi has 49 goals, Neymar has 32, and Suarez has 21. The trio's dominance has boosted Barcelona's goal difference to +78, putting pressure on Real Madrid ahead of their match against Almería.

Andrea McVeigh, 44, was left scarred for life after being knocked down by a cyclist who was riding on the pavement in Bermondsey, south London. The cyclist fled the scene, chased by McVeigh's husband, who was injured in the incident. McVeigh suffered two three-inch gashes to the middle of her forehead and other facial and hand injuries. The Met Police issued CCTV footage of the suspect, who fled after the impact and then sped off. McVeigh is currently off work sick and has two black eyes, a swollen nose, stitches, and a feeling of being very scared to go out onto the street.

Paul Gregory, 51, of Bedford, was fined £795 for having a blue badge, claiming he could only walk 200 metres, when in fact he was a keen walker. He was exposed when Bedford Borough Council staff noticed a newspaper report describing his exploits on a 191-mile hike. Gregory pleaded guilty to two counts of dishonestly obtaining a blue badge by misrepresenting his physical abilities and was ordered to carry out 150 hours of unpaid work and pay a £60 victim surcharge.

Apple has filed a patent for a new method of unlocking its devices using facial recognition, which involves scanning a user's face with the front-facing camera when the handset is moved into a certain position. If the scanned face matches a previously taken photo, the phone unlocks automatically. This system is similar to Android's Trusted face feature, which relies on the user pressing the power button to enable the screen. The patent was filed by Apple in March 2011 and was awarded earlier this week.

Elizabeth Sedway, 51, a cancer patient from California, was ejected from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California because she lacked a doctor's note clearing her to fly. The incident occurred when an airline representative noticed she had put on a surgical mask to shield herself from germs and asked if she needed anything. Mrs. Sedway initially said she was fine, but when the airline employee approached her a second time, she indicated that she might require a little extra time to board the plane because she sometimes felt 'weak.' The family eventually boarded the plane and were awaiting takeoff in their seats when an airline representative came on board and announced that the cancer-stricken passenger could not fly without a note from her doctor. The incident sparked outrage and led to a call for airline policies to be reviewed.

A vintage 1973 E-Type Jaguar was involved in a head-on collision with a 1973 Toyota Kluger on Easter Sunday night in Frenchs Forest, Sydney, resulting in the Jaguar being completely written off. No injuries were reported, but all three adults involved were taken to hospital for precautionary measures. Police are investigating the incident, and the Jaguar's owner expressed sympathy and admiration for the car's rarity. The crash occurred on Warringah Road, and the incident comes after a warning to obey road rules during the Easter long weekend.

Google has established a team dedicated to enhancing the longevity of electronic devices, including phones, tablets, and electric cars, through the development of flexible and wearable technologies. The team, consisting of four individuals, focuses on solid-state, thin-film batteries and subfreezing temperature functions for Project Loon balloons. This initiative follows Google's previous work with Dr. Ramesh Bhardwaj, who led a testing team since 2012. The company has also hired nine new positions related to batteries, including software engineers for iOS battery life and power systems.

The 223ft Explorer is a luxury superyacht designed by British yacht designer Tony Castro, featuring a helipad, infinity pool, and space for 12 guests. It is capable of carrying a helicopter, twin limo tenders, car, submarine, jetskis, paddleboards, and inflatables. The yacht costs approximately 40 million euros to build, making it likely to cost even more to purchase. The layout includes a variety of areas for guests to retreat to, ensuring they don't get bored while sailing around the world. However, the high cost of the yacht means it will likely retail for even more.

Ed Miliband announced his intention to implement rent controls, despite warnings from experts that the plans will backfire and lead to more tenants being evicted. The controversial measures, demanded by the militant Unite union, would cap rents and offer three-year tenancies, but critics argue they will give landlords an incentive to evict tenants and suppress house building.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town fan who said he hopes Arsenal wins has been removed from his role as a mascot for Reading in the FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal. The young supporter was removed after a video emerged of him backing Arsenal, sparking outrage from Reading fans. The Football Association moved him to be a mascot for England instead.

A giant supervoid 1.8 billion light-years across may be responsible for a mysterious 'Cold Spot' in the universe, as proposed by astronomers seeking to understand the cause of this larger-than-expected cold area. If confirmed, the supervoid would be the largest single structure ever found by humanity. The research, published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, was carried out by the Institute for Astronomy at the University of Hawaii at Manoa. The Cold Spot was first discovered by astronomers in 2004 when they were examining a map of the radiation left over from the Big Bang, showing a region 20% less dense than elsewhere. The supervoid appears to be 'roughly spherical' and may even contain a 'significant substructure' at its centre. The Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, will display Abraham Lincoln's chair where he was shot in 1865 as part of its 150th anniversary observance. The chair, which has a dark stain on the back believed to be blood from the shooting, will be removed from its enclosure on April 15 and displayed in an open plaza. Doris Kearns Goodwin will deliver a lecture on April 13. The chair has been part of the museum since its founding 85 years ago.

Jake Boys, a 19-year-old vlogger from Hailsham, England, surprised his girlfriend Emily Canham by booking tickets for One Direction to perform in Cardiff. However, he mistakenly booked plane tickets to the Republic of Ireland instead of Wales, where the concert was actually taking place. The couple is now planning to buy new train tickets to Cardiff for the band's show in June.

A Romanian company has unveiled the Roboscan 2M Aeria, a mobile X-ray scanner that can detect contraband, bombs, and weapons on airplanes. The device, which costs €3 million, is already being used to inspect trucks at borders in Eastern Europe. The company claims it can scan entire planes in about 20 minutes and is the world's first "airplane scanner." While the radiation emitted is not safe for humans, the company believes it could become a vital tool in aircraft safety.

A 54-year-old convicted paedophile, Stephen Munden, has gone on the run after vanishing from a psychiatric unit. Munden, described as having a 'fanatical obsession' with young girls, was detained under the Mental Health Act after sexually touching a three-year-old girl. He is believed to have shaved off his beard before leaving the hospital in Winchfield. Officers are launching a manhunt to find Munden, who suffers from learning difficulties and has been detained at a private facility.

Middlesbrough, led by Aitor Karanka, are currently top of the Championship table with a 7-point lead over second-placed Bournemouth. The division is highly competitive, with only four weeks remaining, and Middlesbrough's buffer over second-place Bournemouth is a point with Watford, their opponents on Monday, and Norwich a point further back. The match at Vicarage Road is a lunchtime kick-off, giving Middlesbrough an advantage. Watford's 18-goal striker Odion Ighalo is eager to play in the English top flight, while Bournemouth have been the surprise package, leading the Championship for 101 days. The promotion race is highly precarious, with the division potentially having a completely different top two on Monday evening if Watford and Norwich win and Bournemouth fail to secure three points against Birmingham. Jonathan Woodgate, Middlesbrough's experienced captain, is hoping to continue playing through the pain.

The latest hair trend is grey hair, with women embracing the look on social media under the hashtag #grannyhair. The trend has gained popularity on platforms like Instagram, with users sharing images of themselves with silver locks. The look is seen as a statement of defiance against traditional beauty standards and a way for women to express themselves. The trend has been popularized by fashion designers like Jean Paul Gaultier, who showcased grey-haired models at Paris Fashion Week.

A couple from Bellefontaine, Ohio, who were struggling with chronic conditions and financial hardships, died from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning after leaving their charcoal grills in their bedroom. The couple, Randy and Jodi Speidel, had created online fundraisers but failed to receive any donations. Their landlord discovered the grills and found them dead in their bedroom. The couple had removed their cats to avoid harming them, and their daughters, Randa and Kira, were left without a father.

Liberal Democrat leader Nick Clegg vowed to continue as leader even if the party is reduced to fewer than 30 MPs, insisting he would fight for his position "in all circumstances." Clegg expressed optimism about the party's prospects and pledged to lead them into and through the next Parliament. Business Secretary Vince Cable said he hoped to be made Chancellor if the Lib Dems form a coalition with the Conservatives, and Clegg appeared to lean towards another deal with the Tories, attributing credit for the Coalition to himself.

A pensioner in Somerset, Terry Cooper, was shocked to see a badger the size of a large pig with six-inch teeth burst through a hedge with two cubs in his garden. Cooper's Jack Russell dog saved him from the attack, but he was left shaken. The National Farmers' Union advises residents to protect their property from badgers by using badger-proof fencing and keeping bins and food bowls secure.

Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose to Porto in the Champions League quarter-final second leg, while the Blues were knocked out of the competition. Mourinho visited Fulham's training ground with his son, Chelsea crashed out of the Champions League, but the club is closing in on the Premier League title with six games to play.

A businessman named Andreas Christopheros, 29, was attacked with corrosive liquid in his face outside his home in Truro, Cornwall, leaving him with life-changing injuries, including a loss of vision and facial scars. Nicole Phillips, 45, from Hastings, was charged with perverting the course of justice and is due to appear at Bodmin Magistrates Court on April 30. Her husband, David Phillips, 48, was already charged with grievous bodily harm with intent.

A Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route has erected signs warning pilgrims not to defecate along the famous path, as angry residents complain about the frequent nature calls. The signs, which show a squatting figure defecating within a red circle with a diagonal line across it, have become an attraction for pilgrims and visitors. The signs are posted next to warnings that urge people not to litter. The pilgrimage attracts thousands of pilgrims every year, but there can be very few places to go when nature calls.

A massive fire consumed a building that was once home to a strip club in Flint, Michigan, on Wednesday afternoon. Flames were seen sweeping the building, and only the building itself and a few nearby power lines were affected. The site was not a vacant facility, and an investigation into what was behind the blaze continues.

A woman of Arab and Jewish descent, Shoshana Hebshi, who was strip-searched at a Detroit-area airport on the 10th anniversary of 9/11, has reached a settlement of $40,000 in a lawsuit filed on her behalf. The settlement is in response to the federal government's decision to give her compensation for being humiliated. The incident occurred when Hebshi was seated next to two Indian-American men, whom crew members had said spent a lot of time in the plane's bathroom. All three were detained, and Hebshi was held for hours before being released. The settlement sends a message that discrimination is not tolerated and will help protect future passengers from similar experiences.

A plane made a crash landing and skidded off the runway at Hiroshima Airport in Japan, injuring 20 people. The Airbus A320 had set off from Incheon International Airport in Seoul, South Korea to Hiroshima when it is believed to have missed the landing point on the runway. Local media reported that the plane spun 180 degrees after impact to be left facing the wrong way on the runway. The airport has been closed as a result of the crash, and emergency services are at the scene, with injured passengers being taken to hospital.

Mark-Francis Vandelli, a wealthy reality star, has opened up his watch collection to the Evening Standard, showcasing 16 expensive timepieces. He revealed his favorite items and the history behind them, including a Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42, a Cartier Tortue Collection Privée, and a Rolex yellow gold Oyster Perpetual. His most expensive watch is a Cartier white gold Moonphase, which he bought for £32,000 and has a sun or moon that moves depending on the hour of the day.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy is selling his extensive collection of antiques in a £100,000 auction after deciding to downsize his home. The collection includes a 3D diorama of the Battle of Agincourt, a longbow made from yew, and a portrait of Hardy holding the bow. The auction, held by Dominic Winter in South Cerney, Gloucestershire, features 238 lots of furniture, paintings, swords, and other items. Hardy, 89, is a military historian who studied with J.R.R. Tolkien and is an expert on the medieval longbow. The sale is part of his downsizing process, and Hardy hopes the items will bring joy to new owners.

A Brazilian commuter, Nelson Felippe, took a photo of two women hugging on a train platform and posted it on Facebook, expressing his disapproval of the scene. The image quickly went viral, with over 100, 000 views in 24 hours. Felippe's post, which initially appeared to be homophobic, actually revealed that he was observing a public transport safety regulation. The post has been praised for its witty way of exposing homophobia.

A young English cricket fan, Jonathan Stevenson, wrote a letter to Richie Benaud, the legendary Australian cricket player, asking for tips on left-handed leg spin. Benaud, who was a wily leg-spin bowler and middle-order batsman, responded with a detailed letter that included tips on different deliveries and how to deliver them. The letter was signed by Benaud and was shared on Twitter as a tribute to the "great man."

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg predicts that virtual reality will play a key role in the future of travel, allowing users to experience destinations from multiple viewpoints and even change their viewpoints to explore locations in more depth. The company has already purchased virtual reality headset maker Oculus and announced plans to support virtual reality on its newsfeed, with the goal of creating a range of human experiences through VR. Marriott hotels have also trialled Oculus Rift on a tour of hotels across America.

A 22-year-old woman with bone cancer was photographed with her boyfriend for their 22nd birthday, despite the couple not being legally married. The photographer, Guo Kai, arranged for professional photos to be taken at the hospital where Dong Hui was being treated. The couple's love and commitment to each other were evident in their photos, and they expressed their love for each other in a heartfelt exchange of vows.

A 34-year-old man, Blaine Boudreaux, was charged with intoxication manslaughter, intoxicated assault, and failure to stop and render aid involving death in connection to three separate DUI collisions in Houston that killed a 6-year-old boy and injured his mother. Boudreaux, who has an extensive DUI record in Louisiana, was allegedly drunk when he ran a red light on Lockwood Drive and slammed his Dodge pickup truck into a Honda Civic, killing the boy and injuring his mother. The man was arrested at the scene after failing a field sobriety test.

Microsoft has launched a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions within the company, partnering with Specialisterne, a Danish nonprofit. The initiative, announced by Microsoft's Corporate VP of Worldwide Operations, Mary Ellen Smith, aims to expand opportunity and represent customers. The positions will be based at Microsoft's Redmond campus and will be run in partnership with Specialisterne. Smith expressed pride in her son's success and the company's commitment to supporting people with autism.

Two deputies involved in the fatal shooting of Eric Harris have been reassigned due to threats against them and their families. The shooting occurred when Reserve Deputy Robert Bates shot Harris, who was trying to arrest him. The deputies are not charged with a crime but have faced criticism for their actions. The sheriff's office has suspended the drug unit pending an investigation into the April 2 shooting. The FBI has cleared the agency of any civil rights violations. The shooting has led to allegations of forgery in training records and unqualified training for the deputy. The family of Eric Harris has demanded justice and changes in policy.

Katie Prager, a 24-year-old woman with cystic fibrosis, is in desperate need of a life-saving lung transplant due to an infection called Burkholderia Cepacia. Her husband, Dalton, has already received new lungs, but Katie is waiting for a transplant at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. Kentucky Medicaid will not cover the out-of-state treatment, leaving the couple in a race against time to save Katie's life.

The Sleep Cycle app data reveals that the world's earliest wake-up time is on Mondays in South Africa, with Americans waking up at 7am and being in the worst mood all week. Slovakia topped the list for sleep quality, while the UK was in 45th place and the US was in 49th. The best sleep quality occurs on Wednesdays, with China recording the highest sleep quality that night. Users in Finland get the most hours of sleep on Saturdays, averaging 8 hours and 2 minutes, while users in Japan get an average of just 6 hours and 9 minutes. The data also shows that people in the Middle East wake up grumpiest on Tuesdays, with the US sleeping in the most and waking up happiest on Fridays.

Frida Kahlo's unpublished love letters to Jose Bartoli, a Catalan artist, are expected to fetch upwards of $120,000 when they go up for auction at Doyle New York on April 15. The letters, written between 1946 and 1949, were saved by Jose until his death in 1995 and comprise more than 100 pages. Frida signed her letters to Jose as 'Sonja' to make it seem like they were from a woman, and the collection includes an original drawing of a sleeping cat, pressed flowers, ribbon, beads, and drafts of Jose's responses.

Red Len McCluskey, the fiery leader of the trade union Unite, is a potent, sinister force in British politics, seeking to use his financial and organizational muscle within the Labour movement to drag Britain back to the dark days of the 1970s. McCluskey, a former Liverpool dock worker who keeps a drawing of Lenin in his office and once boasted of presiding over more strikes than any other union boss, is quite open about his yearning for that period when the unions held the government to ransom. Unite, which has a claimed membership of 1. 42 million, is intertwined with the Labour Party's structure, MPs and finances, and remains addicted to the failed socialist policies of the past, including a major expansion in the public sector, less flexibility in the workplace, higher taxation, and ever more state spending.

A zookeeper at the Zoological Center in Tel Aviv captured footage of various animals drinking water in their enclosures using a GoPro camera. The footage, which lasted 30 hours, showed a range of drinking behaviors, from a rhino almost kissing the surface of the water to a lemur delicately licking it. The zookeeper, Elad Hershkowitz, cut the footage down to four minutes and shared it on social media, sparking curiosity and laughter among viewers.
Just a quarter of voters think David Cameron is hungriest to win the election, a poll reveals today as the Prime Minister tries to step up his campaign passion.

A man charged with assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov has told a court he was beaten and pressured into confessing to the murder. Zaur Dadaev, accused of being involved in the shooting of the politician in Moscow on February 27, told the court he had been abducted, beaten, and pressured into confessing to Nemstov's murder. Dadaev had previously confessed to the killing but now says he was beaten and pressured into making that statement.

A 4-month-old baby boy named Sonit Awal was pulled from the rubble of a Nepal earthquake that killed over 5,000 people. His father, Shyam Awal, frantically searched for him amid the debris for 22 hours before the soldiers found him. Sonit's face was covered in dust, but he was uninjured and taken to Bhaktapur Hospital. The rescue provides hope to a country that has experienced much loss.

A Church of Scientology-affiliated drug rehabilitation center, Narcocon, is attempting to convert a historic property near Camp David into a drug treatment center, despite opposition from local residents and environmentalists. The property, Trout Run, was once the site of President Herbert Hoover's fishing trip, and Narcocon argues that it should be designated as historic to circumvent current zoning laws. The proposed center, which would house 12 patients, has been sued for wrongful deaths and denies trying to convert people to Scientology. The case highlights the tension between religious organizations and local communities over land use and historic designation.

The article discusses the aftermath of the U.S. military withdrawal from Afghanistan, focusing on the challenges faced by expatriates and locals in Kabul. Five men who once spoke English fluently due to their work with NATO have been fired and blacklisted, leading to isolation and fear of retaliation. They sleep in market stalls and avoid traveling to see their families. The city has transformed, with neighborhoods emptying out and new residents reclaiming streets. The U.S. Embassy and NATO declined to comment.

Two Navy SEALs died and another was critically injured while training in a pool at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story in Virginia on Friday. The incident occurred when the SEALs were swimming in lap lanes without wearing gear, and one of them died and the other was pronounced dead at a civilian hospital. The investigation into the incident is ongoing.

NBC, the broadcasting giant, has transported their entire Premier League production from their HQ in Stamford, Connecticut, to England for this weekend's round of matches. This move is expected to increase US interest in the English Premier League, with some 32 million Americans watching at least one top-flight English game live in 2019-20. The move comes as NBC has more than doubled US interest in the league in the past two years. The team includes former Wimbledon midfielder Robbie Earle, retired MLS star Kyle Martino, and former Crystal Palace fan Rebecca Lowe, who is married to former Cheltenham manager Paul Buckle.

Ed Miliband will do "more damage to the country than he did to his brother," Boris Johnson said on the Andrew Marr Show, accusing him of "stabbing the country in the back" by doing a deal with the SNP to get into power.

Dustin Irons, a prisoner in Oregon, was slapped with an extra 30 days behind bars for dropping his trousers and flashing a judge during a court hearing. The judge sentenced him to an additional 30 days for contempt of court. Irons, 26, was arrested for trashing a hotel room and assaulting people inside. He was known as a difficult inmate who needed two officers and handcuffs to be moved.

Jenson Button believes McLaren has improved significantly since the Malaysian Grand Prix, with both he and Fernando Alonso discovering the car was competitive alongside other midfield runners. Despite retiring during the race, Button acknowledges the team still has a long way to go and hopes further steps have been taken going into this weekend's race in Shanghai.

A hospital in Western Australia, Fiona Stanley Hospital, was found to have blood and bone fragments on supposedly sanitized medical instruments, leading to the hospital being stripped of its medical service provider Serco and fined $60,000. The incident has raised concerns about the hospital's sanitization practices and damaged its public image.

Becca Litchfield and Dale, a couple from Nottingham, decided to give up their dream wedding to pay for fertility treatment and IVF. After two failed attempts, they won a wedding competition and were able to have a white wedding. The couple is now celebrating the birth of twins, Darci-Mai and Stanley, and are overjoyed with their luck.

A family-friendly coffee shop in Omaha, Nebraska, had its Facebook page hacked and flooded with pornography after an employee clicked on a malicious link in an email. The hack lasted for almost 24 hours, with the page being replaced with adult cartoons similar to those posted on other major brands. The company issued an apology and removed the inappropriate content, but it was not until a day later that the hacker was kicked out and the page was restored.

A young Shiba Inu puppy at an American Kennel Club center in the United States caused confusion and laughter when it attempted to bark at a young husky dog, leading to a video that captured the playful interaction between the two puppies. The Shiba Inu, which is known for its small size and distinctive appearance, was filmed squeaking and squawking after meeting the husky, attempting to bark at its new companion. The video, which was captured on video, showed the two dogs conversing and engaging in vocalizations, including yapping, whining, and barking. The interaction was captured by a staff member and later shared online, causing amusement among viewers.

Liam Plunkett, an experienced English seamer, is preparing to lead England in the upcoming Test series against West Indies. He aims to use his pace to ruffle batsmen and has recovered from a minor ankle injury. Plunkett is competing for a place in the England Test side with Chris Jordan and Mark Wood, who are both familiar with West Indies conditions.

Paul Smith, a boxer from Liverpool, is set to face Andre Ward in a unification fight for the WBA super-middleweight title. Smith, who has lost two previous title defenses to Arthur Abraham, is seen as a potential warm-up opponent for a rematch with Carl Froch. The WBA has ordered Ward and Froch to meet in a unification fight, with Froch willing to travel to the UK if Ward returns the compliment by fighting in the US. The fight is expected to be a 12-round championship distance.

Tyrus Byrd, the first African American mayor of Parma, Missouri, was sworn in last week but faced a sudden departure of five of her six police officers and several other top officials after her election victory. The resignations were attributed to "safety concerns," with the outgoing mayor citing the departure of the police force, city attorney, clerk, and water treatment supervisor. The town, with a population of 713, has a predominantly black population and has experienced a surge in crime, despite a large police force. The new mayor's father, who was defeated in the election, insists his daughter has a good relationship with the police department.

Manchester City midfielder Yaya Toure will not be forced out of the club but is set to become available this summer. The club is considering offers for the Ivorian, who has played a major role in their recent trophy-winning period. Inter Milan is interested but has doubts over Toure's wages. City will resist any attempt by Valencia to pull out of a £24 million deal for Alvaro Negredo to fund a move for Radamel Falcao.

A new study claims that more than two-thirds of people taking antidepressants may not actually have depression, challenging the common belief that these medications are prescribed for clinical depression. The study, published in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, found that 69% of antidepressant users did not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder. Researchers also discovered that 38% of those taking antidepressants did not meet the criteria for other psychiatric disorders such as obsessive compulsive disorder, panic disorder, social phobia, or generalized anxiety disorder. The study, conducted by U.S. investigators, concluded that antidepressants are commonly used in the absence of clear evidence-based indications.

Doris Fuller, the mother of a mentally ill daughter who killed herself, has revealed how her daughter's bipolar disorder and psychosis led to her death. Fuller wrote about her daughter's life in a long article for the Washington Post, describing how her illness went undiagnosed until her early 20s and eventually drove her to suicide. Fuller said her daughter, Natalie, lived with an incurable disease that filled her head with devils that eventually led to her death. Despite receiving proper treatment, Natalie eventually decided to stop taking her meds, which brought her troubles back, even more acute than before.

A 10-year-old boy named Koby Hodder suffered a cardiac arrest while playing British Bulldog in a school playground, collapsing for 12 minutes before being revived by paramedics. His condition was similar to that of footballer Fabrice Muamba, who also suffered a cardiac arrest during a match. Koby was later diagnosed with the same heart condition as Muamba. The incident led to calls for the game to be banned, as it is considered dangerous and can lead to injuries. Koby's father, Mark, was able to give CPR until paramedics arrived, and he was saved by giving Koby two shocks with a defibrillator.

Baroness Hale of Richmond, Britain's most senior female judge, has proposed reforms to England and Wales' divorce laws to remove the need for allegations of adultery and blame in most matrimonial disputes. She wants to see the bitterness taken out of most divorces by making it take longer to get a divorce and encouraging couples to sort out arrangements for children and money before obtaining a divorce. The reforms would also include a one-year cooling off period after declaring that their marriage has permanently broken down. Lady Hale, who is deputy president to the Supreme Court and the only woman among the 12 Supreme Court justices, is behind the move for 'no fault' divorce in England and Wales 20 years ago.

Tottenham Hotspur is considering a state-of-the-art stadium with a retractable pitch that could accommodate an NFL franchise, potentially becoming the home of a new NFL team in London. The stadium, set to be completed for the 2018-19 season, would feature a "slide-out" grass pitch with an NFL-style synthetic surface. The NFL is said to be within five years of having a permanent franchise in London, and teams are testing logistics for their three games at Wembley this autumn. If Tottenham press ahead with the proposed stadium design and secure the NFL franchise, it would represent a significant blow to the Football Association, who also see the NFL as a lucrative partner for Wembley.

U.S. senators have written to FIFA, calling for Russia to be removed as host of the 2018 World Cup due to its role in the Ukraine crisis and occupation of Crimea. The senators, including John McCain, urge FIFA to move the global competition.

Universal announced that the sequel to the box office blockbuster "Fifty Shades of Grey" will hit theaters on February 10, 2017, and February 9, 2018. The husband of the author, Niall Leonard, will write the script for the second film, while the husband of the author, Erika Leonard, has been credited with keeping a strong amount of creative control when it comes to Universal's adaptations of her books. The second film is titled "Fifty Shades Darker."

West Brom manager Tony Pulis will receive a hero's welcome when he returns to Crystal Palace, but he must wonder if he'll ever be successful at the right end of the Premier League, as his overall record is one of the worst of any long-serving Premier League manager. Pulis has never finished in the top half of the Premier League, and he is currently stuck on 33 points, with four of their final five fixtures coming against Liverpool, Manchester United, Chelsea, and Arsenal. Pulis has never had the best clubs with the most money to manage, but he has turned Stoke City into an established team and is currently favoured to keep Albion up this time.

Fenerbahce, a Turkish football club, has called for the suspension of the Turkish championship following a gun attack on their team bus during a match against Caykur Rizespor. The attack occurred on Saturday night as the bus was driving to the airport. The injured driver, who was taken to hospital, is seeking medical attention. Fenerbahce believes that the attack is not being solved in a way that satisfies the club and public opinion, leading to the suspension of the championship.

A massive snow avalanche struck Everest Base Camp on Saturday, killing at least 17 people and injuring dozens more. The avalanche, which occurred during a 7.8 magnitude earthquake, caused panic among the climbers and local hires, who scrambled to safety. The avalanche struck Base Camp, but many climbers higher up the mountain were unable to descend on their own, with the dangerous Khumbu Icefall deemed impassable. Helicopters brought stranded climbers down from the mountain, and at least 200 people were reported to be stuck in the higher camps. The aftershocks caused further complications, complicating rescue efforts and leaving hundreds of climbers stranded.

Gregory Margolin, a 16-year-old Jewish recruit in the Soviet Red Army during World War II, survived the war and later settled in Donetsk, Ukraine. In 2014, he found himself again in the middle of a war in Eastern Ukraine, where a stray missile hit his house, killing his daughter. Margolin and his family fled to Israel, where they are now living in a refugee center set up by the International Fellowship of Christians and Jews. Margolin's granddaughter, Liora, is amazed by her grandfather's memories of the war and his struggle to remember his own life. The article highlights the ongoing conflict in Eastern Ukraine and the impact of war on individuals and families.

John Carver, Newcastle United's assistant manager, is eager to take charge of the club against Sunderland on Sunday, knowing that a victory could significantly impact his chances of winning the head coach position. Gullit's controversial decision to leave out star players Alan Shearer and Duncan Ferguson in a 1999 derby led to Newcastle's defeat, which Carver believes could be a turning point in his campaign.

The Reverend Al Sharpton delivered a sermon and addressed the Walter Scott situation on Sunday morning, calling for reform in national policing legislation. He is expected to attend a vigil near the scene of the Scott shooting on Sunday afternoon. Sharpton denied that Scott's family barred him from attending his funeral on Saturday because it would cause a 'circus' of media attention.

Brendan Rodgers will speak to Raheem Sterling about his recent controversies, including his alleged use of nitrous oxide and shisha pipe, after the Liverpool forward scored the opener in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United. Rodgers will remind Sterling of his responsibilities as a professional player and will discuss the demands of being a top-class player. Sterling could have had more goals and at one point shot wide with the goal gaping. Rodgers praised Sterling's skill and ability for the first goal and said he will be disappointed that he maybe didn't get three goals this evening, but he was tireless all evening pressing the ball and posing a threat.

Union barons gave more than £1 million to Labour in the second week of the election campaign, boosting the party's war chest and exposing the type of government Ed Miliband would lead as Prime Minister. Labour received £1. 1 million in donations between April 6 and April 12, compared to £492, 512 for the Conservatives. Unison, USDAW, and Len McCluskey's Unite gave £1. 05 million, while the Conservatives received £460, 000 from wealthy individuals.

Passengers on a Qatar Airways flight were stranded at Manchester Airport for five hours after their plane was diverted due to severe winds. The flight landed at Birmingham Airport, where passengers were made to stay in their seats while the aircraft was refueled and a new crew arrived. The delay caused frustration among passengers, who claimed they were left waiting for transport and did not arrive until 7am. The incident prompted police to be called twice to the tarmac, and the airline apologized for the delay, which occurred after the operating crew exceeded their legal flying hours.

Canadian pop sensation Justin Bieber will carry Floyd Mayweather's championship belts into the ring ahead of his $300 million Las Vegas mega-fight with Manny Pacquiao on Saturday. Bieber, who has been close friends with Mayweather for years, will join the fighter on stage during a recent press conference and will be asked to lead out the American's entourage at the MGM Grand. Mayweather, who has a 47-0 record on the line, knows this fight is without doubt the biggest of his career - and the most lucrative.

The article discusses the closure of Corinthian Colleges Inc., a for-profit college chain that has been struggling to hold accountable. Corinthian, which once enrolled over 70,000 students, is now shutting down all of its remaining 28 campuses. The closure is seen as a positive development in the fight against predatory colleges, which enroll only 13% of college students but account for nearly half of all student loan defaults. The article also highlights the aggressive tactics used by for-profit colleges, such as recruiting students through phone calls and leaving messages, and the need to close any remaining for-profit colleges.

Pep Guardiola has denied claims of a dispute with former Bayern Munich club doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit the club after being blamed for the defeat by Porto. Muller-Wohlfahrt claimed the bond of trust was damaged, but Guardiola played down the feud, stating it was his decision and injuries are part of football. Muller-Wohlfahrt had worked at Bayern for almost 40 years and was a world leader in his field.

Wladimir Klitschko, the reigning heavyweight champion, has recalled his dramatic rise to the top on the eve of his world title defence against Bryant Jennings. The Ukrainian superstar will make his return to US soil for the first time in seven years when he takes on the slick Philadelphian at the iconic Madison Square Garden in New York. Klitschko, who won Olympic gold in Atlanta in 1996, has been reminiscing about how it all started for him when he won gold at the Olympics, instantly catapulting him into a hero in his home country. Despite being just a year short of his 40th birthday, Klitschko believes age has no bearing on how long he can go on for. He will make his return to US soil for the first time in seven years at Madison Square Garden.

Jeremy Clarkson, the former Top Gear presenter, has finally spoken out about his high-profile sacking from the BBC2 show, admitting he will "miss" fronting the show. Former presenter Angela Rippon, who first presented the show 38 years ago, said it would be "great" if she were invited back. The BBC announced that Clarkson would not be renewing his contract, citing his "unprovoked" attack on a producer during filming.

In a La Liga match between Barcelona and Celta Vigo, Fabian Orellana of Celta Vigo threw a lump of grass at Sergio Busquets during the closing stages of the match, leading to a red card for Orellana. Referee Inaki Vicandi Garrido awarded Busquets a straight red card, and the incident sparked a heated argument between the players. Despite the incident, Barcelona secured a crucial 1-0 victory, while Real Madrid won 9-1 against Granada.

In 2013, three people died and over 200 were injured when a pair of bombs went off within 12 seconds of each other at the finish line of the Boston Marathon. In 2023, federal Judge George A. O'Toole warned jurors not to attend the Boston Marathon or any events or gatherings related to the anniversary or the current running of the Boston Marathon. The jury convicted Dzhokhar Tsarnaev in the bombings, and the sentencing phase is expected to last four weeks.

Millions of Chinese people marked the Qingming Festival, a three-day holiday in China, by travelling home to their ancestral villages and participating in outdoor celebrations. The festival, which marks the start of spring and celebrates the beauty of nature, is one of the 24 Chinese solar terms and is observed by millions of people across the country.

Paul Simon, 73, has topped the UK album chart for the first time in 25 years with his latest release, The Ultimate Collection. The album, which includes 19 tracks from his 50-year career, including hits like "Mrs Robinson" and "The Only Living Boy in New York," has outsold more youthful musicians like Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. Simon's recent tour with Sting is believed to have been the catalyst in helping him reach the top of the charts.

Iker Casillas, Real Madrid's goalkeeper, insists he will stay at the club even if David de Gea arrives to displace him as first choice keeper. The 33-year-old Spanish international claims he is willing to fight for the jersey he went on to make his own after breaking into the side as a 16-year-old in 1996. Real Madrid has linked to a move for Manchester United's David de Gea, but Casillas says he will continue to fight for the No. 1 jersey. The team is determined to defend their Champions League title, having reached the semi-finals with a 1-0 aggregate victory over local rivals Atletico Madrid.

The UK's employment rate hit a record high of 31 million in the three months to February, with the number of jobs increasing by 557,000 from a year earlier. This achievement was praised by the International Monetary Fund and Chancellor George Osborne, who said the UK had created more jobs in the last five years than the rest of the EU put together. Rolls-Royce announced its biggest-ever order, worth more than £6 billion, to power passenger jets for the Middle Eastern airline Emirates. The UK's fiscal deficit has been significantly reduced over the last few years, and the Chancellor, George Osborne, said the UK is one of the brightest spots in the world economy at the moment.

SsangYong, a Korean automaker, is launching a new sports utility vehicle (SUV) called Tivoli, priced under £13,000, targeting thrifty motorists. The SUV is named after the Italian town of Tivoli, known for its Renaissance architecture and garden, and is available in three trim levels with a choice of front-wheel drive or 4x4. It features a 1.6-liter engine, six-speed manual or automatic transmission, and a five-year unlimited mileage warranty. The Tivoli aims to offer value for money and driver and passenger connectivity, with a personalisation program allowing customers to create their own distinctive car.

A chef, Sam Longhurst, created a 10-inch-tall, half-kilogram burger at the Whole Damn Farm restaurant in Manchester, England, featuring six forms of three different meats, including two beef patties, homemade bacon jam, ham chunks, a whole fried chicken thigh, barbequed pulled pork, and bacon rashers. The burger contains 2,000 calories and was created after a customer challenged the restaurant to a meat challenge.

The Yeo Valley staff canteen, located in Blagdon, North Somerset, has been hailed as the world's best staff canteen due to its high-quality, organic, and locally sourced food prepared by Michelin-starred chef Paul Collins. The canteen offers a variety of dishes, including a quail egg, tomato, and polenta dish, and a fish cake with roasted cherry tomatoes and chervil hollandaise. The menu changes daily, and the canteen is open to the public at higher prices. The canteen has a quirky interior with high tables and stools, and it is run by head chef Jason Eland. The canteen is popular with the 120 dairy workers at the Yeo Valley headquarters, who enjoy the high-quality meals and the scenic views of the Mendips.

B.B. King, a legendary blues musician, was hospitalized for dehydration caused by his Type II diabetes. He is now feeling much better and is back home resting with his grandchildren. King, 89, has used various models of Gibson guitars over the years, and named each one of them Lucille. He has won 30 Grammy nominations and has been inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1987.

On Easter Sunday, New York's Fifth Avenue was transformed into a sea of bizarre hats as people celebrated the holiday in outlandish headgear. The event, known as the Easter parade, featured a mix of conservative and eccentric attire, including floral bonnets, feathered headpieces, and elaborate dioramas inspired by local politicians. The parade, which has been held annually since the 1880s, attracted a diverse crowd, including Christians, Jews, Hindus, agnostics, and atheists, as well as churchgoers dressed in more somber and refined clothing. The event, which started as a strolling display of what prosperous New Yorkers wore, has evolved into a colorful and eclectic celebration of Easter traditions.

Emergency crews in East of England received 1,248 inappropriate calls in two years, including one where a squirrel was reported to have been run over by a car in Epping Forest. The service revealed these calls as part of a list of 2,500 daily calls, with half of them attended by front-line crews, potentially putting lives at risk. The service urged people to use common sense when calling 999 and to stop and think about the potential consequences of making a prank call.

Chelsea players Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake participated in a football challenge with their teammates Loic Remy and Willian, aiming to sink balls into the boot of a car from close range and from long range. Hazard and Ake won the first round, while Remy and Willian won the second round. In the final round, Hazard and Ake won the challenge by shooting from long range, while Remy and Willian were involved in a misfortune when Willian smashed the wing mirror of one of the Audi cars.

Brendan Rodgers criticized Raheem Sterling's advisor, Aidy Ward, for allegedly being manipulated by outside forces and suggested that Sterling would stay at Liverpool if left to make a decision alone. Sterling rejected a contract extension worth £100,000 a week and has just two years left on his deal at the end of the season. Rodgers sat down with Sterling to tell him that his best interest would be served by staying at the club for now, even though there may come a time when he does leave.

Rachel Riley, Countdown's co-presenter, was embarrassed on a recent episode when contestants offered up the eight-letter word "erection" as their answer to the word game. Host Nick Hewer struggled to stifle his laughter, while celebrity guest Dr Phil Hammond provided a nine-letter word "recondite" to save the day. This incident is not the first time the show's host has struggled to contain himself when a rude word has popped up.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, who attempted to buy deadly poison on the internet and was later arrested, has been spared jail after pleading guilty to the attempted purchase. The teenager, who cannot be named for legal reasons, expressed an interest in buying the poison and showed awareness of its toxicity and potential for use in causing harm. He pleaded guilty to trying to buy the toxin at Manchester Youth Court earlier this month. The case highlights the dangers of the dark web and the importance of vigilance in law enforcement.

Three hours after giving birth to her long-awaited baby girl, Lianne Hindle, a 37-year-old mother-of-four, died at the scandal-hit North Manchester General Hospital in December. The incident occurred just months after three babies and one mother died at the maternity unit. The deaths prompted an investigation, and the family of Lianne Hindle, whose partner Chris Barnes and his sister Karen have called for action to prevent further tragedies, has expressed concerns about the care she received.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman, a seven-year-old mother of two, gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Emily, just days after a video surfaced of her training while eight months pregnant. Pittman, who plans to compete in both the Beijing World Championships and the 2016 Rio Olympics, continued to train while pregnant with her son Cornelis, who was born seven months after his mother's first child. Her coach, Mike Hurst, praised her dedication to training during her pregnancy. The athlete's website highlights her son Cornelis as her "success key."

A powerful storm capsized several sailboats participating in a regatta in Dauphin Island, Alabama, resulting in at least one death and multiple missing persons. The storm caused significant damage to the boats and forced crews to search through the night. The storm was reported to be the worst that the participants had seen.

Roseanne Barr, 62, has revealed she is going blind due to macular degeneration and glaucoma, two eye diseases that get progressively worse over time and can steal vision. Her doctors haven't provided a timeline, but her symptoms are worsening. Macular degeneration is a breakdown of the part of the retina that allows us to see fine details in the center of vision, while glaucoma damages the nerve that connects the retina to the brain, and is often caused by fluid build-up and pressure in the eyes. The risk for both diseases goes up for everyone after age 60, with some people, especially African Americans, at higher risk in their 40s. There is no cure for either disease, but treatments may delay the progression of early-stage glaucoma and halt further vision loss in advanced cases of macular degeneration.

A 17-year-old Oklahoma teenager, Chancey Luna, was convicted of first-degree murder in the 2013 shooting death of Australian college baseball player Christopher Lane, who was killed while jogging in Duncan.
