The jury recommended that Luna be sentenced to life in prison without parole. Luna was found guilty of shooting Lane from a passing car, but his defense attorney argued that he meant only to scare Lane. Luna did not testify and the defense called just one witness, his mother. The victim's family was satisfied with the verdict, while Luna's mother expressed remorse for her son's actions.

Arsene Wenger insists his record against Jose Mourinho will not influence Arsenal's match against Chelsea on Sunday. Wenger has lost 12 of their 12 meetings, drawing five and losing seven. The match is expected to be a high-stakes contest, with Chelsea's strengths highlighted as efficient counter-attacks and set-pieces. Wenger emphasizes the importance of the performance on the day rather than the past relationship between the managers.

Manny Pacquiao, a Filipino boxer, has become one of the most recognizable figures in the world of sports after a series of major fights, including a bout against Floyd Mayweather, which is scheduled for Saturday night at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. Pacquiao, who was born into poverty in the Philippines, spent his early career boxing in the Far East before gaining recognition on the big stage in 2001. He has since made a remarkable rise through the weight divisions and is set to face Mayweather in the Fight of the Century.

Jack Grealish, a talented young player, has been caught on camera inhaling nitrous oxide, a drug that can be used recreationally but is also associated with illegal activities. Grealish, who starred for Aston Villa in their FA Cup semi-final win over Liverpool, has become the third top flight starlet to be caught using the drug. Grealish's performance in the match highlights the importance of maintaining a healthy lifestyle and making responsible choices as an athlete.

Sam Barton, a 22-year-old man who underwent £55,000 in cosmetic surgery to resemble reality TV star Joey Essex, was attacked by a group of men with eggs on Easter Monday after being targeted online for his appearance. The attack occurred at a pub in Sutton Coldfield, West Midlands, where Barton had checked in on Facebook minutes before. The incident, which left him with yolk and shell on his face, was believed to be a result of online abuse and tracking of his Facebook posts. Sam Barton, who has spent £20,000 on dental work, £5,000 on Botox, £2,000 on waxing, and £2,500 on tanning, has also been involved in a financial struggle, owing £100,000 on credit cards and store cards. The attack highlights the intersection of celebrity culture, online harassment, and the high costs associated with achieving a desired

A university in Indiana was in lockdown late on Friday night after a 'likely prank call' about an armed person near the main administration building. Police said they received a phone call from someone saying that they had stabbed their roommate at the university, was armed with a shotgun and threatening to blow up the administration building. Manchester University had issued a statement advising students at its North Manchester campus, some 36 miles west of Fort Wayne, to shelter in place. The person was possibly armed with explosives, according to the university. The university continued reposting the shelter in place warning for hours after the original message and had not given the all clear as of 2am.

Edinson Cavani, a key player for Paris Saint-Germain, prepares for a quarter-final clash against Barcelona. Despite facing challenges, including suspension and a goal drought, Cavani is expected to play a crucial role in helping PSG progress beyond the Champions League's last eight.

Derry Mathews has won the interim WBA lightweight title after defeating Tony Luis in a close fight. Mathews, who was drafted in at the last minute, outperformed Luis in the closing rounds and was awarded a 114-112, 114-112, 115-112 decision.

Hull FC defeated St Helens 28-20 in a surprise victory, overcoming a 12-10 deficit after the break. Hull's Jamie Shaul scored the winning try, while St Helens' Jordan Turner scored a try and converted it. The win was Hull's first in three matches and their first since a derby loss to Hull KR.

The United States' undocumented and documented immigrant population could reach a record high of 51 million by 2023, according to U.S. Census figures. By 2060, immigrants could account for 82% of the country's population growth. The Center for Immigration Studies predicts that the undocumented immigrant population could reach 14.8% of the population by 2023, and 78 million by 2060. The report also suggests that without changes to current immigration policy, the total immigrant population in the United States could reach 14.8% of the population by 2023.

Arsenal Under 21s lost 1-0 to Reading U21s in a match that showcased the return of Jack Wilshere from injury, despite the team's other injured players. Martin Keown's son, Niall, scored the only goal for Reading. Wilshere, Diaby, and Gnabry were among the injured players who returned to the field.

Justin Rose, a professional golfer, experienced a decline in his form after a poor performance in Florida, falling outside the world's top 10. To recover, he spent time on the practice ground and shot a 69 at the Shell Houston Open. Rose believes he has made progress and feels confident in his ability to perform well at the Masters.

A Mayfair mansion, once a milking parlour, has gone on the market for £25 million. The property, which was constructed on the site of a former milking parlour in Mayfair, features modern furnishings, a private lift, and a 14-piece dining table. The mansion, which has four bedrooms, is being sold by estate agents Wetherell and Knight Frank.

Bayern Munich's squad is stronger for their recent injury troubles, according to Thomas Muller. The Bavarians, chasing three titles this season, are without key players Arjen Robben, Franck Ribery, Bastian Schweinsteiger, and David Alaba for the Champions League game against Porto. Muller believes the team's unity will help them against Porto. Bayern Munich will rely heavily on Muller and Robert Lewandowski in the absence of Robben and Ribery. Guardiola, the Bayern coach, is eyeing up a Treble of Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal, and Champions League. Porto won four matches and drew twice in the group stage before crushing Basel 5-1 on aggregate in the round of 16.

Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes team-mates, visited Mercedes' Brackley base to collaborate on a winning strategy for the upcoming Chinese Grand Prix. Despite Sebastian Vettel's victory at the Malaysian Grand Prix, the Mercedes team was concerned about Ferrari's tactics and the possibility of another season of Mercedes domination. The team's boss, Toto Wolff, admitted that the team was surprised by Vettel's victory and that the three-stop strategy worked well for them, but they need to analyze why Ferrari was able to go at a faster pace over long runs.

Oklahoma Governor Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to perform executions with nitrogen gas if lethal injection is ruled unconstitutional or becomes unavailable. The bill, signed on Friday, would allow the state to use nitrogen gas to cause a quick loss of consciousness and death from lack of oxygen, with a brief period of unconsciousness followed by death. The bill, which has been signed into law, is the latest in a series of efforts to find alternative methods of execution in the state, following the Supreme Court's review of its use of lethal injections.

Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice in Swansea's 3-1 win over Hull on Saturday, topping EA Sports' Performance Index after another thrilling installment of Premier League action. Gomis, who made a slow start to his career in south Wales, has scored four goals in his last six Premier League games and earned a Game Index score of 52.9 this weekend.

A massive freezer trawler sank in the Sea of Okhotsk off the coast of Russia, killing at least 56 crew members. The ship, carrying 132 crew members, sank in just 15 minutes after an empty fuel tank and lack of ballast caused it to tip over. More than 1,300 people are involved in the massive rescue operation, with 63 survivors rescued so far. The sinking is believed to have been caused by a fishing net weighing 80 tons being pulled in, and 56 bodies have been recovered. The Russian Emergencies Ministry sent an Mi-8 helicopter to treat and transport rescued crew members to hospitals.

A new study suggests that a drug originally developed for women with breast cancer could also help men with advanced prostate cancer. Clinical trials show that olaparib, an inhibitor of PARP proteins, can delay the moment when prostate cancer gets dangerously out of control. The drug works by blocking the cancer cell's ability to repair damage, targeting only cells with genetic defects. Up to 30% of men with advanced prostate cancer have tumours with DNA defects, and these respond particularly well to olaparib. The drug has been granted approval for use in ovarian cancer by the European Commission and the US Food and Drug Administration. The study, led by researchers at the Institute of Cancer Research and the Royal Marsden hospital, found that 16 out of 49 men with advanced prostate cancer responded to the drug, stopping prostate cancer growth and improving responses in medical scans. This suggests that men most likely to benefit from the drug could be identified by testing for mutations in their tumours.

Travel photographer Rhiannon Taylor, 29, from Australia, launched a website called "In Bed With" to review and photograph the most luxurious accommodations around the world. With more than 12, 000 followers on Instagram, she has turned her social media success into a growing business. Taylor travels the world to review beds, pools, and room service, documenting her findings on her website. She has stayed at some of the most exclusive hotels around the world, including the Mineral Springs Hotel in Victoria, Australia, and the Pullman in Melbourne. Taylor has also worked with companies who sell travel products, allowing her to generate further income from featuring them on her site.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was mauled to death by two adult hippos during a fight in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park in eastern South Africa. The mother hippo watched in horror as her calf was flung into the air before being dragged along the surface of the water. The baby died hours after the tussle, with its mother staying with her herd.

The Football Association will contact QPR and Chelsea after an incident where Branislav Ivanovic was struck on the head by a cigarette lighter thrown from a section of home supporters at Loftus Road. Chelsea players celebrated the winning goal, and objects were thrown onto the pitch. QPR is reviewing CCTV footage and appealing to witnesses. The club is banning those involved and will liaise with the Metropolitan Police. Chelsea duo Nemanja Matic and Branislav Ivanovic were targeted by objects thrown from the crowd.

A young mother and her three children were found murdered in their home in Tisdale, Saskatchewan. The suspect in the case was found dead hours later, and while police did not confirm it was a homicide, they did not rule it out. The victim, LaTasha Gosling, 27, and her two daughters, Janyaa, 4, and Jenika, 8, and her son Landen, 7, were discovered early Wednesday. The family had been missing for one day. The suspect and victim had known each other. The family is raising money for their funeral services and has started a GoFundMe page.

Emily Thornberry, a senior Labour politician, has three homes, including a £1 million property she bought from a housing association eight years ago. She has been criticized for opposing the right to buy policy while renting out a property she bought from a housing association. The housing association chiefs have also been accused of hypocrisy for drawing huge salaries and living in mansions while wishing to deny tenants a foot on the property ladder.

Mike Lane, a huntsman, was viciously assaulted by protesters armed with iron bars on ropes during a hunt. Despite evidence pointing to the identity of the attacker, Wiltshire Police dropped the investigation three months later, angering the victim and hunt supporters. The attack occurred when the 30 riders and their hounds were chasing an artificial scent, and the attacker sprayed hounds with citronella to distract them. The suspect's face was captured on video, but he has not been identified. The incident has led to a loss of trust in the police and has sparked protests across the country.

Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes insists he has no intention of leaving the club this summer. The 21-year-old has been linked with Premier League teams Manchester United and Chelsea, but Gomes says he wants to stay at the club. He has netted four times in 25 La Liga appearances since leaving Benfica last summer, helping Valencia to fourth place in the table.

An Australian teenager, Audrey Pekin, was raped twice on Christmas Eve in Bali while holidaying with her family. The incident occurred at a remote home of a man named Henry Alafu, who lured her there after meeting her friends. Alafu allegedly raped her twice, once in a taxi and again in the house. The Indonesian police failed to arrest Alafu, leading to outrage among the Pekin family.

PETA has joined forces with animal rights activist Ashley James to launch an anti-fur campaign against Harvey Nichols, a national department store that previously had a ten-year anti-fur policy. The campaign, titled "Harvey Nichols: Here's the Rest of Your Fur Coat," features a fake skinned fox and aims to raise awareness about the cruelty involved in the fur industry. Harvey Nichols has since re-introduced its fur-free policy, but PETA is still in talks with billboard companies to mount the campaign outside their stores.

Chile has joined several South American neighbors in allowing civil unions between people of the same sex, with President Michelle Bachelet enacting a new law on Monday. The new law will take effect in six months and will give legal weight to cohabiting relationships between two people of the same sex and between a man and a woman. The law is intended to end discrimination faced by common-law couples and gives them greater rights in the realms of property, health care, pensions, and inheritance.

Chelsea are on course to become the most dominant title-winners in Premier League history, leading the table for 257 days as of April 10, 2005/06, according to the article. The team is currently in first place with a seven-point lead over their rivals, with their next three games against QPR, Manchester United, and Arsenal set to be crucial.

Cape Verde, a small country in the Atlantic, is tapping into its rich musical heritage to boost its economy. The country, which has few natural resources, is promoting music and culture as a way to attract visitors and create jobs. The Kriol Jazz Festival, which has been held in Cape Verde for seven years, has become a major event, with artists from around the world performing. The festival has helped to showcase Cape Verde's unique musical styles and has brought people from all over the world to the country.

An old hoax video showing a wave rider surfing in front of the Sydney Opera House has gone viral for the second time, with some users referencing the heavy storms that hit Sydney overnight as the trigger for the strange phenomenon. The video, originally posted by Sydney radio duo Fitzy and Wippa, was quickly reposted by other sources. YouTube commenters pointed out inaccuracies in the video, such as the appearance of rocks around the Opera House and the cardboard-esque appearance of the man in the final shot. Wave experts vowed it was a sham, and Ben Macartney, a swell forecaster, told News.com that it was "theoretically impossible" for ocean swells to break that far inside the Harbour.

Reading, the FA Cup semi-finalists, were defeated 1-0 by Birmingham in a Sky Bet Championship game at the Madejski Stadium. Clayton Donaldson scored the winning goal in the 78th minute. Reading's Adam Federici, who had fumbled a crucial clearance against Arsenal in the last four of the Cup, was retained for the match.

David Luiz, a key player for Paris Saint-Germain (PSG), has been ruled out of the Champions League quarter-final against Barcelona due to a hamstring injury. The 27-year-old Brazilian defender will miss at least four weeks, potentially impacting PSG's title defense and their upcoming match against Barcelona.

The return of Game of Thrones has led to a significant increase in internet piracy, with more than 100,000 illegal downloads per day reported by anti-piracy firm Irdeto. The most illegally downloaded shows were The Walking Dead, Breaking Bad, Vikings, and House of Cards. The HBO network announced a new streaming service, HBO Now, to curb piracy and recapture revenue.

Leicester City will host West Ham United in the Premier League on Saturday. Leicester's Matt Upson is out with an Achilles injury, while West Ham's Winston Reid is back from injury. Leicester's provisional squad includes Schmeichel, Schwarzer, Hamer, Simpson, Moore, Wasilewski, Morgan, Huth, De Laet, Konchesky, King, Knockaert, Albrighton, Schlupp, Cambiasso, James, Mahrez, Nugent, Kramaric, Vardy, Ulloa. West Ham's provisional squad includes Adrian, Jaaskelainen, Cresswell, Jenkinson, Reid, Collins, O'Brien, Noble, Poyet, Song, Amalfitano, Kouyate, Nolan, Downing, Jarvis, Nene, Sakho, Valencia, Cole. The match is scheduled for kick-off at 3pm.

A controversial statue of Lucille Ball, the beloved comedian from "I Love Lucy," has sparked outrage in Celoron, New York, due to its unflattering depiction. The statue, based on a moment from the show, has attracted over 600 likes on a Facebook page called "We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue." The anonymous creator, who claims to be a fan of Ball, argues that the statue should be more like the statues of other comedians like Nick at Nite's "Bewitched" and "The Honeymooners" characters. The town has considered replacing the statue, but it would cost an estimated $8,000 to $10,000 to recast it. The controversy highlights the ongoing debate about how to honor iconic figures in local communities.

A woman who tipped the scales at almost 20st lost nearly half her body weight after being forced to stand during an 11-hour flight due to her fear of crushing the woman in the seat next to her. Sharon Smith, 43, from Halesowen, West Midlands, joined Weight Watchers Online and ran a 10k race, shedding 4st through joining a slimming club and another 4.5 stone after taking up running.

Nicola Bonn, a 34-year-old mother of a 14-month-old daughter named Poppy, started a blog called Upfront Mama to share her experiences and challenges of being a first-time mother. Her candid account of raising a baby has gone viral, and she has shared a post detailing the reasons why she decided to stop justifying herself and apologizing for her decisions. The main hurdles for new mothers, according to Bonn, are the overwhelming opinions from others and the high levels of self-doubt.

Two teenage boys, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, from Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, are feared to have traveled to Syria to join ISIS. Hassan is believed to be related to Hammaad Munshi, who was arrested at 15 for planning to murder non-Muslims. The families are in shock and worried about their safety. The boys have not been in contact with their families for several days and cannot be reached on their mobile phones.

Stephanie Scott, a beloved school teacher from Leeton, was brutally murdered just days before her much-anticipated wedding to Aaron Leeson-Woolley. Her body was found in nearby bushland, and a guest list of 120 people had been invited to her wedding at the picturesque Eat Your Greens venue. The wedding plans were disrupted as the Scott family must now prepare for Stephanie's funeral instead of a wedding.

Southampton is interested in signing Tonny Vilhena, a 20-year-old winger from Feyenoord, who is eager to leave the club this summer. The Saints are also monitoring Jordy Clasie, a £10m-rated midfielder, and are considering making Eljero Elia's loan from Werder Bremen permanent. Southampton is currently seventh in the Premier League and is on track to qualify for the Europa League.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture with beanbags in the library of Ickworth House, Suffolk, in an experiment that has angered heritage experts. The move was designed to encourage visitors to "dwell and take in the atmosphere" but was branded "misguided" by art historian Bendor Grosvenor. The Trust said the beanbag experiment was "short-term" and that it presents each house in context. However, some staff members think the Trust should have used a different sort of seating.

Former Prime Minister John Howard was photographed standing on the footpath outside the Sydney Conservatorium of Music with a flat tyre, while his driver changed it. Felicity Waterford, who was waiting for her daughter at the Conservatorium, approached the pair and offered assistance. The former PM, who was a complete gentleman, agreed to a selfie with Waterford. This incident came weeks after Liberal MP Christopher Pyne was challenged to change a tyre on national television after boasting he was a 'fixer'.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has admitted that midfielder Joey Barton "probably had a point" about the team's loss to Queens Park Rangers earlier this season, citing the example of West Brom being 2-0 up but losing 3-2. Pulis, who has instilled a solid core of players at West Brom, believes that Barton's comments were justified given the circumstances. Pulis also recalled his own experience of leading a team to a 2-0 lead but ending up drawing and losing on penalties, adding that he can't talk about being indestructible in respect to leads. Pulis praised the performances of his team, hoping to continue that success.

A new species of monkey, the Bouvier's red colobus monkey, has been discovered in the remote rain forests of the Democratic Republic of Congo. The primate, which was previously thought to be extinct, was first discovered in 1887 and is only known from three specimens. The discovery was made by researchers Lieven Devreese and Gaël Elie Gnondo Gobolo, who captured the first ever photograph of the monkey. The researchers hope to study the monkey to learn more about it and to protect it from hunters involved in the commercial bushmeat trade.

Kim Kardashian and her family, including her husband Kanye West and daughter North, visited Armenia for an eight-day trip to explore the country, which is the birthplace of their late father Robert Kardashian. The visit includes a stay at the Armenia Marriott Hotel Yerevan, which is located in the capital city of Yerevan. The city is known for its rich history and cultural landmarks, such as the Opera House and the Zvartnots International Airport. The Kardashian-West family is accompanied by bodyguards and police to ensure their safety as they explore the city.

Patrick and Valerie Jubb, British expats living in southern Spain, are facing legal battles with the local town hall over a luxury bed and breakfast they once operated. The couple, who purchased the property in 2008, are attempting to sell it but are now in danger of losing it due to illegal additions made by a previous owner. The Jubbs claim they have done nothing wrong and are seeking to return to the UK, but their money is tied up in the property. The town hall ruled that the first floor, kitchen, and pool were illegally built in 1994, and the Jubbs obtained a certificate stating there were no infractions when they bought the estate. However, the Jubbs argue that the alterations were legalised by land registry officials in 2005, three years before they acquired the estate. The Jubbs are planning to move back to the UK, but their money is tied up in the property.

Apple reported strong sales of iPhones in the first quarter of 2015, with more than 61 million units sold, accounting for over two-thirds of its revenue and profit. The company's iPad revenue fell 29% to $5.4 billion, while Mac computer revenue rose 2% to $5.6 billion. The iPhone's strong performance is attributed to a higher rate of people switching to iPhone compared to previous cycles.

A 3-year-old girl named Elisa, whose mother Natali Castellanos-Tyler died in a car crash, has been having disturbing nightmares and daytime visions about a white van. Her father, Craig Tyler, believes that the van may be connected to the crash. The van has been linked to three hit-and-run incidents in the area.

Researchers at New York University have discovered that the brain can remember 'neutral' or boring events more easily when they are tied to an emotion. This finding suggests that the brain has the remarkable ability to store information that seems inconsequential at the time in case it becomes useful later on. Emotion increases our ability to remember by affecting activity in brain regions involved in emotional processing and also the regions involved in encoding new experiences.

Jahnae Jackson, the girlfriend of a teenager with a life-threatening brain tumour, has raised over $80,000 for his life-saving surgery to be performed by renowned neurosurgeon Dr. Charlie Teo. The 18-year-old has put her psychology studies on hold to care for her boyfriend, who is paralysed and unable to dress himself due to the tumour. The community in the small town of Casino, NSW, has shown overwhelming support for the fundraising effort.

Nedum Onuoha, a QPR centre-back with 15 months left on his contract, is being targeted by Hull City, Everton, West Ham United, Stoke manager Mark Hughes, and West Bromwich Albion. Onuoha played for QPR under Chris Ramsey and has been a regular starter. The club is considering streamlining their squad and has held talks with Stoke about a move for Catania defender Nicolas Spolli. Hull City is also showing interest in West Bromwich Albion striker Victor Anichebe, who is likely to be sold this summer.

Researchers at Yale University have created an interactive map that documents the subtle differences in sentence structure across the United States, revealing regional variations in English grammar. The map, which focuses on the US, also includes data for the UK. The study, conducted using an online crowdsourcing platform, found that presentative sentences like "Here's you a water bottle" were considered normal in the South, while they were almost unheard of in the North. The overall pattern was clear: In the South, people found that sentence to be completely normal, while in the North, it was almost unheard of.

A Canadian man named Kalman Kallai took a rocking chair on a nine-day journey across Canada from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia. He used the chair to enjoy the scenery and took videos of himself rocking and making gestures. The trip was part of his work, and he met his dad along the way. The video shows him posing, dancing, and waving at cows, and he even carried the chair on his head.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood showed his softer side during a press conference by revealing a Twix multi-pack as a win bonus to a young fan who applied for the club's hotseat after Paul Lambert was sacked. Sherwood joked that the win bonus would be sweets and chocolate, and revealed the Twix to the assembled media.

Kell Brook, a world boxing champion, enjoyed an evening at the darts as he watched the Premier League road show come to his home town of Sheffield. Dave Chisnall, a 28-year-old darts player, won both of his games in week 10 to move onto 17 points in second place in the table. Chisnall recorded a 7-3 victory over world champion Gary Anderson before returning later in the evening to thrash James Wade 7-1.

Marco Verratti of Paris Saint-Germain has praised Zlatan Ibrahimovic for his essential role in the club's Ligue 1 goals, stating that his off-pitch contributions are just as important. Ibrahimovic, who has scored 17 goals for the club this season, will be available for selection for the Champions League quarter-final second leg against Barcelona.

The Ministry of Defence accidentally published a secret RAF aerodrome manual containing vital GPS coordinates and runway depth information on their website, which could be used by Argentina to prepare an invasion of the Falklands Islands. The information was accessible to anyone and could cripple Britain's ability to defend the islands. The MoD initially denied the sensitivity of the data but acknowledged the link had been disabled. The incident highlights the importance of maintaining security on military websites and the potential risks of unauthorized access to sensitive information.

Paul Anderson, Huddersfield Giants' coach, aims to boost his team's offensive performance to match their defensive efficiency as they seek to climb back up the Super League ladder. The Giants have fallen from third to ninth after losing all three games over the Easter period, but Anderson believes his team can improve their offense. Anderson attributes the team's recent struggles to issues with their offense and acknowledges that he is responsible for fixing them. If Huddersfield can win their next game, they could leapfrog their French opponents, Catalans Dragons, who have the best defensive record in the league.

In Windsor, two Costa coffee shops, one replacing a cycle shop and the other at a petrol station, are less than 500 yards apart, creating a cluster of coffee shops within a mile of the Dedworth Road HSBC branch. This development has sparked debate among residents, with some expressing concerns about the proliferation of coffee shops in the area.

The British Veterinary Association (BVA) has withdrawn its support for the controversial shooting of free-running badgers in two four-year pilot culls in Somerset and Gloucestershire, stating that the first two years of culling did not demonstrate conclusively that "controlled shooting" could be effective and humane. The BVA still supports badger culling to tackle tuberculosis in cattle. The Environment Secretary has promised to roll out more culls across the country if the Tories win the election, while animal welfare campaigners welcomed the news but criticized the BVA's ongoing support for cage-trapping and shooting.

Portishead founder Geoff Barrow accused streaming services of giving his band's music away for free, saying his band received just £1,700 in royalties despite 34 million plays. Barrow, who also runs the Invada record label, said younger artists are getting a poor deal and that record companies have been quick to upload their music on to these platforms to prop up the collapse in CD sales after music moved online.

Game of Thrones fans who did not want to wait and legally watch HBO's hit series premiere its fifth season tonight have leaked the first four episodes online. The episodes began appearing on torrent download sites on Saturday night, and are thought to have leaked from review copies given to the press. Fans of the show, which follows the ambitions and betrayals of competing noble factions and families in the fantasy world of Westeros, now face the daunting task of avoiding spoilers online as the first four episodes are released over the course of the month.

A best man at a Melbourne wedding left guests in tears after performing an emotional song composed by the groom's younger brother. Daniel Buccheri, 25, composed the song "Stay With Me" to use as his brother Adrian's best man speech at their March 29 wedding. The unique speech, which has been viewed over 100,000 times online, includes tributes to the groom and his bride, as well as a touching account of their brother's love story.

Zara Phillips, the Queen's granddaughter, has revealed how she regained her fitness after the birth of her daughter Mia. She started hitting the exercise bike every morning before her daughter woke up, aiming to get back to her pre-pregnancy fitness level.

Raheem Sterling's interview, in which he said he was not ready to sign a new contract at Liverpool, has angered fans and potentially changed their opinion of him. The interview was ill-timed and did not go well, and it has fueled the fire among fans who want him to leave. Sterling has been linked with a move to Arsenal, and many fans believe that if he wants to go, the club should handle it the way they have before.

In 2016, Jose Mourinho and Pep Guardiola, two of the most successful managers in football history, had a conversation during a Barcelona training session. The image of the two managers deep in conversation became a popular meme on social media. Since then, several other managers from the same era have been spotted together, including Laurent Blanc, Julen Lopetegui, and Albert Ferrer. These managers were all part of the same Barcelona team that won the Spanish Super Cup in 1996, and they have since gone on to manage other clubs. The image of the managers together has become a symbol of the continuity of football management in Spain.

Former Manchester United legend Eric Cantona has declared Paris Saint-Germain forward Javier Pastore the best player in the world, saying he is the most creative and exciting player due to his ability to pass and surprise opponents. Cantona, who won the Ballon d'Or in 1993, praised Pastore's skills, including his ability to score spectacular goals and pass creatively. Despite statistics showing Messi and Ronaldo as the top players, Cantona's assessment was met with controversy, particularly regarding Spain's World Cup victory, which he attributed to Barcelona's influence.

Lorenzo Simon, 34, was found guilty of murder for killing his tenant Michael Spalding, 39, and dismembering his body parts before dumping them in a canal. The case involved dismembering the victim using a hacksaw and stuffing the body parts and tools into two suitcases, which were then thrown into the canal. The trial took 15 hours to decide by unanimous verdict at Birmingham Crown Court. Bird, Simon's girlfriend, was cleared of murder and manslaughter but admitted assisting an offender.

Local councils in Essex and Gloucestershire have created "loneliness maps" to identify areas where elderly residents are most at risk of social isolation. The maps are based on factors such as age, living alone, mental health issues, lack of transportation, and low income. The maps are used to target vulnerable areas and provide support to those in need. The Campaign to End Loneliness recommends that other councils adopt similar maps to identify and address loneliness in their communities.

Dedicated waitress Judy Eddingfield, 65, celebrated her 50th anniversary at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, the only job she has ever had or ever wanted. She started working there in 1965, when she was 15 years old, and has been providing top-notch service for half a century. Eddingfield's mother had been working at the restaurant for 13 years when she began her own career. She met her first husband outside the restaurant and they married 18 months later. Eddingfield's favorite memory was when Jerry Mathers and Tony Dow of the television series 'Leave It to Beaver' came to eat there in the late 1970s.

Former England captain Mike Gatting believes Kevin Pietersen should not walk straight back into the international set-up, even if he piles on the runs for Surrey this season. Pietersen has returned to the LV= County Championship in a bid to stake a claim for an England recall, although the 34-year-old only managed 19 runs against Glamorgan on Sunday. Gatting suggests that England needs to have players who are not playing well to get Pietersen in, and that if he does get runs, it's not the end of it. Pietersen is keen to play for England again after being sacked in 2014, and Bell and Ballance both hit centuries in Antigua while Root also showed signs of good form with scores of 83 and 59. The scorecard was less encouraging for England captain Alastair Cook, who could only manage 11 and 13, stretching his run without a Test century to 33

A 17-year-old college student named Caleb Benn developed an app called "Uploader for Instagram" that allows users to upload photos directly from their computer to the popular photo-sharing platform Instagram. The app, which costs $4.99, has been generating $1,000 a day in revenue for Benn. However, Instagram has filed a lawsuit against Benn, claiming that his app violates the company's terms of service. Benn has until Monday to fix the issue, but he believes that doing so would make the app pointless. The lawsuit highlights the tension between social media platforms and developers who want to monetize their services.

Korean drinking culture, known as "hoe sik," involves multiple rounds of alcohol at multiple venues. Foreign business travelers may find it challenging to participate due to intense pressure to drink. Koreans view drinking as a way to get to know someone and an invitation to listen. To avoid offending someone, follow these seven rules: identify the "higher" person in the relationship, defer to them, and turn your body away from senior figures when drinking.

The Duke of Kent, 79, was admitted to Aberdeen Royal Infirmary after suffering a dislocated hip during an Easter trip to the Royal Family's Balmoral estate. He was successfully treated and is expected to leave hospital later today. The Duke, who is the son of Prince George, has enjoyed a long military career and is the country's top Freemason.

Meter Maids, a 50-year-old tradition of Surfers Paradise, Queensland, have been called into question by local business owners who believe the outdated and controversial practice of young women dressed in gold bikinis walking the main tourist strip and placing money into expired meters is no longer relevant due to advancements in parking meter technology. The Gold Coast Chamber of Commerce president, Peter Yared, argues that Meter Maids are now a business and not a public service, violating anti-touting laws. However, local business owners and the Meter Maids themselves maintain that the practice is a beloved part of the Gold Coast and Surfers Paradise experience, bringing good memories for many tourists.

Greece has denied it will miss a repayment of £330 million to the International Monetary Fund, claiming it will make the payment on April 9. Deputy finance minister Dimitris Mardas stated that Greece will in fact make the payment on time. Greece has drawn up plans to introduce a parallel drachma currency to pay domestic bills, but sources close to the ruling Syriza party claim the government prioritizes paying wages and pensions over loans. Greece may have to go into a silent arrears process with the IMF, causing a furore in the markets and potentially leading to a faster clock ticking.

Turkey has blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after refusing to remove pictures of a prosecutor held during an armed siege last week. The prosecutor, Mehmet Selim Kiraz, died in hospital after being taken hostage by the Revolutionary People's Liberation Party-Front. The government blocked access to social media platforms because the images were "deeply upset" the prosecutor's family.

A young Star Wars fan named Colin Gilpatric wrote a letter to George Lucas, the creator of the Star Wars franchise, asking if Jedi Knights could marry. Lucasfilm responded positively, stating that marriage would not lead to becoming a Sith and that it would be a good way to connect with others. Colin was thrilled to receive the letter and was able to see it in person.

Wisconsin defeated Kentucky in the NCAA basketball tournament semi-finals, securing a spot in the final. Kentucky's unbeaten season was ended, and the team finished the season at 38-1, two wins short of becoming the first undefeated team in college basketball since the 1975-76 Indiana Hoosiers.

Vince Neil, a member of the rock band Mötley Crüe, was criticized for his rendition of the American national anthem at a football game in Las Vegas. His performance was deemed unsatisfactory by many, including former President George H. W. Bush, who called it "disgraceful." The incident highlights the controversy surrounding the national anthem and the potential consequences of poor performance.

A man from Belfast, Ireland, has been charged with grievous bodily harm after punching his younger brother in the head during an argument in Sydney, Australia. The incident occurred in January 2023 at a bar in Kings Cross, Sydney. The brother responsible, Patrick Lyttle, has called for the charges against his brother, Barry Lyttle, to be dropped. Magistrate Graeme Curran is expected to determine if Barry will face a full-time jail term. The case is currently under investigation, and the brothers are reunited after a holiday in Australia.

The family of conjoined twin sisters Faith and Hope Howie, who died 19 days after birth, were devastated to find their gravesite cleared of mementos and flowers after cemetery staff removed everything from the baby section of the cemetery. The Howies had built a small shrine at the gravesite over the past 11 months, but when they returned to retrieve their daughters' belongings, they found the site completely bare. The family was told they were supposed to have been notified they would be cleaned, but the staff had not been properly informed. The Howies were able to retrieve about 25 percent of their memorabilia, and they have maintained the site to ensure it is not treated like rubbish.

Lord Neuberger, the President of the Supreme Court, suggested that Muslim women should be allowed to wear a full-face veil while appearing in court, as it shows respect towards different customs. He emphasized the need for judges and courtrooms to be sensitive to the cultural and social habits of those facing them. This suggestion comes amid uncertainty over the place of Muslim traditional dress in the legal system.

Andre Cole, a 52-year-old Missouri inmate, was executed for the 1998 murder of his ex-wife and her friend, Anthony Curtis, in a fit of rage over child support payments. The execution was carried out by lethal injection at the Eastern Reception, Diagnostic and Correctional Center in Bonne Terre, Missouri. Cole was the third convicted killer put to death in Missouri this year. The execution was met with criticism from some, who argued that Cole was mentally ill and unfit for execution.

Prince Harry will fly out of the UK to Australia without seeing his new niece or nephew, as the Duchess of Cambridge is several days overdue for the birth of her second child. Harry, who will be bumped down to fifth in the line of succession, had returned briefly to hand out prizes at the London Marathon after engagements in Turkey. He was forced to return to Australia for a month-long placement with the army and a week-long official tour of New Zealand.

An alleged fraudster named Justin Jackson has been accused of posing as Oprah Winfrey, her TV network, former Obama aide Reggie Love, Madonna's manager, and others in an attempt to trick people into giving him freebies and jobs worth $2.4 million. Jackson, a Florida man, has been sued by Oprah's TV network and Love, and is being sued by Angel Agarrat, who is also named in a Florida lawsuit attempting to get the pair to stop posing as other people. Jackson has been convicted for grand theft over a ruse in which he tricked a jeweler into lending him items worth $2.4 million by pretending to be Madonna's manager. He has been accused of sending letters purporting to be from Oprah, Love, and Johnny Depp's manager, as well as posing as Oprah's nephew and recommending himself for jobs at hotels.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini has placed a €50 million price tag on Paulo Dybala, telling Paris Saint-Germain they will have to spend big to sign the "new Lionel Messi." Dybala is being tracked by Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, Juventus, and Paris Saint-Germain. Inter Milan manager Roberto Mancini was spotted watching Dybala at a Serie A match. Zamparini told Telefoot that Dybala is the new Messi and wants €40 million for him, but is willing to negotiate for €50 million.

Hundreds of thousands of Brazilians are protesting against President Dilma Rousseff, who is struggling with an economic downturn and a massive bribery scandal. The protests are calling for Rousseff to be impeached. The main issue is an investigation into a multimillion-dollar kickback scheme at the state-run oil company Petrobras, which has been accused of bribing politicians and construction companies to secure lucrative contracts. The protests have grown in size and breadth, with some demonstrators saying they initially voted for Rousseff. The country was already sharply divided during presidential elections, and participation in the protests has not been consistently strong.

Former Manchester United midfielder Eric Cantona has refuted claims he starred in a soft porn film, insisting it is a "piece of art." The French film, "You and the Night," includes a scene in a cage with Cantona in just his underwear. Cantona, 48, says it is not pornography but a work of art and beautiful, though he acknowledges it is too erotic for some.

Psychologists have found that certain types of music can enhance the enjoyment of a fish and chip supper by bringing out specific flavors in the food. The intensity of Nessun Dorma, performed by Luciano Pavarotti, is said to be the perfect accompaniment to dark mouse or coffee, while the high-pitched piano in Billie Holiday's Autumn in New York can help emphasize the autumnal flavor of a pumpkin pudding. The research suggests that music can draw attention to certain notes in a wine or food that are competing in the mind, and that humans tend to match the same sounds to the same tastes.

Raheem Sterling, 20-year-old England player, has been offered a £100,000-a-week contract by Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers, but negotiations have ended in stalemate. Sterling has insisted he is not a 'money grabber' and believes postponing contract talks until the end of the season could be a wise move. Sterling has been linked with moves to Arsenal and leading clubs in Spain. Sterling scored for England in their Euro 2016 qualifier with Lithuania on Friday evening. An Ohio woman, La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, discovered her biological mother, Francine Simmons, works at the same company as her and lives only six minutes away. After connecting the dots, she found out her mother was closer than she could imagine. Simmons, who was 'still in shock' from finding out about her daughter, reached out to friends on social media who knew Simmons and the two eventually decided to meet after a phone call. They found out they work at the same call-center operations company and live six minutes away from one another. Mitchell-Clark also found out that she had three biological younger sisters.

Oscar "Papoo" Hernandez Jr., a convicted gun trafficker, was "awed" by New England Patriots star Aaron Hernandez and "grateful to be noticed" when the football player paid him $15,000 for three guns in April 2013, a month before Odin Lloyd's murder. Hernandez pleaded guilty to weapons charges in connection to his namesake's murder case.

A 33-year-old man named Joel Parker was arrested in Florida for throwing a Snickers bar at a bus driver's head after threatening him and being disruptive during the ride. The driver was not injured, but Parker was arrested for battery and issued a trespass warning. He is also never allowed to use the bus again.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has discussed pre-season plans with Saido Berahino, indicating the striker will remain at the club beyond the summer transfer window. Berahino, who has expressed a desire to play in the Champions League, is likely to be away with Gareth Southgate's England under-21 team in the Czech Republic until late June. Pulis has begun preparations early, with the 21-year-old likely to be included in the England under-21 squad for the upcoming European Championships.

Giovanni Lo Porto, a Sicilian man who worked with the German aid organization Welthungerlife, was abducted by four armed men in Pakistan in 2012 and later killed by a U.S. drone strike. He was working on a reconstruction project in Pakistan following deadly flooding there. Lo Porto was a project manager with the aid group's clean water and sanitation program, working with 8 to 10 fellow international staffers and 100 to 200 locals.

A photographer captured an image of hundreds of sharks swimming just 100 feet from the beach off the coast of south Florida last week. The scene was so intense that it went viral on social media, with users theorizing that the sharks were Blacktips or Spinners, which migrate to breed in shallower waters.

An 11-year-old retired K-9 officer named Zeus was honored in a grand procession in Ridgefield, Connecticut, before he was put down due to a severe degenerative hip disorder and declining health. The tribute was held on Wednesday, and residents lined the streets to watch the cop cars drive by. Zeus had worked with the Ridgefield Police Department for eight years as a K-9 officer and assisted with more than 250 narcotics arrests and helped track down 50 missing or wanted individuals during his career. The tribute was held at Ridgefield Veterinary Hospital, where Zeus was to be euthanized.

Child sexual abuse reports have surged by more than 60% since Operation Yewtree, with thousands of new allegations filed since 2011. Despite a 9% drop in arrests, critics accuse the Government of failing to protect victims. The number of reported cases has increased in South Yorkshire by 577%, with 501 cases investigated in 2014 compared to 74 in 2011. The NSPCC helpline has seen a 81% increase in calls about sexual abuse since the operation was launched in 2012.

Iceland has become a popular filming location for hit TV series and Hollywood blockbusters, with Thingvellir National Park, Svartalfheim, Reykjanes Peninsula, Svinafellsjokull, Skaftafell National Park, Vatnajokull, Dettifoss, and Jokullsarlon lake consistently ranking as filming locations for various productions. The country's stunning landscapes, including waterfalls and glaciers, have been featured in films such as Game of Thrones, Interstellar, Thor: The Dark World, and Prometheus. The Icelandic film industry has grown rapidly, with 17 production services companies operating nationwide, and the country's unique natural beauty continues to attract filmmakers from around the world.

A unique 1850s goal in Victoria, Australia, has sold for $2 million, making it the most expensive property in the country. The property, which was once a maximum security prison, is now being converted into a cozy home. The property is located 60 kilometers north of Melbourne and is said to be haunted by the owners' promise of never seeing a ghost.

Samantha Rawcliffe, a 40-year-old mother-of-two from Morecambe, was diagnosed with functional neurological disorder (FND) after a car accident in May 2021. FND is an umbrella term for a range of neurological symptoms that doctors cannot explain, including uncontrollable shaking, loss of bladder control, and difficulty with motor function. Rawcliffe lost control of her body in the accident and developed symptoms such as uncontrollable shaking and incontinence. She was initially diagnosed with functional neurological disorder in September 2021, and has since been confined to her house, unable to walk and relying on a mobility scooter. She is taking 32 different drugs each day to manage her symptoms, and has given up her job as a teaching assistant.

A controversial statue of Lucille Ball, so terrifying it has been nicknamed 'Scary Lucy', has been removed from a New York town after residents protested its depiction. Sculptor Dave Poulin, who created the statue, admitted to being 'disappointed' in his work and offered to fix it for free. The statue was based on a famous moment from Ball's show 'I Love Lucy', where she pitches an intoxicating health tonic while drunk. Poulin pledged to make a new one, but it would cost an estimated $8,000 to $10,000. The town has since removed the statue and is considering a new tribute to Ball.

Bayern Munich's versatile left-back David Alaba will be out for around seven weeks with a torn knee ligament after being injured while playing for Austria. Alaba, who was out for three months earlier this season, is set to start rehabilitation work in about a month. Bayern Munich is top of the Bundesliga and through to the German Cup last eight, while Alaba has been in excellent form for the club.

Beatrice Nokes, the daughter of two respected solicitors and a Scotland Yard detective, appeared in court today on charges of inciting a ring of prostitutes operating out of properties in Central London. Nokes, a 21-year-old University College London chemistry student, is accused of running the vice ring with her father's partner, Daniel Williams, a 37-year-old Met police officer. Williams, who is suspended from duty, is accused of committing the crimes while on and off-duty. The case has drawn attention due to the high-profile nature of the defendants and the alleged involvement of law enforcement officials.

Diana Doyle, a whistleblower, revealed that a firm linked to the sale of NHS patient data is offering details of eating disorder sufferers, stress, hair loss, dandruff, impotence, snoring, dieters, and those with plastic surgery for just 12p a head. The firm, Sequester, is offering to sell information on 43 different health conditions, including skin problems, insomnia, migraines, and sensitive teeth. The firm also claims to be able to identify those who have had plastic surgery, smoke, wear glasses or contact lenses, and have wills or health insurance. The revelations prompted probes by the Information Commissioner's Office and the Direct Marketing Commission, and a third investigation by the General Pharmaceutical Council into Pharmacy2U, the UK's biggest online pharmacy.

In a touching moment, golf champion Jordan Spieth, 21, expressed his love for his autistic sister Ellie, who was unable to attend the Masters tournament. Despite the absence of Ellie, Spieth's performance was impressive, winning the tournament with a score of 18 under par. He also mentioned that his sister has shaped his upbringing and provided him with perspective. Spieth's victory was described as "even better" than his dreams, and he expressed his hope to be a part of the Masters history for another 50 years.

Dick Advocaat, the Dutch manager of Sunderland, will not underestimate the significance of the Old Firm derby against Newcastle, which is a crucial fixture for both teams. Advocaat, who had previously underplayed the importance of the match in 1998, insists he will not make the same mistake. The match is expected to be a significant one for Sunderland, who are one point above the relegation zone and could be in the bottom three by kick-off. The Sunderland team includes Adam Johnson, who was recently arrested on suspicion of sexual activity with an under-age girl. The match is expected to be a special one for the home crowd, with Advocaat hoping that the fans will support the team.

A heated argument erupted between a young woman and a butcher in Sydney's eastern suburbs over a chicken purchase dispute. Belinda Bartholomew, the girlfriend of Roosters star Aidan Guerra, claimed she was racially abused at a Bondi butcher shop when she tried to change her chicken selection. The butcher, however, denied the claims, stating that he was the one being rude and that she was the one causing trouble. The incident highlights tensions between immigrants and locals in the area.

Freddo Frogs, a popular children's chocolate, has been reduced in size by 20% from 15g to 12g, while the recommended retail price remains the same. This change was made due to manufacturing cost increases that the company cannot absorb. The decision was made by Cadbury's parent company, Mondelez International, which reported a 46% increase in profit before tax from $87 million to $127 million in 2013. The change has been met with mixed reactions, with some customers expressing disappointment and others defending the company's decision.

Hillary Clinton's campaign-in-waiting met on Saturday in its Brooklyn headquarters, a day before the former secretary of state officially announces her campaign for president. Robby Mook, Clinton's soon-to-be campaign manager, distributed a "values statement" outlining the campaign's purpose, goals, and how they plan to win. The document mentions issues that sunk Clinton's first campaign in 2008, emphasizing humility, discipline, and unity. The campaign aims to remain humble, disciplined, and united, and to win on the ground in states. The document also calls on campaign staffers to remain open to diverse views and to bounce back from tough days. Clinton is planning to launch her presidential candidacy on Sunday through a video message on social media, and will travel to Iowa and New Hampshire.

A 29-year-old woman named Kyli Wilfson, who was 26 when she first experienced severe abdominal pain while eating, was diagnosed with chronic pancreatitis, a rare condition that affects less than 0. 01% of people. Despite being told she had acute pancreatitis, her pain persisted, leading to a year and a half of being unable to eat anything. Kyli, who is a self-confessed "food person," had to rely on a feeding tube to survive and had to postpone her wedding due to rapid weight loss. The condition is characterized by an inflammation of the pancreas and requires lifelong feeding through a tube. Kyli found support on Facebook and eventually received a diagnosis, leading to a new appreciation for food and a desire to help others with the condition.

The article discusses memes posted in reference to the leaders' debate, including images of Prime Minister David Cameron and his deputy Nick Clegg superimposed over Christopher Steed and Stephen Webb from Channel 4 series Gogglebox. The memes also feature other party leaders, such as Nicola Sturgeon, Nigel Farage, Natalie Bennett, and Leanne Wood, and include references to the debate's themes of leadership and power.

Amir Khan, a British boxer, is set to face Manny Pacquiao in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, after Mayweather declined the opportunity. Khan, who has been waiting for Mayweather for two years, is now set to fight Pacquiao, who is preparing to face Mayweather on May 2. The fight could take place in November or December in Abu Dhabi, which would be a dream for Khan as he would be a huge attraction in the Muslim world.

A tiny two-bedroom home in Islington, London, has sold for £750,000, despite being only 5ft wide in some areas and 8ft 8in at its widest. The property, which is described as "well proportioned," has two bedrooms, a narrow galley kitchen, and a garden. The home, which was put on the market for £750,000 in 2001, is now under offer for £750,000, with buyers paying £27,000 in stamp duty. The home's narrow dimensions and unique features, such as a galley kitchen, have attracted interest from potential buyers.

Nicola Sturgeon, the leader of the Scottish National Party (SNP), is set to launch an extraordinary bid to "lead the UK" as she unveils a string of policies tailored for a power-sharing deal with Labour. The SNP manifesto includes proposals for British foreign policy, welfare payments, energy bills, and English university tuition fees. Several of Sturgeon's election pledges overlap with Labour policy, such as slashing tuition fees in England from £9,000 to £6,000 and rolling back competition in the English NHS. The SNP aims to build a "progressive alliance" for people "right across the UK," aiming to increase public spending on infrastructure in northern England and Wales. The manifesto includes plans for modest spending increases funded by more borrowing, totaling £180 billion over five years. The SNP's surge in support could trigger constitutional turmoil similar to the 1910 election, which led to the end of Irish Nationalism and the secession of Ireland

Celtic Football Club won the Glasgow Cup for the fourth time in eight seasons, defeating Rangers 2-0 in a match played behind closed doors at Hampden Park. Josh Kerr scored the opening goal for Celtic, while Robby McCrorie missed a penalty for Rangers. The match was notable for being played without major off-field problems, with Rangers taking the game to Celtic but failing to score.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis insisted he will never change his traditional attire of cap, track suit, and white trainers, even though he previously played for Crystal Palace. The 57-year-old manager led his side to a 2-0 victory over his former club Crystal Palace, ending their run of 10 away games without a victory. Pulis, who has worked wonders at West Brom, has virtually assured their survival in the Premier League.

Jameela Jamil, a 29-year-old television presenter and former model, spent £3,000 on having all her amalgam fillings removed and replaced with white fillings after experiencing health problems for nearly seven years. The fillings were removed due to high levels of mercury detected in her blood, which was ruled as the cause of her symptoms, including puffy faces, heavy heads, and fainting. The dental amalgam, made from a mixture of metals including silver, tin, and copper, is used for robust fillings on back teeth. While the amounts taken in from fillings are minuscule, the review by the EU Commission's Scientific Committee in 2008 concluded there was no risk from amalgam.

Suge Knight, the co-creator of Death Row Records, is awaiting trial for murder and attempted murder in Los Angeles Superior Court. Despite being refused an appeal to have his bail reduced from $10 million to $5 million, Knight believes his close friend, the undefeated professional boxer Floyd Mayweather, will bail him out when he wins on Saturday. Mayweather, worth $420 million, is set to land a record pay check after going head-to-head with Manny Pacquiao on Saturday. Fletcher, Knight's attorney, is confident that Mayweather will come to his aid and bail Knight out.

Gizzi Erskine, a 35-year-old TV chef, has a fussy cat named Kimchi that loves crunchy human food like poppadoms, tortilla chips, and taramasalata. Kimchi is described as a British shorthair that won't eat anything unless it's proper meat and loves anything crunchy. Gizzi Erskine has had to put Kimchi on a diet due to her cat's obesity. Kimchi also loves cheese, caviar, and fish, and occasionally indulges in cat food and Dreamies cat biscuits. Gizzi Erskine recently added a new addition to her cat family, Ponzu, named after her favorite Japanese dressing.

A father in Japan took a photograph of his young daughter standing near a rocky outcrop in July 2014, which later sparked controversy online. The photograph, featuring a pair of black boots behind the girl, has been the subject of debate, with some suggesting it could be a trick of the light or a paranormal phenomenon. The father, Martin Springall, 38, said he has no idea what the boots could be and that he does not recall a person standing behind his daughter. The photograph has been shared on Reddit and has sparked discussion about its authenticity and meaning.

The UK government plans to introduce new immigration policies that will require EU migrants to pay an average of £22,000 in tax and national insurance before they can claim benefits. The measures, which will be outlined in the Tory manifesto, will ban EU migrants from receiving benefits for four years and limit access to in-work benefits until they have been in the UK for four years. The crackdown is aimed at reducing net migration to the UK and limiting the appeal of coming to Britain from poorer parts of the EU.

A severely disabled boy, Cody Neatis, has been sleeping on a mattress on the floor in a hospital bed because the hospital does not have a suitable bed for him to sleep in. Cody has Down's syndrome, epilepsy, autism, and is fed by a tube. His mother, Lynne Neatis, has been sleeping on the floor alongside him for the past week, fearing that her son will injure himself or pull out his oxygen. The hospital does not have the specialist high-sided cot needed for Cody to sleep in, and the mother is demanding answers from the local health trust about why they still do not have a suitable bed. Lynne Neatis has been staying in for nine days in August 2013, and she claims that the ward was getting a special needs bed at that time.

Ahead of golf's first major of the year, Derek Lawrenson will bring daily updates from behind the scenes at Augusta National. The article discusses the preparations for the Masters, including the arrival of players like Rory McIlroy, Henrik Stenson, and Tiger Woods, as well as the tradition of gathering around the 16th hole to see which players can skip their golf balls across the water and onto the green.

Juventus have ruled out a move for Manchester United loan star Radamel Falcao after claiming the Colombia striker's wages are 'beyond their means'. Falcao has endured a difficult period at Old Trafford after arriving in an expensive loan deal from Monaco last summer. Juventus general manager Beppe Marotta has claimed that Falcao wanted to come to Turin last summer but the Serie A champions have now taken themselves out of the race to sign him.

David Cameron plans to sell Lloyds Bank shares worth £4 billion if he wins the election, offering them at a discount and encouraging long-term ownership with a loyalty bonus. This is the largest privatisation since Thatcher's era, with a £20 billion bailout by Gordon Brown.

Living near congested roads with high levels of air pollution can cause 'silent strokes' that increase the risk of dementia, according to a study by researchers at Boston University School of Medicine. The microscopic particles, mostly from traffic fumes and factory emissions, alter the structure of the brain and increase the risk of stroke and dementia. The study involved more than 900 people aged 60 and over who did not have dementia or a history of strokes. The researchers found that increases in PM2.5 in towns and cities were linked with a 46% higher risk of silent strokes.

Jessica Ainscough, a 30-year-old wellness warrior who chose unconventional Gerson Therapy over conventional chemotherapy and radiation, died in February after a seven-year-long battle with epithelioid sarcoma. Her partner, Tallon Pamenter, wrote an emotional letter to her followers, revealing that she began a course of targeted radiation in her final weeks, despite the risks and tough decision. The radiation successfully managed to shrink the tumour but caused complications, leading to her death. Ainscough was known for her unconventional approach to cancer treatment and her love for life, which she shared with her followers.

Ten people, including four children, were involved in a multi-vehicle crash on the Brisbane Valley Highway near Fernvale on Wednesday afternoon. Three vehicles collided, resulting in chest and shoulder injuries for a 40-year-old man and a 5-year-old boy, chest pain for a 5-year-old boy, arm injuries for a 27-year-old woman, abdominal pain for a 6-year-old girl, hand lacerations for a man, and minor injuries for six others. Jason McDonald, a 34-year-old volunteer at the Colorado Gator Farm, walked a thin slackline rope over a pool containing more than 50 hungry alligators, including some that measure up to ten feet in length. The son of a Syrian imam who was shot dead on a London street may have met his father's killer just days before the murder. Sources close to the investigation, which is being led by the counter-terrorism unit, told the Sunday Times that Abdul Hadi Arwani, an opponent of Syrian President Bashar Al-Assad, had visited the area where he was killed with his son days before his death. Arwani, 48, was shot and killed in his car on a quiet street in North West London after being called there last Tuesday, apparently to provide a quote for building work.

Hong Kong's Jenny's cookies, a popular buttery treat, have become a major attraction, with tourists and locals lining up for hours to purchase them. The cookies, priced at $9 each, have sparked a black market, with knockoff versions sold at a 70% markup. The original store has signs warning against buying "fake" cookies, but the frenzy continues. Kira Hollis, a 27-year-old mother-of-one from Tamworth, Staffordshire, overcame anorexia and depression by becoming a bodybuilder. Initially diagnosed with borderline personality disorder, she was ordered to go to the gym to gain weight. There, she turned her life around and is now a healthy 9. 5st personal trainer. Lewis Ferguson, a 18-year-old jockey, survived a spectacular fall from Merrion Square during a race at Wincanton on Wednesday. The fall was captured on video and has been viewed by hundreds of thousands of people online. Ferguson, who was mucking out the stables as usual, was hit by the fence and performed a mid-air somersault. He escaped the fall but sustained a cut on his nose. Hillary Clinton launched her campaign in a unique and unconventional way, using a video, new logo, and road trip to rebrand herself and frame her candidacy. Critics dismissed her efforts as "relentlessly, insultingly vapid" and "boring as s---," but marketing experts argue that her launch may have been more successful than initially thought. The campaign aims to flip Clinton's message from self-absorbed to empathetic, and to change how voters emotionally experience her brand.

In Yichuan, Shaanxi province, Grade One students at Yichuan Senior High School organized an outdoor exam in the playground due to insufficient indoor space. The students turned their desks and chairs to avoid being dazzled by the sun and suggested the outdoor exam as a way to broaden their horizons and prevent cheating. Sportsmail has partnered with Gillette to offer a unique chance for one lucky reader to win a pair of Nike Magista Obra boots signed by Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart. The prize includes a new Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor with Flexball technology and shave gel. The competition closes on April 19.

Kecil, a baby orangutan, has been raised by his surrogate mother Maggie at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo. Maggie, 53, has already raised four of her own children and another surrogate which was given to her in 2002. Kecil, who had a tough start to life after his natural mother and another surrogate mother rejected him, found love with Maggie at the third time of asking. The dogs, a Jack Russell and a Staffordshire Bull Terrier, partially ate her body, and the cause of death was an accidental overdose of medication. The inquest was held to determine the exact cause of death, but the dogs' actions were the most likely cause.

Nikola Karabatic, a French handball star, is facing a fraud trial for his suspected involvement in an illegal betting case related to a match between his Montpellier club and Cesson-Rennes. Karabatic, who was briefly detained, is now playing for Barcelona in the Spanish league. The trial is expected to take place within months, and Karabatic faces up to five years in prison and a fine.

A gang of six men, including Ahmed Hassan-Sule, 21, and Mohamed Saleh, 22, were convicted of a string of sexual offenses against teenage girls in Banbury, Oxfordshire. The offenses occurred in cars, woods, and at the defendants' homes from 2009 to 2014. Aaron Hernandez, a former New England Patriots player, faces three more trials after being convicted of murder and other charges in the death of Odin Lloyd. Hernandez is accused of killing two men and wounding another person near a Boston nightclub in July 2012. The trial for the July 16, 2012, shooting deaths of Daniel de Abreu and Safiro Furtado in Boston's South End is set for May 28, but has been postponed. The Emirates Airline has signed a historic deal with the FA Cup, rebranding it as the Emirates FA Cup. The deal, worth £30 million over three years, will add to Emirates' existing portfolio of sporting sponsorships. The deal includes naming rights to Arsenal's Emirates Stadium, the Emirates Cup, and sponsorship of AC Milan. Emirates has also extended its sponsorship with Hamburg until 2019-20.

Michael Phelps, the 18-time Olympic champion, plans to compete in the Rio Olympics next year but won't swim at the world championships in Russia this summer. He was suspended by USA Swimming after a second DUI arrest last fall, and he's undergoing rehab and AA to overcome his addiction. Phelps is back in Arizona for treatment, and his coach is skeptical about his motivation.

Gareth Bale, a key player for Real Madrid, is doubtful for the team's Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid due to a calf injury. The Welsh forward limped off during Real's 3-1 home victory over Malaga on Saturday. Real Madrid's coach, Carlo Ancelotti, hopes to have striker Karim Benzema fit for the match after the Frenchman missed Saturday's encounter with a knee injury.

Scientists warn that older people are more susceptible to emotions when making decisions about retirement investments, particularly during financial crises. A study of 1,204 retired people found that those with better cognitive abilities were less likely to panic and sell investments during market downturns. The study, published in the Journal of Consumer Affairs, suggests that cognitive decline with age can impair decision-making, especially in the face of emotional responses to market losses. The reforms announced by Chancellor George Osborne allow individuals aged 55 and over to withdraw from their pension and take the income they need, with the option to keep the remaining funds invested in the stock market.

Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini should be given more time to turn around the club's fortunes, according to Stuart Pearce, who believes the team should stick with Pellegrini despite recent poor form. Pearce, who spent time at the club as both a manager and a player, attributes City's poor run of form to the fading influence of Ivorian Yaya Toure.

Miley Cyrus, 22, attended the 30th Annual Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony in Cleveland, Ohio, where she posed for a social media snap with somewhat bushy underarm hair. Paul Gregory, a 51-year-old Bedford resident, was fined £795 for having a blue badge, claiming he could only walk 200 meters, when in fact he was a keen walker and member of a mountaineering club. The incident occurred after Bedford Borough Council staff noticed an article in The Westmorland Gazette describing Gregory's exploits on a 191-mile hike. He pleaded guilty to two counts of dishonestly obtaining a blue badge by misrepresenting his physical abilities and was fined £795, ordered to carry out 150 hours of unpaid work, and paid a £60 victim surcharge.

Apple has filed a patent for a new method of unlocking a mobile device using facial recognition. The patent details a system that would automatically unlock a device if the user's face matches a previously taken photo. The system would track the movement of the phone to determine whether it is being used or placed flat on a table. The patent was filed by Apple in March 2011 and was awarded earlier this week.

Elizabeth Sedway, a 51-year-old mother of two battling cancer, was ejected from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California due to her lack of a doctor's note clearing her to fly. A vintage 1973 E-Type Jaguar was involved in a head-on collision with a 1973 Toyota Kluger on Easter Sunday night in Frenchs Forest, Sydney. The crash comes after police warned motorists to obey road rules during the Easter long weekend.

Google has established a team focused on enhancing the longevity of electronic devices, including smartphones, tablets, and electric vehicles. The team, consisting of four individuals, is dedicated to developing and testing various battery technologies, such as flexible and wearable batteries, as well as those capable of operating in subfreezing temperatures. This initiative follows a similar project launched by Apple in 2012, which involved Dr. Ramesh Bhardwaj leading a testing team. The 223ft Explorer is a luxury superyacht designed by British yacht designer Tony Castro, featuring a helipad, infinity pool, and space for 12 guests. It comes with a climate-controlled garage for storing a helicopter, twin limo tenders, car, submarine, jetskis, and other toys. Ed Miliband, the leader of the Labour Party, announced his intention to implement rent controls despite warnings from experts that the plans would backfire. The controversial measures, demanded by the militant Unite union, would cap rents and offer three-year tenancies, but critics argue that they may lead to more tenants being evicted and landlords raising rents during the initial period.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town fan who said he hoped Arsenal would win in a video was removed from his role as a mascot for Reading in the FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal. The young supporter was offered the opportunity to be a mascot for England instead.

A giant supervoid 1.8 billion light-years across may be responsible for a mysterious 'Cold Spot' in the universe, according to astronomers seeking to understand what is causing this larger-than-expected cold area. If confirmed, the supervoid would be the largest single structure ever found by humanity. The supervoid appears to be 'roughly spherical' and may even contain a 'significant substructure' at its centre. The supervoid is thought to be causing a 'less-dense' region of the universe, which can 'sap' the energy of light passing through it. This can be explained by the supervoid acting as a hill, with light climbing the hill and losing energy, while descending the hill and regaining energy. However, some 'exotic physics' is also needed to explain what's happening.

The red, worn chair Abraham Lincoln was shot in at Ford's Theatre in Washington D.C. in 1865 will be displayed in an open plaza on April 15 as part of the Henry Ford Museum's observance of the assassination's 150th anniversary. The chair, which has a dark stain on the back believed to be blood from the shooting, will be removed from its enclosure to be displayed for the event. Jake Boys, a 19-year-old vlogger from Hailsham, England, surprised his girlfriend Emily Canham by booking plane tickets to see One Direction perform in Cardiff.
